title: [P0] gluetun SOCKS/HTTP proxy = open unauth cluster pivot (pentest 008 escalated)
description: netseg LIVE-PROVEN: from an external LAN host, socks5://192.168.1.251:1080 (+ every node hostPort :1080/:8080) reaches authentik-postgres-rw:5432 (SOCKS5 granted) + argocd-server:80 + authentik-server:80 (HTTP 200) — bypassing Traefik lan-only + Authentik forward-auth entirely. gluetun killswitch blocks apiserver+LAN but NOT the pod/service CIDR. FIX: drop the socks/httpproxy Traefik entrypoints if external clients don't need them (consume gluetun in-cluster only), OR add loadBalancerSourceRanges + proxy auth + a CNP; AND tighten FIREWALL_OUTBOUND_SUBNETS to drop 10.244.0.0/16+10.96.0.0/12. traefik/helmrelease.yaml:131-149. Also confirm router WAN-forward status of :1080/:8080.
notes:
RE-VERIFIED STILL LIVE 2026-09-12. Not stale, not already fixed.

The exposure MOVED but did not close. gluetun's own Service is now ClusterIP-only (vpn-gateway/gluetun 10.101.112.43, ports 1080/8080/9999/8000) — no NodePort, no LoadBalancer — so inspecting the Service alone makes this look remediated. It is not: Traefik carries the exposure instead.

  traefik DaemonSet args: --entryPoints.socks.address=:1080/tcp
                          --entryPoints.httpproxy.address=:8080/tcp
  hostPort 1080 AND 8080 bound on ALL FIVE nodes (traefik-76vs6/8wfvf/drwv2/fvn4v/tz2q2)
  IngressRouteTCP vpn-gateway/gluetun-socks + vpn-gateway/gluetun-http-proxy, both 125d old

Reachability confirmed against a node InternalIP from inside the cluster: TCP connect succeeds on both in ~0.5ms. Port 8080 answers HTTP 400 to a plain GET, which is a proxy rejecting a non-proxy-style request, i.e. a live proxy — not a closed port.

Remediation must target the TRAEFIK entrypoints + IngressRouteTCPs, not the gluetun Service. Shares a root with TALOS-lxz5.1.3 (same two ports); fix them together.

title: [#1] Enable Cilium WireGuard transparent encryption
description: infrastructure/base/cilium/values.yaml: replace the commented block with encryption.enabled:true, type:wireguard, nodeEncryption:false. The repo's 'VXLAN 100% packet loss' diagnosis is WRONG — real cause was MTU=1370 vs Nebula-1300; at MTU=1250 on Cilium 1.20 (WireguardOverhead=95 fix) max frame=1250 fits. NO MTU change. Agent-restart only, no reboot. CAVEATS: keep IPv6 disabled (1280 min-MTU would clamp wg0 upward); do NOT set nodeEncryption:true (cilium#46100 frag drops) or strictMode initially (silent plaintext fallback for un-rolled nodes -> hard-drop). Verify: cilium-dbg status | grep -i encryption (Peers==4), hubble observe --unencrypted. Value: very high (retroactively encrypts most of §4/§5/§6). Risk: med, reversible.

title: [#2] TLS on onepassword-connect (ESO credential broker)
description: §6.1: all 124 ExternalSecrets fetch from http://onepassword-connect:8080 — every secret + the Connect bearer token cross the pod net in cleartext (worst offender). Enable TLS on onepassword-connect + flip the ClusterSecretStore connectHost to https. Covers same-node too (unlike WireGuard). Value very high, effort low-med.
notes:
Deferred to a watched follow-up (operator decision 2026-09-11). WireGuard (#1) now encrypts cross-node pod traffic, so the residual value here is same-node + app-layer auth (defense-in-depth), not raw confidentiality. Both touch load-bearing infra (ESO secrets broker / argocd+authentik caches) — do fresh + verified, not at the tail of a long session.
INVESTIGATED 2026-09-11. Connect 1.8.2 DOES support native TLS (OP_TLS_CERT_FILE/OP_TLS_KEY_FILE + OP_HTTPS_PORT=8443) — BUT it serves HTTPS-ONLY (drops http:8080; probed http:8080->000, https:8443->200). So #2 is a HARD CUTOVER of the whole secrets plane, NOT the safe parallel-port approach. Compounded by the ESO onepassword provider having NO caBundle/caProvider field -> ESO controller must trust homelab-ca at the process level (trust-manager useDefaultCAs bundle + SSL_CERT_FILE mount on the external-secrets controller). Cert (onepassword-connect-tls, homelab-ca) is STAGED in the repo (certificate.yaml) for a deliberate cutover. Cutover plan (do together in a watched window): (1) ESO controller trust via SSL_CERT_FILE bundle, verify ES still sync on http; (2) fix connect-api probes to httpGet scheme:HTTPS port:8443; (3) flip both ClusterSecretStores connectHost -> https://...:8443; apply together so connect rolls https-only as ESO switches to https; secrets (k8s Secrets) persist through the refresh gap. Rollback: revert connectHost+probe+deployment to http. WireGuard already encrypts the cross-node hop, so residual = same-node only. Reverted to clean http-only 2026-09-11 (deployment 4d096ddd); ESO 153/154 healthy.
DONE + verified 2026-09-11. Cutover: (A) ESO controller trusts homelab-ca via trust-manager bundle (public+homelab CAs) + SSL_CERT_FILE; (B) Connect serves HTTPS-only on :8443 (OP_TLS_*), probes fixed to https:8443, both ClusterSecretStores flipped to https://...:8443. Result: Connect 2/2 Ready https-only, both stores Ready, ExternalSecrets 153/154 (the 1 = pre-existing decommissioned crossplane-system/aws-credentials) — zero regression. Secrets plane now TLS end-to-end incl. same-node. NOTE: Step B commit was absorbed into a concurrent peer commit (4247b999) via the shared git-index race — changes are correct + live + in HEAD.

title: Scope reconciler RBAC: resourceNames on pods/exec + secrets; drop exec if unused
description: Finding 004 (unscoped pods/exec + secrets/create in ns authentik, bound to SA in media-private = IdP compromise path). infrastructure/base/authentik/private-sso-reconciler.yaml. Add resourceNames; remove pods/exec entirely if the reconciler only patches named secrets. Verify the sister-repo workload's real needs.
notes:
INVESTIGATION 2026-09-09: the consuming workload is a live CronJob 'private-sso-reconciler' in ns media-private running registry.talos00/...private-sso-reconciler:1@sha256:1ba5517... (command: python /scripts/reconcile.py). The script is baked into the image + owned by the sister talos-private repo — NOT visible in this repo. Cannot safely scope pods/exec (dynamic pod names) or narrow secrets/create without reconcile.py. BLOCKED on sister-repo context: need to see what reconcile.py execs (likely 'ak' commands in authentik-server) and which secrets it creates. Do NOT scope blindly — it manages authentik-zipline-oidc + amberdark-outpost-token (live SSO). Next step: read reconcile.py in the talos-private repo, then scope resourceNames / drop exec if the script uses the API instead.
RESOLVED-TO-DECISION after reading talos-private/base/auth/{reconcile,account_sync,native_sso}.py: the SA legitimately needs pods/exec (account_sync runs 'kubectl -n authentik exec deploy/authentik-worker -- ak shell' to provision users) and secrets/create (native_sso does kubectl apply to mint OIDC secrets). NEITHER is resourceName-scopable in K8s RBAC (exec=dynamic pod names; create=object doesn't exist yet). So finding 004's 'add resourceNames' fix is impractical. REFRAME: this SA is effectively authentik-admin via ak shell. Real hardening options: (A) accept + ensure only the CronJob mounts the SA (Role already ns-scoped to authentik) — low effort; (B) rewrite reconciler to use the authentik API + scoped token instead of ak-shell exec → drops pods/exec entirely (sister-repo change). LATENT BUG found: native_sso reads authentik-immich-oidc but the authentik-ns Role get/patch resourceNames=[authentik-zipline-oidc,private-app-sso-credentials,amberdark-outpost-token] omits it → immich-oidc get likely 403s. Decide A vs B with the operator.
close_reason: ACCEPTED current approach per operator (2026-09-09): scoping pods/exec + secrets/create by resourceNames is impractical in K8s RBAC (exec=dynamic pods; create can't be name-scoped), and the exec is load-bearing (account_sync runs 'ak shell' in authentik-worker). Role is already ns-scoped to authentik + used only by the private-sso-reconciler CronJob. Proper fix (API + scoped token to drop exec) tracked as TALOS-lxz5.5.7.

title: Back up the Talos secrets bundle to 1Password before any migration work
description:
BLOCKS EVERYTHING ELSE IN TALOS-0bo8. Do this first.

The cluster's entire identity — machine CA, Kubernetes CA, etcd CA, aggregator CA, service-account key, machine token, k8s bootstrap token, cluster.id/cluster.secret, secretbox encryption secret — currently exists in exactly ONE place: the gitignored file configs/nodes/controlplane.yaml on one laptop. There is no backup. Losing it means the cluster cannot be extended or rebuilt, ever.

Extract it into a proper secrets bundle:

  talosctl gen secrets --from-controlplane-config configs/nodes/controlplane.yaml -o talsecret.yaml

VERIFIED 2026-08-23 that this round-trips exactly — all five CAs, both tokens, cluster.id, cluster.secret and the secretbox secret matched the live cluster byte-for-byte. See docs/02-architecture/talos-config-management.md section C.

Then store it as a 1Password document (recommend item name "talos catalyst-cluster talsecret" in the infra vault) and PROVE retrieval works from a second machine with `op document get`. A backup you have not restored from is not a backup.

Treat the extracted plaintext carefully: it contains CA private keys. Generate into a temp dir and `rm -P` after upload.
acceptance_criteria:
- talsecret.yaml extracted and its contents verified against the live cluster
- Stored in 1Password
- Retrieval verified from a second machine
- Local plaintext copy securely deleted
- etcd snapshot taken
close_reason:
Backed up to 1Password 2026-08-24 as Secure Note 'talos-secrets-bundle', confirmed present by the user.

Contents verified complete before backup (presence only, never values):
    etcd              crt+key
    k8s               crt+key
    k8saggregator     crt+key
    k8sserviceaccount key        <- key-only by design, not a missing cert
    os                crt+key
    cluster.id, cluster.secret, bootstraptoken, trustdinfo.token   all SET

Extracted with:
    talosctl gen secrets --from-controlplane-config configs/nodes/controlplane.yaml \
      -o talos/talsecret.yaml
That EXTRACTS existing identity rather than generating new, so it is reproducible and
non-destructive — the same command run again yields the same material.

Prior to this there was exactly ONE copy, on one laptop, untracked. Losing it would have made
the cluster unrecoverable: every CA would differ on regeneration, so etcd would reject the new
member and kubelet would fail TLS to the API server. Recovery would have meant rebuilding from
scratch and restoring from Velero and CNPG.

Gitignore hardened as part of this. The rules were originally anchored paths
(talos/talsecret.yaml), which would have STOPPED MATCHING after the planned
'mv talos/ configs/' cutover — a subsequent git add would then have staged the whole bundle.
Verified at the time: git check-ignore configs/talsecret.yaml returned nothing. Now matched by
filename (talsecret.yaml, **/talsecret.yaml, clusterconfig/, **/clusterconfig/) and confirmed
ignored under BOTH paths. Do not re-anchor them.

Runbook: docs/05-runbooks/talsecret-1password-backup.md

Stays manual deliberately: the op on PATH is not the 1Password CLI (it resolves to macOS
open), and ESO reaches 1Password through a Connect server running IN the cluster — the wrong
direction, since this is the secret you would need to rebuild that cluster. A bootstrap secret
cannot depend on the thing it bootstraps.

title: Control plane: honest kube-apiserver/KCM/scheduler requests (+11 GiB), and move the 3rd CP off talos03
description:
kube-apiserver is the single largest memory consumer in the cluster and its request is
half its steady state. Worse, one of the three control planes is the node with the
LEAST RAM in the fleet.

## MEASURED (14d)

    container                          node        req    lim     p50     peak
    kube-apiserver                     talos00    4096M  12288M  5918M   8288M
    kube-apiserver                     talos01    2048M   6144M  4562M   5551M
    kube-apiserver                     talos03    2048M   6144M  4699M   5247M
    kube-controller-manager            talos00     128M    512M   343M    364M
    kube-controller-manager            talos01     128M    512M    18M    306M   (non-leader)
    kube-controller-manager            talos03     128M    512M   285M    313M
    kube-scheduler                     talos00      64M    128M   102M    115M
    kube-scheduler                     talos01      64M    128M    53M     96M
    kube-scheduler                     talos03      64M    128M    88M    109M

Every one of these nine containers has a request BELOW its p50. kube-apiserver on
talos00 requests 4096M and sits at 5918M p50 -- the scheduler believes there is 1.8 GiB
on that node that does not exist, per apiserver, times three.

## THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM -- talos03 should not be a control plane

    talos03: 12.5 GiB allocatable, 15.6 CPU
      kube-apiserver peak         5247M
      kube-controller-manager      313M
      kube-scheduler               109M
      (etcd runs in Talos, outside k8s accounting)
      -----------------------------------------
      >= 5.7 GiB = 45% of the node's entire allocatable memory

    talos03 sums to 13.9 GiB of container peaks against 12.5 GiB allocatable (111%)
    while sitting at 18% of CPU requests. It is the CPU-richest and RAM-poorest node
    in the fleet and it is carrying a control plane.

    talos06: 59.8 GiB allocatable, 15.6 CPU, 35% memory used, 32% CPU requested.

RECOMMENDATION: demote talos03 to worker and promote talos06 to the third control
plane. That relocates ~5.7 GiB off the tightest node onto the emptiest one, and leaves
talos03 as a pure worker whose 15.6 CPUs can be used for CPU-bound, low-memory work --
which is the shape it actually has.

This is an etcd member change + Talos machine config change + reboot. It is the single
highest-leverage placement change available and it is NOT reversible cheaply, so it is
the operator's call. The alternative (keep talos03 as CP, evacuate ~4 GiB of media
workloads off it) is covered by the "evacuate talos01 and talos03" child; it works but
it permanently spends half of talos03 on control-plane overhead.

## SIZING (apply regardless of the placement decision)

Control-plane static pods are Talos machine-config, not Flux -- these change in the
machine config / bootstrap patches, not in infrastructure/.
Keep them BURSTABLE with generous limits. A tight memory limit on kube-apiserver
converts a LIST storm into an OOMKill of the control plane, which is strictly worse
than the memory pressure it prevents.

    container                 req now -> new     lim now -> new     class
    kube-apiserver (talos00)   4096M -> 6144M    12288M -> 12288M   BURSTABLE
    kube-apiserver (talos01)   2048M -> 6144M     6144M -> 12288M   BURSTABLE
    kube-apiserver (talos03)   2048M -> 6144M     6144M -> 12288M   BURSTABLE
    kube-controller-manager     128M ->  384M      512M ->   768M   BURSTABLE  (x3)
    kube-scheduler               64M ->  128M      128M ->   256M   BURSTABLE  (x3)

    scheduler accounting delta: +11.0 GiB honest (this is the largest single honest-up
    adjustment in the epic; it is real memory that is already in use and currently
    invisible)

NOTE talos00's apiserver peaked at 8288M vs 5551M/5247M on the other two -- it is the
one behind the VIP taking the majority of traffic. 6144M request / 12288M limit keeps
it burstable rather than pinning it.

## BLOCKED ON MEASUREMENT

The apiserver's own Go heap cannot currently be measured: the ServiceMonitor
keep-regex in infrastructure/base/monitoring/control-plane-scrape/apiserver.yaml drops
go_memstats_* for job="kubernetes". Landing FIX 4 of the alloy child restores it. Until
then it is not possible to say how much of the apiserver's 5-8 GiB is watch cache vs
GC headroom, and therefore whether GOGC/--watch-cache-sizes tuning would help.
notes:
PARTIALLY LANDED 2026-08-24. talos00 and talos01 now at 5Gi request / 7Gi limit, applied via Talos machine config without reboot. Patch tracked at docs/05-runbooks/talos-apiserver-resources-patch.yaml.

Measured: steady state 4886-5299Mi, 7d peak on v1.36.4 containers 6644/5758/5707Mi. Cross-checked against container_memory_rss (6625/5733/5671Mi) to rule out page-cache inflation — it is genuine RSS. The old 6Gi limit was BELOW the observed peak, so this was an OOMKill risk and not just an accounting problem; talos01's apiserver has one restart with reason Error.

talos00 had drifted to 4Gi/12Gi while talos01 and talos03 were 2Gi/6Gi. Now uniform where applied.

REMAINING: talos03. It has 2258Mi free and needs 3072Mi. kube-apiserver is a STATIC pod so raising its request cannot fail to schedule — it would evict other pods off the node instead. Left at 2Gi/6Gi (status quo, still under-declared) rather than deliberately oversubscribing a 12.8Gi node that has already wedged once.

To finish: free ~814Mi on talos03. The only candidates left are six CNPG replicas (crowdsec, forgejo, homeassistant, linkwarden, bookorbit, zipline — all confirmed role=replica on healthy 3/3 clusters). Moving them means the documented rolling migration: delete a replica PVC, let CNPG rebuild it elsewhere, one at a time. Destructive to database volumes — needs explicit user approval.

title: alloy 6GB is apiserver-histogram cardinality, not a leak — fix the keep-regex, then size it
description:
alloy (monitoring/alloy, single replica, currently on talos01) uses 6074Mi against a
1024Mi request and NO limit. It is NOT leaking. Measured cause below.

## THE MEASUREMENT

    prometheus_remote_write_wal_storage_active_series{job="alloy"}   607,637
    go_memstats_heap_alloc_bytes                                     3338 Mi   (live heap)
    go_memstats_heap_inuse_bytes                                     4005 Mi
    go_memstats_next_gc_bytes                                        5658 Mi   (GC target)
    process_resident_memory_bytes                                    6075 Mi

    3338 Mi live heap / 607,637 series = 5.76 KiB per active series. That is normal for
    a prometheus remote-write WAL appender. The memory is CARDINALITY, not a leak.

30d trend -- RSS tracks active series exactly:

    date       07-24    08-02    08-07    08-09    08-16    08-20    08-23
    series    286771   294545   309633   400335   456546   438909   607643
    RSS Mi      1957     1945     2136       --      3082     3129     6104

## ROOT CAUSE (two events, both visible in the series curve)

1. 2026-08-08T22:07:23Z -- ServiceMonitor kube-system/kube-apiserver created by the
   Flux kustomization `control-plane-scrape`
   (infrastructure/base/monitoring/control-plane-scrape/apiserver.yaml). Its
   metricRelabelings are:

       - sourceLabels: [__name__]
         regex: (apiserver_request_.*|etcd_request_.*)
         action: keep

   The comment above it says "the metricRelabelings keep list bounds cardinality
   (~apiserver histograms are the biggest offenders on a full apiserver scrape)".
   It then KEEPS exactly those histograms and drops everything cheap. Series went
   309,633 -> 400,335 across 08-08/08-09.

2. 2026-08-23 -- promotion to 3 control planes tripled the number of apiserver
   instances being scraped by that ServiceMonitor. Series 438,909 -> 607,643, alloy
   3129 -> 6104 Mi, ON THE SAME DAY talos03 wedged.

Current cost of that one ServiceMonitor:

       80,208  apiserver_request_duration_seconds_bucket
       53,136  etcd_request_duration_seconds_bucket
       50,116  apiserver_request_sli_duration_seconds_bucket
       24,480  apiserver_request_body_size_bytes_bucket
      ~21,600  all remaining apiserver_request_*/etcd_request_* count/sum/total
      -------
      229,572  series = 37.8% of alloy's entire WAL

IT IS STILL GROWING. talos03's apiserver pod is 44 min old and only contributes 14,572
of those series so far; talos01 contributes 114,284. When talos03 warms up, expect
~+95,000 more series and alloy at ~7 GiB.

## FIX 1 -- drop the buckets nothing reads (repo grep, all dashboards checked)

Used by dashboards:
  apiserver_request_duration_seconds_bucket -> catalyst-k8s-dashboard.json,
    etcd-snapshot-correlation.json, kubevirt-control-plane.json (x4 panels).
    EVERY query filters verb!~"WATCH|CONNECT".
  etcd_request_duration_seconds_bucket -> kubevirt-control-plane.json (1 panel).

Used by nothing:
  apiserver_request_sli_duration_seconds_bucket   50,116 series  -- zero repo hits
  apiserver_request_body_size_bytes_bucket        24,480 series  -- zero repo hits

Safe drops in infrastructure/base/monitoring/control-plane-scrape/apiserver.yaml:
  - drop __name__ =~ apiserver_request_sli_duration_seconds_bucket      -50,116
  - drop __name__ =~ apiserver_request_body_size_bytes_bucket           -24,480
  - drop apiserver_request_duration_seconds_bucket{verb=~"WATCH|CONNECT"} -24,816
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  total                                                                 -99,412 series
                                                             = 16.4% of alloy's WAL
                                                             ~= -1.0 GiB alloy RSS

  Zero dashboard impact -- every consumer already excludes WATCH|CONNECT.

## FIX 2 -- set GOMEMLIMIT

next_gc is 5658 Mi against a 3338 Mi live heap: Go is allowed to grow to ~1.7x live
before collecting, and RSS follows. Setting GOMEMLIMIT forces the GC to work harder
instead of letting RSS balloon. Add to the alloy container env in
infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/alloy/helmrelease.yaml:

    - name: GOMEMLIMIT
      value: "3750MiB"      # ~= 0.9 * the new memory limit

## FIX 3 -- honest request/limit (do LAST, after fixes 1+2 land and are measured)

    current:   requests.memory 1Gi     limits.memory (none)
    proposed:  requests.memory 4Gi     limits.memory 5Gi     GOMEMLIMIT 4500MiB
               (post-cardinality-fix projection: ~508k series x 5.76 KiB = 2.9 GiB
                live heap, ~3.5-4 GiB RSS with GOMEMLIMIT holding the ceiling)

    If fixes 1+2 are NOT done first, the honest number is requests 8Gi / limits 16Gi
    and it will keep climbing. Do not ship that.

## FIX 4 -- restore observability of the apiserver itself

The keep-regex also drops go_memstats_* and process_resident_memory_bytes for
job="kubernetes", so the apiserver's own heap is UNMEASURABLE right now (see
TALOS child "control plane sizing"). Add to the keep regex -- it is only a few
dozen series:

    (apiserver_request_.*|etcd_request_.*|go_memstats_.*|process_resident_memory_bytes|process_cpu_seconds_total)

## VERIFY

    kubectl port-forward -n monitoring svc/mimir-query-frontend 18080:8080
    curl -H 'X-Scope-OrgID: anonymous' --data-urlencode \
      'query=prometheus_remote_write_wal_storage_active_series{job="alloy"}' \
      localhost:18080/prometheus/api/v1/query
    # expect ~508,000 after fix 1, down from 607,637

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
VERIFIED WITH CORRECTIONS, then implemented (ce07af11+b4068580, re-applied in 421343bd).

The core claim -- cardinality, not a leak -- holds: goroutines flat at ~3.2k across the whole window, and live heap tracks series. But three things in this ticket were wrong:

1. Per-series cost is 3.7 KiB, not 5.76. min_over_time(go_memstats_heap_alloc_bytes[1h]) = 2584Mi over 730,891 series.

2. The series counts were overstated. Measured against Mimir 2026-08-24:
     apiserver_request_sli_duration_seconds_bucket   26,444  (ticket said 50,116)
     apiserver_request_body_size_bytes_bucket         9,472  (ticket said 24,480)
     apiserver_request_duration_*{WATCH|CONNECT}     30,030  (ticket said 24,816)
   Full families incl. _count/_sum: 68,942 series, 9.4% of the WAL -- not the 16.4% claimed.

3. 'RSS tracks active series exactly' is FALSE for the single largest step. Between 2026-08-20T20:00Z and 08-21T02:00Z, with ONE pod and no restart, RSS went 3135Mi -> 5022Mi (+60%) while active series FELL 486,196 -> 425,933 (-12%) and ingest fell 11,282 -> 8,916 samples/s. More memory for less work. Cause not identified; goroutines were flat, remote-write lag was 0, no alloy version change, no target-count change. Worth its own ticket.

The dominant lever turned out to be FIX 2, not FIX 1: next_gc was 5266Mi against a 2584Mi live heap -- exactly GOGC=100 -- so over half of RSS was GC headroom, not data.

Also 'EVERY query filters verb!~WATCH|CONNECT' is imprecise: only 2 of 6 do. The other 4 use positive allowlists (verb=~LIST|GET, verb=~POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE) which exclude those verbs anyway, so the conclusion was right.

RESULT (alloy pod 6 min after rollout):
                 before    after
  RSS            5666Mi    3700Mi   -35%
  next_gc        5266Mi    3207Mi   GOMEMLIMIT holding under 3750MiB
  heap_alloc     4741Mi    2442Mi
  request           1Gi       4Gi   (limit: none -> 8Gi)

Dropped families confirmed gone: body_size 0 series, WATCH|CONNECT 0 series, sli_duration 88 residual.
FIX 4 works -- go_memstats/process_resident for job=kubernetes are back, and they show the apiservers at 3245Mi / 4513Mi / 5540Mi RSS. talos03's apiserver is 5540Mi on a 12.5GiB node; that is directly relevant to the wedge and was previously unmeasurable.

CAVEAT: 484,314 series post-restart is not steady state -- the WAL resets on restart. Expect ~662,000 (730,891 - 68,942) once warm. Re-measure RSS in 24h against the 4Gi request.

title: RESUME HERE: talos01 down after reset, needs USB boot — full state and next steps
description:
STATE AS OF 2026-08-23 ~03:20 — talos01 is DOWN and needs a USB boot. Everything else healthy.

## WHERE WE GOT TO
EPIC 0 completed. EPIC 1 started: talos01 was drained and reset, and did NOT come back.

## *** talos01: WHAT IT NEEDS (do this first tomorrow) ***
Screen shows a bare cursor — no bootable device. talosctl reset wiped the boot disk.

  1. Write this ISO to USB and boot talos01 from it:
     https://factory.talos.dev/image/c9078f9419961640c712a8bf2bb9174933dfcf1da383fd8ea2b7dc21493f8bac/v1.13.2/metal-amd64.iso
     (verified available, 337 MB. This is talos01's OWN factory schematic — iscsi-tools —
     at v1.13.2 to match the cluster. The ISO in configs/ is v1.11.1 and stock: DO NOT USE.)
  2. It comes up in maintenance mode on 192.168.1.177.
  3. Apply a control-plane config built for talos01 specifically — see the landmine below.

## *** THE LANDMINE — the runbook's config is WRONG for both nodes ***
  configs/nodes/controlplane.yaml   install.disk /dev/sda   image ghcr.io/siderolabs/installer (STOCK)
  talos01 actually needs            install.disk /dev/nvme0n1
                                    image factory.talos.dev/installer/c9078f94...:v1.13.2
  talos03 actually needs            install.disk /dev/nvme0n1
                                    image factory.talos.dev/installer/1e17720b...:v1.13.2
                                    schematic: amd-ucode + amdgpu + iscsi-tools (DIFFERENT from talos01)
                                    ISO: https://factory.talos.dev/image/1e17720baa2217bdf64a7caa256011144fce07af5dd12ce18baed735789e7c81/v1.13.2/metal-amd64.iso

Applying the generic controlplane.yaml installs to a disk the node does not boot from with an
image missing its extensions. talos03 would have hit this identically — the reset failure just
got there first.

## BEFORE TOUCHING talos03 — pre-stage, do not repeat tonight
  - Build talos03's control-plane config FIRST (its disk, its schematic image), do not use the
    generic one.
  - Write its ISO to USB BEFORE the reset, not after.
  - Confirm console/physical access. No BMC exists on these machines.
  - Note talos03 also has amdgpu — losing that extension breaks VAAPI transcoding.

## WHAT IS HEALTHY RIGHT NOW (verified)
  nodes: talos00, talos02-gpu, talos03, talos06 Ready. talos01 NotReady.
  etcd:  single voter on talos00, 288 MB, raft applied == index, no alarms.
         Snapshot at .output/talos-etcd-snap, 286150688 bytes, off-Synology.
  CNPG:  authentik 3/3, boomtime 3/3, crowdsec 3/3, forgejo 3/3 — ALL replicas rebuilt.
  ingress: grafana/argocd 200.
  ~44 pods show Unknown — ghosts of talos01's kubelet being unreachable, not real failures.
  talos01 remains cordoned; everything on it was drained BEFORE the reset, nothing lost.

## WHAT WORKED AND SHOULD BE KEPT
  nodeMaintenanceWindow with reusePVC:false on the local-path CNPG clusters did exactly its
  job — authentik-postgres-3 and boomtime-postgres-1 relocated off talos01 to talos03 and
  rebuilt by streaming. Both clusters back to 3/3 without intervention. That setting is still
  applied to authentik-postgres and boomtime-postgres and should be reverted (inProgress:false)
  once talos01 is back.

## THE REAL FIX — TALOS-0bo8 (P1)
Adopt talhelper. Declarative talconfig.yaml describing every node's intent (disk, schematic,
extensions, patches) + SOPS-encrypted talsecret.yaml, both in git; generated configs stay
gitignored. That makes any node rebuildable from the repo, which tonight proved is not
currently true. https://budimanjojo.github.io/talhelper/latest/
CAUTION: talosctl gen config makes NEW PKI unless given the secrets bundle. Live cluster id is
_h70D_fSmLmFjz2mJs8E_j_k — any regeneration must preserve it.

Related: TALOS-8tis (EPIC 1), TALOS-0bo8 (flatten config), TALOS-172v (virt-api cert),
TALOS-z2op (gaming health check).

Checked every CNPG cluster in the fleet, deliberately against the CURRENT field (.spec.plugins + ScheduledBackup/Backup resources), not the deprecated .spec.backup.barmanObjectStore which reads <none> on all of them and is what makes this look uncovered at a glance.

ALL 20 clusters use the barman-cloud.cloudnative-pg.io plugin and have a daily ScheduledBackup. Fleet-wide Backup phases: 468 completed, 8 failed (historical). Every one of the 20 clusters has a phase=completed backup dated 2026-09-12, spanning 02:00-04:30.

title: Ship immich-video-faces spinoff: create GH repo, push 3 repos in order, verify ArgoCD sync
description:
## Background

`immich-video-faces` (face detection app that pulls from Immich's Postgres + REST API) was previously a subdirectory of `talos-private/base/`, deployed as part of the `arr-stack-private` ArgoCD Application. On 2026-07-14 it was lifted out into its own top-level workspace repo (`workspace/immich-video-faces`) so it can be iterated independently while still deploying into the same `media-private` namespace (co-located with immich for in-cluster DNS to `immich-postgres`, etc.).

**All filesystem changes and manifest wiring are DONE and validated locally.** This task is purely the "push in the right order + verify ArgoCD picks it up" execution step. Nothing here requires re-designing — treat it as a runbook.

## What's already been done (do NOT redo)

### `workspace/immich-video-faces/` (new repo, git init'd on `main`, ~101 files staged, uncommitted)
- Full app moved out of `talos-private/base/immich-video-faces/` — 88 originally tracked files + uncommitted mods (Dockerfile, Tiltfile, frontend/**) came along.
- K8s manifests promoted into `k8s/` subdir to match the `catalyst-data` convention (ArgoCD points `path: k8s`). Files in `k8s/`: configmap, cronjob, deployment, ingressroute, kustomization, pvc, service-postgres, service.
- `tilt/kustomization.yaml`: relative path fixed (`../configmap.yaml` -> `../k8s/configmap.yaml`).
- `Tiltfile`: comment updated re: dev.sh location (dev.sh still lives in `talos-private/` and is unchanged).
- Its own `.beads/` dir came along — fresh beads DB, separate from talos-private's.
- `kubectl kustomize workspace/immich-video-faces/k8s/` builds clean.

### `workspace/talos-private/` (detached)
- Removed `- immich-video-faces/` from `base/kustomization.yaml` resources (comment left pointing at the new ArgoCD App).
- Was NOT in the `replacements:` block — no additional unwiring needed.
- `git status` shows 88 deletions + 1 kustomization.yaml edit staged for the spinoff commit.
- `kubectl kustomize workspace/talos-private/base/` still builds clean.

### `workspace/talos-homelab/` (ArgoCD backlink created)
- New file: `infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/immich-video-faces.yaml`
  - Modeled on `catalyst-data.yaml` (HTTPS repoURL, `path: k8s`, `info:` block).
  - Modeled on `arr-stack-private.yaml` for `syncOptions` (`CreateNamespace=false`, `ServerSideApply=true`, foreground prune).
  - `repoURL: https://github.com/TheBranchDriftCatalyst/immich-video-faces.git`, `targetRevision: main`.
  - `destination.namespace: media-private` (same namespace as immich so in-cluster service DNS works).
  - `finalizers: resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io`, retry 5x/5s->3m, prune+selfHeal automated.
  - `part-of: arr-stack-private` label so it groups in the ArgoCD dashboard.
- Added `- immich-video-faces.yaml` to `infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/kustomization.yaml`.
- `kubectl kustomize infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/` builds clean.

## Why ordering matters

ArgoCD reconciles by cloning `repoURL` at `targetRevision`. If talos-homelab is pushed BEFORE the new immich-video-faces repo has a `main` branch, the App goes `ComparisonError` / `Unknown` and needs a manual re-sync after the repo exists. Avoidable by pushing in the order below.

## Runbook (execute in this exact order)

### 1. Create GH repo + push `workspace/immich-video-faces` FIRST
```
cd workspace/immich-video-faces
# Trim before first commit — currently staged:
#   - test.mp4 (63MB) -> move to .gitignore or Git LFS (GitHub warns >50MB, blocks >100MB)
#   - .DS_Store, .venv/, .pytest_cache/, .playwright-mcp/, ~/ -> all should be gitignored
#   - .beads/ -> keep (it's the app's own issue tracker now)
gh repo create TheBranchDriftCatalyst/immich-video-faces --private --source=. --remote=origin
git commit -m "Initial commit: spun out from talos-private"
git push -u origin main
```

### 2. Push `talos-homelab` (creates ArgoCD App -> auto-syncs from repo pushed in step 1)
```
cd workspace/talos-homelab
git add infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/immich-video-faces.yaml \
        infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/kustomization.yaml
git commit -m "Add immich-video-faces ArgoCD Application (spun out of talos-private)"
git push
```

### 3. Commit `talos-private` spinoff (record removal)
```
cd workspace/talos-private
git add -A base/immich-video-faces base/kustomization.yaml
git commit -m "Spin out immich-video-faces to its own repo + ArgoCD app"
git push
```

### 4. Verify ArgoCD adopts the resources cleanly
Because the pods/PVC/service/ingressroute previously existed under the `arr-stack-private` App, ArgoCD may briefly show both Apps claiming the same resources. ServerSideApply + automated prune should resolve this, but verify:
```
kubectl -n argocd get app immich-video-faces -w
argocd app get immich-video-faces
kubectl -n media-private get all -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=arr-stack-private | grep -i ivf   # should be empty
kubectl -n media-private get all -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=immich-video-faces               # should list them
```
If drift/dupes appear: `argocd app get immich-video-faces --refresh`, then `argocd app sync immich-video-faces`. Worst case: `argocd app sync arr-stack-private --prune` then `argocd app sync immich-video-faces`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `TheBranchDriftCatalyst/immich-video-faces` exists on GitHub with `main` branch containing code + `k8s/` manifests
- [ ] `test.mp4` NOT in the first commit (either gitignored or committed via LFS)
- [ ] `workspace/talos-homelab` main pushed with new ArgoCD App manifest
- [ ] `workspace/talos-private` main pushed with immich-video-faces removed from `base/kustomization.yaml` + 88 files deleted
- [ ] `kubectl -n argocd get app immich-video-faces -o jsonpath='{.status.sync.status}'` -> `Synced`
- [ ] `kubectl -n argocd get app immich-video-faces -o jsonpath='{.status.health.status}'` -> `Healthy`
- [ ] Pods running in `media-private` under new App instance label; no duplicate/orphaned resources from `arr-stack-private`
- [ ] Immich UI still reachable (regression check — same namespace shouldn't have been disturbed)
- [ ] Face-detection cronjob visible: `kubectl -n media-private get cronjob | grep -i immich-video-faces`

## Gotchas

- **63MB `test.mp4`** currently staged in new repo. Decide LFS vs. gitignore BEFORE step 1's commit.
- **Namespace stays `media-private`** — do NOT change `destination.namespace`. Immich's Postgres service (`immich-postgres`) is only resolvable in-namespace.
- **`CreateNamespace=false`** is intentional (namespace already exists, owned by arr-stack-private). Do not flip to `true`.
- **arr-stack-private App owns the namespace resource itself** — leave that alone.
- **Local dev (Tilt)** still uses `k3d-bfm-local-dev` cluster spun up by `../talos-private/dev.sh up`. Unchanged.
- **Beads DB** in new repo is fresh. If you want issues on this project, `bd init` inside `workspace/immich-video-faces` and set a prefix (e.g. `IVF`).
- **Prior uncommitted work** (Dockerfile, Tiltfile, frontend/**) moved with the files — first commit includes them. Expected.

## Rollback

If ArgoCD sync fails hard:
1. `argocd app delete immich-video-faces --cascade=false` (delete App, leave resources)
2. Revert talos-private's spinoff commit + re-add `- immich-video-faces/` to `base/kustomization.yaml`
3. `argocd app sync arr-stack-private` (reclaims the ivf resources)
4. Revert talos-homelab's ArgoCD App commit

## Related

- Pattern doc: `workspace/talos-homelab/CLAUDE.md` -> "Adding a New Application (ArgoCD)"
- Reference App: `infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/catalyst-data.yaml` (same shape, different repo)
- Sibling App: `infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/arr-stack-private.yaml` (the App this used to live under)
- Full handoff also mirrored in `workspace/HANDOFF-immich-video-faces-spinoff.md`
notes:
## ⚠️ DEPENDENCY DISCOVERED 2026-08-24 — immich has changed vector extensions

immich v3.1.0 has DROPPED pgvecto.rs support. Confirmed live today, not inferred:

    Error: No vector extension found. Available extensions: vchord, vector

Our DB sidecar is tensorchord/pgvecto-rs:pg16-v0.2.1, which provides the 'vectors' extension.
immich now wants vchord (VectorChord) or vector (pgvector).

immich is currently PINNED to the last working digest and is healthy (4/4):
    ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:release@sha256:c15bff75...
It failed in database.service.js init BEFORE any migration ran, so the schema is untouched and
the pin is a clean rollback, not a patch over damage.

## WHY THIS TICKET SPECIFICALLY

User's own words (2026-08-24): 'i am the pg vector dude, immich-video-faces is going to need to
be updated accordingly to the new vector solution immich has chosen it seems.'

So before shipping immich-video-faces, establish whether it depends on the pgvecto.rs extension
NAME or its operators — 'vectors', vector_dims, <->, <=>, or a pgvecto-specific operator class.
If it does, shipping it now means shipping against an extension that is about to be replaced.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THIS TICKET: does b9i ship BEFORE or AFTER the vector migration? Being tracked
by an agent investigation now; findings will land here.

⚠️ ALSO NOTE: immich's postgres here is a PLAIN DEPLOYMENT SIDECAR, not CNPG. Every other
postgres in this cluster is CNPG with instances:3 on local-path. A vector migration is an
opportunity to move it onto CNPG — bigger and better, but a much larger change. Whether those
should be coupled or sequenced is part of the open question.
## ⚠️ VERIFIED 2026-08-24 — THIS IS UNBACKED WORK, and that raises the stakes

immich-video-faces exists ONLY as uncommitted files on this Mac. Verified directly:

    /Users/panda/catalyst-devspace/workspace/immich-video-faces
    branch main, ZERO COMMITS ('your current branch main does not have any commits yet')
    remote: NONE
    105 uncommitted entries

    real source: 27 python files (22 in src/), 26 frontend ts/tsx, 8 k8s manifests
    plus frontend/, models/, tests/, tilt/, test-data/, AGENTS.md

GitHub repo TheBranchDriftCatalyst/immich-video-faces DOES NOT EXIST — 'Could not resolve to a
Repository'. talos-homelab infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/kustomization.yaml:11 records
why: 'immich-video-faces.yaml REMOVED 2026-08-14 — source repo deleted from GitHub, app was
orphaned with zero tracked resources'.

SO THE TICKET'S PREMISE IS INTACT — it is about CREATING the repo — but the risk profile is
worse than the title suggests. ONE DISK FAILURE OR STRAY rm AND THE ENTIRE PROJECT IS GONE.
There is no remote, no commit, no stash, nothing. This is the least-protected work in the
whole estate and it is tracked as a P0 for a different reason (shipping) than the one that
actually makes it urgent (it is unbacked).

Good news: a .gitignore (27 lines) already exists, so an initial commit will not sweep in
venv/node_modules. The 105 entries are real source.

## RELATIONSHIP TO THE VECTOR MIGRATION — resolved, ship whenever

Earlier concern was that shipping before the VectorChord migration risked wasted work. THAT IS
NOW MOOT: the migration is DONE (see TALOS-cibi). immich runs on vchord + vector, embedding
columns are public.vector.

IVF's SQL is portable and works unchanged — VectorChord reuses pgvector's type names and <=>
semantics. What needs changing is tracked in TALOS-7xxm:
  1. web/queries.py:356 extension check lists ('vector','vectors') and needs 'vchord'
  2. vchordrq probes — invisible today at lists=1, but silently loses face-match recall once
     face_search passes 128,000 rows (currently 23,145)
  3. docker-compose.dev.yml:6 and tilt/dev-immich-stack.yaml:28 still pin
     tensorchord/pgvecto-rs:pg16-v0.2.0 AND run immich-server:release floating — that exact
     combination is what broke prod today

## ALSO NOTE

There is NO immich-video-faces CronJob deployed anywhere in the cluster — no CronJob, Job,
Deployment, StatefulSet or Pod matching video|face in ANY namespace. So the 23,134 IVF-produced
asset_face rows (of 23,146 total) are from an earlier era; nothing has been writing them
recently. Those rows survived the migration bit-for-bit.
## USER DECISION 2026-08-24: make it a proper repo — but HOLD OFF for now

User's words: 'we need to make immich face thing a proper repo, lets hold off on it'.

So the direction is settled — it becomes a real repo with a real remote — but the timing is
deliberately deferred. DO NOT git init/commit/push or create the GitHub repo without the user
saying go. Recording this so nobody 'helpfully' commits it in the meantime.

⚠️ THE RISK REMAINS UNMITIGATED WHILE WE WAIT: zero commits, no remote, 105 uncommitted entries
on one Mac, GitHub repo does not exist. If the machine dies, the project dies with it — along
with whatever produced 23,134 of the 23,146 asset_face rows now living in immich.

If a cheap interim hedge is ever wanted, a purely LOCAL 'git add -A && git commit' needs no
remote, publishes nothing, is trivially amendable when the real repo is set up, and retires
nearly all of the loss risk. Offered, not done.

title: Root cause meltdowns: Cilium identity bloat (19k stale CRDs) saturates etcd
description:
## Why this issue exists

After 11+ meltdowns over a week, the actual root cause is identified.

## Root cause

Cilium has 19,439 CiliumIdentity CRDs for only 180 live pods. Per-cilium-agent restart, the agent does a LIST that returns 30MB / 9438+ identity objects (etcd log: `apply request took too long, took:107ms, response: range_response_count:9438 size:29733630`). This saturates etcd → apiserver → KubePrism returns EOF mid-response → cilium-agent fatal at startup (`failed to start: ... EOF`) → kubelet restarts cilium-agent → loop.

cilium-operator ALSO crashlooping (189 restarts/20h) so identity GC never completes a 15-min interval.

## Identity pollution composition

| Source | Count |
|---|---|
| Dagster jobs (`dagster/run-id`, `dagster/op`) | ~15k (Dagster was migrated to catalyst-data repo, leaving residue) |
| Velero pod-volume-backup | 2,594 |
| Batch jobs (`job-name`, `batch.kubernetes.io/job-name`) | 18,710 |
| Live pods | 180 |

## Fix (two parts)

1. **Flux values change** — add `labels:` filter to `infrastructure/base/cilium/values.yaml` excluding high-churn labels (`job-name`, `batch.kubernetes.io/*`, `controller-uid`, `pod-template-hash`, `dagster/*`). Stops NEW pollution.
2. **One-shot cleanup script** — delete CiliumIdentity CRDs not referenced by any live CiliumEndpoint. Drops etcd query payload from 30MB → ~50KB. Stops the cascade immediately.

## How to verify

- cilium-agent restart count stops climbing
- cilium-operator restart count stops climbing
- `kubectl get ciliumidentities | wc -l` drops to ~250 (live + system identities)
- etcd `apply request took too long` warnings cease for `/registry/cilium.io/ciliumidentities`
notes:
## Completion (2026-05-30)

**Cleanup**: 19,438 → 150 CiliumIdentities (149 in-use + 1 system-ish).
**Cluster stability**: cilium-agents stable at 144-149 restarts for 90+ min (was every 8 min before). cilium-operator stable at 189 restarts (was crashlooping).
**Etcd**: queries on /registry/cilium.io/ciliumidentities/* now 3KB instead of 30MB.

## Commits

- `bdb89d7` — root-cause fix (label filter, cleanup script, pod-cleanup integration, alerts, dashboard)
- `dc64bd7` — activated Flux management for Cilium (TALOS-ocj)

## Remaining

Awaiting Flux reconcile to apply label filter to live cilium-config. Monitor active.

title: EPIC: HA control plane — promote talos01 + talos06 to CPs (stacked etcd 3-member)
description:
## Why

The 2026-05-27, 2026-05-29 (and the 2026-05-21, 2026-05-22) cluster meltdowns ALL had the same root cause class: **single control plane node + single etcd member + workloads colocated on the CP + Cilium agent on CP is its own apiserver's CNI**. This is "circular dependency with no slack" — a single jitter on talos00 kills the entire cluster.

The architect, cilium expert, and SRE council members all converged on: HA control plane is the **structural** fix. Every other change (memory bumps, probe tuning, webhook policy) is a bandage.

## Target topology

- **3 CPs**: talos00 (192.168.1.54), talos01 (192.168.1.177), talos06 (192.168.1.19)
- **2 workers**: talos02-gpu (192.168.1.144 — GPU stays as pure worker), talos03 (192.168.1.30 — pure worker)
- **Stacked etcd** (3-member raft quorum, can survive 1 node loss)
- After promotion: consider `allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes: false` if workload pressure on CPs is too high (decide based on metrics)

## Sub-tasks (will file as separate issues)

1. Generate new control-plane configs for talos01 and talos06 (`talosctl gen config`)
2. Add a Talos VIP for apiserver HA (e.g. 192.168.1.50 floating among the 3 CPs) — OR ensure KubePrism works (TALOS-kp-debug)
3. `talosctl apply-config` to talos01 and talos06 with CP config (this is a destructive node transition — re-installs the node)
   - **Pre-step: drain & cordon talos01 and talos06**
   - **Pre-step: ensure no irreplaceable PVCs on these nodes**
4. Watch etcd member join — `talosctl etcd members` should show 3 members
5. Re-run KubePrism verification on the 3 CPs
6. Switch Cilium `k8sServiceHost` to VIP or localhost:7445
7. Update CLAUDE.md and docs to reflect new topology
8. File post-cutover validation runbook

## Risks

- **Destructive**: applying CP config to existing worker nodes wipes them (Talos reinstall). Schedule downtime.
- **etcd quorum during transition**: If we promote sequentially, there are moments with 2 members (no quorum loss tolerance). 
- **PVC affinity**: Some workloads have node-affinity to talos01/06 (e.g. NFS provisioner, local-path PVs). Need to migrate.

## Sequencing

- Do AFTER TALOS-kp-debug (we need apiserver-HA reachable from Cilium pods)
- Do BEFORE TALOS-fed-enable (federation + HA is a cleaner story)
- Do AFTER TALOS-cilium-gitops (Cilium needs to be GitOps so reconciles don't race the topology change)

## Acceptance

- `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{...}'` shows 3 control-plane nodes
- `talosctl etcd members` shows 3 healthy members
- Force-kill one CP → cluster stays operational (validated test)
- Cilium agents stay healthy through the transition
- Documentation updated (CLAUDE.md, README, runbooks)
acceptance_criteria:
- 3 healthy CPs, 3-member etcd raft quorum
- Survives 1 CP loss in chaos test
- Cilium points at HA endpoint (VIP or KubePrism)
- Documentation updated
- Post-cutover incident-free for >1 week
notes:
2026-05-30 04:58 UTC PRIORITY ESCALATED P1 → P0.

After 10 meltdowns in ~14 hours, the structural single-CP fragility is no longer
"theoretical risk we should address eventually" — it's the active recurring root
cause. Throttle fix (TALOS-r10) helped (2h uptime vs 1hr previously) but didn't
eliminate. Kernel-capture data confirms it's NOT kernel panics — userspace
disruption on talos00 cascades into cluster-wide outage in a way that 3 CPs would
prevent.

Captured evidence (kernel-capture + alloy-node + Loki dashboard infrastructure
built today during incident response — see TALOS-fa7):
  - Talos kernel healthy through every meltdown (no panic patterns in /var/log/
    kernel-capture/talos00.log across multiple boots)
  - cilium pods restart in BURSTS during recovery from each force-reboot, but
    stable between meltdowns
  - apiserver becomes externally unreachable while talos00 services (etcd, apid,
    kubelet) stay healthy → kube-apiserver static pod isn't serving outside
    requests for some reason

The pre-flight from the runbook (docs/05-runbooks/ha-control-plane-migration.md)
still applies. Heavy state migration needed:
  - MinIO data on talos01 (where Velero backups live!) — MUST migrate before promotion
  - 5+ Postgres databases + Neo4j on talos06 — migrate via pg_dump + restore OR move
    to NFS storage class
  - 1 KubeVirt VM (gaming/Windows gameserver) on talos06 — live migrate or accept
    downtime
  - CoreDNS replica spread (currently 2 replicas, one on each affected node) —
    scale to 3 with anti-affinity before promotion

Next steps when scheduling the HA migration window:
  1. Block out 4-6 hour maintenance window
  2. Backup MinIO contents externally first (don't trust our backups while migrating
     the node holding backups!)
  3. Run pg_dump on all Postgres workloads on talos01/06 to external storage
  4. Follow the runbook step-by-step

This is the actual fix. Filing as P0.

title: Local cscli API ops broken post-TLS: LAPI pod creds still http:// (+ read-only bouncer key)
description: After the CrowdSec LAPI TLS migration (TALOS-3pdz), the LAPI pod's /etc/crowdsec/local_api_credentials.yaml still has url: http://0.0.0.0:8080 while the LAPI serves HTTPS -> every API-based cscli command in the LAPI pod fails with 'Client sent an HTTP request to an HTTPS server' (decisions list/add/import/delete, alerts list/delete, allowlists). Also the local login is a READ-ONLY bouncer key (crowdsec-web-ui), so even fixed to https it can't write decisions. Only DB-direct cscli commands (machines) work -> machine-prune survives by luck. FIX: point the local client url to https + insecure_skip_verify (or ca_cert) via chart values/entrypoint, and if we want local write-ops, give it a machine (not bouncer) credential. Surfaced while building blocklist-import (needs a machine cred + https to import decisions).
notes: FIXED + verified 2026-09-11. Root cause was NOT a missing config — the chart forces LOCAL_API_URL=https://localhost:8080 + INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY=false and the LAPI cert has a localhost SAN. The break was a STALE local_api_credentials.yaml (emptyDir persisting a pre-TLS http:// url; entrypoint skips regen when the file exists). kubectl rollout restart deploy/crowdsec-lapi regenerated it https. Verified: cscli decisions list/import/delete, alerts list, allowlists inspect all work in the LAPI pod. My initial env-override attempt was ineffective (chart env wins) and was reverted; left a note in helmrelease.yaml for recurrence.

title: Alert severity is uniformly warning: a total prod outage is indistinguishable from memory pressure
description:
Every alert that fired during the 100-minute boomtime outage was severity=warning or info. Nothing anywhere is critical. count by (alertname,severity) (max_over_time(ALERTS{alertstate="firing"}[12h])) returned: ServiceDown warning x12, KubePodNotReady warning x12, ExternalSecretNotReady warning x2, CrowdSecDecisionInventoryUnavailable warning, DagsterHighMemoryUsage warning x4, NodeHighCPUUsage warning, plus info-level noise.

So the monitoring DETECTED everything and COMMUNICATED nothing. A cluster-wide 403 and a hard-down app produced exactly the same signal as Dagster using a lot of RAM. The boomtime encryption-key ESO alert had been firing for weeks in that same undifferentiated stream.

The problem is not missing alerts -- it is that ~30 chronically-firing warnings make the class worthless, so a NOVEL alert carries no information.

WORK:
1. Tier severity by blast radius. "users cannot reach the app", "the only copy of a secret is unbacked", "an ingress path is 403ing fleet-wide" are critical; resource-pressure warnings are not.
2. Drive the chronic firers to zero -- fix or delete them (12 ServiceDown and 12 KubePodNotReady are almost certainly known-dead things). An alert that is always on is not an alert.
3. Route critical somewhere that actually interrupts; alertmanager-discord already exists as the bridge.
4. Only then is "a new warning appeared" meaningful.
notes:
DONE (edf9c14c): KubePodNotReady no longer matches phase=Failed (tombstones) 12->4; ServiceDown excludes Succeeded pods 4->3; KubePodCrashLoopBackOff warning->critical. Both exprs verified against live Mimir, all three confirmed live after flux reconcile.
BLOCKED ON USER DECISION (2 items):
 1. discord-critical and discord-default post to the SAME webhook URL, so a critical alert is visually identical to a warning in Discord. Needs a second Discord channel+webhook, then a second Secret for the bridge.
 2. Dead-mans switch is NOT ARMED: the alertmanager-heartbeat Secret does not exist, so $HEARTBEAT_URL is still the inert .invalid placeholder. PipelineHeartbeat has been firing every 60s into nothing. If the whole observability stack dies, nothing external notices. Needs a healthchecks.io / uptime-kuma ping URL.
REMAINING NOISE (real, not tombstones): 4x bt-radar/bt-agent stuck Pending; 3x pihole exporter down; 4x DagsterHighMemoryUsage firing on cnpg postgres + barman sidecars in catalyst-data (selector looks too broad / mislabeled).

title: ESO: a never-synced ExternalSecret shadowing a hand-made Secret is a silent single-copy secret
description:
boomtime/boomtime-encryption-key had refreshTime: NEVER and syncedResourceVersion: NONE since 2026-07-23 -- it never synced ONCE in ~7 weeks. The commit that added it also hand-created the Secret (no ownerReferences, no ESO annotations) to unblock the deploy, and the 1Password field was never created. Net effect: the cluster held the ONLY copy of the AES-256 key protecting every stored Wakatime API key and Amazon device credential. Any `kubectl delete secret`, namespace rebuild, or cluster restore would have destroyed it permanently, and nothing would have noticed until decryption started failing.

Now fixed for this instance (field added to 1Password, ESO synced, Secret adopted).

THE CLASS, not the instance:

1. DETECT THE SHADOW. `refreshTime: NEVER` + a Secret of the target name existing WITHOUT an ownerReference is a precise, cheap signature for "GitOps believes this is managed; it is not, and the only copy is unbacked". Distinct from an ES that synced before and is merely stale -- that one still has a vault copy and is far less urgent. Alert on the shadow case specifically, and at a severity that matches data loss (see TALOS alert-tiering bead).

2. AUDIT: cluster-wide sweep found 153 healthy, 1 never-synced (crossplane-system/aws-credentials -- no shadow Secret, so it is dead config rather than a risk) and 0 erroring. Decide whether aws-credentials should exist at all; delete it if not, because a permanently-firing alert is what hid this one.

3. The generic ExternalSecretNotReady alert already existed and WAS FIRING for boomtime-encryption-key -- confirmed via max_over_time(ALERTS[30d]). Detection was never the gap. See the alert-tiering bead: it fired at severity=warning alongside two other chronic ESO firers and ~24 other chronic warnings.
notes:
DONE (0feb9da1): ExternalSecretNeverSynced added at CRITICAL, for=1h. Separates "never worked" (unbacked single copy = data loss) from "stopped working" (vault copy exists, only next rotation at risk) via `unless` on a 7d lookback of Ready=True. Verified live: returns exactly one series, and correctly no longer returns boomtime-encryption-key now that it syncs.
boomtime-encryption-key RESOLVED: user added the 1Password field; ESO synced for the first time ever; Secret adopted (ownerRefs now present); value confirmed IDENTICAL to the running pods key by sha256 comparison, so a restart is safe.
NEEDS A DECISION: crossplane-system/aws-credentials is the one firing series and it is a REAL second instance of this class, not noise -- providers installed and healthy, but group.cloudwatchlogs hello-whoami has been SYNCED=False for 18d with "connect failed: cannot get terraform setup" because 1Password has no `aws-crossplane` item (wants access_key_id + secret_access_key). No Secret exists, so nothing to lose. Either populate the item or tear the stack down. Deliberately NOT muted.

title: CrowdSec bouncer: implicit scheme inheritance + no synthetic check on the pod->ingress path
description:
The Traefik bouncer plugin defaults crowdsecAppsecScheme to crowdsecLapiScheme when unset (bouncer.go: `if config.CrowdsecAppsecScheme == "" { config.CrowdsecAppsecScheme = config.CrowdsecLapiScheme }`). Moving the LAPI to TLS (TALOS-3pdz) therefore dragged AppSec to https silently; AppSec :7422 serves plain HTTP, so every appsecQuery failed at the transport and crowdsecAppsecUnreachableBlock: true 403d EVERY request through Traefik, cluster-wide. Fixed in fb6ae0b0 by pinning crowdsecAppsecScheme: http.

TWO FOLLOW-UPS, neither of which the one-line fix covers:

1. AUDIT for the same class. Any other plugin/chart value that silently inherits a sibling when empty is one migration away from the same outage. Grep the vendored plugin config surface for `== ""` defaulting, and pin every scheme/host/port the bouncer takes rather than relying on defaults.

2. SYNTHETIC CHECK on the path that actually broke. Nothing tested pod -> Traefik -> service. External probes hit 192.168.1.54 and stayed green the entire outage because they bypass the bouncer; the in-cluster hop is the one that 403d. Want a CronJob or blackbox target that curls a known host FROM a pod and alerts on non-2xx, since that is the exact signal that was missing for 100 minutes.

Evidence: traefik access log showed DownstreamStatus 403 with OriginStatus 0 (never forwarded) and all latency in Overhead (middleware). cscli decisions list showed 13 decisions, all external scanners, none matching internal space -- it was never a ban.
notes:
PARTLY DONE (db172b3c): ingress-path probes + IngressPathDown alert.
Root cause of the blind spot: all 13 blackbox targets were DIRECT service URLs, so none crossed Traefiks websecure entrypoint or middleware chain (traefik-internal:9000/ping is Traefiks own health endpoint, which middlewares never touch). All stayed green for 100 minutes. External checks cannot cover it either -- auth.knowledgedump.space resolves to 192.168.1.54 from LAN but Traefik ClusterIP from a pod, and the external path was fine the whole time.
Added: probes for boomtime.knowledgedump.space and the exact OIDC discovery URL that 403d, both verified probe_success=1 live. Also found probe_success had NO alert at all (dashboard only) -- IngressPathDown now covers ingress-* at critical.
STILL TO DO: the audit half. Grep the vendored bouncer plugin config surface for other `== ""` sibling-inheritance defaults and pin every scheme/host/port explicitly rather than relying on defaults. crowdsecAppsecScheme was one; there may be more.
close_reason: Ingress-path probes + IngressPathDown shipped (db172b3c); the audit half was split out

title: [AUTO] Composition-adoption observability: label convention + KSM-CRS exporter + Grafana Compositions folder
description: Foundation for DRYing up. (1) Labeling convention catalyst.io/composition=<type> patched onto EVERY composed resource (inner manifest, not just the Object wrapper) so managed resources are queryable; also leverage crossplane.io/composite. (2) Exporter: kube-state-metrics CustomResourceStateMetrics (declarative, prefer over a custom Job per 'operator CRDs over glue') emitting composite counts + per managed-kind managed-vs-unmanaged so PromQL can find look-alikes (a CNPG Cluster / IngressRoute / NetworkPolicy WITHOUT the composition label = drying-up candidate). (3) Grafana: a 'Compositions' FOLDER, one GrafanaDashboard CR per composition (CatalystCNPGAppDB, NetworkIngress), scales as adoption grows — accordion rows per composition. JSON+CRD only, no sync scripts. (4) LOC-DRIED metric: track lines of YAML removed by each migration (e.g. an annotation catalyst.io/replaced-loc, or a computed panel) so the dashboard reports total lines dried up. This is the 2nd of 2 adoption dashboards.
notes: DONE + verified live in Mimir: label convention (12/12 composed CNPG clusters labeled), KSM CRS exporter (catalyst_composite_info=12, catalyst_managed_resource_info split 12 managed / 8 drying-up candidates), Grafana 'Compositions' folder + composition-owned dashboard (DashboardSynchronized=True). commonLabels fix for the composite composition label (v2 nests compositionRef under spec.crossplane). Remaining: (1) backfill catalyst.io/replaced-loc annotations as the 8 candidates migrate (LOC panel reads 0 until then); (2) add IngressRoute/NetworkPolicy GVKs to the CRS + a per-composition dashboard when CatalystWebSecureIngress lands.

title: [AUTO] CatalystWebSecureIngress XRD+Composition (declarative app-ingress)
description: Crossplane composite modeled on CatalystCNPGAppDB. One XR per app declares INTENT (host, backend svc/port, auth group, clients, public?) and the composition renders: IngressRoute (websecure + web-redirect pair), NetworkPolicy (ingress from Traefik + declared clients), forward-auth middleware ref, and optionally the Authentik app/provider blueprint. Kyverno stays as the GUARDRAIL layer (deny combined entrypoints, deny unclaimed public hosts, deny routes without a policy) — it validates; Crossplane provisions. Design in infrastructure/base/catalyst-websecure-ingress/.
notes:
MVP/crownstone = talos-private: pilot CatalystWebSecureIngress on the well-governed forward-auth set (headlamp, kubeview, guacamole, windows-vnc) first — smallest, most consistent surface, already the 'good' pattern. Prove the composition there, then roll to public/knowledgedump apps and the CNPG-DB netpol sweep (l2sm.6).
Scope += OPTIONAL external-dns: the composition also emits the DNS record for public/lan hosts (external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/hostname annotation on the IngressRoute, or a DNSEndpoint CR) — gated by exposure: public|lan-only. Full sandwich per app: IngressRoute pair + NetworkPolicy + middleware chain + Authentik app/provider blueprint + optional external-dns record.
MVP DONE + verified live end-to-end: CatalystWebSecureIngress XRD+Composition deployed (net.catalyst.io/v1alpha1), composes websecure+web IngressRoute pair + NetworkPolicy via provider-kubernetes (scoped RBAC added). kubeview converted: 39 lines -> 1 claim, re-homed to kubeview.talos00 (302->Authentik SSO confirmed, old priv host 404), NetworkPolicy added (had none). Kyverno tls-default fires on composed routes. Wired into adoption observability: catalyst_composite_info=1, catalyst_managed_resource_info kind=IngressRoute (2 managed / 225 look-alike candidates), replaced_loc=39 — all live in Mimir + composition-owned dashboard in the Compositions folder. Remaining scope: SSO-blueprint generation (blocked by Authentik fixed configMaps mount, TALOS-lxz5.5.6); clients + externalDNS fields (v2).

title: Repo directory-structure refactor — group infrastructure/, reclassify infra↔apps, consolidate tests
description:
Tracks `docs/02-architecture/repo-restructure-plan.md` (846 lines, fully validated — see its §14
validation log, V1–V26).

## Problem

`infrastructure/base/` is 46 flat directories. Beyond that, six components are misclassified,
four are dead/unwired, and 10 Jest suites each carried a redundant package.json + lockfile +
node_modules.

## Approach

Insert ONE grouping layer of 9 dependency-ordered groups (00-bootstrap → 80-platform), drop the
vestigial `base/` level, move genuine applications out of `infrastructure/`, and consolidate the
test tree to a single dependency root.

## HARD CONSTRAINT

**No namespace changes.** Every move is a directory move. Plan §8 proves namespace invariance:
nothing derives a namespace from a path, and `kustomize build` output is path-independent, so a
matching SHA per component IS the proof.

## Validation harness

`kustomize build` fingerprint over all 62 Flux paths, before vs after. Baseline: **59 OK**,
plus 3 pre-existing failures (`applications/catalyst-llm` is dangling at HEAD; `poisonarr/base`
and `crossplane-demo/flex` are working-tree deletions). Acceptance: the 59 SHAs must be
IDENTICAL after the move, compared as a SET (paths change by design).

## ⚠️ The landmine

Most Flux Kustomizations set `prune: true`. The `git mv` and the `path:` rewrite MUST land in
the SAME commit. A commit where the ks still points at the old path makes Flux see an empty
source and **prune live resources**.

Also: `flux reconcile kustomization` applies the ALREADY-fetched revision — use `--with-source`
or you validate stale state.

## Key findings

- F1  `infrastructure/base/talos-dr/` has ZERO manifests — only tests
- F2  `shared/gluetun-sidecar` referenced by no kustomization — dead
- F3  `nebula` exists twice, neither Flux-wired
- F4  `nvidia-cdi` referenced ONLY in a YAML comment — never deploys
- F5  `hybrid-llm` has no Flux ks but 14 doc references
- F10 2 Flux Kustomizations point at non-existent paths
- F13 `jest.config.js` index/worktree conflict over the honeypot project (blocks Phase 1 commit)
- F14 SPIRE embedded in cilium values, history of expired-token CrashLoops — separate decision

## Reclassification (§15/§16)

MOVE infra → apps: `forgejo`, `infra-control`, `whoami`, `gpu-inference`.
SPLIT `vpn-gateway`: gateway stays, `secure-chrome`/`secure-webtop`/`securexng` move.

STAYS in infra despite app smell: `registry` (Zot serves `registry.talos00` — **4 workloads
pull images through it**), `authentik`, `minio`, `monitoring`, `databases`, `mail`.

RETRACTED: `honeypot` + `iocaine` are NOT apps. CrowdSec tails Cowrie's stdout
(`honeypot/deployment.yaml:123`) and Bot Wrangler feeds iocaine. They are IPS sensors →
`30-security/edge/` with crowdsec. This implements the deferred **TALOS-c4q**.

## Lesson

Flux `dependsOn` encodes **apply ordering, not runtime data flow**. Do not use it alone to
classify infra vs app — it is blind to log-shipping and image-pull relationships.

## Open questions (plan §13 + §15.10 + §16.6)

Q1 numeric prefixes? · Q2 drop `base/`? · Q3 hybrid-llm fate · Q4 nebula canonical copy ·
Q5 nvidia-cdi wire-or-delete · Q6 gpu-inference tier · Q7 tests layout (ANSWERED: Option A) ·
Q8 do applications/ at all · Q10 two-tier vs three-tier · Q11 gpu-inference · Q12 (RESOLVED
by §16) · Q13 vpn-gateway split · Q14 mail · Q15 nest `edge/`?
acceptance_criteria: All 59 currently-OK kustomize build SHAs identical after the move (compared as a set); no namespace changed; no Flux Kustomization left pointing at a missing path; docs updated.
notes: §17 added after epic creation: Taskfile consolidation. 7 Taskfiles at repo root -> keep Taskfile.yaml, git mv the 6 domain files into taskfiles/. Only functional edit is the root includes: block (6 lines); task namespaces are preserved because the include KEY defines the namespace, not the filename. 46 refs repo-wide, mostly docs; docs/07-reference/taskfile-organization.md must be rewritten not sed'd. Validation: 'task --list-all' byte-identical before/after. Tracked as F15 + phase 4b. Zero cluster risk, independent of the infra grouping.

title: Port-forward WAN:22 to the Cowrie honeypot — OPERATOR ACTION, do not automate
description:
The final switch that makes the honeypot internet-facing. USER IS DOING THIS THEMSELVES — deliberately kept out of automation.

## THE FORWARD

    router WAN :22  ->  192.168.1.19 : 2222     (talos06, Cowrie SSH)

⚠️ DECIDE SEPARATELY whether to forward telnet. Cowrie also listens on 2223 for telnet, but
exposing a second protocol doubles the attack surface for a sensor that mostly sees SSH scanning.
Recommendation is SSH only to start; add telnet later if the SSH data proves interesting.

## ⚠️ DO NOT DO THIS UNTIL THE HARDENING LANDS

Verify first — the suite is the acceptance criteria:

    npm test -- --selectProjects honeypot-security

As of filing: 10 pass / 4 fail. ALL 14 MUST PASS BEFORE FORWARDING. The open ones are:
    automountServiceAccountToken === false
    zero serviceaccount mounts in running containers
    seccompProfile RuntimeDefault
    ingress admits world on :2222

That last one is the one that makes this ticket pointless if skipped: the CiliumNetworkPolicy
currently admits only 192.168.1.0/24 and 10.244.0.0/16. Forward the port without fixing it and
Cilium SILENTLY DROPS every attacker packet — the dashboard reads zero, which is
indistinguishable from 'no attacks'. That false-comfort reading is what started this whole
investigation.

## WHAT TO EXPECT ONCE LIVE

A public SSH honeypot is scanned within MINUTES. If nothing appears within the hour, something
is wrong — check in this order: the forward itself, then the Cilium ingress policy, then
cowrie.json inside the pod, then Loki.

Verify from OUTSIDE the network, not from the LAN. A LAN-side test hits hairpin NAT and proves
nothing: 108.64.138.156:22 already accepts a TCP connect from inside while port 22 is closed on
all five nodes, so that accept is the router/ISP edge rather than the cluster.

## AFTER IT IS LIVE

  - confirm real external source IPs appear in Loki ({namespace="honeypot", container="logship"})
  - the Cowrie Ops dashboard should stop reading zero
  - log volume will rise sharply — Loki is the durable record; the pod's emptyDir holds only
    ~11h and is lost on reschedule

## BLAST RADIUS, for the record

Egress is default-deny with kube-dns:53 the ONLY exception, and there are zero apiserver-reaching
egress rules. That is what stops a compromised honeypot doing lateral movement, outbound
scanning, C2 or exfil. Container is non-root, capabilities drop ALL, no hostNetwork/hostPID/hostIPC.
⚠️ NEVER add an egress rule to this namespace without thinking hard about what you are handing
to a machine you are inviting attackers into.

DNS egress remains open and is a KNOWN ACCEPTED RISK — see the DNS-tunnelling pentest ticket.

title: Blackbox-probe the app fleet: replica-count alerts cannot see an app broken behind a passing readiness probe
description:
Fallout from TALOS-l407.

TALOS-l407 added the kubernetes-apps readiness alert group (deployment/sts/ds/pod). Verified working: it would have caught kasa-exporter (62.7h at zero available replicas) and hot-ones (10.2h), and it fires live on whisparr's restart loop.

It does NOT close the homeassistant case, and the premise that it would was wrong.

MEASURED: kube_deployment_status_replicas_available for homeassistant reads 1 across ALL 121 samples of the last 30 days. It has a working HTTP readiness probe (GET / on the http port). The Deployment was Available the entire time it was reportedly unusable. No replica-count rule can detect that by construction -- the probe returns 200 while the app behind it is broken.

That failure class needs blackbox/synthetic probing of the actual user-facing endpoint. blackbox-exporter is deployed (infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/blackbox-exporter/) but currently targets only TWO endpoints:
  - http://grafana-service.monitoring.svc:3000/api/health
  - http://mimir-alertmanager.monitoring.svc:8080/
