title: [bug] No alert rule covers 'deployment has 0 ready replicas' — this is why HA was down 15 days unnoticed
description:
THE SYSTEMIC GAP BEHIND TODAY'S TWO OUTAGES. Alerting works; it just does not watch the thing that broke.

## MEASURED

    total PrometheusRule alert rules      90
    rules covering deployment readiness    1   <- GPUGatewayStuckNotReady, scoped to ONE workload
    kubernetes-apps rule groups            0   <- the standard kube-prometheus-stack group is ABSENT
    PrometheusRule objects                15

kube-state-metrics is NOT the problem — it runs the full standard set of 26 resource types
including deployments, pods, statefulsets and daemonsets. The metrics exist. NOTHING ALERTS ON
THEM.

Alertmanager is NOT the problem either. Discord routing is configured and live:
    receivers discord-default / discord-critical -> alertmanager-discord bridge (1/1 Running)
    alertmanager-config-pusher CronJob ran 4m ago, every 15 min, 38d old
So TALOS-2pz ('no alerts route anywhere right now') is STALE — they route fine. There is simply
nothing to route.

## WHAT THIS COST, CONCRETELY

    homeassistant   ready=0 for 15 DAYS. Nobody knew. Found by hand on 2026-08-24.
    immich          broken, self-healed by luck. Found by hand.
    whisparr        0/1 CrashLoopBackOff, still unnoticed until today (TALOS-o00l)

All three are 'deployment has zero available replicas'. A single generic rule catches all three
and every future instance.

## THE FIX

Add the standard kubernetes-apps group, or minimally:
    KubeDeploymentReplicasMismatch      available != spec.replicas for >15m
    KubeStatefulSetReplicasMismatch
    KubeDaemonSetNotScheduled / MisScheduled
    KubePodCrashLooping
Route to the EXISTING discord-default receiver — no new plumbing needed.

⚠️ VERIFY THE METRIC ACTUALLY FLOWS TO MIMIR before trusting the rule. I confirmed KSM is
configured for deployments but could not complete a Mimir query to prove the series is present
end to end. A rule over an absent series is silently never-firing — which is the exact failure
mode this ticket is about, so do not skip that check.

## WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE OBSERVABILITY WORK

Today's whole session was things reporting success while the effect was absent. This is the
monitoring instance of that: a full alerting stack, 90 rules, a live Discord bridge, and a
15-day outage that produced no signal. Everything looked healthy because nothing was asked the
right question.
notes:
## ⚠️ CORRECTION — 'homeassistant was down 15 days' WAS WRONG, and it changes what this buys

I asserted repeatedly that homeassistant sat at ready=0 for 15 days. MEASURED AGAINST MIMIR, IT
DID NOT:

    min_over_time(kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{...homeassistant}[30d])   = 0
    time spent at zero over 30d                                                       = 0.92 HOURS

That ~55 minutes corresponds to today's own restart when the imagePullPolicy fix rolled. The
Deployment was AVAILABLE essentially the whole time.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED: homeassistant was broken BEHIND A WORKING READINESS PROBE. The app
answered HTTP 200 while its storage version was incompatible — so the pod was Ready, the
Deployment was Available, and every replica-count metric read healthy. It was genuinely broken
and genuinely invisible, but not in the way I described.

⚠️ CONSEQUENCE: NONE OF THE RULES IN THIS TICKET WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT. An app broken behind a
probe that still returns 200 is invisible to any replica-count rule BY CONSTRUCTION. That needs
blackbox probing, and blackbox-exporter currently targets only 2 endpoints (grafana,
mimir-alertmanager), neither user-facing. Tracked as TALOS-jyo7.

This warning is also in the rule file header so the alerts cannot create false confidence.

## WHAT THE GAP DID COST — measured from history, not assumed

    kasa-exporter   62.7 HOURS at zero available replicas
    hot-ones        10.2 hours
Both unnoticed. Both WOULD have fired under these rules. So the ticket's value stands — the
justification was just attached to the wrong outage.

## ALSO CORRECTED: whisparr was 1/1 Running, not 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff

Which is exactly why it was caught by the restart-RATE rule and correctly NOT by
replica-mismatch: a container that recovers between crashes keeps its Deployment Available. That
is why those are separate rules rather than one.

## THE FULL CHAIN IS PROVEN END TO END

    02:14:37  KubePodCrashLooping -> firing, media-private/whisparr-7bd8fbdd6-kkbzt
              activeAt 01:59:37, walked pending -> firing across the full 15m 'for:' window
              active in Alertmanager, routed to receivers ['discord-default']

metric -> rule -> ruler -> firing -> Alertmanager -> discord-default. All 4 groups loaded,
every rule health=ok.

NOT VERIFIED, stated plainly: no Discord message was observed landing — verification stops at
Alertmanager showing the alert active with the receiver attached. The 1h 'for:' on the two
critical NoAvailableReplicas rules has never been exercised end to end.
KubeDaemonSetMisScheduled currently matches nothing cluster-wide.

title: [bug] beads in talos-private never dolt-commits issues — data lost on server stop
description:
Two tickets were silently destroyed in workspace/talos-private today. This is a persistence defect, not a user error, and it needs a decision.

## WHAT HAPPENED

TALOS-0lf (the immich vector-migration ticket) and TALOS-il4 both vanished within ~30 minutes
of creation. Confirmed by two independent agents: one read TALOS-0lf in full, then minutes
later the same 'bd show' from the same directory returned 'no issue found'.

## ROOT CAUSE — established forensically, not guessed

Beads NEVER dolt-commits issues in that repo. They live indefinitely in the UNCOMMITTED WORKING
SET of the running dolt server.

    TALOS.dolt_log newest commit    2026-08-12   (all schema migrations, no issues)
    on-disk noms files last written 2026-08-17
    bd dolt commit                  reports 'Nothing to commit' WHILE the issue is visibly
                                    present via bd show

So an issue exists only inside the writing session of one server PID. 'bd dolt stop' rolled it
back — while PRINTING 'Flushed working set for 1 database(s) before server stop'. The command
reported a successful flush and did the opposite.

Not recoverable: grep for TALOS-0lf across the entire repo, all 10 .darc backups, and the 7.4MB
dolt server log returns ZERO hits. A control grep for a surviving ID hits 2 files, so the
search method is sound.

## THE GIT-TRACKED STATE IS A FOSSIL

.beads/ is carefully curated for git tracking (10 .darc archives committed, a deliberate
.beads/.gitignore), so committing it LOOKS like the persistence mechanism. It is not working:

    git-tracked issues.jsonl        3 issues
    live dolt DB                    9 issues
    noms files                      7 days without a write

Committing that preserves a fossil and invites a future 'restore' that would destroy current
state.

## ⚠️ A DOLT REMOTE IS NOT THE FIX

talos-private has no dolt remote (bd sync / bd dolt push both error with 'bd dolt remote add
origin <url>'). The obvious move is to add one. THAT WOULD NOT HELP — bd dolt push pushes dolt
COMMITS, and beads has not made one since 12 Aug. Both the stale git state and the loss on
shutdown are downstream of the same root cause: issues never leave the working set.

Adding a remote would make it LOOK fixed while changing nothing, which is worse than the
current honest failure.

## talos-homelab IS NOT AFFECTED — verified

    bd sync    does a real pull -> recompute-blocked -> push, reports 'Sync complete'
    every ticket filed today resolves
The two repos behave differently. Do not generalise from one to the other in either direction.

## WHAT TO DECIDE

  1. Is git-tracked .beads/ the intended design for talos-private, or a half-migration? Commit
     339b53c is 'feat(beads): migrate storage backend from SQLite to Dolt server' — this may be
     an incomplete migration rather than a design.
  2. Should talos-private use beads at all, or should its issues live in talos-homelab's
     database, which demonstrably works?
  3. Worth a beads bug report upstream: 'bd dolt stop' claims to flush the working set and then
     discards it, and 'bd dolt commit' reports 'Nothing to commit' for issues that bd show
     returns.

## CURRENT MITIGATION

TALOS-7sx recreated in talos-private (currently resolves, 9 issues) but is at the SAME RISK.
The durable copy of the full migration plan is in TALOS-cibi here. Treat any talos-private
ticket as at-risk until this is resolved.
close_reason:
RESOLVED 2026-08-25. Root cause was NOT a beads design flaw — it was an accidental, untested pre-release corrupting the schema.

## WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED

Homebrew had beads v1.2.1 installed. GitHub marks v1.2.0 AND v1.2.1 as PRE-RELEASE; v1.2.2 is
the supported stable. v1.2.1's own error text calls itself 'the accidental, untested
v1.2.0/v1.2.1 release'.

That accidental binary ran schema migrations pushing every DB it touched to schema v65. The
stable binary only knows up to v53 and REFUSES a v65 DB:
    'schema version mismatch: database is at v65, binary knows up to v53 (12 migrations ahead)'

So the earlier symptoms — 'issues live in the working set', 'bd dolt stop discards them', 'bd
dolt commit says nothing to commit while bd show returns the issue' — were all the broken v1.2.1
binary mishandling its own over-migrated schema. It was one cause with several faces, not a
fundamental persistence design problem.

## THE FIX (applied to BOTH repos)

1. brew upgrade beads 1.2.1 -> 1.2.2 (stable)
2. per upstream RECOVERY-1.2.1.md: roll schema_migrations back to v53 via the dolt CLI
   (DELETE WHERE version > 53 + DOLT_COMMIT)
3. verify bd works and data survives

⚠️ The recovery guide's documented db path (.beads/embeddeddolt/<db>) was WRONG for us — the
real db is the non-system database containing schema_migrations, found via SHOW DATABASES.
Running the DELETE at the documented path silently matched 0 rows and reported 'nothing to
commit' — success-looking, fixes nothing. Had to target the actual db (TALOS) explicitly.

## VERIFIED — NO DATA LOST

The v1.2.1 schema changes were strictly ADDITIVE (upstream confirms), so nothing was dropped:
  - talos-homelab: 595 issues, bd works, schema v53
  - talos-private: 9 issues (TALOS-7sx + brand tickets), bd works, schema v53
  - CANARY TEST: created an issue in talos-private, ran bd dolt stop, restarted — it SURVIVED.
    That is the exact operation that silently destroyed TALOS-0lf under the broken binary. The
    stop/restart persistence bug is GONE on the correct binary+schema.

talos-private's recovered .beads/ committed + pushed (no dolt remote there, so git-tracked state
is the durable record). Backups retained at .beads.backup-pre-recovery in both repos.

## STILL OPEN AS A SEPARATE CONCERN

A workspace-wide sweep is running (beads-sweep agent) to find and fix any OTHER repo whose
beads DB was pushed to v65 by the same accidental binary. Any hit gets the same recovery.

## PREVENTION

The accidental release got in via brew. Pinning beads to a known-good stable, or watching for
pre-release tags before upgrading, would prevent recurrence. Not enforced — flagging for the
user.

title: [ref] immich vector migration is tracked in talos-private TALOS-0lf
description:
POINTER ONLY — the work and its detail live in the talos-private repo, because that is where immich's manifests are. This ticket exists so the dependency is visible from talos-homelab and does not get lost.

    WORK TICKET:  TALOS-0lf  in  workspace/talos-private  (bd show TALOS-0lf from that dir)
    ⚠️ Both repos use the TALOS- prefix with SEPARATE beads databases. TALOS-0lf is NOT
       resolvable from this repo. cd to workspace/talos-private first.

## WHY IT MATTERS HERE

immich is PINNED to an old digest and must stay pinned until that migration is done. immich
v3.1.0 dropped pgvecto.rs support:

    Error: No vector extension found. Available extensions: vchord, vector

Our sidecar tensorchord/pgvecto-rs:pg16-v0.2.1 provides 'vectors'. Currently 4/4 Running on
digest c15bff75, healthy, data intact — it failed in init BEFORE any migration ran.

⚠️ DO NOT UNPIN, and do not set imagePullPolicy: Always on immich, until TALOS-0lf is resolved.
Either will re-break it immediately. The pin IS the mitigation.

## WHAT IT BLOCKS IN THIS REPO

TALOS-b9i (P0, ship immich-video-faces) — the user flagged that immich-video-faces will need
updating for immich's new vector solution. If it binds to the pgvecto.rs extension name or its
operators, shipping before the migration may be wasted work. Open question recorded on b9i.

TALOS-z3cy (Kyverno mutate forcing pull policy) — must be DIGEST-AWARE, not blanket Always.
Blanket Always is what broke immich: on a long-stale tag it fast-forwards the app across every
release at once. A digest-pinned image must be left alone by that policy.
notes:
== RESEARCH COMPLETE 2026-08-24 (read-only; nothing changed) ==

ANSWERS TO THE THREE QUESTIONS

1. vchord or pgvector?  -> VectorChord (vchord). VectorChord is built ON pgvector and
   requires it, so pgvector stays installed as a dependency. immich v3.1.0 code:
   VECTOR_EXTENSIONS = [VectorChord, Vector] and it picks the FIRST match, i.e. vchord wins
   whenever both are available (server/src/constants.ts:37, database.repository.ts:41-47).
   Version gates in v3.1.0 constants.ts: postgres '>=14.0.0', vchord '>=0.3 <2',
   pgvector '>=0.5 <1'.

2. MUST EMBEDDINGS BE REGENERATED?  -> NO. Proven, not assumed.
   database.repository.ts reindexVectors() does, in ONE transaction:
       DROP INDEX IF EXISTS <idx>
       ALTER TABLE <t> ALTER COLUMN embedding SET DATA TYPE real[]
       ALTER TABLE <t> ALTER COLUMN embedding SET DATA TYPE vector(512)
       CREATE INDEX ... USING vchordrq (embedding vector_cosine_ops)
   The real[] round-trip is the extension-agnostic bridge. Verified against the LIVE db that
   the required assignment casts exist:
       pg_catalog._float4 -> vectors.vector   castcontext 'i'
       vectors.vector -> pg_catalog._float4   castcontext 'i'
   and read-only proof: SELECT array_length(embedding::real[],1) FROM face_search -> 512.
   So values are preserved bit-for-bit; only the INDEX is rebuilt.

3. Documented path?  -> Yes, and it is automatic. immich ships TRANSITIONAL postgres images
   carrying vchord + pgvector + pgvecto.rs together, so the server can read the old type and
   write the new one in one startup. Upstream's own docker-compose for v3.1.0 STILL defaults
   to a transitional image (14-vectorchord0.4.3-pgvectors0.2.0), so this is not a temporary
   hack. Detection reads pg_available_extensions (what the IMAGE ships), which is exactly why
   we failed: tensorchord/pgvecto-rs ships only 'vectors'.

LIBRARY SIZE (measured live, media-private/immich-5c4dbd66f6-mmhtq)
   assets 431 (254 image / 177 video) | smart_search 423 rows, 1488 kB
   face_search 23145 rows, 64 MB | asset_face 23146 | person 85 | db 213 MB
   pg 16.8, extension 'vectors' 0.2.1 in schema 'vectors'
   search_path is DATABASE-level: ALTER DATABASE immich SET search_path='"$user", public, vectors'
   -> post-migration 'vector' resolves to public.vector (pgvector) because public precedes vectors.
   Reindex cost at this size: seconds. targetListCount(count<128000) = 1, so both indexes get
   lists=[1], probes=1.
   Worst case IF something forced a re-embed: 172 videos x ~20 keyframes through InsightFace
   buffalo_l on 1 CPU worker = hours, not minutes. Avoided entirely by the above.

TARGET IMAGE
   ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres:16-vectorchord0.4.3-pgvector0.8.1-pgvectors0.2.1
   digest sha256:13d1ff1638f54be482620d0ef1eb2b004c99bfd674d06359ae0b91d8f5b5696b
   (pg 16.10, matches our pg16 + pgvectors 0.2.1 exactly; highest pg16 tag that still carries
   pgvecto.rs). Built 2025-10-07.

*** THE NFS LANDMINE — this is what couples the CNPG decision ***
   immich-app/base-images commit 05727095 (2026-07-10, PR #358) added an fstype guard to
   immich-docker-entrypoint.sh: PGDATA on anything other than ext2/3/4|xfs|btrfs|zfs|f2fs|tmpfs
   causes exit 1 unless IGNORE_DATABASE_FSTYPE=true.
   Our PVC immich-postgres is 5Gi RWX on fatboy-nfs-appdata = NFS.
   - The 0.4.3 transitional image (built 2025-10-07) PREDATES the guard -> starts fine on NFS.
   - 16-vectorchord1.1.1-pgvector0.8.5 (built 2026-08-11, pg 16.14) POSTDATES it -> hard-fails
     on our NFS PVC without the override.
   Upstream now enforces our own house rule. So: extension migration can be done in place on
   NFS today, but staying on a maintained DB image later REQUIRES the move off NFS.
   -> RECOMMEND SEQUENCE, NOT COUPLE. Phase 1 = extension swap in place (contained, reversible,
   unblocks the v3 pin). Phase 2 = CNPG on local-path NVMe instances:3 (TALOS-hx77.10), from a
   clean vchord-only state via pg_dump/restore, which also drops the pgvecto.rs baggage and the
   database-level search_path override. Coupling them turns a 20-minute change into a project
   and puts the only rollback behind a storage migration.

CNPG OPERAND NOTE for TALOS-hx77.10: official CNPG images do NOT ship vchord and ImageVolume is
   off cluster-wide. Viable operand: ghcr.io/tensorchord/cloudnative-vectorchord (pg16/17/18
   tags exist). Doing Phase 1 first means Phase 2 needs only that image, NOT the third-party
   pgvecto.rs+vchord hybrid (corentingiraud/cnpg-pgvector-vectorchord) it would otherwise need.

PRE-FLIGHT CHECKS ALREADY RUN (live, read-only)
   20 immich schema migrations pending (DB is at 1775165531374; v3.1.0 tops out at 1784836013770).
   Reviewed the destructive-looking ones:
   - 1780435471692-DeleteMismatchedAssetFaces: deletes asset_face where person.ownerId != asset.ownerId.
     Measured live: 0 rows match. No-op for us. This was the main risk to the 23k IVF faces.
   - 1784836013770-MinFacePreferenceMigration: user_metadata only, harmless.
   immich getSchemaDrift() uses tables:{ignoreExtra:true} so IVF's video_face_scan_log will not
   trip it, and drift is a WARN not a failure.

ORDERED PLAN (each step names its rollback)
   0. pg_dump -Fc the immich DB to a location outside the PVC. THIS is the rollback point;
      Velero's velero-daily-all covers media-private but is a crash-consistent filesystem copy
      of a running postgres on NFS, which is not a database backup. Rollback: restore the dump.
   1. Swap ONLY the postgres sidecar image to the transitional tag above. Leave immich-server /
      immich-ml on the c15bff75 / a2501141 pins. Set DB_STORAGE_TYPE: HDD (NFS is not SSD; the
      image defaults SSD and the conf template tunes random_page_cost/effective_io_concurrency
      accordingly). Rollback: revert the one image line; pgvecto.rs data is untouched because
      v2.7.5 keeps using 'vectors'.
   2. Verify v2.7.5 still boots clean and \dx shows vectors 0.2.1 plus vchord+vector now merely
      AVAILABLE (not yet installed). Rollback: same as step 1.
   3. Unpin immich-server and immich-ml to v3.1.0 (pin the v3.1.0 digests, do NOT go back to a
      floating :release tag - see TALOS-1t2q). On boot immich will CREATE EXTENSION vchord CASCADE,
      run the 20 migrations, and reindex clip_index + face_index into vchordrq.
      Watch for "Reindexing clip_index"/"Reindexing face_index" and "Reindexed".
      Rollback: revert to the c15bff75 pin AND restore the step-0 dump - after this step the
      column type has changed, so the image revert alone is NOT sufficient.
   4. Verify: \dx shows vchord + vector installed; \d face_search shows vector(512) with a
      vchordrq index; face_search still has 23145 rows and smart_search 423; search + people
      pages work in the UI.
   5. Optional cleanup once stable: DROP EXTENSION vectors; and reset the database-level
      search_path. Do NOT do this before immich-video-faces is confirmed working.
   6. Do NOT move to 16-vectorchord1.1.1-pgvector0.8.5 while on NFS - it will refuse to start.
      That bump belongs with TALOS-hx77.10.

immich-video-faces impact: filed separately. Short version - its SQL is portable (both
extensions name the type 'vector' and define '<=>'), so this is NOT the breaking change it
looked like. IVF has already run in prod: 172 videos in video_face_scan_log, 23134 of 23146
asset_face rows sit on IVF-scanned assets. That corpus is preserved by step 3.

## ⚠️ POINTER CORRECTED — the talos-private ticket is now TALOS-7sx, not TALOS-0lf

TALOS-0lf was LOST. The talos-private beads DB rolled back under us and the ticket vanished
within ~30 minutes of creation, along with TALOS-il4. Recreated as TALOS-7sx.

    WORK TICKET:  TALOS-7sx  in  workspace/talos-private
    ⚠️ Both repos use the TALOS- prefix with SEPARATE databases. Neither ID resolves from the
       other repo. cd to the right directory first.

⚠️ THE talos-private BEADS DB IS UNRELIABLE — three disjoint views of reality observed:
    .beads/issues.jsonl (portable export)   TALOS-il4, TALOS-qoz, TALOS-hgo
    live dolt DB                            TALOS-2ks, TALOS-lu3
    both created tickets                    in neither
It also has NO dolt remote configured, so bd sync / bd dolt push cannot work there; git-tracked
.beads/ files are the only persistence. Commit b9e6afa captured state 'including TALOS-0lf' and
the ticket still disappeared afterwards. TREAT ANY TICKET FILED IN talos-private AS AT RISK
until this is repaired. The full plan below is the durable copy.

# THE MIGRATION PLAN — durable copy, talos-homelab beads is healthy

TARGET: VectorChord (vchord), NOT plain pgvector. VectorChord is built ON pgvector and reuses
its types, so pgvector remains installed as a dependency. immich's VECTOR_EXTENSIONS is
[VectorChord, Vector] and it takes the FIRST match, so vchord wins whenever both exist.

>=0.5 <1. (The docs site says >=0.7 <0.9 for pgvector — stale, trust the code.)

WHY WE FAILED, EXACTLY: database.repository.ts:41 queries pg_available_extensions — what the
IMAGE SHIPS, not what is installed. tensorchord/pgvecto-rs ships only 'vectors'. The error's
'Available extensions: vchord, vector' is immich's SUPPORTED set, not a readout of our DB.
Our pin is v2.7.5 (IMMICH_SOURCE_REF in the running container).

TRANSITIONAL IMAGE — carries vchord + pgvector + pgvecto.rs simultaneously so the server reads
the old type and writes the new one in a single startup. Not a stopgap: upstream's
docker-compose FOR v3.1.0 still defaults to a transitional image.
    ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres:16-vectorchord0.4.3-pgvector0.8.1-pgvectors0.2.1
    sha256:13d1ff1638f54be482620d0ef1eb2b004c99bfd674d06359ae0b91d8f5b5696b

## EMBEDDINGS DO NOT NEED REGENERATING — proven read-only, not assumed

reindexVectors() does, in one transaction: DROP INDEX; ALTER COLUMN embedding SET DATA TYPE
real[]; ALTER COLUMN embedding SET DATA TYPE vector(512); CREATE INDEX USING vchordrq. The
real[] round-trip is the extension-agnostic bridge. Verified against the LIVE db that the
required assignment casts exist (pg_cast shows vectors.vector <-> pg_catalog._float4 both
directions, castcontext 'i'), and proved it: SELECT array_length(embedding::real[],1) FROM
face_search returns 512. Values preserved; only the index is rebuilt.

MEASURED LIVE: 431 assets (254 image / 177 video), smart_search 423 rows / 1.5MB, face_search
23,145 rows / 64MB, asset_face 23,146, person 85, DB 213MB. targetListCount() returns 1 under
128,000 rows so both indexes get lists=[1]. REINDEX COST: SECONDS. The counterfactual if a
re-embed had been needed: 172 videos x ~20 keyframes through InsightFace buffalo_l on one CPU
worker — hours.

## ⚠️ THE NFS LANDMINE — this sets a real deadline

immich-app/base-images commit 05727095 (2026-07-10, PR #358) added an fstype guard to the
postgres entrypoint: PGDATA on anything but ext2/3/4|xfs|btrfs|zfs|f2fs|tmpfs exits 1 unless
IGNORE_DATABASE_FSTYPE=true. Our immich-postgres PVC is 5Gi RWX on fatboy-nfs-appdata — NFS.
Upstream now enforces our own house rule.
    0.4.3 transitional image   built 2025-10-07, PREDATES the guard  -> starts fine on NFS
                               (pg 16.10 vs our 16.8 — minor bump, no pg_upgrade)
    16-vectorchord1.1.1        built 2026-08-11, POSTDATES it        -> HARD-FAILS on NFS
So Phase 1 can be done in place today, but staying on a MAINTAINED db image later REQUIRES the

## DECISION: SEQUENCE, DO NOT COUPLE

Phase 1 = extension swap in place. Contained, reversible, unblocks the pin.
Phase 2 = CNPG on local-path NVMe instances:3, from a clean vchord-only state via
          pg_dump/restore.
Coupling turns a ~20-minute change into a project and puts the only rollback behind a storage
migration. Sequencing also SIMPLIFIES phase 2: from a clean state it needs only

would otherwise require. Official CNPG images do NOT ship vchord and ImageVolume is off
cluster-wide, so a third-party operand is unavoidable either way.

## ORDERED STEPS, ROLLBACK NAMED AT EACH

0. pg_dump -Fc to somewhere OFF the PVC. THIS IS THE ROLLBACK POINT. Velero's
   velero-daily-all covers media-private but it is a crash-consistent filesystem copy of a
   RUNNING postgres on NFS — not a database backup.
1. Swap ONLY the postgres sidecar image to the transitional tag. Leave server/ML pinned. Set
   DB_STORAGE_TYPE: HDD — NFS is not SSD and the image's conf template tunes random_page_cost
   and effective_io_concurrency off that env.
   Rollback: revert one image line; pgvecto.rs data untouched since v2.7.5 still uses 'vectors'.
2. Verify v2.7.5 boots clean, \dx still shows vectors 0.2.1, vchord+vector merely AVAILABLE.
3. Unpin server + ML to v3.1.0 DIGESTS — do NOT return to floating :release (cf. TALOS-1t2q).
   On boot: CREATE EXTENSION vchord CASCADE, 20 pending migrations, both indexes reindexed into
   vchordrq. Watch for 'Reindexing clip_index' / 'Reindexed'.
   ⚠️ ROLLBACK AFTER THIS STEP REQUIRES THE STEP-0 DUMP. The column type has changed; reverting
   the image alone is NOT sufficient.
4. Verify: \dx shows vchord + vector; \d face_search shows vector(512) + vchordrq index;
   face_search still 23,145 and smart_search 423; search and people pages work.
5. Optional later: DROP EXTENSION vectors, reset the database-level search_path. NOT before
   immich-video-faces is confirmed working.
6. Do NOT jump to 16-vectorchord1.1.1 while on NFS.

## PRE-FLIGHT ALREADY RUN

All 20 pending migrations reviewed for destructive operations.
1780435471692-DeleteMismatchedAssetFaces deletes asset_face where person.ownerId !=
asset.ownerId — MEASURED LIVE, 0 rows match, no-op. That was the main risk to the 23k faces.
MinFacePreferenceMigration is user_metadata only. immich's schema-drift check uses
tables:{ignoreExtra:true} so immich-video-faces' video_face_scan_log will not trip it, and
drift is a WARN not a boot failure.

⚠️ SUSPEND the immich-video-faces CronJob for the migration window. k8s/cronjob.yaml runs
daily at 03:00 with write connections; nothing may insert into face_search during the
ALTER COLUMN / reindex. Unsuspend after, and confirm its safety report reads vchord.
## ✅ PHASE 1 COMPLETE 2026-08-24 — and the plan had one materially wrong assumption

immich is on VectorChord. 4/4 Running, v2.7.5, 0 restarts. Landed as 048cdda in talos-private.

    pg_extension    vchord 0.4.3 + vector 0.8.1    (vectors/pgvecto.rs DROPPED)
    embedding type  public.vector
    indexes         face_index + clip_index, both vchordrq, lists=[1]
    face_search 23145 · smart_search 423 · asset_face 23146 · person 85 · asset 431

## ⚠️ CORRECTION: STEP 1 AND STEP 3 ARE THE SAME STEP

The plan assumed the column-type change was gated behind unpinning the server to v3.1.0. IT IS
NOT. immich v2.7.5 prefers VectorChord and migrates itself the moment vchord is merely
AVAILABLE. From immich-server's own logs, ~40s after the new postgres pod came up:

    Creating VectorChord extension
    Reindexing clip_index (This may take a while, do not restart)
    Reindexing face_index
    Reindexed clip_index / Reindexed face_index
    Dropping pgvecto.rs extension
    Running migrations / Finished running migrations

ZERO DDL was issued by hand. immich did all of it.

CONSEQUENCE: the step-2 checkpoint the plan describes — 'vectors still installed, vchord merely
available' — IS NOT REACHABLE with a v2.7.5 server. Swapping the DB image IS the irreversible
step. Rollback now requires BOTH reverting the manifest to tensorchord/pgvecto-rs AND restoring
the dump; reverting the image alone leaves a DB whose columns the old image cannot read.

ANYONE RUNNING THIS ELSEWHERE MUST KNOW THIS. Do not plan a checkpoint between the two.

## EMBEDDINGS PRESERVED BIT-FOR-BIT — verified, not assumed

md5 over (id || ':' || embedding::real[]) ordered by id, comparing the pre-change dump restored
on pgvecto.rs against the live post-migration DB (real[] is format-stable across the type change):

    face_search   a8848a5747430013578e281cfb550063 / 23145   dump AND live IDENTICAL
    smart_search  6065f844bbd39fdc12f03af1d81403dc / 423     dump AND live IDENTICAL

All 23,145 face embeddings survived the vectors.vector -> real[] -> vector round trip exactly.
No re-embedding. The 172 videos of InsightFace work is safe.

Search is live, not merely present: EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows 'Index Scan using face_index ...
Order By: (embedding <=> $0)' returning 5 rows.

## THE ROLLBACK POINT — verified three ways

    /Users/panda/catalyst-devspace/.backups/immich/immich-pre-vectorchord-20260824-184451.dump
    77,901,230 bytes, sha256 b7288066f18671f8b93a9e991704bf49888d90c98fd719103aa6b32dd6318230
    second copy on a DIFFERENT PVC (immich-ml-cache) at /cache/_db-backups/, same sha256
    sidecars: immich-globals-20260824.sql (roles + SCRAM hash), immich-db-settings-20260824.txt
              (the ALTER DATABASE search_path — pg_dump -Fc without --create does NOT carry these)

Verified by pg_restore --list (502 TOC entries), a FULL TRIAL RESTORE into a throwaway pod
(counts matched live exactly), and md5 content comparison of both embedding tables.

## DB_STORAGE_TYPE: HDD took effect

random_page_cost 4, effective_io_concurrency 1. The SSD template would have forced 1.2 / 200,
which is wrong for NFS — those two settings are the ONLY difference between the templates.

## LESSON WORTH KEEPING: do not read config out of OCI layer blobs

A false alarm mid-run came from extracting postgresql.hdd.conf by scanning layer blobs
smallest-first: layers SHADOW each other and a superseded copy was read, showing
shared_preload_libraries='vchord.so' alone. Running the image and reading the effective file
showed 'vchord.so, vectors.so' — both preloaded, as a transitional image should. The bad
revision never reached the cluster (ArgoCD stayed on e74d90d; pod age unchanged). Cost was git
noise only: b305bc1 and 048cdda are byte-identical, 5272673 is their exact inverse.

## STILL TRUE

The NFS deadline is unchanged. This postgres image (built 2025-10-07) is the LAST one that
starts on our NFS PVC — its entrypoint predates base-images 05727095 and contains no fstype
guard. Staying on a maintained DB image still requires the move to local-path first
(TALOS-hx77.10), and Phase 2 now only needs a vchord-capable operand
(ghcr.io/tensorchord/cloudnative-vectorchord), NOT the pgvecto.rs+vchord hybrid — that baggage
is gone.

## THE 'DO NOT UNPIN' CAVEAT IS RESOLVED

v3.1.0 required vchord; vchord is installed. Its ~20 schema migrations are still pending.
Unpinning is now a normal decision rather than a known-broken action.

title: [bug] ~/.curlrc has global -v and -k: every curl leaks auth headers and skips TLS verification
description:
A registry credential was exposed during the Bluetooth extension work because
~/.curlrc sets -v globally. This is a machine-wide vector, not a one-off mistake.

## WHAT HAPPENED

An agent ran 'curl -u <user>:<pass>' to verify registry auth. Because ~/.curlrc contains -v,
curl printed the full request headers to stderr, including:
    Authorization: Basic <base64>
which trivially decodes to the registry.talos00 credential. It is now in a session transcript
in recoverable form.

ROTATE THE registry.talos00 PASSWORD. That is the only real remediation for the exposure
itself; the entries below prevent recurrence.

## THE TWO PROBLEMS

~/.curlrc is a symlink to catalyst/@dotfiles-2024/dotfiles/.curlrc

    line 8:  -v     Verbose. Prints request AND response headers for EVERY curl invocation on
                    this machine, from any script or tool. It SURVIVES -s — verified: a
                    'curl -s -o /dev/null' still emitted request-header lines to stderr. So
                    any tool that shells out to curl with credentials leaks them into
                    whatever captures its stderr: CI logs, agent transcripts, terminal
                    scrollback, shell history if redirected.

    line 5:  -k     Permit unsafe SSL. Disables certificate verification for EVERY curl on
                    this machine. That is a silent downgrade of every HTTPS call any script
                    makes — including ones fetching credentials or code. Arguably worse than
                    the -v issue because it fails open and invisibly.

## SUGGESTED FIX

Remove both from the global rc. Neither belongs in a machine-wide default:
  - -v is a debugging flag. Pass it per-invocation when debugging.
  - -k should be per-invocation and deliberate, scoped to the one host with a self-signed
    cert (e.g. the UniFi controller at 192.168.1.1, which is the likely original reason).

Keep -L and the user-agent if they are wanted; those are preferences, not security controls.

## NOT DONE BY ME

~/.curlrc is a symlink into catalyst/@dotfiles-2024, and CLAUDE.md warns that changes there
may break symlinks throughout the workspace. Left for the user to change deliberately.

## DEFENSIVE NOTE FOR TOOLING

Anything scripted that passes credentials to curl should use -q (ignore .curlrc) or, better,
avoid credentials on the command line entirely — a mode-600 config file or --netrc. -q is the
one-character fix that makes a script immune to whatever the user's rc happens to contain.
close_reason:
Closed as ACCEPTED RISK — the user's decision, 2026-08-24: 'the registry.talos00 password is fine for now ignore it, curlrc leak fine as well'.

Recording what was accepted so it is a decision rather than an oversight:

  ~/.curlrc line 8 is -v, and it SURVIVES -s (verified: curl -s -o /dev/null still emits
  request headers). Any tool on this machine that shells out to curl with credentials leaks
  them into whatever captures stderr — CI logs, agent transcripts, terminal scrollback.
  That is how the registry.talos00 credential for user 'panda' ended up in a session
  transcript in recoverable form.

  ~/.curlrc line 5 is -k, disabling TLS certificate verification for EVERY curl invocation
  on this machine. Arguably the more serious of the two because it fails open and invisibly.

Both are inside a LAN-only homelab, and the registry is not internet-facing, which is a
reasonable basis for the call.

Not fixed because ~/.curlrc is a symlink into catalyst/@dotfiles-2024 and the project's own
CLAUDE.md warns that changes there break symlinks across the workspace — so it is the user's
to change deliberately, not something to alter in passing.

DEFENSIVE NOTE for anything scripted: pass -q to ignore .curlrc entirely, or avoid credentials
on the command line (a mode-600 config file, or --netrc). -q is the one-character fix that
makes a script immune to whatever the user's rc happens to contain. Reopen if the registry is
ever exposed beyond the LAN.

title: media-experimental: 11 apps + restore CronJob all pinned to talos03, the least-RAM node that wedged today
description:
The pin itself is CORRECT and well-built -- do not just delete it. applications/media-experimental/base/_instance/deployment.yaml:41-49 sets requiredDuringScheduling nodeAffinity on kubernetes.io/hostname = ${MEDIA_EXPERIMENTAL_NODE:=talos03}, and the comment above it explicitly explains it is the deliberate second half of a storage pin, written after sonarr proved a pod stays welded to a node once its PVC is gone. backup/cronjob-restore.yaml:55 reads the SAME variable so fresh WaitForFirstConsumer PVCs provision where the pods are going. cluster-settings.yaml:24 holds the value.

Real constraint confirmed: 11 local-path config PVCs, all 5Gi, all with PV nodeAffinity to talos03 (audiobookshelf-config, audiobookshelf-metadata, bindery, booksonic, chaptarr, kavita, komga, libation, librarr, livrarr, mylar3, storyteller).

THE PROBLEM IS THE CHOICE OF NODE, NOT THE MECHANISM. talos03 has 15.0Gi -- the least RAM in the cluster -- and it wedged on memory today and needed a physical power cycle. 11 apps went down together and could not move.

Two options, needs a decision:
  (a) Point MEDIA_EXPERIMENTAL_NODE at a larger node and run the documented restore runbook (applications/media-experimental/base/backup/README.md). Keeps the design, moves the blast radius somewhere it can absorb it. LOW RISK, machinery already exists and is tested.
  (b) Migrate the 11 config PVCs to fatboy-nfs-appdata (dynamic NFS, Immediate binding, not node-bound) and drop the affinity entirely. Fully unpinned.

RECOMMEND (a). Option (b) has a real hazard: komga/kavita/audiobookshelf/mylar3 keep SQLite config DBs, and SQLite on NFS is the exact corruption pattern this repo already avoided by putting plex-db-local and jellyfin-db-local on local disk. (b) would need per-app assessment, not a blanket move.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
DECISION (user, 2026-08-24): LEAVE media-experimental pinned to talos03. Closing as
won't-do, not as unresolved.

Rationale from the user: the workload there is shrinking over time, so paying a data
migration now to unpin something that is on its way out is not worth it.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE ONE-LINE CHANGE THE AUDIT IMPLIED. There are 13 node-bound PVs on
talos03 for this namespace. Changing MEDIA_EXPERIMENTAL_NODE alone would send 11 workloads
plus the restore CronJob to a node where their volumes do not exist — they would come up
empty or Pending. The correct procedure is the full runbook in
applications/media-experimental/base/backup/README.md: back up and PROVE the restore, scale
to zero, delete the PVCs, repoint the variable, restore, bring back up. Seven steps across
11 live workloads.

That machinery is real and proven — it ran end to end earlier today after talos03 was wiped,
restoring 12/12 archives with every file sha256-verified and correct uid:gid ownership. So
the option stays available at any time. It is simply not free.

WHAT MAKES LEAVING IT DEFENSIBLE NOW. talos03 is materially safer than it was this morning:
  - maxPods capped 200 -> 60 (it runs 27), so it can no longer be packed to the ceiling
  - memory reserved: 1Gi system + 1Gi kube + 500Mi evictionHard, so it evicts rather than
    wedging
  - alloy and loki-chunks-cache steered off it and talos01
It reached 0.61 GiB free over the last 7 days and wedged once; none of the above creates
memory, but together they change the failure mode from 'needs a physical power cycle' to
'sheds a pod'.

REVISIT IF: media-experimental grows rather than shrinks, or talos03 approaches its floor
again. The measurement to watch is min_over_time(node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes[7d]) for
talos03 — not pod count, not requests.

title: plex + jellyfin are hard-pinned to talos02-gpu by *-db-local, not by the GPU affinity they advertise
description:
Both Deployments carry only a SOFT preferredDuringScheduling nodeAffinity on intel.feature.node.kubernetes.io/gpu, plus a gpu.intel.com/i915: 1 resource request. Read alone, that says 'can run on either GPU node'. It cannot.

The real constraint: plex mounts plex-db-local and jellyfin mounts jellyfin-db-local, both local-path 1Ti PVCs bound to rec-media-plex-db-local / rec-media-jellyfin-db-local (recovery/pv-recovery-2026-05-09.yaml), both with PV nodeAffinity to talos02-gpu. Verified live -- both pods on talos02-gpu.

This is a LEGITIMATE pin: those are the SQLite metadata DBs, deliberately kept off NFS. But it is INVISIBLE at the Deployment level, and it means a talos02-gpu outage takes both media servers down even though talos06 has identical Intel Arc hardware and a free i915.

NOT a metadata removal. The question to answer is whether the DB volumes should move (and to what), or whether we accept it and document the pin at the Deployment so nobody reads the soft affinity as freedom of movement. No action taken.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
DECISION (user, 2026-08-24): KEEP plex and jellyfin constrained to the GPU nodes. Close this
as won't-do rather than treating the constraint as a problem to solve.

The audit flagged these as 'read as movable but are not'. That reading was correct
mechanically but the constraint is DELIBERATE, and the tradeoff was put to the user
explicitly:

  - Their nodeAffinity is ALREADY preferredDuringScheduling (weight 100) for
    intel.feature.node.kubernetes.io/gpu. Affinity is not what pins them.
  - The hard pin is resources.limits['gpu.intel.com/i915'] = 1, set in
    applications/arr-stack/overlays/gpu/{plex,jellyfin}-gpu-patch.yaml:31.
  - That resource request is ALSO what makes the Intel device plugin grant /dev/dri.
    Extended resources are all-or-nothing, so you cannot request one conditionally.

Therefore: dropping it to gain schedulability would lose hardware transcoding EVERYWHERE,
including on the two Arc nodes. A hostPath /dev/dri with type DirectoryOrCreate was offered
as a middle path (schedule anywhere, real HW on Arc nodes, CPU fallback elsewhere) and was
also declined — it bypasses the device plugin's accounting.

Accepted consequence, stated plainly: if BOTH talos02-gpu and talos06 are unavailable, plex
and jellyfin do not run. That is a considered trade of availability for transcode quality on
a media server, not an oversight.

VERIFIED WORKING as of this decision: plex on talos02-gpu with /dev/dri/card0 and
renderD128 present in-container and limits gpu.intel.com/i915=1 granted. Both Arc nodes
carry 0x8086:0x7d51 Arrow Lake-P [Arc Pro 130T/140T] and advertise i915=10.

DO NOT 'fix' this in a future affinity sweep.

title: frigate: nodeSelector talos02-gpu justified by a GPU detector it does not use
description:
applications/scratch/frigate/deployment.yaml:3 says "Uses Intel Arc on talos02-gpu via OpenVINO for person detection". FALSE: applications/scratch/frigate/configmap.yaml:30 configures 'detectors: cpu / type: cpu / num_threads: 4', with a TODO to try the -openvino image someday. The live pod requests no gpu.intel.com/i915.

What frigate DOES need is /dev/dri, hostPath-mounted (deployment.yaml:137-139) for 'hwaccel_args: preset-vaapi' video decode. That is satisfied by talos02-gpu AND talos06 -- both carry the i915 + intel-ucode Talos extensions and advertise gpu.intel.com/i915=10. talos01 has an Intel iGPU PCI device (8086:46b3) and the NFD label, but NO i915 extension: its gpu-plugin logs 'failed to read by-path dir: /dev/dri/by-path: no such file or directory' and it advertises zero i915. So the GPU-capable set is exactly {talos02-gpu, talos06}.

BLOCKED ON STORAGE: frigate-config (1Ti) and frigate-media (1Ti) are local-path PVCs whose PVs (rec-scratch-frigate-config, rec-scratch-frigate-media, from recovery/pv-recovery-2026-05-09.yaml) carry nodeAffinity to talos02-gpu. Removing the nodeSelector alone changes nothing.

PROPOSAL (needs approval): swap the hostname nodeSelector for 'intel.feature.node.kubernetes.io/gpu-arc: "true"' -- honest about the real requirement, widens to 2 nodes -- and decide separately whether the 1Ti recording volume is worth migrating. Also fix the false header comment either way.

title: Reclaim ~260GB/node: stale catalyst-data CI images never GC'd on talos06 + talos02-gpu
description:
Filed 2026-08-24 after a full disk-consumption investigation of talos06 (82% full) and talos02-gpu.

## VERDICT
The GPU/transcode-cache hypothesis is FALSE. tdarr transcode-cache is an emptyDir
(sizeLimit 300Gi) and measured 6 bytes on talos06, 88 bytes on talos02-gpu. It cannot
leak — it is destroyed with the pod.

The real consumer is the containerd image store, and it is 73% stale CI images from
the catalyst-data namespace, whose Deployments have been scaled 0/0 for 105 days.

## MEASURED (2026-08-24)
talos06     /var 997.4 GB, 819.3 GB used (82.1%), 178.1 GB free
talos02-gpu /var 1904.6 GiB cap, 662 GiB used (35%)

Breakdown talos06 (du, apparent size):
  /var/lib/containerd  350 GB   <- 887 unique images, 310.9 GB of layer content
  /var/lib/rancher     202 GB   <- local-path PVs; 161 GB of it is ONE file,
                                   gaming/windows-gameserver-disk disk.img (KubeVirt)
  /var/log             0.3 GB
  /var/lib/kubelet     ~15 GB local (the 77 TB du reading is NFS traversal, not local)

Breakdown talos02-gpu:
  /var/lib/containerd  330 GB   <- 836 unique images, 299.7 GB
  /var/lib/rancher      24 GB
  /var/log             0.3 GB

## THE STALE IMAGES
ghcr.io/thebranchdriftcatalyst/{media-ingest,data-explorer,open-leaks,congress-data,
knowledge-graph,knowledge-graph-api} — one image per git commit, pushed by
argocd-image-updater (infrastructure/base/argocd/image-updater/catalyst-data-image-updater.yaml).

  talos06      306 images  261.6 GB  (media-ingest alone: 87 images, 227.5 GB)
  talos02-gpu  210 images  238.8 GB  (media-ingest alone: 91 images, 219.7 GB)

All pulled April 2026. Zero live pods reference them. The whole catalyst-data namespace
is 0/0 replicas (media-ingest, congress-data, knowledge-graph, knowledge-graph-api,
dagster-*, neo4j) and has been for 105 days. The Flux entry is commented out in
clusters/catalyst-cluster/flux-system/kustomization.yaml:132.

## WHY NOTHING PRUNES THEM
kubelet image GC is purely threshold-driven and age-based GC is DISABLED:
  kubectl get --raw /api/v1/nodes/talos06/proxy/configz | jq .kubeletconfig
    imageGCHighThresholdPercent: 85
    imageGCLowThresholdPercent:  80
    imageMaximumGCAge: "0s"     <- disabled (Talos default)
talos06 sits at 82.1% — just under the 85% trigger. talos02-gpu is at 35%. So kubelet
has never run image GC on either node, and never will until talos06 crosses 85%.
Nothing else prunes images on Talos.

## RECLAIM (do not run blind — read first)
Generated command lists (one 'talosctl image remove <repo>@<digest>' per line):
  /private/tmp/claude-501/.../scratchpad/remove-192.168.1.19.sh    (talos06,     306 lines)
  /private/tmp/claude-501/.../scratchpad/remove-192.168.1.144.sh   (talos02-gpu, 210 lines)
Regenerate with: talosctl -e 192.168.1.54 -n <ip> image list --namespace cri

Conservative floor: 261.6 GB on talos06, 238.8 GB on talos02-gpu (that is the summed
compressed layer size; the unpacked snapshot footprint is larger). talos06 goes from
82% to roughly 56% or better.

## NOT THE PROBLEM (ruled out, with numbers)
- tdarr transcode cache: 6 B / 88 B. Empty. emptyDir, cannot leak.
- Container writable layers: 2.5 GiB total on talos06, 1.3 GiB on talos02-gpu.
- Orphaned local-path PV data: 27 dirs have no matching PV, but 26 of them are
  deliberately re-adopted by hand-made 'rec-*' PVs pointing at the same path.
  Only genuine orphan: media/prowlarr-db-local on talos02-gpu, 8.2 MB. Irrelevant.
- The Released PVs from TALOS-nt01: all 33 are storageClass fatboy-nfs-appdata,
  zero node-local. They occupy Synology NFS, not node disk. Not related.
- Log rotation: /var/log is 303 MB / 312 MB. containerLogMaxSize 10Mi x 5 files, fine.
- Sabnzbd's 315 GB and tdarr's 38 TB under /var/lib/kubelet/pods are NFS mounts
  (Synology), not local disk. du of /var is misleading for this reason.

title: Reconcile extension drift: get iscsi-tools onto talos00, talos02-gpu and talos06
description:
Deliberately SEPARATE from the config migration — this one reboots nodes and carries real risk, so it should not ride along with an otherwise non-disruptive change.

Measured 2026-08-23, live vs git:

| node | git schematic | live schematic | live extensions | status |
| talos00 | c9078f94 (iscsi-tools) | none — stock ghcr installer | NONE | DRIFT |
| talos01 | c9078f94 | c9078f94 | iscsi-tools | ok |
| talos02-gpu | 9ffda6da (i915, intel-ucode, iscsi-tools) | 4b3cd373 | i915, intel-ucode | DRIFT |
| talos03 | 1e17720b | 1e17720b | amd-ucode, amdgpu, iscsi-tools | ok |
| talos06 | 6b32ee67 (intel-ucode, i915, mei, iscsi-tools) | 16be3b98 | intel-ucode, i915, mei | DRIFT |

All five git schematic files were re-POSTed to factory.talos.dev and their content still hashes to the ID in their header, so the files are internally consistent — the schematics were edited on 2026-01-16 to add iscsi-tools and three nodes were simply never re-imaged.

IMPACT: talos00, talos02-gpu and talos06 cannot attach Democratic-CSI iSCSI volumes. The kubelet extraMounts for /etc/iscsi ARE present on all five nodes, so the mount exists but the tooling behind it does not — which is why this has been invisible. A workload needing iSCSI that lands on one of these three fails for a reason that points nowhere near the real cause.

talos00 is also still on the STOCK ghcr.io installer with no extensions at all, i.e. it has never run the schematic git claims for it.

FIX: upgrade each drifted node with its correct per-node factory installer image (use `talhelper gencommand upgrade` once TALOS-dnfy lands). One node at a time, health check between, control plane last. Then confirm `talosctl get extensions` matches talconfig on all five.

Also confirm the intent first: is iscsi-tools actually wanted on talos00, given it is the RAM-limited control-plane-only node? If not, the fix is to correct git rather than the node.
acceptance_criteria:
- Intent confirmed for talos00 (extension wanted, or git corrected)
- All drifted nodes upgraded to their declared schematic
- talosctl get extensions matches talconfig on all five nodes
- Democratic-CSI iSCSI volume attach verified on a previously-drifted node
- task talos:verify reports zero drift
close_reason:
CONVERGED, closed on the user's explicit decision (2026-08-24): 'keep the iscsi stuff it will be used at some point.'

Force-closed because the blocking dependency on TALOS-1ujn is real but points FORWARD, not at
remaining work here. This ticket's own scope is obsolete; what is left belongs to 1ujn.

THE DRIFT NO LONGER EXISTS. The talhelper migration resolved it by converging git downward
onto the nodes. Verified two ways: per-node generated install image == live install image
including schematic hash, and verify-diff.py at 0 across all five nodes. The acceptance
criteria — 'all drifted nodes upgraded', 'Democratic-CSI volume attach verified' — are
OBSOLETED rather than met.

iSCSI IS ENTIRELY UNUSED: no CSI drivers exist in this cluster at all, no Democratic-CSI, no
iSCSI StorageClass, zero iSCSI PVs, no pending PVCs. Checked the DATA not just the wiring —
/var/lib/iscsi is EMPTY on both nodes that have the tooling and /etc/iscsi holds only the
auto-generated initiatorname. iSCSI has never attached a volume here.

WHY THE ASYMMETRY: iscsi-tools was added 2026-01-16 for Democratic-CSI Synology iSCSI. That
effort was never wired into Flux, never ran, and its last artifact was deleted 2026-08-09 as an
abandoned orphan leaking a DSM credential (94211176, TALOS-rpyc). It reached two of five nodes
before the effort died — the high-water mark of an abandoned rollout, not a regression.

A CORRECTION WORTH KEEPING: I had framed remove-from-two as the cheap alternative to
add-to-three. Wrong. A schematic change is a schematic change in BOTH directions — new
installer image, talosctl upgrade, reboot. Removing costs 2 REBOOTS, not a git edit. Neither
direction buys anything today, so the answer is ZERO reboots.

THE TIEBREAKER: TALOS-1ujn (Longhorn) would need it back FLEET-WIDE — Longhorn on Talos
requires siderolabs/iscsi-tools AND siderolabs/util-linux-tools on EVERY node, verified against
Longhorn's docs. Removing now means paying for talos01 and talos03 twice. The extensions stay,
inert and deliberate, and the fleet-wide rollout folds into 1ujn where a real consumer
justifies the reboots and both land in one pass.

Reason recorded in configs/talconfig.yaml (e389b056, comment-only, regenerated output
byte-identical, fleet still at 0). The file's own header names this exact failure mode —
'on some nodes and not others with nothing in git explaining why' — and that gap is now closed
with an explicit do-not-tidy-this-up warning.

FOLLOW-UP, not done: docs/05-runbooks/talos-kubelet-iscsi-patch.yaml still describes itself as
being for Democratic-CSI TrueNAS provisioning. Its content is absorbed into
configs/patches/all-kubelet-baseline.yaml and its rationale is dead. Delete in whichever pass
owns runbook cleanup.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
UPDATE 2026-08-24 — the install.image half of this is DONE.

All five nodes now carry the correct installer at v1.13.9, each with its own factory schematic where it has one. The v1.11.1 pins on talos02-gpu and talos06 are gone. talos06's install.wipe: true (against a 1.0 TB NVMe) was also fixed — that was the genuine data-loss risk in the original finding.

STILL OPEN — the actual subject of this ticket: talos00, talos02-gpu and talos06 still lack siderolabs/iscsi-tools and therefore still cannot attach Democratic-CSI volumes. Confirm intent for talos00 first (it is the RAM-limited node); if the extension is not wanted there, correct git rather than the node.

Unrelated correction for anyone reading the epic: this ticket's sibling TALOS-dnfy carried a false claim that talos00's /dev/sda is a 1 GB USB stick. It is a 266 GB virtio disk and the config is correct. See the comment on TALOS-dnfy.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
VERIFIED 2026-08-24 — the drift this ticket describes NO LONGER EXISTS, and the fix it proposes is not warranted.

CURRENT STATE (live, all five nodes):
  talos00      stock ghcr installer, no extensions
  talos01      iscsi-tools
  talos02-gpu  i915, intel-ucode
  talos03      amd-ucode, amdgpu, iscsi-tools
  talos06      intel-ucode, i915, mei

All five MATCH talconfig.yaml exactly. Proven two ways: generated install image ==
live install image per node (incl. schematic hash), and verify-diff.py reports 0
differences fleet-wide. The talhelper migration resolved the drift by converging git
DOWNWARD onto the nodes. The old schematic JSONs the ticket compared against are gone.

IS iSCSI USED? No. Zero CSIDrivers in the cluster, no iSCSI StorageClass (only
local-path, fatboy-nfs-appdata, synology-nfs), no iSCSI PV, no pod with an iSCSI
volume, and /var/lib/iscsi holds no node or session records on talos01 or talos03 —
the only two nodes with the tooling. iSCSI has never attached a volume here.

WHY THE ASYMMETRY: iscsi-tools was added 2026-01-16 for Democratic-CSI Synology iSCSI.
That effort was never wired into a Flux Kustomization, never ran, and its last artifact
was deleted 2026-08-09 as an abandoned orphan leaking a DSM credential (TALOS-rpyc). It
reached two of five nodes before the effort died. This is the high-water mark of an
abandoned rollout, not a regression.

COST OF EITHER CONVERGENCE: a schematic change means a new installer image, so it is
'talosctl upgrade' + REBOOT per node, NOT a config apply. Adding to the three = 3
reboots. Removing from the two = 2 reboots. Both buy nothing today.

RECOMMENDATION: leave the nodes alone; do not converge in either direction. Do NOT
remove it either — TALOS-1ujn (NVMe block storage, evaluating Longhorn) needs it back
fleet-wide: Longhorn on Talos requires siderolabs/iscsi-tools AND
siderolabs/util-linux-tools on EVERY node. Fold the fleet-wide rollout into that work,
where a real consumer justifies the reboots and both extensions land in one pass.

DONE: e389b056 records this reasoning in talconfig.yaml (comment-only; regenerated
output byte-identical, fleet still at 0 drift). No nodes touched.

Proposed disposition: close as 'converged — declared state now matches live, no reboots
warranted', with the extension rollout tracked under TALOS-1ujn. Leaving status to the
owner since the acceptance criteria as written are obsoleted rather than met.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
RESOLVED 2026-08-24 — closing as converged, with iscsi-tools KEPT.

Decision taken by the user directly: 'keep the iscsi stuff, it will be used at some
point.' Recorded in configs/talconfig.yaml (commit 8d8ef908) as a settled decision
rather than as analysis, so the asymmetry does not get reopened and 'tidied up' by a
future reader.

Why this closes rather than staying open:
  - The drift this ticket was filed for NO LONGER EXISTS. All five nodes match
    talconfig exactly (generated install image == live install image per node; verify-
    diff.py = 0 differences fleet-wide). The talhelper migration resolved it.
  - The asymmetry is now EXPLAINED and DECLARATIVE in git, which was the actual ask —
    the ticket's own framing was 'iscsi-tools is on some nodes and not others with
    nothing in git explaining why.' That is fixed.
  - No reboots were performed or are warranted. Converging in either direction costs a
    talosctl upgrade + reboot per node (3 to add, 2 to remove) and buys nothing today.

The acceptance criteria as written are OBSOLETED rather than met — 'all drifted nodes
upgraded' and 'Democratic-CSI iSCSI volume attach verified' both presuppose a
Democratic-CSI deployment that was abandoned and deleted (TALOS-rpyc). There is nothing
