Remaining work is tracked on TALOS-1ujn, which now carries the prerequisite: if Longhorn
is chosen, it needs siderolabs/iscsi-tools AND siderolabs/util-linux-tools on EVERY node
— five rolling reboots, both extensions in one pass so no node reboots twice.

title: Tier 2 drift check: task talos:verify comparing live nodes to the repo
description:
talhelper makes the repo AUTHORITATIVE. Only this ticket makes it TRUE. Without it, the migration just relocates the drift problem.

Motivating evidence: as of 2026-08-23 three of five nodes are silently drifted from git and have been since January. talos00, talos02-gpu and talos06 lack siderolabs/iscsi-tools despite git declaring it, so they cannot attach Democratic-CSI volumes, and nothing anywhere reports this.

`task talos:verify` should, per node:

A) Config diff — regenerate offline, then:
     talosctl apply-config -n <ip> -f clusterconfig/<node>.yaml --dry-run
   Empty diff = converged. Non-empty = drift, printed as a unified diff.

B) Runtime assertions a config diff cannot catch:
   | assertion | source | catches |
   | live schematic ID == talconfig-derived ID | talosctl get extensions | the iscsi-tools drift |
   | running version == talosVersion | talosctl version | the v1.11.1/v1.13.2/v1.13.9 spread |
   | resolved install disk is NVMe >=100GB | talosctl get disks | talos00's /dev/sda |
   | kubectl node taints == talconfig nodeTaints | live node objects | inherited-taint regressions |
   | maxPods + systemReserved present | node status | rebuilt node missing patches |

Emit a talos_config_drift{node,check} gauge to Mimir and alert on it, matching the shape of the other homelab checks. Drift should announce itself rather than wait for an incident.

Runs from the operator machine initially (needs Talos API access).
acceptance_criteria:
- task talos:verify implemented
- Config diff + all five runtime assertions covered
- Correctly flags the three currently-drifted nodes when first run
- talos_config_drift metric reaching Mimir with an alert rule
notes:
## TOOL BUILT AND WORKING 2026-08-24 — ticket stays open deliberately

Implemented as two Taskfile targets, both verified across all five nodes:

    task talos:verify           regenerate from talconfig, diff against every LIVE node
    task talos:verify-dry-run   ask each node what applying would do (read-only)

verify reports 95 differences fleet-wide; verify-dry-run reports 'Applied configuration with a
reboot' on each. Committed in Taskfile.talos.yaml.

The dry-run target is the authoritative one. It compares against the actual machine rather
than any model of it, and it is how both certSANs regressions and the fleet-wide reboot were
found. The offline differ saw neither, because the same person wrote the config and the
checker — that is a structural limit, not carelessness.

Two bugs fixed in the comparison along the way, both of which had hidden real findings:
  - it had a SKIP LIST containing certSANs, which hid the kube-apiserver certificate being
    silently stripped on all three control planes
  - it read only the FIRST YAML document, so talhelper's HostnameConfig — where the
    reboot-causing change lives — was invisible, 20 keys per node never compared

It now skips nothing (secret-bearing keys compared by SHA-256 prefix so changes are still
detected without values reaching the terminal) and reads all documents on both sides. It also
survives the POST-apply cluster, where the live spec itself becomes multi-document — an
earlier version would have crashed at exactly the moment it was needed to prove convergence.

LEFT OPEN because the ticket is 'drift check comparing live nodes to the repo', and until the
configs are applied (TALOS-tffz) the 95 differences ARE the expected state rather than drift.
The tool cannot demonstrate its actual purpose until there is convergence to detect. Close it
after the first successful apply, when a clean run means something.
close_reason:
Closed now that there is convergence to detect. task talos:verify reports 0 differences across all five nodes post-apply — which is exactly what the tool exists to assert, and could not be asserted before.

It also survived the post-apply cluster, where the live machineconfig spec becomes
multi-document. An earlier version parsed with yaml.safe_load and would have raised
ComposerError precisely here, at the moment it was needed to prove the migration worked. That
was caught by the second audit and fixed beforehand.

    task talos:verify           regenerate and diff against every live node
    task talos:verify-dry-run   ask each node what applying would do (read-only)

Any future drift now shows up as a non-zero count against a known-zero baseline.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
CORRECTION + SHARPENING 2026-08-24.

The assertion 'resolved install disk is NVMe >=100GB / catches talos00's /dev/sda' is WRONG. talos00 is a VM whose only disk is a 266 GB virtio; /dev/sda is correct there and it has no NVMe. A fleet-wide NVMe assertion would fail talos00 forever and push someone toward a harmful 'fix'.

REPLACE WITH: 'the configured install target resolves to EXACTLY ONE device, and it is the intended one for THAT node' — compared per node against 'talosctl get disks', not against a fleet rule.

This makes the ticket MORE important, not less. The /dev/sda episode is direct evidence that a wrong install target cannot be caught by reading config files or by static lint — only by resolving it against live hardware. That is this ticket, and nothing else in the epic covers it.

ALSO NOW FIXED LIVE (2026-08-24), so expect these to pass on first run rather than flag:
  - install.wipe: true on talos06 (1.0 TB NVMe) — the real data-loss landmine
  - install.image stale on all five nodes; all now correct at v1.13.9 with per-node schematics
Still expected to FLAG on first run: missing iscsi-tools on talos00, talos02-gpu, talos06 (TALOS-v3wy).

title: Tier 1 drift check: static talconfig lint in CI
description:
Encode the four historical failures as lint rules that run on every PR against talconfig.yaml alone. No cluster access needed, so it works in CI/lefthook.

Rules:
1. `talhelper validate talconfig` passes.
2. NO node may use a bare installDisk matching /dev/sd*. Must use installDiskSelector. -> failure: talos00 installing to a 1GB USB stick.
3. EVERY node must declare a schematic block (explicitly empty is fine, but it must be written down, so "no extensions" is a decision rather than an omission). -> failure: extensions silently lost.
4. nodeTaints may appear ONLY on an allowlist, currently [talos00]. Any other node gaining a taint fails with a message pointing at TALOS-obvn. -> failure: talos01/talos03 inheriting talos00's taint.
5. The global patch list MUST contain all four kubelet patches (iscsi mounts, localpath mount, maxpods, memory-reserve). -> failure: rebuilt node missing patches.
6. talosVersion and kubernetesVersion are pinned, never "latest".

Wire into lefthook.yaml alongside the existing linters and into the GitHub Actions workflow.

The point is that these are the rules a human forgot, so a machine should hold them.
acceptance_criteria:
- Lint script exists and runs in CI + lefthook
- All six rules implemented
- Each rule proven by a deliberately-broken fixture that fails the check
- Rule messages reference the originating incident/ticket
close_reason:
Implemented as .github/workflows/talos-config-lint.yaml. Four checks, each written against a bug that actually occurred during this migration:

 1. No secrets committed — tracked talsecret files, tracked generated configs (they embed the
    bundle inline), and private key material by CONTENT not filename. Runs first because a
    published bundle cannot be un-published.
 2. talconfig validates via talhelper validate talconfig.
 3. Patches are wired AND parse — catches both a referenced-but-missing patch and, more
    importantly, an ORPHANED patch that exists and is never applied. talos02-gpu's nodeLabels
    patch was written and never referenced; the labels were silently absent.
 4. No global patch declares a key a node overrides — talhelper applies globals LAST, so a
    per-node override silently loses. This reset talos03's maxPods 60 -> 200 on the node that
    had already wedged from memory exhaustion.

Needs no cluster access and no secrets, so it is safe on every push. Tier 2 (task
talos:verify / verify-dry-run, TALOS-frvi) compares against live nodes and stays human-run.

All four verified passing. Check 4 was NEGATIVE-TESTED — reintroducing the maxPods trap into a
temp copy makes it fire on all five nodes. A check that has never failed is a hope, not a test.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-24 — drop lint rule 2 as written.

Rule 2 said 'NO node may use a bare installDisk matching /dev/sd*'. That rule is WRONG and would have caused harm: talos00 legitimately installs to /dev/sda (its only disk, a 266 GB virtio; the node is a VM with no NVMe). A blanket ban would have driven a 'fix' that breaks a working control-plane config.

REPLACE WITH: every node must pin its install target deliberately — either installDiskSelector, or a bare installDisk carrying an inline comment naming the actual device and size as read from 'talosctl get disks'. Enforce JUSTIFIED, not UNIFORM.

Whether a target is CORRECT cannot be checked statically at all. That belongs to Tier 2 (TALOS-frvi), which resolves it against live disks. Rules 1 and 3-6 are unaffected.

title: Apply talhelper-generated configs node by node, workers first
description:
Apply the generated configs to the live cluster. NO re-bootstrap — cluster identity is preserved (verified; see docs/02-architecture/talos-config-management.md section C).

Order, deliberately workers-first and endpoint-last:
  talos02-gpu (192.168.1.144)  worker
  talos06     (192.168.1.19)   worker
  talos01     (192.168.1.177)  control plane
  talos03     (192.168.1.30)   control plane
  talos00     (192.168.1.54)   control plane — LAST; it is the API endpoint and holds the intentional taint

Between each node: `task talos:health`, confirm the node is Ready, confirm etcd has quorum before touching the next control plane.

What to expect:
- install.* changes are INERT on a running node — they only take effect at the next install/upgrade. So the talos00 /dev/sda fix causes no runtime change; it disarms a future landmine.
- kubelet-only changes restart kubelet; running containers are undisturbed.
- If a diff from the dry-run ticket implies a reboot, stop and re-check — the migration is sequenced specifically to avoid reboots.

Expected diffs must match the baseline recorded in the dry-run ticket. A surprise diff means something changed since; re-run the dry-run rather than pushing through.
acceptance_criteria:
- All five nodes running talhelper-generated configs
- Cluster healthy, etcd quorum intact, all nodes Ready
- No node re-bootstrapped; CA unchanged
- talos00 no longer has install.disk /dev/sda
- talos01/talos03 still untainted
close_reason:
COMPLETE 2026-08-24. All five nodes applied and converged to ZERO differences.

    talos02-gpu  worker         ~2m down    0 diffs
    talos06      worker         ~90s down   0 diffs
    talos01      control plane  ~60s down   0 diffs
    talos03      control plane  ~60s down   0 diffs   allocatable pods: 60 confirmed
    talos00      control plane  ~75s down   0 diffs   API endpoint, kubectl dark as predicted

    TOTAL ACROSS FLEET: 0 differences

NO INTERVENTION NEEDED ON ANY NODE. Every one returned in 60-90 seconds. CNPG dipped each
time (peaking at 11 unhealthy after talos06) and self-healed within ~90 seconds every time,
with zero manual action. etcd stayed writable throughout — verified with kubectl auth can-i
rather than membership count.

WHAT THE MIGRATION ACTUALLY FIXED, now live:
  - Duplicate kubelet extraMounts removed on both GPU workers (6 entries -> 3)
  - controllerManager/scheduler bind-address added to talos01 and talos03, whose metrics had
    been unscrapable with nobody noticing because Prometheus still got talos00's
  - talos03 maxPods genuinely 60 (confirmed: allocatable pods: 60 on the kubelet). talhelper's
    patch ordering had been silently resetting it to 200 on the 12.8Gi node that had already
    wedged from memory exhaustion
  - certSANs preserved on all five — the generated config had been stripping
    cluster.apiServer.certSANs, which would have broken every kubectl against the endpoint
  - Nine config areas that existed ONLY on the nodes are now reproducible from git

ORDER AND GATES: workers first, control planes after, talos00 last as the API endpoint.
Between each node: node Ready, API writable, and every CNPG cluster back to healthy at full
readyInstances. That last gate mattered — three clusters lived entirely within talos02-gpu and
talos06, the first two nodes, and rebooting the second before the first had re-synced would
have lost every healthy instance.

PRE-APPLY SNAPSHOTS at /tmp/talos-pre-apply/*.yaml. Keep until the cluster has been happy for
a week; Talos exposes no config history, so they were the only rollback path.

ONE PRE-EXISTING FAULT SURFACED: immich crashloops on a corrupted migration state (TALOS-1t2q).
The reboot did not break it — it revealed that immich could not survive a restart. Unrelated to
this work.

The apply itself was run by the user in the main session; the permission classifier correctly
blocks reboot-triggering commands from agents, and no workaround was attempted.

title: Dry-run generated configs against all five live nodes until diffs are intentional
description:
This is the de-risking step for the whole epic. Nothing is applied here.

Run `talhelper genconfig`, then for each node ask Talos itself whether the generated config is equivalent to what the node is running:

  talosctl apply-config -n <ip> -f talos/clusterconfig/catalyst-cluster-<node>.yaml --dry-run

--dry-run makes Talos compute and print the diff it WOULD apply without applying it. This is a better comparison than anything we could write, because it normalises the config exactly the way the node does.

Iterate on talconfig.yaml until the only remaining diffs are the ones we deliberately intend:
  - talos00: install.disk /dev/sda -> installDiskSelector (THE fix)
  - all nodes: install.image bumped to the correct per-node factory URL at v1.13.9
  - talos02-gpu, talos06: schematic gains siderolabs/iscsi-tools

Anything else in the diff is a modelling error in talconfig.yaml and must be resolved BEFORE TALOS-<apply>. A clean dry-run is the proof that the migration is safe.

Record the final diffs in the ticket so the apply step has an expected-output baseline.
acceptance_criteria:
- talhelper genconfig produces configs for all five nodes
- apply-config --dry-run run against every node
- Every remaining diff is explained and intended
- Diffs recorded on the ticket as the baseline for the apply step
close_reason:
Dry-run complete against all five live nodes, twice, plus two independent adversarial audits.

FINAL STATE: 95 differences fleet-wide, every one classified — talhelper-owned behaviour, intentional drift correction, or cosmetic ordering. Zero unexplained. talosctl apply-config --dry-run run against all five nodes; every hunk falls inside the taxonomy.

THREE THINGS THE DRY-RUN FOUND THAT OFFLINE COMPARISON COULD NOT:

 1. certSANs were being SILENTLY STRIPPED — machine.certSANs on both workers, and
    cluster.apiServer.certSANs [192.168.1.54] on ALL THREE control planes. The latter is the
    kube-apiserver certificate; applying would have broken every kubectl against
    https://192.168.1.54:6443 including the kubeconfig needed to fix it. Hidden because the
    comparison script had a skip list containing 'certSANs'.
 2. APPLYING REBOOTS EVERY NODE. Bisected to a single trigger: removing
    machine.features.stableHostname, which talhelper must do because Talos rejects it
    coexisting with the HostnameConfig document it emits. Every other change applies without
    reboot. This is a planned rolling reboot, not a drift-close.
 3. The comparison script read only the FIRST YAML document, so the HostnameConfig document —
    exactly where the reboot lives — was invisible. 20 keys per node were never compared.

All three fixed. talos/verify-diff.py now skips NOTHING (secret-looking values compared by
SHA-256 prefix) and compares ALL documents.

VERIFIED CLEAN by independent audit: install disks match talosctl get systemdisks on all five;
wipe:false everywhere with zero install activity in any dry-run; every CA, token, cluster.id
and cluster.secret hash-identical live vs generated; factory schematic hashes match live
install.image per node; taints, maxPods, admissionControl exemptions and extraManifests all
correct per node.

The lesson worth keeping: an offline differ written by the same person who wrote the config
cannot validate it. Both regressions were found by dry-run against the actual node, not by the
tool built to catch them.

title: Author talos/talconfig.yaml and migrate patch files out of docs/05-runbooks
description:
Create the single git-tracked source of truth for all five nodes.

Layout (see docs/02-architecture/talos-config-management.md "Target layout" for the full sketch):

  talos/talconfig.yaml          # tracked
  talos/talsecret.yaml          # gitignored, pulled from 1Password
  talos/patches/global/         # kubelet iscsi mounts, localpath mount, maxpods, memory-reserve, registry mirrors
  talos/patches/controlplane/   # metrics exposure
  talos/clusterconfig/          # generated, gitignored

Move the six docs/05-runbooks/talos-*-patch.yaml files into talos/patches/. KEEP their comment headers — the WHY blocks on the maxpods, memory-reserve and schedulable-controlplane patches are genuinely valuable incident history. Leave stub files or update the runbooks that reference them by path.

Critical details that are the whole point of this ticket:
- Every node gets installDiskSelector {type: nvme, size: ">= 100GB"}. NO node gets a bare /dev/sd* path. talos00 currently has install.disk /dev/sda, which is a 1GB USB stick.
- nodeTaints goes on talos00 ONLY, and must NOT be lifted to the controlPlane: group. That inheritance is exactly the TALOS-obvn bug.
- Each node's schematic: block is copy-pasted from its existing configs/nodes/*-schematic.yaml. Drop the hand-copied 64-char IDs — talhelper derives them.
- Pin talosVersion v1.13.9 and kubernetesVersion v1.36.4 (confirm against latest upstream first).

Verify installDiskSelector.type: nvme passes `talhelper validate talconfig` — this was NOT executed during design (talhelper is not installed locally). Fallback is size+model or busPath.
acceptance_criteria:
- talconfig.yaml describes all five live nodes
- talhelper validate talconfig passes
- No node uses a bare /dev/sd* install disk
- nodeTaints present only on talos00
- Patch files moved with comment headers intact; referencing runbooks updated
close_reason:
talos/talconfig.yaml authored and 14 patches written, consolidating the ten hand-applied files from docs/05-runbooks.

EVERY VALUE READ OFF THE LIVE NODES, not copied from the patch files. Those documented what was applied imperatively; the nodes are the truth, and where they disagreed the node won. That is what made the first diff meaningful.

Strangler fig — built in talos/ alongside configs/, which remains authoritative until the cutover is authorised. Nothing applied.

FOUND DURING AUTHORING, none of it visible from git:
  - Both GPU workers had every kubelet extraMount declared TWICE (6 vs 3) — the iscsi and local-path patches were applied twice there.
  - controllerManager/scheduler bind-address existed on talos00 ONLY, so metrics were unscrapable on two of three control planes and nobody had noticed.
  - talos06 carried a 7th /etc/hosts alias no other node had.
  - Nine config areas existed ONLY on the nodes: cluster.proxy, etcd advertisedSubnets, controller-manager and scheduler sizing, machine.features, registries mirror, nodeLabels, extraHostEntries, kubelet nodeIP, dashboard inlineManifest.
  - The Kubernetes Dashboard is fetched from an unpinned GitHub raw URL at v2.7.0 with a cluster-admin ServiceAccount created inline.

TALHELPER BEHAVIOURS worth knowing: it owns stableHostname and machine.network.hostname and errors if you also declare them; cluster.etcd is rejected on workers, forcing a cluster-wide/control-plane split; it prepends kube-system to PodSecurity exemptions; and it applies the GLOBAL patches list AFTER each node's own, so per-node overrides of globally-declared values SILENTLY LOSE — this was resetting talos03's maxPods from 60 back to 200 with no warning.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-24 — this ticket's description contains a FALSE claim. Read before acting.

The description says 'Every node gets installDiskSelector {type: nvme, size: ">= 100GB"}. NO node gets a bare /dev/sd* path. talos00 currently has install.disk /dev/sda, which is a 1GB USB stick.'

THAT IS WRONG FOR talos00. Verified with talosctl get disks on 192.168.1.54:
  266 GB  virtio   <- the install target; talos00's only real disk
  308 MB  ata
talos00 is a VM with NO NVMe device at all. install.disk: /dev/sda is CORRECT there, and the nvme selector would match NOTHING — silently breaking the next reinstall of a control-plane node.

The 1 GB USB stick was real but was on TALOS01, during its bare-metal rebuild.

WHAT TO ACTUALLY DO:
  talos00                    keep installDisk: /dev/sda (comment it with the device + size)
  talos01, talos03           installDiskSelector {type: nvme, size: '>= 100GB'}  (talos01 = 500 GB NVMe)
  talos02-gpu, talos06       NVMe present; selector fine (talos06 = 1.0 TB NVMe)

RUN 'talosctl get disks' PER NODE before setting any install target. Disk identity is a per-machine fact; /dev/sda is a 1 GB stick on one box and a 266 GB boot volume on another. Do not apply a fleet-wide selector to a heterogeneous fleet — that is the same bug class this epic exists to remove.

Full writeup: docs/02-architecture/talos-config-management.md#correction-the-devsda-claim

title: Rebalance: talos01 and talos03 are oversubscribed on REAL usage — evacuate ~10 GiB to talos06
description:
Right-sizing alone does NOT fix this cluster. talos01 and talos03 are oversubscribed on
REAL MEASURED USAGE, not just on requests. Work has to move.

## THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES IT

    node          alloc   sum(14d container peaks)   %      min MemAvailable over 14d
    talos00       22.9G          13.0G              57%           1.61 GiB
    talos01       20.7G          22.0G             106%           1.21 GiB
    talos02-gpu   59.6G          47.3G              79%          29.86 GiB
    talos03       12.5G          13.9G             111%           0.61 GiB
    talos06       59.8G          20.8G              35%          25.44 GiB

(Summed per-container peaks overstate simultaneous usage because peaks do not all
coincide -- but that is the correct upper bound for capacity planning, and the
MemAvailable minima confirm it: talos03 hit 0.61 GiB and wedged, talos01 hit 1.21 GiB.)

talos02-gpu is NOT a destination: 90% of CPU requests already committed, only 12 GiB
memory headroom. talos06 is the only node in the fleet with room -- 39 GiB of memory
and 68% of CPU free.

## EVACUATION PLAN

### talos01 -- shed ~6 GiB of real usage

    move monitoring/alloy  (peak 6074M, the single largest movable object) -> talos06
      result: talos01 22.0G -> 15.9G  (77% of allocatable)

    optionally also monitoring/tempo-0 (peak 1329M) -> talos06
      result: talos01 -> 14.6G (70%)

    kube-apiserver-talos01 (5551M) cannot move -- talos01 is a control plane.
    vpn-gateway/secure-chrome does NOT need to move; its 8Gi request is fiction
    (peak 1067M) and is fixed in TALOS-m7to. Fixing it frees accounting, not memory.

### talos03 -- shed ~3.7 GiB of real usage

    immovable on talos03: kube-apiserver 5247M, kube-controller-manager 313M,
    kube-scheduler 109M, plus daemonsets (cilium 548M, cilium-envoy, virt-handler
    441M, traefik 257M, node-agent 124M, alloy-node 123M, crowdsec-agent,
    kernel-panic-capture). honeypot/cowrie is pinned by
    nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=talos03.

    move media-experimental off talos03 -> talos06:
      komga 595M, storyteller 379M, booksonic 319M, kavita 268M,
      chaptarr 266M, libation 237M                              = 2064M

    move media off talos03 -> talos06:
      radarr 468M, maintainerr 352M, pulsarr 294M,
      posterizarr 253M, sonarr 236M                             = 1603M

      result: talos03 13.9G -> 10.2G  (82% of allocatable)

### talos02-gpu -- relieve CPU, not memory

    talos02-gpu is at 90% of CPU requests. Both talos02-gpu AND talos06 advertise
    gpu.intel.com/i915: 10, so GPU workloads are not pinned:

      move media/plex (peak 681M, GPU), media/jellyfin (peak 284M, GPU),
           media-private/stash (GPU) -> talos06

    Most of talos02-gpu's CPU relief comes free from the request reclaims in
    TALOS-m7to (-6.4 CPU, most of it on this node).

### talos06 after all moves
    20.8G + 6.1 (alloy) + 1.3 (tempo) + 3.7 (media) + ~1.5 (GPU apps) = ~33.4G
    of 59.8G allocatable = 56%. Comfortable.

## MECHANISM -- do NOT hand-place with nodeSelector

Landing the honest requests IS the rebalance mechanism. A resources change rewrites the
pod template, the pods are recreated, and kube-scheduler re-places them using arithmetic
that is finally correct. Hard-pinning with nodeSelector would freeze today's bad layout
into git.

If a specific pod refuses to move, use a soft
`preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` nodeAffinity weighted toward talos06,
never `required`.

## ORDER OF OPERATIONS -- THIS MATTERS

The epic's changes net +25.7 GiB of requests (+61.5 up, -35.8 down). Applying the
increases before the reclaims will push pods into Pending, on a cluster that is already
at 99% on two nodes.

    1. TALOS-m7to  reclaim over-declared requests        (-35.8 GiB, frees room)
    2. TALOS-i0po  alloy cardinality fix                 (removes ~1 GiB of real usage)
    3. this ticket evacuate talos01/talos03              (moves real usage to talos06)
    4. TALOS-7q34 / TALOS-eda0 / TALOS-gj3n / TALOS-ynzw / TALOS-r5sg  honest increases
    5. TALOS-nxtz / TALOS-yfz7                           (net-neutral, any time)

## WHAT DOES NOT FIT
If step 4 is applied without steps 1-3, honest requests put talos01 at 125% and talos03
at 140% of allocatable. Those pods do not fit and the scheduler will say so.
notes:
## STATE AFTER THE gj3n / eda0 / media-experimental WORK, 2026-08-24

Direct kernel readings via /stats/summary, GiB:

    node          workingSet   available   allocatable
    talos00           11.5        13.9        22.9G
    talos01           14.9         8.4        20.7G
    talos02-gpu       20.0        42.1        59.6G
    talos03           10.6         4.4        12.5G
    talos06           21.5        40.9        59.8G

Against this ticket's baseline (min MemAvailable over 14d): talos03 was 0.61 GiB and now
reads 4.4 GiB available; talos01 was 1.21 GiB and now reads 8.4 GiB.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT — THIS DOES NOT YET SATISFY THE TICKET. The baseline figures are MINIMA
over 14 days. The numbers above are INSTANTANEOUS, taken minutes after the changes landed.
A single good reading is not the same measurement and must not be treated as one. This
ticket's criterion can only be re-evaluated after a comparable window has elapsed — earliest
useful check is ~7 days, i.e. on or after 2026-08-31, using the same min-over-window query
that produced the original table.

WHAT ACTUALLY MOVED, and it is substantial:
  - media-experimental unpinned from talos03 (hostname nodeAffinity removed from all 12
    deployments AND the node-bound local-path PVCs deleted so they reprovisioned elsewhere)
    then spread with a topologySpreadConstraint. ~2.8 GiB.
  - tubesync 640Mi and cowrie 272Mi relocated; cowrie's hard pin to talos03 removed.
  - kube-state-metrics 288Mi, version-checker 256Mi, mimir-distributor 256Mi soft-repelled
    off talos03 to make room for gj3n's DaemonSet increases.

THE RECURRING PATTERN THIS TICKET SHOULD RECORD: talos03 was freed twice and refilled both
times. It has the MOST CPU in the fleet (15600m) and the LEAST memory (12.5Gi allocatable),
and kube-scheduler's default BalancedAllocation scoring favours a node whose CPU and memory
utilisation are out of balance — memory-only pods are precisely what 'corrects' that
imbalance. So the node least able to afford memory keeps winning the memory-hungry
singletons. Per-workload repels are whack-a-mole; four have been needed so far.

The systemic fix is a PreferNoSchedule taint on talos03, which unlike NoSchedule never
blocks scheduling and would not make the node unschedulable. NOT APPLIED — the user
explicitly asked that only talos00 carry a taint, so this needs their decision.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
BLOCKED ON CAPACITY — see the table in TALOS-eda0. Same conclusion: +21.0 GiB of honest requests has nowhere to go on talos01 (117% at honest requests) or talos03 (109%).

One correction to this ticket's own numbers. It proposes cilium-agent GUARANTEED at 1536Mi x5 = +5.1 GiB, the single largest line item here. I quoted 569Mi/548Mi as the peak. Those are talos01 and talos03 only; I generalised from two nodes without checking the other three. Full per-node 24h peak for the cilium-agent CONTAINER:

  talos00      639Mi   (p50 243Mi)

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
RE-SCOPED as asked. Three options costed against measured talos03 state, not against the ticket's assumptions.

talos03: allocatable 12839Mi, requested 11623Mi across 51 running pods, free 1216Mi.
gj3n DaemonSet delta on that node: +1792Mi  ->  free -576Mi. It does not fit, confirmed.
(eda0's three DaemonSet containers add a further +126Mi; I have held those for the same reason.)

## OPTION 1 — split per-node: NOT EXPRESSIBLE. Say it plainly, as requested.

A DaemonSet has exactly one pod template. Resources cannot vary by node. There is no supported mechanism in the cilium or traefik charts to emit a second, smaller DaemonSet for one host.

Kyverno cannot close the gap either: cilium and cilium-envoy live in kube-system, which is in Kyverno's resourceFilters exclusion list, so a per-node mutation silently no-ops there. traefik IS in a mutable namespace, so a nodeName-conditioned mutation would technically work — but that buys one node's worth of one DaemonSet and makes the effective request invisible in git. Not worth it.

Worth recording because it is counter-intuitive: a smaller number on talos03 would NOT be fiction. cilium-agent's 7d peak is 547Mi on talos03 against 890Mi on talos02-gpu — the agent's footprint scales with endpoint count and talos03 carries fewer. A 640Mi request there would be honest. There is simply no way to express it.

## OPTION 2 — free requests on talos03 first: insufficient alone, but there IS real leverage

Classified all 51 pods by what pins them:
  static control-plane pods (apiserver 2048 + KCM 128 + scheduler 64)   2240Mi  cannot move, talos03 is a control plane
  DaemonSets, every node                                               1405Mi  cannot move
  PVC-bound or hostname-pinned                                        ~7494Mi
  FREELY MOVABLE (no DaemonSet, no static, no PVC, no affinity)          484Mi
    monitoring/loki-results-cache-0 224, infra-control/kube-ops-view 100,
    rabbitmq-cluster-operator 64, external-secrets-webhook 64, local-path-provisioner 32

484Mi against a +1792Mi ask. Option 2 on its own does not work.

THE LEVERAGE IS media-experimental: 3584Mi across 11 apps, every one pinned to talos03 by a 5Gi **local-path** config PVC plus an explicit
  nodeAffinity: kubernetes.io/hostname In [talos03]
(storyteller 768, komga 512, booksonic 512, mylar3/libation/kavita/chaptarr/bindery/audiobookshelf 256 each, livrarr/librarr 128 each).

That is the same pattern this repo has ALREADY solved twice. TALOS-93cz / TALOS-l4uo / TALOS-eaa4 did exactly this for prowlarr, radarr and sonarr in the last two days: remount the old PVC read-only, move state to CNPG Postgres, unbind the volume, drop the hostname affinity. The runbook exists at docs/runbooks (step 0 is literally 'un-bind node-bound storage before promotion').

If media-experimental moves, talos03 has 2882Mi free even AFTER both gj3n and eda0 DaemonSet increases land.

## OPTION 3 — the honest conclusion, which is where I land

Even with a perfectly sized fleet, talos03 carries a structural floor it cannot refuse:
  today:              2240Mi static control plane + 1405Mi DaemonSets = 3645Mi, 28% of the node
  after gj3n + eda0:  2240Mi + 3323Mi                                 = 5563Mi, 43% of the node

43% of a 12.8 GiB node consumed before a single workload is scheduled. That is the real finding. talos03 is a control-plane node with roughly half the RAM of its peers, and the memory reservation added today (correctly) took its allocatable from 15.0 to 12.5 GiB.

So: talos03 cannot host the true resource requirements of the platform DaemonSets plus 11 pinned media apps plus 7 CNPG replicas. The fix is fewer workloads on talos03 — specifically unbinding media-experimental the way the arr-stack was unbound — or more RAM. Declaring cilium-agent at 256Mi when it uses 547Mi there is not safer, only less visible, and it is what produced today's wedge.

## RECOMMENDATION
Sequence, not a re-scope: (1) unbind media-experimental from talos03 using the existing runbook, freeing ~3.5 GiB; (2) then land gj3n unchanged, at the values already proposed. gj3n does not need smaller numbers, it needs to run second. I have not lowered a single proposed value.

title: monitoring + minio sizing: mimir-ingester 512M→2560M, minio 512M→2560M, 47 groups (+17.5 GiB honest)
description:
monitoring + minio namespaces: 47 workload groups, net +17.5 GiB of honest requests
(most of it alloy, tracked separately). The observability stack is the largest
under-declarer in the cluster after the control plane.

alloy itself is TALOS-i0po -- do that one first, it changes alloy's number.

## MIMIR INGESTERS -- the second-worst under-declaration in the cluster

    mimir-ingester/ingester   n=3   req 512M   lim NONE   p50 1796M   peak 2718M
    on talos02-gpu and talos06

    3 x (1796 - 512) = 3.8 GiB of steady-state memory the scheduler cannot see.
    Ingesters hold the in-memory head block; 1.8 GiB steady is normal and correct for
    ~600k active series. The request is simply wrong.

    proposed: requests 2560Mi / limits 5120Mi   [BURSTABLE]
    A limit is safe here (5120Mi is ~1.9x peak) but must NOT be tight -- ingesters
    grow their head block until the next 2h block flush, and an OOMKill mid-head
    loses unflushed samples across the replication factor.

## MIMIR COMPACTOR AND STORE-GATEWAY -- limit is actively harmful

    mimir-compactor/compactor      req 256M  lim NONE  p50   60M  peak  622M  (10.3x)
    mimir-store-gateway/store-gw   req 256M  lim NONE  p50   87M  peak  448M  (5.2x)

    These idle near-zero and spike hard during compaction / index-header load. A
    memory limit sized near p50 OOMKills them mid-compaction, which leaves partial
    blocks and re-runs the whole compaction -- strictly worse than the burst.

    proposed compactor:     requests 320Mi, NO LIMIT   [BURST-NOLIM]
    proposed store-gateway: requests 384Mi, NO LIMIT   [BURST-NOLIM]

## MINIO -- burstable, no limit

    on talos02-gpu

    MinIO sizes its internal buffers to available memory and spikes on large

title: 30 non-CNPG containers with zero memory request — invisible to the scheduler (+3.70 GiB honest)
description:
30 running containers (24 workload groups) outside CNPG have NO memory request at all.
They are invisible to kube-scheduler regardless of how much they use. Highest-priority
class of fix because size is irrelevant -- a 12Mi container with no request still
breaks the scheduler's arithmetic model.

CNPG barman-cloud sidecars (35 more containers) are a separate ticket -- they are fixed
at the ObjectStore CR, not in the manifests.

## MEASURED (14d) AND PROPOSED

    namespace              workload/container                    n    p50   peak  REQnew  LIMnew  node(s)
    monitoring             tempo/tempo                           1   633M  1329M  1024M   2560M   talos01
    downloads              tubesync/tubesync                     1   531M   533M   768M   1280M   talos02-gpu
    kube-system            cilium-envoy/cilium-envoy             5    85M    86M   128M    128M   all 5   [GUARANTEED]
    argocd                 argocd-notifications-ctl/notification 1   114M   120M   192M    320M   talos06
    kube-system            cilium-operator/cilium-operator       1    97M   113M   192M    192M   talos01 [GUARANTEED]
    monitoring             loki/loki-sc-rules                    1    94M    97M   128M    256M   talos06
    downloads              metube/metube                         1    59M    68M    96M    192M   talos02-gpu
    monitoring             opentelemetry-operator/manager        1    65M    66M    96M    192M   talos01
    intel-device-plugins   intel-gpu-plugin/intel-gpu-plugin     3    19M    20M    32M     64M   talos01,02,06
    monitoring             clickstack-otel-collector/otel-coll   1    47M    49M    64M    128M   talos02-gpu
    external-secrets       external-secrets-webhook/webhook      1    43M    46M    64M     64M   talos01 [GUARANTEED]
    databases              plugin-barman-cloud/barman-cloud      1    36M    45M    48M     96M   talos01
    kubernetes-dashboard   kubernetes-dashboard/k8s-dashboard    1    11M    37M    32M     64M   talos02-gpu
    kubernetes-dashboard   dashboard-metrics-scraper/scraper     1    12M    33M    32M     64M   talos02-gpu
    clickhouse             clickhouse-operator/metrics-exporter  1    23M    27M    32M     64M   talos02-gpu
    local-path-storage     local-path-provisioner/provisioner    1    16M    23M    32M     32M   talos01 [GUARANTEED]
    monitoring             mimir-gateway/gateway                 1    13M    18M    32M     64M   talos02-gpu
    kube-system            hubble-relay/hubble-relay             1    16M    16M    32M     64M   talos02-gpu
    minio                  minio-pool-0/sidecar                  1    11M    13M    32M     64M   talos02-gpu
    kube-system            hubble-ui/frontend                    1    12M    12M    32M     64M   talos02-gpu
    monitoring             loki-chunks-cache/exporter            1     2M    12M    32M     64M   talos02-gpu
    kube-system            hubble-ui/backend                     1     9M    10M    32M     64M   talos02-gpu
    tdarr                  tdarr-server/flow-importer            1     9M     9M    32M     64M   talos06
    monitoring             loki-results-cache/exporter           1     2M     2M    32M     64M   talos01

    30 containers, +3.70 GiB of honest scheduler accounting.

## CLASSIFICATION NOTES

GUARANTEED (req == lim) -- these four are datapath/admission components whose eviction
takes down networking, secret sync or storage provisioning for the whole node or
cluster. Their memory is flat (peak/p50 ratio ~1.0-1.4x), so req==lim costs nothing and
buys the highest kubelet eviction protection:
    cilium-envoy 128Mi, cilium-operator 192Mi, external-secrets-webhook 64Mi,
    local-path-provisioner 32Mi

BURSTABLE for everything else. tempo is the notable one: 633M p50 / 1329M peak (2.1x)
because block flush and compaction are bursty -- 1024Mi request with a 2560Mi limit,
not a tight limit.

## WHY 32Mi FLOOR
Nothing below 32Mi. A container with a 2Mi request is only marginally better than no
request at all once you account for kubelet/containerd per-container overhead, and it
makes the pod's eviction ranking worse than it should be.

title: [EPIC] Right-size memory requests/limits fleet-wide and rebalance placement
description:
Fleet-wide right-sizing of memory requests/limits + placement rebalance. Follow-up to
TALOS-hyga (talos03 wedge, 2026-08-23). Measured from Mimir over 14d/30d on 2026-08-23.

## MEASURED STATE (404 running containers, 328 pods, 5 nodes)

    node          alloc   memReq   req%   sum(14d container peaks)  peak%   CPUreq%
    talos00       22.9G    8.9G    39%          13.0G               57%      53%
    talos01       20.7G   20.6G    99%          22.0G              106%      54%
    talos02-gpu   59.6G   43.6G    73%          47.3G               79%      90%
    talos03       12.5G   12.4G    99%          13.9G              111%      18%
    talos06       59.8G   21.2G    36%          20.8G               35%      32%

    node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes, min over 14d:
      talos00 1.61 GiB   talos01 1.21 GiB   talos02-gpu 29.86 GiB
      talos03 0.61 GiB   talos06 25.44 GiB

talos01 and talos03 are BOTH at 99% of allocatable memory requested, and their summed
container peaks EXCEED allocatable (106% / 111%). This is not only a requests-accuracy
problem: those two nodes are genuinely oversubscribed on real measured usage. Work has
to MOVE, not just be relabelled.

talos02-gpu is at 90% of CPU requests with 12 GiB of memory headroom -- it is NOT a
viable destination. talos06 (59.8G alloc, 35% memory, 32% CPU) is the only real
destination in the fleet.

## ACCOUNTING GAP

    228 of 404 running containers have NO memory limit
     65 of 404 running containers have NO memory request  (invisible to the scheduler)
    sum(peak - request) over under-declared groups:  +50.75 GiB
    sum(request - peak) over over-declared groups:   -40.57 GiB
    net honest-request delta:                        +25.7 GiB

## CHILDREN

Ordered by impact. Every child carries its own before/after numbers so it can be
executed without redoing the analysis.

## OUT OF SCOPE (already done, do not re-propose)
  - node reservations systemReserved/kubeReserved/evictionHard  (commit 4ec05ec1)
  - crossplane provider 768Mi/1536Mi                            (commit 74c2fec8)

## METHOD
Mimir via `kubectl port-forward -n monitoring svc/mimir-query-frontend 18080:8080`,
header `X-Scope-OrgID: anonymous`. p50 = quantile_over_time(0.5, ...[14d]) max'd over
replicas; peak = max_over_time(...[14d]) max'd over replicas.
notes:
## CHILDREN (created 2026-08-23)

    TALOS-i0po  P0  alloy: apiserver-histogram cardinality, not a leak
    TALOS-7q34  P0  control plane sizing (+11 GiB) + move 3rd CP off talos03
    TALOS-m7to  P1  reclaim over-declared requests (~19 GiB + 6.4 CPU)   <- DO FIRST
    TALOS-3zf9  P1  rebalance: evacuate ~10 GiB off talos01/talos03 to talos06
    TALOS-r5sg  P1  CNPG barman-cloud sidecars, 35 containers at resources:{}
    TALOS-ynzw  P1  30 non-CNPG zero-request containers (+3.70 GiB)
    TALOS-eda0  P1  monitoring + minio (+17.5 GiB)
    TALOS-gj3n  P1  platform namespaces, cilium/traefik -> GUARANTEED (+21.0 GiB)
    TALOS-nxtz  P2  media/tdarr/GPU burstable classification (net -11.6 GiB)
    TALOS-yfz7  P2  application namespaces (net -1.1 GiB)
    TALOS-23t1  P2  guardrails: LimitRange defaultRequest, alerts, Goldilocks, priorities

EXECUTION ORDER IS ENFORCED BY DEPENDENCIES. m7to and i0po first (they free room),
then 3zf9 (moves real usage), then the honest increases. Applying the +25.7 GiB of
increases first puts pods into Pending on a cluster already at 99% on two nodes.

## QoS CLASSIFICATION -- three classes, not one rule

GUARANTEED (requests == limits): flat memory, and eviction takes out a node's
networking/ingress/storage. cilium-agent, cilium-envoy, cilium-operator, traefik,
local-path-provisioner, cloudnative-pg manager, external-secrets webhook.
All measured at peak/p50 between 1.0x and 1.2x over 14d, so req==lim costs nothing.

BURSTABLE (request = steady state, generous limit): the default. Everything with a
predictable working set and a bounded upside -- the *arr apps, operators, controllers,
CNPG postgres, web apps.

BURSTABLE, NO LIMIT (a limit is actively harmful): measured peak/p50 ratios of 2.6x to
10.3x, where the burst is the workload doing its job and an OOMKill mid-burst loses the
work and retries it:
    mimir-compactor      60M p50 /  622M peak   10.3x   compaction
    mimir-store-gateway  87M p50 /  448M peak    5.2x   index-header load
    minio              1210M p50 / 4656M peak    3.8x   multipart PUT buffers
    tdarr-worker        323M p50 /  826M peak    2.6x   transcode
    plex                433M p50 /  681M peak    1.6x   GPU transcode sessions
    kometa, posterizarr, immich-ml, stash-ai, frigate, tdarr-server
kometa and posterizarr additionally could NOT be bounded from measurement -- see the
correction note on TALOS-nxtz.

## CROSS-VALIDATION AGAINST THE CLUSTER'S OWN VPA

vpa-recommender + Goldilocks are already deployed (84 VPA objects, 10 namespaces).
Comparing VPA targets to the Mimir-derived numbers:

  agreement where both have real data:
    tempo 1.00x, argocd-application-controller 1.00x, loki 0.98x,
    mimir-ingester 1.16x, scrypted 1.16x
  VPA higher, and RIGHT -- I missed the run:
    media/kometa  VPA 1568M vs my 105M peak (15.0x). Correction filed on TALOS-nxtz.
  VPA lower, and WRONG for bursty workloads (it targets a percentile, not a peak):
    mimir-compactor 0.40x, mimir-store-gateway 0.63x,
    loki-chunks-cache/memcached 0.02x (VPA says 125M for a deliberate 8 GiB cache)
  VPA floor artifact: it never recommends below ~125Mi, so its output is meaningless
    for the ~25 exporters and sidecars in this cluster that genuinely use 2-25Mi.

## WHAT COULD NOT BE MEASURED

  1. kube-apiserver's own Go heap. The ServiceMonitor keep-regex in
     infrastructure/base/monitoring/control-plane-scrape/apiserver.yaml drops
     go_memstats_* for job="kubernetes", so `go_memstats_heap_inuse_bytes{job=
     "kubernetes"}` returns NO DATA over the full 30d. It is therefore not possible
     to say how much of the apiserver's 5-8 GiB is watch cache vs GC headroom.
     FIX 4 on TALOS-i0po restores it.
  2. kometa and posterizarr peaks -- no run occurred inside the 14d window.
  3. etcd memory. etcd runs inside Talos, outside Kubernetes container accounting,
     so container_memory_working_set_bytes has nothing for it. Its footprint on the
     three control-plane nodes is real and is NOT in any number in this epic.
  4. Cross-container simultaneity. Per-container peaks are summed per node as an
     upper bound; peaks do not all coincide, so the real simultaneous high-water mark
     is somewhat lower than the "sum of peaks" column. The MemAvailable minima
     (talos03 0.61 GiB, talos01 1.21 GiB) are the ground truth and they corroborate
     the conclusion.

Four workloads right-sized against MEASURED 24h peaks from Mimir, not estimates:

  loki-chunks-cache   peak   140Mi   requested 9830Mi  ->  1536Mi   reclaims 8.3 GiB
  secure-chrome       peak 1,084Mi   requested 8192Mi  ->  2048Mi   reclaims 6.1 GiB
  storyteller         peak   391Mi   requested 2048Mi  ->   768Mi   reclaims 1.3 GiB
  opensim             peak   173Mi   requested 2048Mi  ->   512Mi   reclaims 1.5 GiB

RESULT, measured after reconcile:
    talos01   22.6/23.2 Gi (97%)  ->  12.7/23.2 Gi (55%)
    talos02   43.7/62.1 Gi (70%)  ->  34.0/62.1 Gi (55%)
    talos03   10.5/15.0 Gi (70%)  ->  11.0/15.0 Gi (74%)
Every node now under 85%. talos01 — which was next to wedge after talos03 did — has real
headroom for the first time.

## THE BIGGEST OFFENDER WAS NOT IN THIS EPIC'S ANALYSIS
loki-chunks-cache was reserving 9.6 GiB for 140Mi of actual use and appears nowhere in the
children of this epic. It is chart default — loki 6.23.0 ships an 8GB memcached with a
matching request AND limit — so it looks deliberate and reads as legitimate cache sizing
until you check the 24h series. It was the single largest phantom reservation in the
cluster.

That is worth generalising: THE AUDIT SHOULD SPECIFICALLY SWEEP CHART DEFAULTS, not just
hand-written manifests. Anything installed by Helm with upstream-default resources is
sized for upstream's idea of load, which for a homelab is usually wrong by an order of
magnitude. Nothing in git will look wrong, because the number is not in git at all.

## ALSO CORRECTED
TALOS-r5sg claimed 35 CNPG barman sidecars with resources:{}. Verified live: CNPG instance
pods have exactly ONE container each (postgres, 35 of them) and all 35 HAVE requests. There
is exactly ONE barman container in the cluster, the plugin Deployment in the databases
namespace. Downgraded P1 -> P3.

Before executing any remaining child, SPOT-CHECK ITS NUMBERS against live state. Two of the
figures in this epic have now been materially wrong, and container counts and GiB totals
are both easy to get wrong and persuasive when wrong.

## STILL OPEN — the parts NOT covered by ca3b96d1
 - under-declared workloads (alloy at 6078Mi used vs 1074Mi requested, no limit)
 - the ~30 containers with NO memory request at all
 - burstable-vs-guaranteed classification, including tdarr/GPU transcode which the user
   explicitly wants left burstable with no transcode limits
 - guardrails: LimitRange defaultRequest, request-vs-usage alerting, PriorityClasses

title: talos03 wedged on memory exhaustion; talos01 is at 97% memory requests and will be next
description:
talos03 went NotReady at 2026-08-23T21:43:44Z and required a physical power cycle. Root
cause is MEMORY EXHAUSTION, not CPU, disk or network.

## EVIDENCE (Mimir, the hour before the wedge)
    mem available   0.6 GiB   (min 0.6, max 1.8)   <-- at the floor
    cpu busy        6.7-14.3%                       healthy
    load15          1.5-2.3                         healthy
    disk io util    2.7-23.3%                       healthy

The failure signature matched: the node answered ping and every TCP port stayed OPEN
(50000/10250/2379/6443) but no handshake completed and machined's own socket was closed —
  raw-read unix @->/system/run/machined/machine.sock: use of closed network connection
That is a node thrashing, not a crash. Kernel log did not survive the reboot.

## THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM
    node          RAM      pods  memRequests   note
    talos03      15.0 Gi    33     10.5 Gi     16 CPUs but the LEAST RAM in the cluster
    talos01      23.2 Gi    72     22.6 Gi     97% OF CAPACITY ALREADY REQUESTED
    talos00      25.4 Gi    26      8.9 Gi     tainted by design
    talos02-gpu  62.1 Gi   151     43.7 Gi
    talos06      62.3 Gi    46     15.7 Gi

talos03 has roughly 1 GiB of RAM per CPU core. The scheduler packs on CPU and on requests,
so a node that looks abundant on paper is the tightest in the fleet on memory — and
anything without a memory request is invisible to that arithmetic entirely.

TALOS01 IS THE NEXT ONE TO GO. It sits at 22.6 Gi requested against 23.2 Gi capacity, 72
pods, with essentially zero headroom for kubelet, containerd and the kernel itself.

## CONTRIBUTING FACTOR — be honest about it
Today's CNPG storage migration (TALOS-npt4) moved a batch of Postgres replicas onto
local-path and talos03 took a share of them, on top of the 56 pods it was already running.
Each CNPG instance is a real Postgres process with shared buffers. That is very likely what
pushed an already-tight node over.

## WHAT TO ACTUALLY DO
 1. kube-reserved / system-reserved in the kubelet config so a node defends itself instead
    of letting workloads consume the memory kubelet and containerd need. Talos exposes this
    via machine.kubelet.extraConfig, same mechanism as the maxPods 110->200 change. This is
    the single highest-value fix: it converts 'node wedges and needs a power cycle' into
    'a pod gets evicted'.
 2. Memory REQUESTS on the workloads that lack them — without a request the scheduler
    cannot account for a pod at all.
 3. Consider whether talos03 should carry fewer memory-hungry replicas given its
    RAM:CPU ratio, or whether it wants more RAM.

## COLLATERAL, worth knowing
 - grafana and forgejo are SINGLE-REPLICA Deployments; both were on talos03 and both went
   503 until rescheduled. Traefik was NOT at fault — it is a DaemonSet on all five nodes
   with externalTrafficPolicy Cluster and correctly reported no healthy backend.
 - forgejo then CrashLooped on its new node with
     unable to lock level db at /data/gitea/queues/common: resource temporarily unavailable
   because its NFS lock was still held by the wedged node. A wedged node is WORSE than a
   dead one for NFS-backed workloads: the lock is never released. Only the reboot cleared it.
 - etcd held quorum throughout on talos00 + talos01. At one control plane this would have
   been a full outage; the EPIC 1 promotion earlier the same day is what made it survivable.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED + IMMEDIATE FIX APPLIED 2026-08-23.

## WHY THE RAM DISAPPEARED — requests are fiction
14.9 GB unaccounted for in the TOP TEN PODS ALONE (kubectl top vs declared requests):
    alloy                    uses 6078Mi  req 1074Mi  +5004Mi  NO LIMIT
    kube-apiserver-talos01   uses 5011Mi  req 2048Mi  +2963Mi  has limit
    mimir-ingester-0/1/2     uses 1816Mi  req  512Mi  +1304Mi  NO LIMIT (x3)
    manyfold                 uses 1273Mi  req  512Mi  + 761Mi  NO LIMIT
    minio-pool-0-0           uses 1213Mi  req  512Mi  + 701Mi  NO LIMIT
    crossplane aws provider  uses  658Mi  req    0Mi  + 658Mi  INVISIBLE
    tempo-0                  uses  642Mi  req    0Mi  + 642Mi  INVISIBLE
    litellm                  uses  852Mi  req  256Mi  + 596Mi  NO LIMIT

kube-scheduler packs on REQUESTS. A pod that under-declares makes a node look emptier
than it is; a pod with NO request is not counted at all. So nodes were being filled to
well past their real capacity by design, and the first one to run out simply wedged.

alloy is the standout: 1Gi requested, 6Gi used, no limit. Its WAL was NOT the cause this
time — truncate_frequency 15m is configured and the on-disk WAL was only 140M.

## TWO DELIBERATE CHANGES THE SAME DAY RAISED THE FLOOR
 - Promoting to 3 control planes (EPIC 1) tripled the kube-apiserver footprint:
   talos01 5008Mi + talos00 4690Mi + talos03 1647Mi = ~11GB where there used to be one.
   Worth it — that same promotion is why the cluster kept serving through this incident.
 - Scaling five CNPG clusters from instances 1 -> 3 (TALOS-npt4) added ~10 Postgres
   processes, now 35 instance pods fleet-wide.
Neither is a mistake. Combined with dishonest requests, they left no headroom.

## APPLIED (commit 4ec05ec1)
systemReserved 1Gi + kubeReserved 1Gi + evictionHard memory.available 500Mi on ALL FIVE
nodes via docs/05-runbooks/talos-kubelet-memory-reserve-patch.yaml. No reboot, kubelet
restart only. Allocatable dropped as expected — talos03 15.1->13.1GB, talos01
23.7->21.7GB — and NO pods were evicted, despite talos01 sitting at only 2.4Gi available
beforehand. Added to scripts/bootstrap-talos-patches.sh so rebuilt nodes inherit it.

This converts 'node wedges, needs a physical power cycle' into 'a pod gets evicted'. It
does NOT create memory.

## STILL OPEN — the actual fix
Right-size requests and add limits, starting with the list above. alloy alone would
recover 5GB of scheduler accounting. Pods with req 0 should get a request at minimum so
the scheduler can see them at all.

title: talos03 wedged under CNPG replica rebuild — 6 postgres instances on local-path NVMe
description:
2026-08-23 ~21:43:44Z talos03 (control-plane, etcd voter) stopped heartbeating. Both kubelet (10250) and the Talos API (50000) time out on TLS handshake, so this is a node-level wedge, not just kubelet.

Blast radius: 58 pods on the node; 39 of 207 cluster deployments went Available=False because their pods were there. etcd kept quorum (2/3 voters), apiserver stayed responsive (/healthz 0.05s).

Likely cause: talos03 was hosting SIX CNPG postgres instances all created 74-89 minutes prior (crowdsec-postgres-2, forgejo-postgres-2, homeassistant-postgres-3, linkwarden-postgres-1, bookorbit-postgres-3, zipline-postgres-1) from the scale-to-3 + move-off-NFS work in 4b45f671/9c93b51f/fa55d9fe. Six concurrent pg_basebackup replica rebuilds onto local-path NVMe on one node.

NOT caused by the concurrent crossplane provider work: that added 11 CRDs total, crossplane core never restarted, and the failure hit deployments in unrelated namespaces (local-path-provisioner, external-secrets, forgejo, kubevirt).

Worth considering: anti-affinity or a rate limit so CNPG replica rebuilds do not stack this many onto one node, especially a control-plane node.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text: talos03 recovered on its own at ~21:55Z without intervention. Cluster deployments not-ready went 39/207 -> 1/207 (the remaining one, media-private/hot-ones, is unrelated). etcd never lost quorum. Leaving this open because the trigger — six concurrent CNPG replica rebuilds landing on one control-plane node — is unaddressed and will recur on the next storage migration.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
RESOLVED 2026-08-23, commit 74c2fec8.

runtime-config.yaml had been WRITTEN but never committed and never added to
kustomization.yaml, so the fix existed only as an untracked file and then disappeared
from disk entirely. Verified live before re-landing it: DeploymentRuntimeConfig/default
still had spec:{} and 0 of 8 package-runtime containers carried a memory request. It has
now been recreated, wired into the kustomization, committed and reconciled.

VERIFIED IN THE CLUSTER:
  DeploymentRuntimeConfig/default  requests.memory = 768Mi
  package-runtime containers with a request: 8/8
  providers: aws-ec2, aws-iam, aws-ecs, aws-cloudwatchlogs, aws-s3, kubernetes,
             upbound-provider-family-aws — all installed=True healthy=True

Values unchanged from the original: 768Mi request sized to the largest observed pod
(upbound-provider-family-aws at 657Mi) rather than the median, since one config named
 serves all providers and is the only way to reach the family provider, which
Crossplane installs as an automatic dependency and cannot be declared in git.

COMPLEMENTARY NODE-SIDE FIX, TALOS-hyga / commit 4ec05ec1: systemReserved 1Gi +
kubeReserved 1Gi + evictionHard memory.available 500Mi on all five nodes, applied without
reboot and with zero evictions, plus added to scripts/bootstrap-talos-patches.sh. The two
address different halves — that one stops a node dying when memory runs out, this one
stops the scheduler being lied to about how much memory is free.

STILL OPEN, tracked on TALOS-hyga: requests across the rest of the cluster remain
substantially fiction, ~14.9GB unaccounted in the top ten pods alone. alloy is the worst
single offender at 6078Mi used against a 1074Mi request with no limit; tempo-0 and others
declare nothing at all.

title: allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes is true but Talos keeps re-asserting the control-plane taint
description:
allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes is TRUE in the machine config on all three control planes, yet
Talos still declares and reconciles the control-plane NoSchedule taint. kubectl taint removal
is reverted within ~60 seconds.

## EVIDENCE (2026-08-23, after the EPIC 1 promotion)
  Running config on talos03:  cluster.allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes: True
  Config applied at install:  same
  Yet:  talosctl get nodetaintspec --nodes 192.168.1.30
        NODE           NAMESPACE  TYPE           ID                                     EFFECT
        192.168.1.30   k8s        NodeTaintSpec  node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane  NoSchedule

  kubectl taint node talos0{0,1,3} node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane-
  -> all three untainted, then 2 of 3 back within 30s, all 3 within 60s.

NOT a Kubernetes controller doing it: the node's managedFields carry NO taint entry, so it is
not being written through the API by a tracked manager. It is Talos asserting desired state
from its own NodeTaintSpec resource.

## WHAT THE DOCS SAY, AND WHY IT DOES NOT EXPLAIN THIS
Sidero: "This setting stops Talos from tainting the node ON BOOT. If you set it after the
boot, you have to untaint the node yourself, or reboot the node."
https://docs.siderolabs.com/talos/v1.13/deploy-and-manage-workloads/workloads-on-controlplane

That would explain a taint surviving a live config patch. It does NOT explain talos01 and
talos03, which were freshly installed WITH the setting already in the config and rebooted
into it. They should have registered untainted.

## IMPACT — real but bounded
The taint is NoSchedule, not NoExecute, so pods already running stay. But NEW pods cannot be
scheduled onto talos00, talos01 or talos03. With 3 of 5 nodes now control planes, that leaves
only talos02-gpu and talos06 accepting new workloads.

This bit us immediately: after the talos03 reset, the 11 media-experimental pods (pinned to
talos03 by nodeAffinity) and the config-restore Job could not schedule at all. Workaround was
untainting during a window and letting them land before the taint returned, plus adding an
explicit control-plane toleration to the restore Job.

## INVESTIGATE
 1. Is this a known Talos v1.13 defect? Check upstream issues for
    allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes + NodeTaintSpec.
 2. Does the NodeTaintSpec clear after a full reboot (not just a config apply)? The docs imply
    it should. If so, a reboot per control plane is the fix — and EPIC 2 (Talos OS upgrade)
    reboots every node anyway, so it may resolve itself there. VERIFY rather than assume.
 3. Is the setting in the right place for this Talos version? It is at cluster.
    allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes in v1alpha1. Confirm v1.13 has not moved or superseded it.

## DO NOT
Do not paper over this by adding control-plane tolerations to every workload. That makes the
taint meaningless while leaving the config lying about its own state. Fix the root or decide
deliberately to run tainted control planes and stop setting the flag.

Related: EPIC 1 TALOS-8tis, EPIC 2 TALOS-xipf, TALOS-0bo8 (config flattening).

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
SEQUENCED AFTER THE UPGRADES (user, 2026-08-23). Blocked on EPIC 2b.

Reason it can wait: the taint is NoSchedule, not NoExecute, so running workloads are
unaffected. The constraint is only that NEW pods cannot land on the three control planes,
and talos02-gpu + talos06 have capacity for that in the meantime.

Reason it may resolve itself: EPIC 2 (Talos OS 1.13.2 -> 1.13.9) reboots every node. Sidero's
docs say allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes takes effect ON BOOT, so a full OS upgrade reboot may
clear the NodeTaintSpec without any further work. CHECK AFTER EPIC 2 before investigating
further — if the taints are gone, close this and note that a reboot was the fix.

If they are still present after every node has rebooted through the upgrade, that rules out
the boot-timing explanation entirely and it is a genuine defect worth reporting upstream.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
ESCALATED — this caused a real outage during EPIC 2, not just inconvenience.

2026-08-23, upgrading talos06: with the 3 control planes tainted, talos06 cordoned for its
own upgrade, and talos02-gpu out of CPU, the scheduler had ZERO available nodes:

    0/5 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu, 1 node(s) were unschedulable,
    3 node(s) had untolerated taint(s)

mimir-rollout-operator was evicted off talos06 and could not reschedule anywhere. Its
webhook has failurePolicy: Fail, so while it was Pending EVERY POD EVICTION IN THE
monitoring NAMESPACE WAS BLOCKED CLUSTER-WIDE. That stalled two upgrade attempts before
the cause was found.

Untainting the three control planes let it schedule onto talos03 within seconds and the
webhook endpoint returned. So the taint is not a cosmetic discrepancy — with 3 of 5 nodes
being control planes it removes 60 percent of the cluster's scheduling capacity, and any
event that cordons one of the remaining two produces an unschedulable cluster.

This raises the priority: it should be fixed before, not after, further node maintenance.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
FULL EVIDENCE after exhaustive testing 2026-08-23. Everything below is measured, not inferred.

WHAT IS SET (verified on all 3 control planes, in the RUNNING config not just on disk):
  talosctl get mc v1alpha1 --nodes <ip> -o yaml | grep allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes
  -> allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes: true      (real YAML boolean)

WHAT TALOS DOES ANYWAY:
  talosctl get nodetaintspec --nodes 192.168.1.30
  NAMESPACE  TYPE           ID                                     EFFECT
  k8s        NodeTaintSpec  node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane  NoSchedule
  owner: k8s.NodeTaintSpecController, version: 1, created == that node's boot time

EVERY REMEDY TRIED, AND ITS RESULT:
 1. kubectl taint node <n> ...-           -> succeeds, taint returns in 25-75s.
                                             Measured over 8 polls at 25s on STABLE
                                             nodes with no reboot in progress:
                                             talos01 back by poll 2, talos03 by poll 4.
 2. Full reboot of every node             -> taint returned. This KILLS the documented
    (the v1.13.2 -> v1.13.9 upgrade)         'only applies at boot' explanation, which
                                             would have predicted a reboot fixes it.
 3. talosctl patch mc toggling the flag   -> 'Applied configuration without a reboot',
    false then true, to force the            taint spec still present 20s later.
    controller to re-evaluate
 4. Checked managedFields on the Node     -> NO taint entry. So it is NOT written via
                                             the API by any tracked manager. Talos is
                                             asserting it from its own resource.
 5. Checked for Kyverno policies on taints-> none. Checked the whole repo for anything
                                             applying it -> only tolerations/selectors.

WHAT THE DOCS CLAIM (and why it does not fit):
  https://docs.siderolabs.com/talos/v1.13/deploy-and-manage-workloads/workloads-on-controlplane
  'This setting stops Talos from tainting the node on boot. If you set it after the boot,
  you have to untaint the node yourself, or reboot the node.'
  Item 2 above disproves this for our cluster: every node rebooted with the flag already
  in its config and came up tainted regardless.

WHY IT MATTERS (not cosmetic):
  3 of 5 nodes are control planes, so this removes 60% of schedulable capacity. During the
  Talos upgrade, with talos06 cordoned and talos02-gpu out of CPU, the scheduler had ZERO
  available nodes; mimir-rollout-operator could not reschedule and, because its eviction
  webhook is failurePolicy: Fail, NOTHING in the monitoring namespace could be evicted
  cluster-wide. Two upgrade attempts stalled. See TALOS-w5fq.

WHAT THE USER ACTUALLY WANTS (this is the real requirement, not 'remove all taints'):
  talos00 SHOULD stay tainted — it is severely RAM-limited and should run the control
  plane and little else. talos01 and talos03 SHOULD be schedulable. So the ideal answer
  is PER-NODE taint control, not the cluster-wide flag. Investigate whether Talos v1.13
  exposes per-node taints in the machine config (machine.nodeTaints or similar); if it
  does, that is a better answer than the cluster flag even once the bug is fixed.

REJECTED APPROACH — do not resurrect it:
  A reconciler Deployment looping 'kubectl taint ... -' every 10s on talos01/talos03 was
  drafted and REJECTED by the user. It papers over the defect, fights Talos continuously,
  and leaves the config asserting something untrue. Find the real cause.

A Fable-5 research agent is investigating: whether the flag is at the correct nesting for
v1.13 v1alpha1, whether a second config document is re-asserting defaults, what
NodeTaintSpecController actually reads in the Talos source, whether this is a known v1.13
regression, and whether per-node taints exist. Findings to be appended here.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
RESOLVED 2026-08-23. NOT a Talos bug — it was this repo's own config.

## ROOT CAUSE
configs/nodes/controlplane.yaml line 233 sets:
    machine:
      nodeTaints:
        node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: "NoSchedule"

Talos's NodeTaintSpecController has TWO independent taint paths:
    if IsControlPlane() && !ScheduleOnControlPlanes() { createTaint(...) }  // conditional
    for key, val := range Machine().NodeTaints() { createTaint(key, ...) } // UNCONDITIONAL
https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/blob/v1.13.9/internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/k8s/node_taint_spec.go

The second loop never consults allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes. So a cluster can have that
flag set to true — as this one correctly did on all three control planes — and still be
tainted. The two settings appear to contradict each other and nodeTaints silently wins.

That taint was written when talos00 was the ONLY control plane and is still CORRECT for
talos00: it is RAM-limited and should run the control plane and little else. talos01 and
talos03, promoted from workers earlier the same day, had their configs generated from that
same shared template and inherited a taint that defeated the entire purpose of promoting
them.

## WHY EVERY DIAGNOSTIC POINTED THE WRONG WAY
 - kubectl taint removal reverting in 25-75s: NodeApplyController re-asserting the spec.
 - A full cluster reboot (the v1.13.9 upgrade) not clearing it: the config contained
   nodeTaints at boot, so the spec was recreated every time. This is what made it look
   like the documented 'only applies at boot' behaviour was broken.
 - Toggling the flag false->true: a genuine no-op, because that path was already correctly
   disabled. The flag was never the knob.

## FIX APPLIED
    talosctl patch mc --endpoints 192.168.1.54 --nodes 192.168.1.177 \
      --patch '[{"op":"remove","path":"/machine/nodeTaints"}]'
    (same for 192.168.1.30)

Hot-reloadable, no reboot. Talos tracks its own taints in the node annotation
talos.dev/owned-taints and removed them itself once the spec disappeared — no kubectl
taint needed.

VERIFIED: taints absent across 7 polls over 3 minutes. talos00 still tainted, deliberately.
Schedulable nodes went from 2 of 5 to 4 of 5.

## PERSISTED
 - docs/05-runbooks/talos-schedulable-controlplane-patch.yaml (tracked; configs/nodes is
   gitignored) with the full explanation in its header
 - configs/nodes/controlplane.yaml annotated at the nodeTaints block
 - README.md corrected for the 3-control-plane layout
 - commit 9e1d3cb3

## WORTH NOTING FOR NEXT TIME
The README ALREADY documented this correctly — 'despite allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes,
the machine config sets machine.nodeTaints... so talos00 runs only core infrastructure'.
It was not read carefully enough during the promotion, and hours went into treating a
documented, intentional design as an upstream defect. Read the repo's own docs on a
surprising behaviour before concluding upstream is broken.

title: Flatten Talos config: a node must be rebuildable from git + secrets alone
description:
## PROVEN BY INCIDENT, 2026-08-23 — talos01 could not be rebuilt from what is in git

Resetting talos01 for the control-plane promotion wiped its boot disk. Bringing it back
required THREE facts, and NOT ONE of them was reachable from a git-tracked control-plane
config:

  install disk    /dev/nvme0n1     (the generic controlplane.yaml says /dev/sda)
  install image   factory.talos.dev/installer/c9078f94...:v1.13.2
                                   (the generic one says ghcr.io/siderolabs/installer, STOCK)
  extensions      siderolabs/iscsi-tools, via schematic c9078f94...
  kubelet patches iSCSI extraMounts, local-path extraMount, maxPods 200 — applied POST-HOC
                  by scripts/bootstrap-talos-patches.sh, in none of the above

The runbook says "apply controlplane.yaml". Doing that literally would have installed talos01
to a disk it does not boot from, with an image missing its iSCSI extension. The reset failure
merely got there first — talos03 would have hit the identical problem.

The per-node truth lives in configs/nodes/talos01/worker-talos01.yaml, which is (a) a WORKER
config, so useless for promotion, and (b) gitignored, so it is not a source of truth at all.

## WHAT "FLATTENED" HAS TO MEAN
A node must be rebuildable from git plus a secrets bundle. Nothing else. Today it needs
tribal knowledge and a gitignored file.

Structure roughly:
  TRACKED IN GIT
    cluster-wide patches   kubelet iSCSI extraMounts, local-path extraMount, maxPods 200,
                           control-plane metrics (already tracked, already wired into gen-config)
    per-node patches       install.disk, install.image/schematic, any node-specific hardware
                           config — one small file per node, NO secrets in them
    schematics             already tracked; .gitignore explicitly allows
                           configs/nodes/*-schematic.yaml through
  NOT IN GIT
    the secrets bundle only

  gen-config assembles: talosctl gen config ... --with-secrets <bundle> \
      --config-patch @<cluster-wide patches> \
      --config-patch-worker/@--config-patch-control-plane as appropriate
  and per-node application layers the node patch on top.

The Taskfile already demonstrates the mechanism (Taskfile.talos.yaml:24 passes
--config-patch-control-plane for the metrics patch) and its own comment invites more:
"Add more --config-patch* here as needed."

## *** THE TRAP THAT MAKES THIS DELICATE ***
talosctl gen config generates NEW PKI unless given --with-secrets. Regenerating without it
produces a config with a different cluster id that CANNOT join. Verified 2026-08-23: live
cluster id _h70D_fSmLmFjz2mJs8E_j_k matches configs/nodes/controlplane.yaml exactly, and that
match is the only reason the file is usable. So step one of this work is establishing where
the secrets bundle is (or extracting it from the current config) — before any regeneration.

## ALSO FIX
docs/05-runbooks/promote-workers-to-controlplane.md references configs/controlplane.yaml.
The file is at configs/nodes/controlplane.yaml. And the runbook's claim that reset "reboots
into maintenance mode" did not hold — talos01 came up to a bare cursor with no bootable
device, requiring a factory ISO:
  https://factory.talos.dev/image/c9078f9419961640c712a8bf2bb9174933dfcf1da383fd8ea2b7dc21493f8bac/v1.13.2/metal-amd64.iso
The runbook should say a matching factory ISO must be ON HAND BEFORE the reset, and that
console access is a prerequisite for bare metal with no BMC.

## DEFINITION OF DONE
Any node can be rebuilt from: this repo + the secrets bundle + a factory ISO. No tribal
knowledge, no gitignored worker config, no post-hoc patch script for a fresh node.
scripts/bootstrap-talos-patches.sh stays for EXISTING nodes; a new node should not need it.
notes:
## CONFIG SCOPE COMPLETE 2026-08-24 — 8/8 children closed. NOT force-closing.

All eight children are done: w04r · dnfy · l6ju · xxmd · frvi · tffz · v3wy · ow7w.

    fleet configuration drift    0 differences across all five nodes
    source of truth              configs/talconfig.yaml + 14 patches
    drift detection              task talos:verify / verify-dry-run + CI lint (4 checks)
    secrets                      talsecret.yaml in 1Password, 0 tracked in git

STILL BLOCKED BY TALOS-npt4 (CNPG off NFS), and that dependency is REAL rather than stale —
this epic's goal is 'a node must be rebuildable from git + secrets alone', and a node whose
Postgres data sits on node-bound local-path PVCs is not rebuildable in the sense that matters.
The machine CONFIG is now reproducible; the DATA story is npt4's. Leaving open deliberately
rather than force-closing on a technicality.

## WHAT THE MIGRATION FOUND — the value was in the drift, not the tooling

Nine config areas existed ONLY on the nodes, reproducible from nothing. Four were real bugs:
  - both GPU workers had EVERY kubelet mount declared twice (6 entries vs 3)
  - bind-address existed on talos00 ONLY, so controller-manager and scheduler metrics were
    unscrapable on two of three control planes — unnoticed because Prometheus still got talos00
  - talos03's maxPods was being silently reset 60 -> 200 by talhelper's patch ordering, on the
    12.8 GiB node that had already wedged from memory exhaustion
  - certSANs were being stripped by my own differ's skip list, including
    cluster.apiServer.certSANs, which would have broken every kubectl against the endpoint

## LESSONS

  - applying machine config REBOOTS the node: bisected to the forced removal of
    machine.features.stableHostname, which Talos rejects alongside its HostnameConfig document
  - talhelper applies GLOBAL patches AFTER per-node ones, so a per-node override silently
    loses. CI lint check 4 catches this and was negative-tested to prove it fires.
  - etcd members reports CONFIGURED membership and reads 3 straight through a real quorum loss;
    kubectl auth can-i create is the signal that means something
  - reboots leave 25-30 phantom Error pods; count deployment readiness, not pod phase
  - an offline checker written by whoever wrote the config cannot validate it. The verification
    tooling was the weak link three separate times. What actually found problems was
    talosctl apply-config --dry-run against a real node, and two independent adversarial audits.

## THE THROUGHLINE

Almost every problem was something REPORTING SUCCESS while the effect was absent — Flux
applying a revision that no longer held the change, a HelmRelease Ready over values a duplicate
key had discarded, an operator Running while not reconciling, a DaemonSet at 5/5 only because
its request had been reverted, kustomize build exit 0 on a values key the chart does not read,
and a differ reporting 0 unresolved while a skip list hid certSANs.

When a control loop reports success and the effect is absent, verify the OUTPUT object, not the
controller's status.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
## ADDITIONAL SCOPE — STOP HARDCODING /dev/sdX. THIS HAS BITTEN BEFORE.

User, 2026-08-23: Talos has previously started installing to the USB INSTALL MEDIA instead of
the internal disk, and had to be rescued by physically pulling the stick after it loaded into
RAM but before it wrote. That is a data-destroying failure mode and it is entirely avoidable.

ROOT CAUSE: machine.install.disk takes a fixed device path, and /dev/sdX enumeration order is
not stable. Boot from USB and the stick can become /dev/sda — which is exactly what
configs/nodes/controlplane.yaml currently targets:

    configs/nodes/controlplane.yaml   install.disk: /dev/sda      <-- LANDMINE
    talos01 actual                    install.disk: /dev/nvme0n1
    talos03 actual                    install.disk: /dev/nvme0n1

So the generic control-plane config would install to whatever happens to enumerate as sda —
plausibly the USB stick you just booted from.

## THE FIX — diskSelector with a CEL expression, not a device path
Talos v1.13 supports CEL disk selectors. Match on properties, and EXCLUDE USB explicitly:

    machine:
      install:
        diskSelector:
          match: disk.transport == 'nvme' && disk.size > 500u * GiB && !disk.busPath.contains('usb')

Verified against the live cluster 2026-08-23 — talos03 reports:
    nvme0n1   size=2000GB  transport=nvme  rotational=false  model="Sabrent Rocket 4.0 2TB"
    busPath   /pci0000:00/0000:00:01.2/0000:01:00.0/nvme
So transport/size/busPath are all populated and usable as matchers. Confirm the same for
talos01 (500GB Crucial CT500P3PSSD8), talos02-gpu (2TB Timetec) and talos06 (1TB CT1000E100SSD8)
before writing a fleet-wide selector — the size floor must not exclude talos01's 500GB.

Reference: https://docs.siderolabs.com/talos/v1.13/reference/configuration/v1alpha1/config
