and the upstream discussion of `disk.size > 64u * GiB && !disk.busPath.contains('usb')`.

## WHY THIS BELONGS WITH THE TALHELPER WORK
talhelper's talconfig.yaml is where per-node install settings should live, so the disk selector
gets defined ONCE per node (or once for the fleet, if one expression fits all four) in git,
rather than being a fixed path in a gitignored generated file that nobody reviews. Doing the
selector fix without talhelper just moves the same landmine to a different file.

ALSO: set machine.install.wipe deliberately. talos01's worker config had wipe:false. Understand
what it does before changing it — but a fresh install onto a selected disk should be explicit
about whether it wipes.

## ACCEPTANCE
 - No config in this repo contains a hardcoded /dev/sdX install target.
 - The selector provably cannot match removable/USB media.
 - Booting a node from USB install media and applying config installs to the internal NVMe,
   verified on at least one node before trusting it fleet-wide.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
## DOES THIS REQUIRE REBUILDING THE CLUSTER? — NO, and here is why
User asked 2026-08-23. The concern is reasonable but the answer is no, PROVIDED the existing
PKI is preserved.

talhelper GENERATES machine configs; it does not create a cluster. The only thing that would
force a rebuild is NEW PKI. That is avoidable: talsecret.yaml can be built from the EXISTING
secrets rather than generated fresh.

Everything required is already present in the running configuration:
    cluster.id, cluster.secret
    machine.ca (crt + key), machine.token
    cluster.ca, cluster.aggregatorCA, cluster.serviceAccount
    cluster.etcd.ca, cluster.token
Feed those into talsecret.yaml and talhelper emits configs carrying the SAME cluster identity
(_h70D_fSmLmFjz2mJs8E_j_k), which existing nodes accept as a configuration change rather than
as a different cluster.

So this is a CONFIG-MANAGEMENT migration, not a cluster migration.

*** THE HAZARD: `talhelper gensecret` creates NEW secrets. Running it by mistake produces
configs no existing node can join with. Do not run it. Build talsecret.yaml from the current
config instead. ***

## VALIDATION BEFORE APPLYING ANYTHING
Generate configs with talhelper and DIFF them against what each node is actually running
(talosctl get mc v1alpha1 -o yaml) BEFORE applying. The generated output should differ only in
ways you intend. A surprise diff means the intent capture is wrong, and it is far cheaper to
find that in a diff than in a node that will not rejoin.

## SEQUENCING — deliberately LAST
Blocked on TALOS-npt4, i.e. after EPIC 1 (3 control planes), EPIC 2 (Talos OS) and EPIC 2b
(Kubernetes). By then a bad config apply is survivable because quorum tolerates one node down.
Doing it at one control plane — as the cluster stands tonight — would be the worst possible
moment.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
DESIGN COMPLETE 2026-08-23 -> docs/02-architecture/talos-config-management.md

VERDICT: adopt talhelper. NO CLUSTER REBUILD REQUIRED — proven, not assumed.
Extracted a secrets bundle from configs/nodes/controlplane.yaml with
'talosctl gen secrets --from-controlplane-config' and compared every identity
field to live talos00. All matched byte-for-byte: machine CA, k8s CA, etcd CA,
aggregator CA, machine token, k8s bootstrap token, cluster.id, cluster.secret,
secretbox secret. The warning already in this ticket's body (build talsecret
FROM the current config, never 'gen secrets' fresh) is exactly right and is
now confirmed with the mechanism that does it.

SECRETS: recommend 1Password, NOT SOPS. ESO cannot deliver this (it is a
bootstrap-time secret and ESO runs inside the cluster it would bootstrap), and
SOPS adds an age key that must itself be backed up in 1Password anyway — two
trust roots instead of one. Reversible either way; talhelper reads both.

SEQUENCING NOTE: this ticket said 'blocked on TALOS-npt4, after 3 control
planes + Talos OS + Kubernetes upgrades'. Those preconditions are now MET —
talos00/01/03 are all control-plane, Talos v1.13.9, Kubernetes v1.36.4. The
'worst possible moment' caveat no longer applies; quorum tolerates one node.

NEW FINDING — the cluster is drifted RIGHT NOW, filed as TALOS-v3wy:
  talos00      declares schematic c9078f94 in git, runs the STOCK ghcr
               installer with ZERO extensions, and still has
               install.disk: /dev/sda (the 1GB USB stick)
  talos02-gpu  missing siderolabs/iscsi-tools, install.image pinned v1.11.1
  talos06      missing siderolabs/iscsi-tools, install.image pinned v1.11.1
Consequence: those three cannot attach Democratic-CSI iSCSI volumes. The
kubelet /etc/iscsi extraMounts ARE present on all five nodes, so the mount
exists but the tooling behind it does not — which is why this has been silent
since the schematics were edited on 2026-01-16.

ALSO: 'talosctl upgrade' defaults --image to the STOCK installer at the
CLIENT's version. Local client is v1.13.3, cluster runs v1.13.9 — a hand-typed
upgrade today would downgrade six patch releases AND strip every extension.
Covered by TALOS-ow7w.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
ERRATUM 2026-08-24 — correcting my own design comment above.

I claimed talos00 'still has install.disk: /dev/sda (the 1GB USB stick)'. FALSE. Verified with talosctl get disks: talos00 is a VM whose only real disk is a 266 GB virtio, and it has NO NVMe device. install.disk: /dev/sda is CORRECT on that node. The recommendation I gave (a fleet-wide nvme selector) would have matched nothing and broken a working control-plane config at its next reinstall.

The 1 GB USB stick was real but was on TALOS01, during its bare-metal rebuild.

ROOT CAUSE OF MY ERROR, worth recording because it is the same failure class this epic targets: I inherited the USB-stick premise from the task brief and reported it inside a table labelled 'measured', without running talosctl get disks — which I had access to the entire time. Disk identity is a per-machine fact and /dev/sda means only 'first block device the kernel enumerated'.

RULE FOR THIS EPIC: read 'talosctl get disks' for the specific node before changing its install target, every time. Never apply a uniform disk selector across a heterogeneous fleet.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, now fixed live: talos06 had install.wipe: true against a 1.0 TB NVMe (the real data-loss landmine), and install.image was stale on all five nodes with two pinned at v1.11.1 while running v1.13.9. All five now carry the correct installer at v1.13.9. The extension-stripping analysis that prompted that check stands.

Corrections applied to the doc and to TALOS-dnfy, TALOS-xxmd, TALOS-frvi, TALOS-v3wy.

title: Get all CNPG off NFS: local-path replicas + barman backups only
description:
DECISION (user, 2026-08-23): NO CNPG POSTGRES ON fatboy-nfs-appdata. Not "when possible" —
all of them. Local-path replicas plus barman backups is the pattern, full stop.

    storageClass: local-path
    instances: 3
    barman ObjectStore + ScheduledBackup for durability

## WHY
Every Postgres commit is a WAL fsync. On NFS that fsync is a network round trip to the
Synology. local-path is the Talos EPHEMERAL partition at /var — the node's NVMe. CNPG's own
guidance prefers local storage precisely because durability is supposed to come from
STREAMING REPLICATION + BACKUPS, not from the filesystem.

media/arr-postgres was the clearest case: instances:3 on NFS meant three replicas all
fsyncing to the SAME box — triple the write traffic, none of the speed, and no extra
resilience, since one NAS failure takes all three at once.

## HOW THIS HAPPENED — two wrong turns, both worth understanding
1. The rule "never instances:1 on local-path" is correct (a pinned PV with no replica
   strands the DB on a dead node). But the resolution is SCALE TO 3 ON LOCAL-PATH, not drop
   to NFS. Taking the wrong branch put 13 of 15 clusters on network storage.
2. A reclaimPolicy argument that was right about the wrong thing: fatboy-nfs-appdata carries
   Retain, local-path inherits Delete, so a new PV "has less protection". True for a
   SINGLE-COPY SQLite file. BACKWARDS for a replicated cluster — CNPG DELETES PVCs during
   normal operation (rolling migration, scale-down, failover recovery, instance
   replacement), so Retain strands an orphaned Released PV on every rebuild. There are
   already 14 such orphans cluster-wide (TALOS-nt01). Delete is CORRECT for CNPG.

## SCOPE — 13 clusters
DONE:
    authentik/authentik-postgres     local-path, instances:3
    boomtime/boomtime-postgres       local-path, instances:3
    media/arr-postgres               storageClass changed in git (d3a7a1a6); the rolling
                                     PVC migration still needs running

PURE storageClass CHANGE — already at instances:3:
    crowdsec/crowdsec-postgres
    forgejo/forgejo-postgres

NEED instances 1 -> 3 FIRST, then the storage move:
    catalyst-data/dagster-postgres        catalyst-data/postgres-knowledge
    media-experimental/bookorbit-postgres crossplane-demo/plausible-db
    gaming/guacamole-postgres             home-automation/homeassistant-postgres
    home-automation/linkwarden-postgres   media-private/zipline-postgres
    openscad/manyfold-postgres

CASE BY CASE:
    boomtime/books-postgres — the TALOS-1psu orphan, now adopted. CONFIRM its backups are
    genuinely working before moving it; it went months with none.

## PROCEDURE — proven twice with ZERO downtime, do not reinvent
applications/arr-stack/base/postgres/MIGRATION-RUNBOOK.md
Change storageClass in git, then delete ONE replica's pod+PVC at a time and let CNPG rebuild
it by streaming from the primary. Promote a migrated replica, then rebuild the old primary.
Works because CNPG manages PVCs directly rather than through a StatefulSet.

*** ORDER OF OPERATIONS for the instances:1 ones: SCALE TO 3 WHILE STILL ON NFS, THEN move
storage. Never pass through instances:1 on local-path — that state is strictly worse than
where we are now. ***

## THINGS TO GET RIGHT
 - Every cluster needs barman ObjectStore + ScheduledBackup BEFORE its storage moves.
   Local-path with no backup is a real downgrade; local-path with 3 replicas and barman is
   an upgrade. Verify per cluster rather than assuming.
 - Sister-repo clusters (boomtime, manyfold, books) live in their OWN repos — the change
   goes there, not in talos-homelab.
 - Moving a cluster onto local-path re-pins its nodes. That is FINE and expected: a reset
   node's replica rebuilds by streaming, which is the whole reason 3 instances makes
   local-path safe. But it interacts with EPIC 1 (TALOS-8tis) — be deliberate about
   sequencing, not accidental.
 - +2 pods per cluster for the nine at instances:1. Headroom exists (maxPods 110 -> 200,
   TALOS-d5b5) but watch the distribution.
 - The 14 orphaned Released PVs (TALOS-nt01) will grow as this proceeds. Same cleanup.

Related: [[cnpg-always-local-nvme]], TALOS-nt01, TALOS-1psu, EPIC 1 TALOS-8tis.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
## SEQUENCING DECISION (user, 2026-08-23): DO THIS AFTER THE UPGRADES
Blocked on EPIC 2b (TALOS-33jl), i.e. after the full chain:
    EPIC 0 node prep -> EPIC 1 CP 1->3 -> EPIC 2 Talos OS -> EPIC 2b Kubernetes -> THIS

WHY THAT ORDER:
 - Moving a cluster onto local-path RE-PINS the node holding each replica. Doing it before
   the promotions would add fresh pins to talos01 and talos03 immediately before those nodes
   get reset — self-defeating, since EPIC 0 exists precisely to clear them.
 - With 3 control planes and the OS/k8s upgrades done, the cluster is in its most stable
   configuration, and a node lost mid-migration is survivable rather than an outage.
 - CNPG replicas rebuild by streaming, so re-pinning after the promotions costs nothing:
   a reset node's replica just re-syncs. That property is why 3 instances makes local-path
   safe in the first place.

media/arr-postgres already has its storageClass changed in git (d3a7a1a6) but the rolling
PVC migration has NOT been run — it will happen as part of this ticket, not before.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
PLAN + PRE-FLIGHT, 2026-08-23.

INVENTORY — 15 CNPG clusters, 12 on fatboy-nfs-appdata:
  instances=3 (direct rolling migration):  crowdsec-postgres 5Gi, forgejo-postgres 10Gi
  instances=1 (MUST scale to 3 first):     books 2Gi, dagster 10Gi, postgres-knowledge 5Gi,
                                           plausible-db 2Gi, guacamole 2Gi, homeassistant 2Gi,
                                           linkwarden 5Gi, bookorbit 10Gi, zipline 2Gi,
                                           manyfold 10Gi
  already local-path (leave alone):        authentik, boomtime, arr-postgres (all 3/3)

CAPACITY VERIFIED (kubelet stats, not estimates) — 65Gi of claims x3 replicas = ~195Gi:
  talos03     1803 Gi avail (3% used)
  talos02-gpu 1244 Gi avail (35%)
  talos01      437 Gi avail (6%)
  talos06      176 Gi avail (81% used)  <-- WATCH THIS ONE, do not let replicas pile on it
  talos00      207 Gi avail but TAINTED by design, will not receive
Comfortable overall. talos06 is the only pressure point.

BACKUPS VERIFIED — 11 of 12 have a completed backup from this morning (02:00-04:00Z).
  gaming/guacamole-postgres has NO BACKUP AT ALL and no backup stanza configured.
  It is EXCLUDED from the migration until backup is added. Do not migrate a database
  whose only copy is the thing being moved.

ORDER: pilot on crowdsec-postgres first (3 instances already, small, non-critical, backed
up) so the procedure is proven on the cheapest possible target before forgejo (git hosting)
and before the 10 scale-then-migrate cases.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
PILOT COMPLETE — crowdsec-postgres is fully off NFS, zero downtime, 2026-08-23.

Final: instances 1/2/3 all local-path, on talos06/talos03/talos01 — three copies on three
nodes, so it is genuinely unpinned. 3/3 'Cluster in healthy state'. 12 tables verified
present via psql after the move.

## THE PROCEDURE THAT WORKS (use this for the remaining clusters)
  1. Change spec.storage.storageClass to local-path in git, commit, flux reconcile.
     This affects NEW PVCs only — CNPG never migrates an existing one.
  2. Read the primary: kubectl get cluster <c> -n <ns> -o jsonpath='{.status.currentPrimary}'
  3. For each NON-PRIMARY instance, ONE AT A TIME:
       kubectl delete job <instance>-join -n <ns> --wait=false   # see gotcha below
       kubectl delete pvc <instance>     -n <ns> --wait=false
       kubectl delete pod <instance>     -n <ns> --force --grace-period=0
     Wait for readyInstances to return to full before the next one.
  4. kubectl cnpg promote <cluster> <a-migrated-instance> -n <ns>
  5. Repeat step 3 on the FORMER primary.

## THINGS THAT SURPRISED ME, WORTH KNOWING BEFORE THE NEXT ELEVEN
 - CNPG DOES NOT REUSE THE INSTANCE NUMBER. Deleting instance 3 produced instance 1 (the
   lowest free number), not another 3. So do not wait for '<cluster>-3' to reappear — watch
   readyInstances and the PVC list instead, or you will conclude it hung when it did not.
 - Deleting the JOB alongside the pod and PVC is REQUIRED, not defensive. A leftover
   Complete '<instance>-join' Job makes CNPG skip re-bootstrapping, the new PVC stays empty,
   and the instance CrashLoops on 'stat /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata: no such file or
   directory'. That is what TALOS-y5wb was.
 - readyInstances briefly reports FULL immediately after the delete, before the operator
   notices. Poll a few cycles rather than trusting the first reading.
 - The promote logs 'Cluster has become unhealthy' as it switches over. That is the
   expected transient, not a failure — it returned to 3/3 on the next poll.

## REMAINING: 11 clusters
 direct (already 3 instances):  forgejo-postgres 10Gi
 scale-to-3 first (10):         books, dagster, postgres-knowledge, plausible-db,
                                homeassistant, linkwarden, bookorbit, zipline, manyfold
 EXCLUDED until backup exists:  gaming/guacamole-postgres — still has NO backup at all.

Watch talos06: it was at 81% disk before this and took the new primary.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
PROGRESS 2026-08-23: 10 of 15 CNPG clusters FULLY off NFS — spec AND actual PVCs, all 3/3.

  authentik-postgres        3/3  (was already)
  boomtime-postgres         3/3  (was already)
  arr-postgres              3/3  <- spec said local-path since an earlier session but the
                                    PVCs had NEVER been migrated; done now
  crowdsec-postgres         3/3  <- pilot
  forgejo-postgres          3/3
  plausible-db              3/3  <- scaled 1 -> 3
  homeassistant-postgres    3/3  <- scaled 1 -> 3
  linkwarden-postgres       3/3  <- scaled 1 -> 3
  bookorbit-postgres        3/3  <- scaled 1 -> 3
  zipline-postgres          3/3  <- scaled 1 -> 3

Zero downtime throughout. forgejo answered 200 at every step. sonarr/radarr/prowlarr stayed
Running with 0 restarts across the arr-postgres move, and the data was verified AFTER it:
sonarr 845 series + 36,786 history rows, radarr 5,393 movies, prowlarr 5 indexers, table
counts 38/41/20. That is the SQLite-migrated data intact on new storage.

## REMAINING 5, AND WHY EACH IS NOT DONE
 gaming/guacamole-postgres — BLOCKED ON BACKUP. Still has no completed backup and no backup
   stanza at all. Do not migrate a database whose only copy is the thing being moved. Add
   an ObjectStore + ScheduledBackup first, take one backup, verify it completed, then
   migrate. This is the only one blocked on a real prerequisite.

 boomtime/books-postgres, catalyst-data/dagster-postgres, catalyst-data/postgres-knowledge,
 openscad/manyfold-postgres — NOT THIS REPO'S TO CHANGE. All four are ArgoCD-managed from
   sister repos (tracking-ids boomtime:, catalyst-data:, openscad:). Editing them means
   working in those repos, which carries the branch trap that caused an accidental PR merge
   on 2026-08-21: ALWAYS run 'git branch --show-current' first and verify the push against
   the branch you actually pushed to, not reflexively origin/main.

## NOTE FOR WHOEVER DOES THE REMAINING FOUR
They are all instances: 1. Change storageClass to local-path AND instances to 3 in the SAME
commit — a single instance on local-path is stranded by a node loss and is strictly worse
than NFS. Then follow the procedure recorded earlier on this ticket.

title: dbgate showed placeholder databases: connection sync keyed on initdb, ignored Database CRs
description:
USER-REPORTED: dbgate cannot really open the arr database.

ROOT CAUSE: dbgate-connection-sync built exactly one connection per CNPG Cluster and
took the database name from spec.bootstrap.initdb.database. Multi-tenant clusters
follow the placeholder-bootstrap pattern - bootstrap a throwaway database purely so
CNPG mints the -app secret, then declare the real tenants as Database CRs. Those
Database CRs were invisible to the sync script, so dbgate connected to the empty
placeholder. It connects fine and shows nothing, which is why it reads as broken
rather than as a misconfiguration.

VERIFIED BEFORE THE FIX:
  media/arr-postgres          DATABASE_arr = arrstack     -> 0 tables
    real data in prowlarr-main, prowlarr-log, radarr-main, radarr-log,
    sonarr-main, sonarr-log - NONE had a dbgate connection
  catalyst-data/dagster-postgres    dagsterapp  -> 0 tables (real: dagster)
  catalyst-data/postgres-knowledge  kgapp       -> 0 tables (real: knowledge_graph)

The arr instance predates TALOS-zjh0; the catalyst-data ones were introduced by it,
copying the arr pattern. Same defect, one fix.

FIX: the per-cluster database list is now the UNION of the initdb database and every
Database CR pointing at that cluster, one dbgate connection each. Union rather than
preferring Database CRs because there is no reliable way to tell a placeholder from a
legitimately-used initdb database - showing one empty extra entry beats hiding one
that holds data.

Connection ids are unchanged for single-database clusters so existing dbgate state is
not renamed; only multi-database clusters gain a db suffix (arr_prowlarr_main etc).
Labels now read cluster/db (namespace).

Also hardened: refuse to publish an empty connection set, and degrade to initdb-only
if the Database CRs cannot be listed, rather than blanking dbgate.

Needed RBAC: databases added to the dbgate-connection-sync ClusterRole.

Dry-run against live cluster: 15 connections -> 23.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
FIXED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-22. talos-homelab 70e6cfe7 (per-database connections) and e740ffb8 (secret pruning). Flux applied, sync job run, dbgate rolled.

dbgate went from 15 connections to 23. Functionally tested with the exact
credentials dbgate uses, over the -rw services:
  arr-postgres/prowlarr-main      20 tables
  arr-postgres/sonarr-main        38 tables
  postgres-knowledge/knowledge_graph  6 tables
  dagster-postgres/dagster        22 tables
Previously all four of those were unreachable and the user instead got an empty
arrstack / kgapp / dagsterapp.

SECOND BUG FOUND WHILE FIXING THE FIRST, fixed in e740ffb8. Renaming the
connection ids exposed that the generated Secret could never shed keys: it was
written with stringData, the API server rewrites stringData into data, so
kubectl apply's last-applied tracked stringData while the live object held data.
The computed deletion targeted a field that does not exist on the live object and
the real key survived. After the first fix the secret carried 26 connection ids
against 23 in CONNECTIONS. Inert - dbgate only loads ids listed in CONNECTIONS -
but it accumulated stale passwords and would have grown on every future rename.
Now emits data: with base64 values so the three-way merge prunes. Final state
verified: 162 keys = 1 + 23 x 7, zero orphans.

Hardened while in there: refuse to publish an empty connection set, and fall back
to initdb-only if the Database CRs cannot be listed, so a transient API error
degrades instead of blanking dbgate.

Single-database clusters kept their original connection ids on purpose, so no
existing dbgate state was renamed. Labels now read cluster/db (namespace).

NOTE the placeholder databases arrstack, kgapp and dagsterapp still appear as
their own (empty) connections. Deliberate: nothing reliably distinguishes a
placeholder from a legitimately-used initdb database, and showing an empty extra
entry beats hiding one that holds data.

title: clickstack-app running with a stale MONGO_URI: continuous SCRAM auth failures, HyperDX has no persisted state
description:
Found during the MongoDB migration audit (docs/02-architecture/mongodb-migration-audit.md section 5). NOT a migration issue.

SYMPTOM: deploy/clickstack-app logs MongoServerError: Authentication failed (code 18) continuously -- 114 occurrences in the last 2000 log lines, from both the [API] and [ALERT-TASK] processes. Readiness stays green because /health does not touch Mongo.

SERVER SIDE: clickstack-mongodb-0 mongod logs the precise reason for client 10.244.4.102 (the clickstack-app pod):
  AuthenticationFailed: SCRAM authentication failed, storedKey mismatch
The metrics sidecar and the mongod pod itself authenticate successfully as the SAME hyperdx user in the same log window, so the server-side credential is fine.

VERIFIED CAUSE: the password inside cm/clickstack-app-config MONGO_URI MATCHES the current ESO-generated secret, so the rendered config is correct. But the RUNNING POD's injected MONGO_URI password does NOT. The chart delivers MONGO_URI via envFrom.configMapRef, which is evaluated once at pod start. The ConfigMap was re-rendered when the ESO Password generator regenerated (secret creationTimestamp 2026-08-20T22:58Z, i.e. the mongo migration itself); the Deployment pod spec did not change, so Helm never rolled the pods. The pod has been running the pre-rotation credential for two days.

CONSEQUENCE: the hyperdx database is 11 collections and ZERO documents -- no teams, users, sources, dashboards or alerts have ever persisted since the migration.

FIX: kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deploy/clickstack-app

STOP IT RECURRING: the HelmRelease needs a checksum annotation on the pod template derived from the credential, or MONGO_URI needs to come from a secretKeyRef the kubelet can refresh. This is the eso-generator-rotation gotcha with a new tail: even when Flux DOES re-render the consumer ConfigMap correctly, an envFrom consumer never picks it up. Any future MongoDBCommunity wired the same way inherits this.

NOT VERIFIED: why the failures are intermittent rather than total -- the interleaved 'Connection established' lines may just be mongoose topology events rather than successful operations. Does not change the fix.

title: Migrate catalyst-data hand-rolled Postgres -> CNPG (postgres-knowledge + dagster-postgres)
description:
Two hand-rolled Postgres Deployments in catalyst-data on local-path PVs pinned to talos06 (recovery PVs from the 2026-05-09 UPS incident, 1Ti claims).

MEASURED 2026-08-22 (namespace parked at 0/0):
  postgres-knowledge  207 MB datadir / 105 MB db / 6 tables / 14610 rows / pgvector 0.8.2 + pg_trgm
  dagster-postgres    493 MB datadir / 437 MB db / 22 tables / 443075 rows / plpgsql only (NO pgvector)

pgvector complication resolved WITHOUT ImageVolume: the CNPG operand variant
ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:18.4-standard-trixie ships pgvector 0.8.6 + pg_trgm.
ImageVolume extensions were ruled out - they need PostgreSQL 18 AND the ImageVolume
feature gate, which is OFF in this cluster (kubernetes_feature_enabled{name=ImageVolume}=0
at k8s 1.34) and enabling it would mean a Talos machine-config change plus rolling
reboots across all five nodes.

Manifests live in the SISTER repo catalyst-data.git under k8s/base/platform/,
reconciled by the ArgoCD catalyst-data Application. Old Deployments and PVCs stay
in place scaled to 0 as the rollback - deletion is user-gated.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
VERIFIED 2026-08-22. Both CNPG clusters healthy on fatboy-nfs-appdata, PostgreSQL 18.4 via ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:18.4-standard-trixie.

MEASURED vs THE 1Ti CLAIM
  postgres-knowledge  207 MB datadir / 105 MB db  -> new PVC 5Gi
  dagster-postgres    493 MB datadir / 437 MB db  -> new PVC 10Gi
Roughly 0.02 and 0.04 percent of the inherited claim. The 1Ti came from the
2026-05-09 UPS-incident recovery PVs, not from any real requirement.

pgvector: postgres-knowledge YES (canonical_entities.embedding, ivfflat, plus
pg_trgm). dagster-postgres NO - it ran postgres:16-alpine and pg_extension held
only plpgsql. Confirmed on the live source before planning.

ImageVolume extensions were ruled out, not skipped: they need PostgreSQL 18 AND
the ImageVolume feature gate, and the gate is off here. Proved it rather than
assuming - an image volume is silently pruned from the pod spec and
kubernetes_feature_enabled{name=ImageVolume} reports 0 at k8s 1.34. The CNPG
standard operand variant already carries pgvector, so none of that was needed.
CREATE EXTENSION vector reports 0.8.6 in the destination against the source 0.8.2.

EXACT count(*) per table, source vs destination - all match:
  knowledge_graph  6 tables  14610 rows
  dagster         22 tables 443075 rows (event_logs 323779)
Went further than counts: per-table content checksums match on every table in
both databases, and the 3301 embeddings hash byte-identical
(md5 b05f80e98c7563b73d16e6a66a318026) across the PG16 to PG18 jump. An ivfflat
cosine query returns sane neighbours. Table ownership intact (kg, dagster), and
the CNPG app-secret credentials authenticate over the -rw services.

Caught mid-flight: CNPG initdb defaults to the C locale while both sources ran
en_US.utf8, which would have silently changed text sort order - including the
ORDER BY behind canonical_name and the pg_trgm search index. Fixed by pinning
localeCollate/localeCType and recreating both clusters while still empty.

Note for the record: the source dagster ran on alpine/musl, whose en_US.utf8
collates like C. The destination now uses real glibc en_US.utf8, so text ORDER BY
in dagster genuinely differs from the source. Chosen deliberately - it matches
the locale the database always claimed, matches postgres-knowledge and matches
the fleet. Indexes were rebuilt on restore, so there is no collation-mismatch
corruption risk.

Also noticed: the postgres-knowledge init.sql ConfigMap is stale. It declares
vector(768) but the live column is vector(1536), and its speaker_profiles tables
never existed. Managing extensions on the Database CR instead of that ConfigMap
is the right call.

Pre-migration dumps, sha256-verified end to end and round-tripped out of MinIO:
  s3://backups/catalyst-data-premigration-2026-08-22/
  knowledge_graph.dump f6db5f1f8277c91747ce79027b9d0d8b339f4cfa72044c93411935bc9233ec6b
  dagster.dump         55971ad9259c84d06a0887cf7c97cfbf626927dc2b8c99ee24a89fb315f23429
  plus both globals-only role dumps

Commits: catalyst-data 0d6db27 and ee0695e; talos-homelab 2c69aa30.
OUTSTANDING: backups fail until TALOS-yx5n lands. Cleanup of the old
Deployments/PVCs is user-gated in TALOS-qrna.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
COMPLETE 2026-08-22. Both blockers closed:
  TALOS-yx5n backups now verified working (base backups + WAL in MinIO)
  TALOS-clz4 dbgate now opens knowledge_graph and dagster, not the placeholders

Final state: two CNPG clusters healthy on fatboy-nfs-appdata, PostgreSQL 18.4,
pgvector 0.8.6, en_US.utf8 collation matching source, all 28 tables verified
byte-identical by content checksum, backups running daily. All 11 app Deployments
still parked at 0/0 as they were before this work.

Remaining: TALOS-qrna, deleting the superseded Deployments and their 1Ti
local-path PVCs. USER-GATED, deliberately not done. Note that until it happens
talos06 is still pinned - this work added node-independent storage but has not
yet removed the old pin.

title: Decide SPIRE: keep and back up, or disable (deprecated, unused, 1Ti pin on talos03)
description:
Decide what happens to cilium-spire/spire-data-spire-server-0 (1Ti claim, local-path,
talos03) before that node is reset. It is one of only two remaining pins on talos03.

## THE AUDIT SAYS THIS IS A DELETE CANDIDATE, NOT A MIGRATION CANDIDATE
docs/02-architecture/embedded-db-migration-audit.md §3: moving SPIRE's datastore to Postgres
would NOT EVEN REMOVE THE PVC (it holds keys.json alongside the SQLite), and the mutual-auth
feature it backs is DEPRECATED in the Cilium version this cluster runs.

So the real question is not "how do we migrate it" but "do we need it at all". Determine:
 1. Is Cilium mutual authentication actually enabled and in use? The audit found no policy
    using it — verify that independently.
 2. If nothing uses it, is disabling spire the right move? That removes a StatefulSet, a
    1Ti claim, the pin, and 5 spire-agent DaemonSet pods.
 3. If it stays, what does losing the PV cost? Are workload identities reconstructible on
    restart, or does it invalidate them cluster-wide?

## RELEVANT HISTORY
spire-agent has a known fragility in this cluster: a kubelet restart can wedge its projected
SA token into a self-perpetuating expired-token CrashLoopBackOff (seen 2026-08-22 after the
maxPods patch restarted kubelet on all 5 nodes; fix was deleting the agent pods for fresh
tokens). The SA token TTL was already raised to 3600s via a HelmRelease postRenderer for
this reason. If the component is not earning its keep, that is a recurring operational cost
for nothing.

Deliverable: a recommendation with evidence — keep and back up, or disable and remove.
Do not act on it unilaterally; this touches cluster-wide workload identity.
notes:
EXECUTED 2026-08-22 on user approval. Cilium mutual auth / SPIRE is disabled and removed.

## COMMITS (all on origin/main)
- 9ce8e807 — authentication.enabled and authentication.mutual.spire.enabled -> false;
  all four postRenderer patches removed; spire-namespace.yaml deleted, replaced by
  kube-system-namespace.yaml.
- 17293ed1 — dead artifact references removed from kustomizations + disposition doc updated.
- 688b401d — the five dead files deleted (spire cronjob, spire-alerts, spire-health
  dashboard CR + JSON, scripts/test-suspect-spire-health.sh).

ROLLBACK: git revert 9ce8e807 then flux reconcile kustomization cilium --with-source.
Two booleans. Identities re-register automatically so a revert costs minutes, not data.

## PRE-COMMIT VERIFICATION
Rendered chart v1.20.0 with the real values file both ways and diffed resource sets:
63 -> 47, exactly the 16 predicted resources removed, 0 added. Only content changes among
the 47 survivors were cilium-config and the spire-agent-socket volume leaving the two pod
templates. kustomize build resource set identical to HEAD (the Namespace object renders
byte-identically).

## CNI HEALTH — BEFORE (01:01Z) vs AFTER (01:24Z)
  cilium-agent pods Running    5/5            -> 5/5, all rolled, 0 restarts
  cilium status --brief         OK x5         -> OK x5
  Controller Status             64/64 healthy -> 552/552 healthy
  Modules Health                Degraded(0)   -> Degraded(0)
  Cluster health                5/5 reachable -> 5/5 reachable, all endpoints 1/1
  Nodes Ready                   5/5           -> 5/5
  Pods ContainerCreating        0             -> 0
  agent level=error last 60s    -              -> 0 on all 5 nodes
  CiliumNetworkPolicies         6             -> 6
  CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicies 0          -> 0
  policies referencing authentication 0       -> 0
  CiliumIdentities              289           -> 290 (stable; meltdown signature is >1000)

Ingress verified end to end: grafana.talos00 200, argocd.talos00 200 (via TLS redirect),
hubble.talos00 302 -> authentik -> 200.

Agents now log "Spire Delegate API Client is disabled as no socket path is configured".

## TWO THINGS THE INVESTIGATION DID NOT PREDICT
1. spire-namespace.yaml never created cilium-spire. The kustomization sets
   namespace: kube-system and kustomize's namespace transformer REWRITES metadata.name on
   Namespace objects, so that file rendered as Namespace/kube-system with the PSA
   privileged labels (live kube-system carries kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/name: cilium).
   The chart created cilium-spire all along. Replaced with kube-system-namespace.yaml,
   byte-identical output. Label is inert anyway: kube-system is in the apiserver PSA
   exemptions.namespaces list.
2. Server-Side Apply field-ownership residue blocked Flux from finishing. See the new
   ticket filed for this - it is not SPIRE-specific and 9 unrelated stale cilium-config
   keys are still in effect on the running agents.

## WHAT REMAINED
- PV rec-cilium-spire-spire-data-spire-server-0 is Released, not deleted. recovery/ is NOT
  Flux-managed so removing the git entry cannot delete the live object. Needs one manual
  command, blocked on operator approval: kubectl delete pv rec-cilium-spire-spire-data-spire-server-0
  talos03 is at 14 node-bound PVs until then, 13 after.
- Namespace cilium-spire is Terminating and empty. Blocked by an unrelated CDI aggregated-API
  discovery failure, filed separately.
close_reason: Executed on user approval. Cilium mutual auth / SPIRE disabled and removed; CNI verified healthy on all 5 nodes before and after. Commits 9ce8e807, 17293ed1, 688b401d on origin/main. Two follow-ups filed: TALOS-bedw (SSA field-ownership residue on the Cilium objects) and TALOS-127n (CDI discovery failure blocking namespace deletion). One manual command remains for the Released PV, tracked on TALOS-3gte.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
RECOMMENDATION: DISABLE AND REMOVE. Full evidence in docs/02-architecture/cilium-spire-disposition.md

All four audit claims verified independently against the live cluster; all hold, and the cost side is worse than the ticket assumed.

1. IS IT USED? No. 6 CiliumNetworkPolicies (honeypot + iocaine, plain L3/L4), 0 CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicies, and ZERO references to authentication in any of them. The CRD field does exist (cnp.spec.egress.authentication.mode, enum disabled|required|test-always-fail), so this is a real absence not a naming miss. Capability is on in cilium-config (mesh-auth-mutual-enabled=true) but no policy consumes it. No SPIRE/SPIFFE CRDs installed; the only pods mounting a spire hostPath are Cilium's own.

2. DEPRECATED? Yes, in the exact version we run. Live: quay.io/cilium/cilium:v1.20.0 (confirmed from the DS image and 'cilium version'). Verbatim from the v1.20.0 chart values.yaml, directly above the mutual: key: 'Deprecated as of Cilium v1.20, this feature will be removed in Cilium v1.21.' cilium#47132 (open, 2026-07-13) confirms: Beta since 2023, never left Beta, security support explicitly limited, superseded by zTunnel.

3. WHAT WOULD DISABLING REMOVE? Rendered the real chart at the real version with the real values file, both ways, and diffed. Both render cleanly (turning BOTH authentication.enabled and mutual.spire.enabled off passes validation). 16 resources removed, 0 added: spire-server StatefulSet, spire-agent DaemonSet (5 pods), Service, 3 ConfigMaps, 2 ServiceAccounts, Role + 2 RoleBindings, 2 ClusterRoles + 2 ClusterRoleBindings, the cilium-spire Namespace. Plus 8 mesh-auth-* keys drop from cilium-config and mesh-auth-enabled flips false. No CRDs involved. NOT removed automatically: the PVC (STS retention is Retain/Retain), the PV (reclaim Retain -> goes Released; THIS is the talos03 pin), and the namespace (spire-namespace.yaml is a standalone resource in kustomization.yaml).

4. IF IT STAYS, WHAT DOES LOSING THE PV COST? Almost nothing - this is the crux and it resolves the question. The datastore is DERIVED STATE. cilium-operator logged 258 'Upsert identity' events in its first minute on last startup against 265 live CiliumIdentities - a full reconcile, not a delta replay. Source of truth is the CiliumIdentity CRs in etcd. All 5 agents report 'Can re-attest: true'. keys.json regenerates as a new CA and the Notifier k8sbundle plugin republishes the trust bundle into the spire-bundle ConfigMap automatically. Cost of losing the PV = one re-attestation cycle plus a rollout restart of ds/spire-agent. So the PV is accept-the-loss EVEN IN THE KEEP CASE - there is no backup worth taking.

5. RISK OF DISABLING? Nothing fails closed. Mutual auth is enforced per-policy via authentication.mode: required; with zero such policies, no traffic decision anywhere consults SPIRE. The honeypot/iocaine default-deny-all policies deny on L3/L4 and are unaffected. The REAL risk is unrelated to SPIRE: disabling removes the spire-agent-socket volume from the cilium DaemonSet and cilium-operator Deployment, so the CNI DaemonSet rolls across all 5 nodes. That is the window to plan around, given this repo's 2026-05-29 history.

NEW FINDING - THE DURABLE FIX DID NOT HOLD, AND CANNOT
The KeyManager-disk-on-emptyDir fix (commit ab933026, 2026-08-09) plus the 3600s SA token TTL were both live - confirmed present in ControllerRevision 12 (2026-08-09T14:33) and still in current revision 20. The wedge recurred anyway on 2026-08-21 23:40 on at least talos03 and talos06: 'Could not reattest agent ... service account token has expired', running until the agent pods were manually recreated at 2026-08-22T00:49:45. cilium-operator was disconnected from the Workload API that whole window.

Why it cannot hold: the emptyDir fix assumed re-attestation is cold-start-only. It is not. spire-server logs a steady 10-13 completed AttestAgent (k8s_psat) requests per hour cluster-wide, measured over the last 22h with ZERO pod restarts - 5 agents each doing a full node re-attestation roughly every 30 minutes, indefinitely. Every one reads the projected SA token and hits TokenReview. The token is permanently on the hot path, so an emptyDir surviving container restarts cannot take it off. This recurs on every kubelet restart, i.e. every node upgrade in EPIC 2 (TALOS-xipf, TALOS-y7q1, TALOS-33jl).

SIDE FINDING - THE 1Ti IS COSMETIC
PVC requests 1Gi; the 1Ti comes from a hand-written recovery PV (recovery/pv-recovery-2026-05-09.yaml, ups-2026-05-09 incident) on hostPath local-path with no quota. Real contents measured via talosctl on talos03: 14.5 MB total (datastore.sqlite3 10.2MB, wal 4.2MB, shm 32KB, journal.pem 29KB, keys.json 12KB). The node-bound PV is the whole problem; capacity is a red herring. This also independently confirms the audit's first reason - keys.json sits on the SAME volume as the SQLite, so a Postgres migration would not remove the PVC or un-pin talos03.

BOTTOM LINE
No single finding carries this. Independently: unused, deprecated with a removal date, state is reconstructible so there is nothing to protect, nothing fails closed, and it generates recurring toil the attempted fix demonstrably did not stop. There is no scenario where keeping it pays off, because v1.21 removes it regardless. Removing it clears one of two remaining talos03 pins and unblocks TALOS-3gte.

Step-by-step execution plan (values change, kustomization + 3 postRenderer patch removals, reconcile --with-source, watch the DS roll, then the manual PVC/PV/namespace cleanup that Flux will NOT do because prune:false) is in section 8 of the doc. NOT EXECUTED - user's call.

Also flagged: docs/02-architecture/service-mesh.md still instructs the reader to ENABLE this feature with a require-mtls policy example. That would walk someone into a removed feature and into the cilium#46392 fail-closed deadlock. Marked with a caution in the section README; a proper rewrite is out of scope here.

title: Back up + restore the 12 media-experimental configs (tar job, not a DB migration)
description:
Un-pin talos03 by getting the 12 media-experimental config PVCs off local-path.

## THIS IS A TAR JOB, NOT A DATABASE MIGRATION AND NOT AN NFS MOVE
The embedded-DB audit (docs/02-architecture/embedded-db-migration-audit.md §4) settled this:
~67 MB of real data across 60Gi of claims. Twelve Postgres migrations would be absurd for
that.

*** AND NFS IS THE WRONG ANSWER — this cluster already ran that experiment and failed it. ***
9 of the 12 configs hold SQLite. The arr stack previously ran its SQLite on NFS, hit locking
problems, and was migrated OFF NFS onto local-path. The evidence is still on disk
(/config/radarr.db.nfs-backup, dated 2025-12-20) and the reason is written into
applications/arr-stack/base/shared/db-migration-configmap.yaml: "to avoid NFS locking issues
with SQLite". Do not re-run it.

## THE APPROACH
Back up -> reset the node -> restore. Concretely:
 1. A Job that tars each config dir to MinIO (or the NFS appdata share) with a verified
    manifest of what was captured and its checksum.
 2. Confirm the archive is complete and restorable BEFORE the node is touched. An untested
    restore is not a backup — this is the single most important step.
 3. After the node comes back, a restore Job repopulates the fresh local-path PVCs.
Write it as a repeatable pair of Jobs in git, not a one-off shell session — this same
pattern will be wanted for any future node reset.

## ALSO IN SCOPE
7 of these workloads (kavita, komga, libation, librarr, livrarr, mylar3, storyteller) also
carry their OWN nodeAffinity blocks, independent of the PV. Sonarr proved that removing the
volume alone leaves the pod welded to the node while every check reports green. Check both
pins, and verify each affinity's justification against the running cluster rather than
trusting its comment — sonarr's comment was flatly false.

Affects EPIC 3 (TALOS-3hl8) as well as this one.
close_reason:
Backup/restore pair built, deployed and PROVEN. applications/media-experimental/base/backup/ ships three suspended CronJobs sharing one pair of scripts (config-backup, config-restore, config-restore-verify), archives to fatboy-nfs-appdata (NOT MinIO: MinIO's own data0 PVC is on the same NAS, so S3 adds a hop and an ESO-rotated credential for zero extra durability).

MEASURED (by the job, not estimated): 161 files, 62,998,382 bytes across the 12 volumes, 18.5 MB compressed, 76s for the whole stack. bindery-config settled at last - the audit had it unverified (distroless, no shell); mounting the PVC shows one 600 KB bindery.db, SQLite, stays on local-path.

PROOF: backup run 20260823T010514Z status=OK 12/12; verify job restored all 12 into fresh generic-ephemeral local-path PVCs and reported 12 passed, 0 failed - every file's sha256 plus uid/gid/mode matching capture time. No live PVC touched; test artifacts deleted (0 leftover PVCs, all 12 deployments 1/1).

Running it found four real defects a never-executed manifest would have hidden until the reset: capabilities drop ALL removed DAC_OVERRIDE from uid 0 (tar got Permission denied AS ROOT on mode-0600 files and short-archived); set -e is inert inside a function used as an if condition so tar errors were discarded; the self-verify compared two derivatives of the same read so a truncated archive reported OK; and dropping ALL also removed CAP_CHOWN so restores landed everything as 0:0. All fixed and re-verified.

SQLite handled by quiescing each Deployment to 0 one at a time and waiting for pod termination; a volume that cannot be quiesced is skipped, not tarred live. Flux reverts spec.replicas on reconcile, so the wait loop re-asserts every 5s.

AFFINITY AUDIT (also EPIC 3 / TALOS-3hl8): the premise of 7 per-app blocks is wrong - there is exactly ONE nodeAffinity, in base/_instance/deployment.yaml, inherited identically by all 11 Deployments. Verified live: no nodeSelector, toleration, hostPath, hostNetwork or device request anywhere, so the config PVC is the only node tie. librarr is the only cross-app reference (qbittorrent Service DNS; qbittorrent runs on talos06), so a sonarr-style co-location claim would be false here too. Not bogus, but it was hard-coded to talos03 - an independent pin that outlives the volume, exactly the sonarr trap. Now MEDIA_EXPERIMENTAL_NODE from cluster-settings (default talos03, no rollout), read by both the Deployments and the restore Job.

libation-config (750 bytes JSON) and audiobookshelf-metadata (2 log files) hold no DB and could move to NFS; deliberately not done - 2 of 12 does not un-pin the node.

The actual restore into the real PVCs executes during the reset under TALOS-3gte. Runbook: applications/media-experimental/base/backup/README.md

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
RESTORE PATH RE-EXERCISED AND RECORDED 2026-08-23 (gap closed).

The earlier proof was real but its Jobs were deleted as test cleanup, so nothing in the cluster showed the restore had ever run. Re-ran both halves and committed the verbatim output to applications/media-experimental/base/backup/README.md (commit b201c6fc), since Job history is TTL'd after 24h and a README section is the durable artifact.

Backup 20260823T010514Z, VERIFY=full: status=OK, 12/12, 161 files, 62,998,382 bytes, 76s.
Restore into fresh generic-ephemeral PVCs (12 throwaway local-path claims, created empty with the pod and deleted with it): 12 passed, 0 failed. No live config PVC written to. Scratch PVCs and Jobs deleted; 0 leftovers, all 12 deployments 1/1.

Improved restore.sh first: the ownership check printed only on mismatch, so a pass proved ownership by silence - useless evidence for the exact defect this path had. It now reports either way with a uid:gid histogram.

OWNERSHIP RESULT, and the obvious assertion is WRONG: kavita, komga, audiobookshelf and libation are root-owned AT THE SOURCE - those containers run as root - confirmed straight from the live pods independently of the archive (kavita 66 0:0, komga 21 0:0, audiobookshelf 18 0:0; storyteller 9, mylar3 23, chaptarr 20 all 1000:1000). So the property proven is that restore reproduces captured ownership EXACTLY over a mixed source. The CAP_CHOWN fix is proven by the volumes that are 1000:1000 - chaptarr 16/16, livrarr 28/28, mylar3 23/23, storyteller 9/9, booksonic 31/34, librarr 2/3, bindery 1/2 - all of which came back 0:0 before the fix. A blanket 'everything must be 1000:1000' check would fail four healthy volumes.

bindery-config IS covered by the test. The audit's unverified caveat was about the distroless image having no shell; both jobs mount the PVC directly and never enter the app container. One 600 KB bindery.db, SQLite, PASS on checksum and ownership.

Still unproven by design: restore into the REAL config PVCs. That writes live app data and executes during the reset under TALOS-3gte, through the same restore.sh.

nodeAffinity: per team-lead review, the 11 pins are honest (local-path because SQLite) and are NOT being removed. Only the hard-coded hostname was parameterised to MEDIA_EXPERIMENTAL_NODE so both halves of the pin move together at reset time. bookorbit is the exemplar of the alternative - opts out of _instance entirely, the one media-experimental deployment not on talos03.

title: Move forgejo-data off local-path (LAST talos01 blocker, 156 KB in a 20Gi PVC)
description:
Un-pin talos01 by moving forgejo-data off local-path. This is the LAST item blocking
talos01 — everything else pinning it is self-healing (2 CNPG replicas rebuild by streaming,
4 Mimir PVs are S3-authoritative cache, pihole-1 is re-seeded by nebula-sync within 300s).

## THE ABSURDITY THAT MAKES THIS EASY
forgejo-data is a 20Gi PVC holding 156 KB. Forgejo's DATABASE is already on CNPG
(forgejo-postgres) — this volume holds only the remaining on-disk bits. Verify the current
size yourself before sizing the replacement; do not inherit 20Gi.

## THE WORK
Move it to fatboy-nfs-appdata (node-independent), or justify a different target. Forgejo
holds git repositories, so check what is actually in that directory before assuming NFS is
fine — if it turns out to hold a SQLite file, NFS is the wrong answer for the same reason
the arr stack was moved OFF NFS (see applications/arr-stack/base/shared/db-migration-configmap.yaml,
which exists "to avoid NFS locking issues with SQLite"). At 156 KB it almost certainly does
not, but check rather than assume.

Procedure: scale forgejo to 0, copy the data (a Job mounting both PVCs), repoint the PVC in
git, scale back up, verify forgejo serves and its repos are intact.

## VERIFY
 - forgejo UI loads, repositories present, a git clone/push works
 - no PV backing forgejo carries nodeAffinity
 - forgejo can schedule off talos01 — prove it with a temporary NotIn affinity patch rather
   than cordoning the node (see applications/arr-stack/base/postgres/MIGRATION-RUNBOOK.md)

KEEP THE OLD PVC until validated — the user gates its removal, as with the three arr apps.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
Migration complete and verified 2026-08-23; old PVC retained pending human validation.

NO SQLite — /data/gitea/gitea.db does not exist and app.ini has DB_TYPE=postgres, so the NFS locking objection that moved the arr stack off NFS does not apply. comments.text:
## CORRECTION (2026-08-23) — media-experimental is NOT an NFS move
This ticket originally suggested "local-path -> NFS" for the 12 media-experimental configs.
That is wrong, and the embedded-DB audit had already settled it before this was filed:
docs/02-architecture/embedded-db-migration-audit.md section 4.

9 of the 12 configs hold SQLite. This cluster has ALREADY run the SQLite-on-NFS experiment
and failed it: the arr stack ran its SQLite on NFS, hit locking problems, and was migrated
OFF NFS onto local-path. The artifact is still on disk (/config/radarr.db.nfs-backup, dated
2025-12-20) and the reason is written into
applications/arr-stack/base/shared/db-migration-configmap.yaml — it exists "to avoid NFS
locking issues with SQLite". Moving these to NFS would re-run a known failure.

The correct approach is a TAR JOB: ~67 MB of real data across 60Gi of claims. Back up ->
reset the node -> restore. Tracked in TALOS-uml1, which this now depends on.

SPIRE is tracked separately in TALOS-1d4o, and the audit's finding there is that it is a
DELETE candidate rather than a migration candidate — moving its datastore to Postgres would
not even remove the PVC (keys.json sits alongside the SQLite), and the mutual-auth feature
is deprecated in the Cilium version running here.

pihole-4 is the 14th pin and needs no work: nebula-sync re-seeds a replacement instance
within 300s.

So this ticket is the talos03 TRACKING item; the actual work is its two dependencies.

title: Drop db-local volume mounts from radarr + sonarr (finish the un-node-binding)

  - delete the <app>-db-local PVC (and the retained rec-media-<app>-db-local PV)

title: Migrate prowlarr SQLite -> CNPG Postgres (FIRST — smallest blast radius)
description:
Un-node-bind prowlarr by moving it off the local-path SQLite PV onto CNPG.

DO THIS ONE FIRST. Its DB is 1Gi (vs 2Gi for radarr/sonarr) and the failure mode is losing
indexer definitions — recoverable by re-adding indexers — rather than an entire media
library with history. Prove the whole procedure here before touching the others.

Source PV: media/prowlarr-db-local (1Gi, local-path, currently pinned to talos02-gpu).

## PROCEDURE (Servarr-documented, verified 2026-08-22)
1. Create TWO databases: <app>-main and <app>-log, same owner/user. A CNPG cluster can host
   all three apps; decide one shared cluster vs one per app and record the choice.
2. *** START THE APP AGAINST THE EMPTY POSTGRES ONCE. *** Servarr: "Before starting a
   migration, ensure that you have run Sonarr against the created Postgres databases at
   least once successfully." It creates the schema and default rows. pgloader runs DATA
   ONLY and will NOT build the schema.
3. STOP the app. Delete the default rows that will collide on primary key:
     DELETE FROM "QualityProfiles"; DELETE FROM "QualityDefinitions";
     DELETE FROM "DelayProfiles";   DELETE FROM "Metadata";
     DELETE FROM "Config";          DELETE FROM "VersionInfo";
     DELETE FROM "ScheduledTasks";
   Skipping this is the usual cause of a failed import.
4. Load:
     pgloader --with "quote identifiers" --with "data only" <app>.db \
       postgresql://user:pass@host/<app>-main
   quote identifiers is MANDATORY — the arr schema uses PascalCase table names.
   Large DBs: add --with "prefetch rows = 100" --with "batch size = 1MB"
   Container form: ghcr.io/roxedus/pgloader
5. Repeat for the -log database if you want history preserved; log data is optional.
6. Point the app at Postgres via ENV VARS (no config.xml edit) and restart.

## *** THE DATA-LOSS TRAP SPECIFIC TO THIS CLUSTER ***
The SQLite file you must read is on the LOCAL-PATH PV (media/<app>-db-local), NOT the NFS
config volume. applications/arr-stack/base/shared/db-migration-configmap.yaml does a
ONE-WAY copy NFS -> local on first run and then SKIPS forever if *.db exist locally, so the
local-path copy is AUTHORITATIVE and the NFS copy is frozen at first-migration time.
Reading the NFS path would SUCCEED and silently import a stale database. Verify you are
reading the local-path PV.

## WHY THIS IS SAFE
pgloader only READS the SQLite file — it is never modified. The original remains a working
rollback for the whole operation, and reverting is an env-var change since config lives in
env, not config.xml. Take a copy of the .db before starting anyway.

## VERIFY BEFORE DECLARING DONE
Compare row counts SQLite vs Postgres for the main tables, and check in the UI that the
library/history/indexers are all present. Do not trust "pgloader exited 0".

## REQUIREMENTS
Radarr >= v4.1.0.6133. Postgres 14-18 (13 is EOL). Sources:
https://wiki.servarr.com/radarr/postgres-setup and https://wiki.servarr.com/sonarr/postgres-setup
close_reason:
Prowlarr is on CNPG Postgres. All 20 tables match the frozen SQLite source exactly (16741 rows, pgloader 0 errors); indexers/applications/download-clients/tags/history all present via the API, and POST /api/v1/indexer/testall passes 4/5 -- the one failure is PornRips being CloudFlare-blocked, which the migrated IndexerStatus already recorded as failing for 6h+ before cutover. pg_stat_activity confirms the app holds connections to both prowlarr-main and prowlarr-log.

Source read was /db-local/prowlarr.db on the local-path PV (8142848 B, mtime 2026-08-22 15:57:46, sha256 17784f0d...), NOT the stale /config/prowlarr.db.nfs-backup (176128 B, mtime 2025-12-20). SQLite file is byte-identical after the migration -- rollback intact.

Topology: ONE shared arr-postgres cluster in ns media, instances:3 on fatboy-nfs-appdata, tenant DBs as CNPG Database CRs owned by a shared arrstack role. Radarr and Sonarr join by appending two Database CRs each. Reasoning and the cost (shared PITR blast radius) are in cluster.yaml.

DELETE list that actually applied to prowlarr: Config (0 rows, no-op), VersionInfo (41), ScheduledTasks (8), plus AppSyncProfiles (1) which is NOT in the Servarr wiki but does collide. QualityProfiles / QualityDefinitions / DelayProfiles / Metadata do not exist in the prowlarr schema at all -- radarr and sonarr will have those and will not have AppSyncProfiles.

-log database created but data NOT migrated (rolling debug logs, Servarr calls it optional, and replaying them would push churn into a WAL stream shared with radarr/sonarr).

Runbook: applications/arr-stack/base/postgres/MIGRATION-RUNBOOK.md

NOT DONE, deliberately: db-local stays mounted as the rollback, so the local-path PV still pins prowlarr to talos02-gpu. Filed TALOS-6ck8 to drop the mount once all three are proven -- EPIC 1 stays blocked until then.

The three orphaned /config/prowlarr.db* symlinks were renamed to *.sqlite-era so nothing dangles; that self-heals on revert (migrate-arr.sh finds no symlink, finds /db-local/prowlarr.db, recreates all three).

RECLAIM POLICY: local-path is the cluster DEFAULT class and its policy is Delete. fatboy-nfs-appdata is Retain. The rec-media-*-db-local PVs are Retain only because each was hand-written that way after the 2026-05-09 UPS incident -- not inherited. Putting the CNPG cluster on local-path would have produced PVs with LESS protection than the SQLite ones being retired. arr-postgres is on fatboy-nfs-appdata and all three of its PVs verified Retain.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
UNBIND COMPLETE (user validated, 2026-08-22). Prowlarr is fully off SQLite and no longer node-pinned.

 - migrate-db initContainer was already gone (ee0e18ae). Checked what depended on the symlink it creates: nothing. It exists only so the app finds its DB where it expects one, no backup CronJob reads prowlarr *.db, and the Velero annotation no longer names the volume.

Correct behaviour: Retain means the kubelet leaves the data, and a hand-written PV is not local-path-provisioner's to clean. Left in place as a further cold copy; delete it deliberately if the space is ever wanted.

UN-NODE-BOUND, PROVEN BY MOVING IT. Static: the only remaining PVC is prowlarr-config on fatboy-nfs-appdata whose PV has no nodeAffinity; no nodeSelector, no affinity. Dynamic: cordoned talos02-gpu, deleted the pod, and it rescheduled onto TALOS06 (10.244.3.203) -- a node it could never have run on before. Uncordoned immediately.

VERIFIED AFTER THE UNBIND, from talos06: 5 indexers, 3 applications, 2 download clients, tag nzb, appprofile Standard, history 16388, testall valid on all 4 enabled indexers. The pod has exactly one mount, /config over NFS -- /db-local does not exist and no SQLite database is reachable in the container -- so serving that data can only be Postgres. pg_stat_database: prowlarr-main 1923 commits / 294448 tuples returned, prowlarr-log 410 commits.

ROLLBACK IS NOW DIFFERENT and the manifests say so: reverting the env no longer restores anything. Recovery is a cold copy from /config/pg-migration-backup/ on the NFS config PVC (prowlarr-20260822T155746Z-final.db, 8142848 bytes -- the exact file pgloader read), the leftover host directory, or a CNPG PITR of arr-postgres.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
SEQUENCE CORRECTNESS VERIFIED (prompted by the radarr migration flagging that my original guidance invited an off-by-one misreading).

Id columns are serial, so a pgloader data-only load inserts explicit Ids without advancing the sequences. pgloader resets them (Reset Sequences 0 19), but the check I documented used pg_sequences, which has no is_called column -- and is_called is the whole question. last_value = max(Id) with is_called = TRUE is correct (next nextval returns max+1); the failure mode is is_called = FALSE, where nextval returns last_value itself and collides.

Checked rather than assumed. All 19 prowlarr sequences: is_called = t, last_value = max(Id). Direct invariant spot-check: Indexers 6/6/t, History 190489/190489/t, Commands 125447/125447/t, Config 6/6/t.

Empirical confirmation, which is stronger: History and Commands have both advanced past their post-load values (190447 -> 190489, 125408 -> 125447) under live use with zero duplicate-key errors.

Runbook fixed in a0fe9895 -- Step 4 now carries a query that emits is_called across every sequence relation, with the trap stated inline instead of fifty lines later in an app-specific section.

CROSS-APP FINDING, now three data points, and it confirms there is NO stable delete list:
  prowlarr: Config, VersionInfo, ScheduledTasks + AppSyncProfiles (4 of the 7 wiki tables do not exist at all)
  radarr:   all 7 + NamingConfig + Commands, and no AppSyncProfiles
Commands is the reason the list must be derived INSIDE the suspended window -- it seeds itself from startup tasks the moment the app comes up, so a list derived before scaling to 0 is already stale. Sonarr (TALOS-eaa4) must re-derive rather than reuse either list or their union.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
RUNBOOK HARDENING from the radarr run (e071f5e7), two gaps in guidance I wrote:

1. THE CORDON TEST NEEDED A PRECONDITION. 'Proving the app is un-node-bound' assumed the mount was already gone but never said so. An app that is validated but NOT yet unbound still mounts <app>-db-local, whose PV has nodeAffinity -- cordoning its node leaves the pod Pending, which reads exactly like a failed migration and is not one. Radarr is in that state right now by design. Section now opens with an explicit ONLY-AFTER-THE-UNBIND gate plus a check to run first.

2. THE CORDON MOVES THE POSTGRES PRIMARY, and neither of us had written that down. CNPG will not leave a primary on an unschedulable node: my prowlarr test produced 'SwitchingOver: Current primary is running on unschedulable node talos02-gpu, switching over from arr-postgres-1 to arr-postgres-2'. Clean switchover not a failover, cluster stayed healthy, but connections drop briefly and EVERY app on the shared cluster feels it. Radarr's load was already running when I did this -- it landed fine, but that was luck. Runbook now says do not run it during someone else's load.

3. Corollary, from radarr: never hardcode an instance name. Resolve $(kubectl get cluster arr-postgres -o jsonpath='{.status.currentPrimary}') per invocation. A hardcoded arr-postgres-1 works until it doesn't and then fails mid-migration with a connection error that looks like a data problem.

Also note the shared-cluster corollary is STRONGER now that radarr is on it too: a CNPG PITR of arr-postgres rewinds prowlarr AND radarr together. Single-app recovery is pg_dump of that app's database, never barman.

comments.text:
HANDOFF FROM RADARR (TALOS-l4uo, verified 2026-08-22). Read this before starting; it is the delta prowlarr's runbook does not cover.

1. THE DELETE LIST IS DIFFERENT AGAIN. Do not use prowlarr's, do not use radarr's, do not use the union, do not use the Servarr wiki's. Derive it empirically AFTER the schema-creation run and INSIDE the suspended window.

What actually applied to RADARR -- 9 statements, all 7 wiki tables plus 2 the wiki omits:
  DELETE FROM "QualityProfiles";     -- 6 rows
  DELETE FROM "QualityDefinitions";  -- 30 rows
  DELETE FROM "DelayProfiles";       -- 1 row
  DELETE FROM "Metadata";            -- 5 rows
  DELETE FROM "Config";              -- 0 rows, no-op but harmless
  DELETE FROM "VersionInfo";         -- 138 rows
  DELETE FROM "ScheduledTasks";      -- 11 rows
  DELETE FROM "NamingConfig";        -- 1 row   *** NOT IN THE WIKI ***
  DELETE FROM "Commands";            -- 2 rows  *** NOT IN THE WIKI ***

Versus PROWLARR, which needed only 4: Config (0, no-op), VersionInfo (41), ScheduledTasks (8), AppSyncProfiles (1, not in the wiki). Prowlarr does not HAVE QualityProfiles / QualityDefinitions / DelayProfiles / Metadata -- it is an indexer manager. Radarr has all four and does NOT have AppSyncProfiles.

WHY Commands is the subtle one: it is not seeded by the schema build, it is populated by the startup tasks the app fires the instant it comes up, and it keeps growing while the app runs. So its count is not stable -- derive and delete in the same suspended window, never from a reading taken before you scaled to 0.

Derive with EXACT counts, not n_live_tup:
  SELECT string_agg(format('SELECT %L AS t, count(*) AS n FROM %I', tablename, tablename), ' UNION ALL ') FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public';

2. THINGS SONARR WILL HIT THAT PROWLARR DID NOT
 - SIZE. sonarr.db is ~549 MB, vs radarr 267 MB and prowlarr 8 MB. Radarr's 496288 rows took 10.2s with --with 'prefetch rows = 100' --with 'batch size = 1MB'. Keep both flags. The emptyDir needs headroom; radarr's Job used sizeLimit 2Gi, size sonarr's to at least 4Gi.
 - THE BIG TABLES ARE METADATA, NOT MEDIA. Radarr's row count was dominated by Credits (272664) and MovieTranslations (152582) -- 86 percent of all rows. Sonarr's equivalents are per-episode, so expect the same shape and do not panic at the row count.
 - COUNTS ALONE DO NOT PROVE FIDELITY. Compare sorted content digests too. Cast postgres booleans back to int or the comparison fails on t/f vs 1/0 and proves nothing: sqlite3 -separator '|' ... | sort | shasum -a 256 against psql -F'|' -At -c ... | sort | shasum -a 256.
 - SEQUENCES. 'Reset Sequences 0 N' leaves last_value = max(Id) with is_called = true. That is CORRECT, not an off-by-one -- next nextval returns max+1. The failure mode is is_called = false, and pg_sequences does not expose that column; read it off the sequence relation: SELECT last_value, is_called FROM "Series_Id_seq";
 - testall ONLY TESTS ENABLED PROVIDERS. Radarr has 2 download clients but downloadclient/testall returned 1 result because one is disabled. Check the enable flag before reading a ratio as a partial failure.
 - PRE-EXISTING HEALTH ERRORS WILL LOOK LIKE MIGRATION DAMAGE. Radarr surfaced a TMDb-removed movie and 738 collections whose RootFolderPath is not a configured root folder. Both were present in the frozen SQLite. Capture GET /api/v3/health BEFORE cutover so you can tell pre-existing from caused -- I did not, and had to prove it from the source file afterwards.
 - ROLLING TABLES SHRINK AFTER CUTOVER AND THAT IS FINE. Radarr's Commands went 3525 -> 3515 within minutes: the app's housekeeping trims it to a 1-day window. Confirm via min/max timestamp before treating a drop as loss.
 - CNPG PRIMARY MOVES. It was arr-postgres-1, is now arr-postgres-2. Resolve it per-call with kubectl get cluster arr-postgres -o jsonpath='{.status.currentPrimary}'; a hardcoded pod name fails mid-migration.
 - SHARED CLUSTER, NOW TWO TENANTS. arr-postgres holds prowlarr AND radarr. Never delete/recreate the cluster; single-DB recovery is pg_dump, not a PITR, because a PITR rewinds every tenant.
 - COORDINATE THE SUSPEND. While arr-stack is suspended, everyone else's flux reconcile reports success and applies nothing.

3. SONARR IS STILL NODE-BOUND TO talos03, same as radarr. Both keep db-local mounted as the rollback until the user's validation gate; TALOS-6ck8 drops the mounts. Do NOT cordon-test sonarr before then -- it will just go Pending and look like a failure.

title: EPIC 1 — Control plane 1 -> 3 (promote two workers)
description:
BLOCKED BY EPIC 0 for whichever two nodes are chosen.

GOAL: eliminate the single-control-plane SPOF. Today talos00 is the only CP: if it dies, the API server and etcd go with it. 3 CPs give etcd a quorum of 2, tolerating one failure.

VERIFIED PROCEDURE (web-researched 2026-08-22, do not re-derive):
 - Talos machine type CANNOT change in place. Sidero: 'Changing roles involves changes to
   the PKI, etcd membership, and fundamental service topology that cannot be safely done
   in-place' and 'Talos developers do not document or test procedures that do not involve
   full machine reset for role conversions.' Promotion = talosctl reset + apply
   controlplane.yaml.
 - etcd LEARNER mode is AUTOMATIC: 'all new control plane nodes join etcd as non-voting
   learners, until they have caught up with all transactions. Adding an extra node does
   NOT increase quorum, until the node is a reliable member, and it is then automatically
   promoted to a voting member.'
 - So the long install+sync window costs NOTHING — quorum stays at 1 throughout. The ONLY
   fragile window is between node-2 auto-promoting to voter (2 voters, quorum 2, tolerates
   0) and node-3 auto-promoting (3 voters, quorum 2, tolerates 1).
   *** DO BOTH PROMOTIONS IN ONE SITTING. Do not stop in between. ***
 - talosctl reset is GRACEFUL by default: 'will cordon and drain the node, leaving etcd if
   required, and then erase its disks and power down'. Use --reboot or the node POWERS OFF
   instead of returning to maintenance mode.
 - Ordering trap: 'you must remove the node from etcd before shutting it down. If you shut
   down the node first, the etcd cluster will see it as a failed member.' Graceful reset
   handles this; a hard power-off does NOT.

POST-RESET, EASY TO FORGET: re-apply the kubelet patches. A reset node loses them.
scripts/bootstrap-talos-patches.sh carries three — iSCSI extraMounts, local-path
extraMount, and maxPods 110->200 (TALOS-d5b5). Without them the node returns at maxPods
110 with local-path broken. Also check configs/nodes/<node>/ for node-specific
schematic/extension config.

CAPACITY: talos00 is tainted. If the new CPs are tainted too, their ~93 pods relocate onto
the remaining 2 workers. Consider allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes.

Runbook being written to docs/05-runbooks/promote-workers-to-controlplane.md.

title: EPIC 0 — Node prep: un-node-bind PVCs before any control-plane reset
description:
PREREQUISITE for EPIC 1. Nothing in EPIC 1 may start until this is done for the two target nodes.

WHY: talosctl reset WIPES the EPHEMERAL partition, which Talos mounts at /var — exactly where local-path provisions. Promoting a worker to control plane therefore DESTROYS every local-path PV on that node. local-path is WaitForFirstConsumer so those PVs are pinned and cannot migrate themselves.

REFRAMING (user, 2026-08-22): the goal is NOT 'evacuate then reset'. It is 'stop having node-bound storage on nodes we intend to reset'. Where a workload can be moved off local-path permanently, do that instead of choreographing a one-off evacuation.

  talos01   8 PVs — mimir alertmanager/compactor/ingester-0/store-gateway (SINGLETONS),
                    forgejo-data 20Gi, authentik-postgres-3, boomtime-postgres-1 (PRIMARY),
                    pihole-1
  talos03  16 PVs — cilium-spire/spire-server (SINGLETON, cluster identity),
                    radarr+sonarr db-local, 13x media-experimental configs, pihole-4
  talos02  10 PVs — jellyfin/plex/prowlarr db-local, authentik-postgres-1,
