title: Kyverno mutate: force imagePullPolicy Always on any non-semver tag
description:
End the floating-tag bug class permanently instead of fixing it one app at a time.

## WHY A POLICY AND NOT MORE MANIFEST EDITS

This bug has now been diagnosed THREE separate times and fixed per-app each time:
    fcc6c601   arr-stack, five months ago
    bookorbit  deployment.yaml:152 carries a comment reasoning about exactly this bug
    TALOS-6gnx today, after it took down Home Assistant for 15 days and broke immich

Each fix was correct and each was applied to one application rather than the class. That is the
root cause of the recurrence.

## THE SPECIFIC FRAGILITY THIS CLOSES

Roughly 40 workloads are currently safe ONLY because of an implicit Kubernetes default:

    :latest and untagged  -> Always          (safe)
    EVERY other tag       -> IfNotPresent    (dangerous when the tag floats)

Verified by server-side dry-run on this cluster. Note this is the opposite of intuition — the
tag that reads most reckless is the one Kubernetes protects, and :stable/:release/:main are the
dangerous ones. It is exactly why the casualties were homeassistant (:stable), immich
(:release) and open-webui (:main).

So if anyone ever retags one of those ~40 from :latest to :stable, THE POLICY SILENTLY FLIPS
to IfNotPresent and the bug returns WITH NO DIFF TO REVIEW. The manifest change would look
entirely innocuous.

## THE RULE

Mutate imagePullPolicy to Always on any container whose tag is not a semver-ish pin. Something
like: if the tag matches ^v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ or is a sha256 digest, leave it; otherwise force
Always.

## CAVEATS THAT MATTER

  - ⚠️ KYVERNO CANNOT MUTATE kube-system, kyverno, kube-public or kube-node-lease — they are
    in its resourceFilters exclusion list, and mutations there silently NO-OP. Anything in
    those namespaces still needs the explicit manifest value.
  - Always LIVE-PROBE a mutate policy after applying. A Kyverno mutate that does not fire
    produces no error and no signal; it just quietly does nothing. Confirm with a server-side
    dry-run that the field actually appears.
  - Always is not the same as pinning. It fixes 'which version does THIS NODE have' but not
    'which version is running at all'. For stateful apps a version pin is still better, and
    TALOS-6gnx lists 44 candidates in priority order.

## SCOPE NOTE

This covers Flux-managed workloads in talos-homelab. The eight ArgoCD applications sourced from
sister repos are governed by the same admission controller at runtime, so the policy WOULD
apply to them — which is a strong argument for doing it here rather than auditing nine repos
by hand. Verify that assumption before relying on it.

title: Audit stateful workloads for floating tags + imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent
description:
Three apps have now hit the same bug. Treat it as a pattern rather than fixing them one at a
time as they break.

## THE BUG

A floating image tag (:latest, :stable, :release, or untagged) combined with
imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent means a node serves whatever it cached — possibly months ago —
and never re-pulls. THE RUNNING VERSION BECOMES NODE-DEPENDENT.

For a stateless app that is untidy. For anything with a database, a migration system or a
storage-version field it is a LATENT OUTAGE: the app upgrades its own on-disk state while
running on a node with a newer image, then cannot read it back after rescheduling onto a node
with an older cached one.

## CONFIRMED CASUALTIES

    arr-stack       fixed 5 months ago in fcc6c601 — the original diagnosis
    homeassistant   :stable + IfNotPresent. UnsupportedStorageVersionError, storage v2 vs max
                    supported v1. DOWN 15 DAYS unnoticed. Fixed 2026-08-24.
    immich          :release. Corrupted kysely migration state. Self-healed.

## WHY IT KEEPS RECURRING

Nothing detects it while the pod keeps running. Both 2026-08-24 casualties had ready=0 for
10-15 days with nobody knowing, because nothing had restarted them. It only surfaces on a
RESCHEDULE — and node reboots reschedule everything at once, so failures arrive in batches
during exactly the maintenance window when you least want surprises.

A rolling reboot is in effect an audit of which workloads survive a restart. Two failed.

## WHAT TO DO

 1. Enumerate every workload with a floating tag AND imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent (or no
    explicit policy — the default is IfNotPresent for tagged images).
 2. For anything STATEFUL — a database, migrations, or a storage-version field — either set
    imagePullPolicy: Always, or pin to an explicit version. Pinning is better: it makes a
    version change a reviewable commit rather than something that happens whenever a pod moves.
 3. For stateless workloads Always is sufficient.

Do this BEFORE the next reboot cycle rather than discovering it during one. The Bluetooth
node upgrades (TALOS-1mog) will reboot four nodes.
notes:
## ⚠️ SCOPE BOUNDARY — HALF THE FLEET IS NOT AUDITABLE FROM THIS REPO

An audit of talos-homelab covers only Flux-managed workloads. EIGHT ArgoCD applications are
sourced from sister repos and are structurally invisible to it:

    arr-stack-private   talos-private.git      <- CONTAINS IMMICH AND STASH
    boomtime            boomtime.git           k8s/overlays/talos00-knowledgedump
    catalyst-data       catalyst-data.git      k8s
    catalyst-llm        catalyst-llm.git       k8s/talos00
    catalyst-ui         catalyst-ui.git        k8s
    dungeon-library     dungeon-library.git    k8s
    kasa-exporter       kasa-exporter.git      k8s
    openscad            openscad.git           k8s/overlays/talos00

THIS MATTERS BECAUSE IMMICH — one of the two casualties that triggered this ticket — LIVES
THERE. Verified: deployment immich in media-private carries
argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id: arr-stack-private:apps/Deployment:media-private/immich, and is
still ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:release with imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent in the live
cluster. It WILL break again on the next reschedule.

Live-cluster measurement after this repo's fixes landed:
    floating-tag containers, Always:        62
    floating-tag containers, IfNotPresent:  12   <- the remainder
Of those 12, the ones outside this repo include immich-server, immich-machine-learning, stash,
and open-webui (catalyst-llm).

## FOLLOW-UP REQUIRED IN THE SISTER REPOS

The same audit has to run in each ArgoCD-sourced repo. talos-private.git is the priority since
it holds immich. This cannot be closed as done while the app that motivated it remains
unfixed in a repo nobody has looked at.

Note the dual-GitOps split is working correctly here — app manifests belong in app repos. The
gap is that a fleet-wide audit needs to be fleet-wide, and 'the fleet' is nine repos.

## ⚠️ THE RULE, CORRECTED — the danger predicate is the opposite of intuition

Verified by server-side dry-run against this cluster (k8s 1.36.4), not assumed:

    busybox:latest    -> Always          busybox:stable   -> IfNotPresent
    busybox           -> Always          busybox:release  -> IfNotPresent
    busybox:1.36      -> IfNotPresent    busybox:main     -> IfNotPresent

:latest and untagged default to ALWAYS. EVERY OTHER TAG defaults to IfNotPresent.

So the tag that reads most reckless is the one Kubernetes protects, and the safe-sounding
floating tags are the dangerous ones. THIS EXPLAINS THE ENTIRE CASUALTY LIST:
    homeassistant  :stable      immich  :release      open-webui  :main
The arr-stack was only ever vulnerable because it carried an EXPLICIT IfNotPresent overriding
the safe default — which is precisely what fcc6c601 removed.

CORRECT DANGER PREDICATE:
    explicit IfNotPresent on any floating tag
    OR any non-:latest floating tag (explicit or defaulted)

Consequences for anyone re-running this audit:
  - ~40 :latest workloads that a naive grep flags are ALREADY SAFE
  - secure-webtop (:ubuntu-kde) looked untouched and was silently defaulting to the dangerous
    value — a grep for the literal string 'IfNotPresent' would have missed it entirely

## INVENTORY — 211 container specs across applications/ + infrastructure/

    FINE    version-pinned                    108
    FINE    digest-pinned                       4
    HIGH    floating + stateful (now Always)   44
    MEDIUM  floating + stateless (now Always)  37
    n/a     SMP patches with no image line     18

CRITICAL (floating + stateful + dangerous policy) — ALL 13 FIXED:
  - media-experimental/_instance: one explicit IfNotPresent in a shared skeleton inherited by
    11 apps; NINE override with a floating tag AND keep a SQLite library DB on a config PVC
    (audiobookshelf, bindery, chaptarr, kavita, komga, libation, librarr, mylar3, storyteller).
    One line fixed all nine.
  - linkwarden: :latest + Prisma migrations against CNPG. The immich failure mode exactly.
  - secure-webtop: DEFAULTED IfNotPresent via :ubuntu-kde. Stateless in the end, but invisible
    to a grep.

HIGH (44, left alone deliberately — pinning is a judgement call about WHICH version):
  Priority for pinning, where a version change rewrites on-disk state:
    1. homeassistant + matter-server (:stable) — already bit us, highest value
    2. pulsarr (knex), linkwarden (Prisma), the nine media-experimental SQLite apps,
       zipline, tubesync, scrypted
    3. linuxserver *arr images — lower risk, and fcc6c601 documents :latest there as a
       deliberate choice. Leave.
  Nothing was pinned blind: for homeassistant the storage is at version 2 and the correct pin
  is whichever build wrote it, which is not readable off the cluster. Always is the safe
  intermediate. Currently-running digests are available for all 44 if digest pins are wanted.

## THE ONE A MANIFEST GREP CANNOT FIND

infrastructure/base/cert-manager-issuers/desec-webhook.yaml has NO Deployment in the repo —
only HelmRelease values, tag: latest + pullPolicy: IfNotPresent, which never appear adjacent to
an image: line. This webhook gates DNS-01 issuance for EVERY certificate in the cluster. A
silently different build on one node would surface as a renewal that mysteriously stops working
months later. Fixed in 0248859f. It was the only HelmRelease in the repo with a floating tag.

## THE PATTERN HAS NOW BEEN DIAGNOSED THREE TIMES AND FIXED PER-APP EACH TIME

applications/media-experimental/base/bookorbit/deployment.yaml:152 already carries a comment
reasoning about exactly this bug, and is correctly pinned. So: fcc6c601 (arr-stack), bookorbit,
and now this audit. Each time the fix was applied to one app rather than the class. THAT is the
root cause of the recurrence, not any individual manifest.

## THE PERMANENT FIX WORTH ITS OWN TICKET

~40 workloads are currently safe ONLY because of the implicit :latest -> Always default. If
anyone retags one to :stable, the policy silently flips to IfNotPresent and the bug returns
WITH NO DIFF TO REVIEW. A Kyverno mutate rule forcing imagePullPolicy: Always on any non-semver
tag would end this class permanently. Caveat: Kyverno cannot mutate kube-system.

## ODDITIES FOUND, NOT TOUCHED

  - infrastructure/base/gpu-inference/broker-deployment.yaml: image is
    :PLACEHOLDER-NOT-BUILT-YET. Not deployable.
  - infrastructure/base/bootstrap-crds/crds/prometheus-operator-crds.yaml does not YAML-parse
    (tag:yaml.org,2002:value constructor error). Vendored bundle, no workloads — but no static
    linter is reading that file either.
  - Pre-existing gitleaks flag on linkwarden/deployment.yaml:42 from commit 421343bd. Reports,
    does not block. Unrelated to this work.

## talos-private COMPLETE — 0 dangerous combinations remain (independently verified)

    digest/version pinned        8
    floating but SAFE (Always)   5
    still dangerous              0

Four CRITICALs fixed by DIGEST PIN rather than Always, after Always caused a live immich
outage. All healthy, 0 restarts:
    immich/immich-server   :release@sha256:c15bff75
    immich/immich-ml       :release@sha256:a2501141
    stash/stash            :latest@sha256:e1624844
    stash-ai/postgres      pg16@sha256:ccc6e83d

## THE CLIFF LIST — tags resolved live against what is running

Only ONE workload is on a cliff, and it is a hard one:
    immich-server:release  ->  b434cb92 (v3.1.0)   running c15bff75 (v2.7.5)
A MAJOR version ahead with a dropped postgres extension. ⚠️ ANYONE WHO 'UPDATES IMMICH' BY
RE-FLOATING THAT TAG REPRODUCES THE OUTAGE EXACTLY. Warning comment is at
base/immich/deployment.yaml:69 in talos-private; TALOS-7sx / TALOS-cibi own the migration.

## ⚠️ redis IS THE ONLY REMAINING LIVE SPLIT — and it is the proof of the whole bug

    redis:7-alpine   tag resolves to ff02b58f
                     running ee64a64 on talos06, 6ab0b6e on talos02-gpu
THREE DIFFERENT DIGESTS for one tag. Caught when the recovered immich pod picked up a different
redis layer than its predecessor on the same tag. Left unfixed deliberately: it is stateless
(no volumeMounts at all) so there is no fast-forward hazard, and the correct fix is Always
rather than a pin — but applying it restarts the immich pod, which was not worth bouncing a
just-recovered service for a benign cache. FOLD INTO THE VECTORCHORD MIGRATION WINDOW.

## STANDING RISK, not a cliff

stash-ai-server:latest defaults to Always, so it SILENTLY UPGRADES ON EVERY POD RESTART — with
a postgres DB behind it. It never accumulates a large jump, so it is far safer than immich was,
but a breaking upstream release lands ungated. Pinning ba7c35aa is free whenever that should be
gated.

whisparr is frozen on a PRE-EXISTING digest pin of unknown age. Nobody knows how far behind it
is. Worth dating. (Separately CrashLooping on a liveness probe — TALOS-o00l.)

## CORRECTLY LEFT ALONE — the judgement calls

    hot-ones:v3          NOT floating. git log -L shows v1->v2->v3 as explicit release commits.
                         IfNotPresent is correct. Same digest on talos03 and talos06.
    browserless/chrome   :latest defaults to Always, stateless (emptyDir)
    traefik/whoami       same
    pgvecto-rs:pg16-v0.2.1  version-pinned, resolves equal to running

## UNRELATED PRE-EXISTING FINDING

talos-private tdarr-patches has a 'patches:' block whose 'target:' matches nothing — it renders
as a NO-OP. Confirmed dead against the live cluster: synology-666 volume count on both
tdarr-server and tdarr-worker is 0. Someone believes that mount works and it does not.

title: [bug] Floating image tags on stateful apps: immich and Home Assistant both broken by version/storage mismatch
description:
immich-server crashloops on startup. PRE-EXISTING FAULT, surfaced by an unrelated reboot —
the container had simply been running continuously since before it mattered.

## THE ERROR

    Migrations failed: Error: corrupted migrations:
      previously executed migration 1771478781948-PeopleSearchIndex is missing
        at #ensureNoMissingMigrations (kysely/dist/cjs/migration/migrator.js:487)
        at DatabaseRepository.runMigrations (server/dist/repositories/database.repository.js:315)
    microservices worker exited with code 1 -> Killing api process

The database's migration table records 1771478781948-PeopleSearchIndex as applied, but that
migration does not exist in the running image. kysely refuses to proceed when history
references a migration it cannot find, so the server exits and the pod crashloops.

## WHY IT SURFACED NOW, AND WHY THE REBOOT IS NOT THE CAUSE

Found 2026-08-24 during the talhelper rolling apply, when talos02-gpu rebooted and immich was
rescheduled onto talos06.

The reboot did not break immich. It revealed that immich COULD NOT SURVIVE A RESTART. The
schema/binary mismatch was already present; the process had just never been asked to run
migrations again since the image changed underneath it.

Ruled out as causes:
  - Storage. All four PVCs are NFS (immich-postgres, immich-uploads, immich-ml-cache on
    fatboy-nfs-appdata; private-content-pvc on synology-nfs). Nothing is local-path pinned, so
    the move between nodes was clean and the data followed.
  - The migration work. Nothing in the machine-config change touches application state.
  - Node health. talos06 is Ready, every other workload on it is fine.

The ReplicaSet is 10 days old with ready=0, which is consistent with the fault predating today
and only mattering at restart.

## LIKELY CAUSE

An immich image upgrade that removed or renamed a migration, against a database that had
already run it. immich pulls ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:release — a FLOATING TAG, so the
running image can change under the deployment without any manifest change. That is almost
certainly how the mismatch arrived, and it will recur.

## FIXES, in preference order

 1. PIN THE IMAGE to the version whose migration set matches the current schema, then upgrade
    deliberately. This also stops it happening again — a floating :release tag on a stateful
    app with migrations is the underlying problem, not just this instance.
 2. Identify which immich version contained 1771478781948-PeopleSearchIndex and run that
    version once to bring schema and history into agreement, then move forward.
 3. LAST RESORT: delete the offending row from immich's kysely migration table. This tells
    immich a migration never ran when it did. Only safe if you have confirmed what that
    migration changed and that the schema still reflects it. Back up immich-postgres first.

## DO NOT

Do not roll back the Talos machine-config apply. It is unrelated, and reverting it costs a
second reboot for no benefit.

## RELATED

Same class as the argocd-image-updater floating-tag issues. Worth auditing which other
stateful workloads track a moving tag: a floating tag plus schema migrations is a latent
outage waiting for the next restart, and restarts are exactly what a node reboot causes.
notes:
## UPDATE 2026-08-24 — immich RECOVERED ON ITS OWN, but a SECOND app has the same disease

immich is now 1/1 Running. Its migration state resolved after repeated restart attempts —
no intervention. Leaving this ticket open anyway, because the ROOT CAUSE is unfixed and it
just demonstrated itself on a second application.

## HOME ASSISTANT: same class, worse prognosis

    homeassistant-789d7df74c   desired=1 ready=0   age 15 DAYS

    UnsupportedStorageVersionError: Storage file http has version 2 which is newer than
    the max supported version 1; upgrade Home Assistant or restore
    Storage file core.device_registry was created by a newer version of Home Assistant

Its on-disk config was written by a NEWER version than the image now running. Broken for 15
days before today's reboots — like immich, the container had simply been running continuously
and never asked to re-read its own storage.

Unlike immich this will NOT self-heal. A storage-version downgrade is not automatic; it needs
either the newer image pinned back, or a restore from backup.

## THE ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE, common to both

A FLOATING IMAGE TAG ON A STATEFUL APPLICATION.

    immich         ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:release
    homeassistant  (verify its tag — same shape)

The running container keeps serving while the tag moves underneath it. Data gets migrated or
upgraded by whatever version happened to start last. Then ANY restart pulls the current tag,
which may no longer match the data on disk. Nothing detects this until a restart happens — and
node reboots cause restarts, so the faults surface in BATCHES rather than one at a time.

Both of today's casualties had been broken for days or weeks with nobody knowing, because
nothing had restarted them.

## RECOMMENDED, in order

 1. AUDIT every stateful workload for floating tags — :latest, :release, :stable, or no tag.
    Anything with a database, a migration system, or a storage-version field is at risk.
    This is the fix; the two below are cleanup.
 2. PIN those images to explicit versions and upgrade deliberately, so a version change is a
    reviewable commit rather than something that happens whenever a pod restarts.
 3. Fix Home Assistant specifically: identify the version that wrote the storage (check the
    storage version fields against HA release notes) and pin to it, or restore config from
    backup and start on a known version.

## NOT CAUSED BY THE TALHELPER MIGRATION

Both faults predate it — immich's ReplicaSet was 10 days old, Home Assistant's 15 days, both
with ready=0. The rolling reboot revealed them; it did not create them. All five nodes
converged to zero differences and every other workload came back healthy.
close_reason:
BOTH APPS RECOVERED. Root cause found and fixed for Home Assistant; immich self-healed.

## HOME ASSISTANT — fixed, 1/1 after 15 days down

Root cause was NOT a corrupted upgrade. It was imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent on a FLOATING TAG:

    image: ghcr.io/home-assistant/home-assistant:stable
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

With IfNotPresent a node serves whatever it cached — possibly months old — and never re-pulls.
So THE RUNNING VERSION DEPENDS ON WHICH NODE THE POD LANDED ON. HA upgraded its on-disk
storage to version 2 while on a node with a recent :stable, then rescheduled onto a node whose
cached :stable predated that format:

    UnsupportedStorageVersionError: Storage file http has version 2 which is newer than the
    max supported version 1

Fixed by setting imagePullPolicy: Always on both the home-assistant container and the
python-matter-server sidecar, which had the identical pairing. A restart pulled the current
:stable and it came up 1/1 immediately — confirming the diagnosis, since nothing about the
storage changed.

## IMMICH — self-healed

Recovered to 1/1 without intervention; its kysely migration state resolved after repeated
restart attempts. Same underlying class (floating :release tag), different symptom.

## THE PATTERN, which is the actual finding

A FLOATING TAG PLUS IfNotPresent IS A LATENT OUTAGE WAITING FOR A RESCHEDULE. Nothing detects
it while the pod keeps running, and both apps had been broken for 10-15 DAYS with ready=0 and
nobody knowing, because nothing had restarted them.

Node reboots restart everything at once — so this class surfaces in BATCHES. A rolling reboot
is, in effect, an audit of which workloads can actually survive being restarted. Two failed
that audit.

EXACTLY THE BUG ALREADY FIXED FOR THE arr-stack IN fcc6c601 five months ago: 'imagePullPolicy
Always for :latest images — IfNotPresent made version node-dependent'. It recurred because the
fix was applied to one app rather than treated as a pattern.

## FOLLOW-UP FILED SEPARATELY

The fleet-wide audit — which other stateful workloads pair a floating tag with IfNotPresent —
is worth doing before the next reboot cycle rather than discovering it during one.

title: Enable Bluetooth on Talos: ship bluetooth/btusb as a system extension
description:
Make the cluster's five Bluetooth radios usable. Gated behind talhelper consolidation
(TALOS-0bo8) so the change lands as declarative config rather than more hand-applied drift.

## STATUS: BUILT AND STATICALLY PROVEN, NOT APPLIED

Both gates PASS. No node touched.

    CRC GATE        313 distinct symbols from four modules pulled off live talos06
                    (tg3, e1000e, hid-multitouch, xor — net/PCI/DMA/HID/crypto),
                    CRC-checked against our rebuilt Module.symvers. ZERO mismatches.
    vermagic        identical: '6.18.44-talos SMP preempt mod_unload modversions '
    CONFIG GATE     final .config diffed against /proc/config.gz from the running kernel:
                    33 differences, EVERY ONE inside the CONFIG_BT* namespace.
                    Zero n->y outside it, so nothing built-in moved — which is precisely
                    why the CRCs hold.

Config delta was two lines; the rest came from Kconfig defaults and select:
    -# CONFIG_BT is not set
    +CONFIG_BT=m
    +CONFIG_BT_HCIBTUSB=m

Modules: bluetooth.ko (2.3MB), btusb.ko, btintel.ko, btrtl.ko, btbcm.ko — all signed,
dep graph coherent.
Extensions built: talos-bluetooth (5 modules) and talos-intel-bt-firmware (88 intel/ibt-*
files, 31MB). Realtek stays on the official siderolabs/realtek-firmware.

## THE APPROACH — not modules-only over the stock kernel

bluetooth.ko does not exist in the stock kernel, so there is nothing to extract. What was
done: rebuild the OFFICIAL kernel from its exact pinned inputs (pkgs f541ca4, linux 6.18.44,
the six siderolabs patches, same LLVM toolchain), then DISCARD the kernel and package only
the .ko files it emitted. Nodes keep running Sidero's official vmlinuz. That is what makes
the CRC gate both necessary and sufficient, and it is NOT a kernel fork — per Talos release
it is a re-run of the same build, not a rebase of carried patches.

## THE KERNEL ARG — get this exactly right

module.sig_enforce=0 SILENTLY FAILS. Talos appends extras after defaults with overwrite
enabled for only console and talos.platform (pkg/imager/imager.go:386-412), so both =1 and =0
land on the cmdline, and the kernel then refuses the downgrade (kernel/params.c:334-355,
-EROFS). Use the NEGATION, which deletes the default outright:
    --extra-kernel-arg=-module.sig_enforce
Note the = form for imager; a bare -module.sig_enforce parses as a CLI flag.
First-boot check is by ABSENCE:
    talosctl -n <ip> read /proc/cmdline | tr ' ' '\n' | grep sig_enforce   # correct = NO output

## RFKILL — a red herring, settled with evidence

CONFIG_BT's stanza is 'depends on RFKILL || !RFKILL' — the tristate level-matching idiom,
tautological at the boolean level. Its job is forbidding BT=y against RFKILL=m. With RFKILL=n
the !RFKILL branch is true. Proven empirically: the build completed with RFKILL off and BT=m,
and neither module imports a single rfkill symbol.

BONUS DIAGNOSTIC: with CONFIG_RFKILL=n, hdev->rfkill is never allocated, so HCI_RFKILLED can
never be set (hci_core.c:2637). If hciN appears on the pilot and HCIDEVUP fails, rfkill is
DEFINITIVELY not the cause — look at firmware.

## RADIO INVENTORY — verified from /sys/kernel/debug/usb/devices, Cls=e0(wlcon)

    talos00       none            VM. Keep signature enforcement ON.
    talos01       8087:0026       Intel
    talos02-gpu   8087:0037       Intel
    talos03       0bda:b85b       Realtek     ONE radio (its 0d8c:0014 is a C-Media AUDIO adapter)
    talos06       0bda:a728 + 8087:0026       the ONLY capacity-2 node

All four types report Cls=e0 Sub=01 Prot=01 and match btusb's generic interface-class alias
usb:v*p*d*dc*dsc*dp*icE0isc01ip01in* — no VID/PID entry needed for any of them. Declare the
module explicitly anyway rather than relying on modalias autoload:
    machine: {kernel: {modules: [{name: btusb}]}}

## NO BLUEZ — ship modules only

HCI User Channel bind calls mgmt_index_removed() and fails -EBUSY if the adapter is UP.
bluetoothd and go-ble cannot coexist on one adapter. The extension ships no userspace at all.

## A TRAP FOR WHOEVER DEBUGS THIS LATER

Our modules' signer certificate reads EXACTLY what Sidero's does — O=Sidero Labs, Inc. /
CN=Build time throw-away kernel key — because x509.genkey is committed upstream and hardcodes
those fields while the keypair regenerates per build. You CANNOT tell an official module from
ours by inspecting the signer string; only real signature verification does. Anyone comparing
signer strings will conclude the signature is fine and look elsewhere.

## THE SECURITY TRADE — the user's decision, not ours

Disabling module signature enforcement removes the requirement that kernel modules carry a
valid signature; any .ko the node can read becomes loadable. It is NOT remotely exploitable on
its own — loading a module needs CAP_SYS_MODULE, i.e. the Talos API (already total control) or
a privileged workload. It is a privilege-escalation AMPLIFIER: it upgrades 'attacker has a
privileged container' from 'can disrupt the node' to 'can execute arbitrary ring-0 code'.
Mitigating: Talos is immutable, loaded modules do not survive reboot, and lockdown is already
FORCE_NONE with SecureBoot unused. Aggravating: it is a CIS/KSPP hardening default an auditor
would flag, and it is easy to set once and forget.
Scope it per node. talos00 has no radio and should keep enforcement.

## REMAINING

 1. Push both extension images to registry.talos00.
 2. Build per-node installers with imager, re-declaring each node's EXISTING extensions in the
    same invocation — this is the step talhelper exists to make reproducible.
 3. talosctl upgrade, one node at a time. REBOOTS. Requires the user at the keyboard.

Pilot order: a disposable Pi first if one exists (zero blast radius, free reboots), otherwise
talos06 — the only node with both an Intel and a Realtek radio, so it validates both firmware
paths on one machine. talos00 never.

Artefacts (nothing committed): runbook, extension sources, build script, and the reusable gate
scripts crcgate.py / rungate.py are in the session scratchpad.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-08-24 (read-only): READINESS ASSESSMENT — this is now gated ONLY on the user's yes.
* Its stated dependency TALOS-0bo8 (talhelper flattening) is 8/8 children closed and 'Eligible for closure'. bd still lists TALOS-1mog as blocked purely because the parent epic has not been closed. Closing TALOS-0bo8 mechanically unblocks this.
* configs/talconfig.yaml is live (204 lines) with per-node schematics for talos01/02-gpu/03/06 and stock for talos00 — the reproducible-installer mechanism this ticket needs in step 2 exists.
* Build artefacts verified present in THIS SESSION's scratchpad, all uncommitted: btout/ (manifest + 5 .ko: bluetooth, btusb, btintel, btrtl, btbcm), fwout/ (intel-bt-firmware manifest), and per-node installer-amd64.tar (143MB each) already built for talos01, talos02-gpu, talos03, talos06.
* RISK: those artefacts live in a session-scoped scratchpad under /private/tmp/claude-501/.../b488e0a8-.../scratchpad. If it is cleaned, the kernel rebuild (hours) must be redone. Committing the extension sources + build script + crcgate.py/rungate.py is cheap insurance and needs no reboot.

## ⚠️ BUILD ARTEFACTS RESCUED 2026-08-24 — they were one /tmp cleanup from being lost

The kernel build outputs were sitting in a SESSION-SCOPED SCRATCHPAD
(/private/tmp/claude-501/.../b488e0a8-.../scratchpad/) belonging to a session that has since
ended. That directory is eligible for cleanup at any time, and losing it would have cost hours
of kernel rebuild PLUS the entire CRC verification gate.

COPIED TO: .scratch/bluetooth-build-artifacts/ (32MB, verified byte-identical, sha256 of the
.ko set a338e035ce8b0dbc)

    btout/     5 signed .ko modules + manifest
    fwout/     89 Intel Bluetooth firmware files
    crcgate.py rungate.py + a README explaining what they are

NOT copied, deliberately: installers/ (578MB of per-node installer-amd64.tar for talos01,
talos02-gpu, talos03, talos06). Those are ASSEMBLED FROM the modules and firmware, so they are
cheap to regenerate and expensive to store. The kernel build is the expensive part and that is
what the 32MB preserves. They may still be in the old scratchpad until it is cleaned.

⚠️ .scratch/ IS GITIGNORED. These files now exist in exactly ONE place — local disk. This
retires the /tmp-cleanup risk, not the disk-loss risk. The intended durable home is
registry.talos00, which is step 1 of this ticket's own REMAINING list and is still not done.

## READINESS ASSESSMENT — effectively one 'yes' away

Both hard gates PASS and are documented:
  - 313 symbols CRC-checked against modules pulled off LIVE talos06, zero mismatches
  - vermagic identical
  - 33 config differences, every one inside CONFIG_BT*, ZERO n->y transitions
configs/talconfig.yaml is live with per-node schematics for the four radio nodes and stock for
talos00. Installers are already built.

REMAINING BEFORE THE USER CAN SIMPLY SAY YES:
  1. push the two extension images to registry.talos00 — NOT DONE. (Registry catalog returns
     401; not verified either way, treat as not done.)
  2. the user's decision on module.sig_enforce. Use the NEGATION FORM -module.sig_enforce;
     =0 silently fails because Talos appends args after defaults and the kernel refuses the
     downgrade with -EROFS. Verify by ABSENCE of the token in /proc/cmdline.

⚠️ The installers live in registry.talos00, which is HOSTED ON THE CLUSTER THEY UPGRADE. Fine
for one node; be deliberate about several at once.

title: [bug] GPU udev rules are untracked drift — a node rebuild silently kills hardware transcode
description:
The udev rules granting non-root access to /dev/dri/renderD128 are LIVE on talos02-gpu and
talos06 but exist nowhere in tracked git. Rebuild either node and they vanish.

## EVIDENCE

    talosctl -n 192.168.1.19  get machineconfig | grep -c 'renderD\*'   -> 2
    talosctl -n 192.168.1.144 get machineconfig | grep -c 'renderD\*'   -> 2

The only occurrence in the repo is a COMMENTED-OUT block at configs/nodes/worker-base.yaml:327
and configs/nodes/controlplane.yaml:326 — Talos's own generated documentation example, not
applied config — and configs/nodes/ is gitignored (confirmed with git check-ignore).

So they were applied by hand and never captured.

## WHY IT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY UNTIDY

/dev/dri/renderD128 defaults to root-only. The rules chown it to group 44 and the consumers
join that group: plex (fsGroup 44), plex-gpu-patch, jellyfin-gpu-patch, frigate.

Without the rules those pods still START. They simply cannot open the render node, and
hardware transcode falls back to CPU or fails per-stream. Nothing crashes. Nothing alerts.
The symptom surfaces weeks later as 'Plex got slow', with no obvious link to a node rebuild.

## FIX

Tracked patch written at docs/05-runbooks/talos-gpu-udev-rules-patch.yaml following the same
convention as the other nine talos-*-patch.yaml files. Applying it is a no-op today since the
rules are already live; its value is that a rebuilt node can be restored from git.

## WORTH GENERALISING

Audit for other hand-applied machine-config drift. This one was found incidentally while
investigating device access for Bluetooth. There may be more, and the same silent-failure
shape applies to anything in machine config that a workload depends on.

## SCOPE NOTE

The file-permission pattern works here because a DRM render node IS a file. It does NOT
generalise to Bluetooth — hciN has no device node, only an AF_BLUETOOTH socket endpoint and a
sysfs directory, so GROUP=/MODE= has nothing to apply to. That case needs capabilities. See
TALOS-hb5b.
close_reason:
RESOLVED by the talhelper migration. The rules are now declarative, tracked, and applied.

    configs/patches/gpu-udev-rules.yaml   tracked in git
    referenced by talos02-gpu and talos06 in talconfig.yaml
    both rules live on both nodes, verified post-apply:
        SUBSYSTEM=="drm", KERNEL=="renderD*", GROUP="44", MODE="0660"
        SUBSYSTEM=="drm", KERNEL=="card*",    GROUP="44", MODE="0660"
    /dev/dri/renderD128 is crw-rw---- root video, and Plex can open it

The original problem was that these rules were LIVE on both GPU nodes but existed nowhere in
tracked git — the only copy was a commented-out example inside a gitignored file. A node
rebuild would have silently killed hardware transcode: the pods still start, they just cannot
open the render node, and it surfaces weeks later as 'Plex got slow'.

That is now impossible. The rules regenerate from talconfig, and any drift shows up as a
non-zero count in task talos:verify against a known-zero baseline.

Worth recording why this was found at all: it surfaced incidentally while investigating device
access for Bluetooth, not through any check. The general lesson — hand-applied machine config
that a workload silently depends on — is exactly what TALOS-0bo8 set out to eliminate, and
this was the concrete instance that proved the problem was real rather than theoretical.

title: minio-operator silently stops reconciling — Tenant CR and live StatefulSet diverge with no error
description:
The MinIO operator stopped watching and never restarted its informers. The pod stayed
Running with 0 restarts for 11 hours and reported nothing wrong.

## SYMPTOM — divergence with no error anywhere
    kubectl get tenant minio -n minio -o jsonpath='{.spec.pools[0].resources.requests.memory}'
      -> 3328Mi        (the CR, correct, applied by Flux from git)
    kubectl get sts minio-pool-0 -n minio -o jsonpath='{...requests.memory}'
      -> 512Mi         (the live workload, stale)
Flux was green. The Tenant CR was correct. The operator was Running. Only the thing the
operator is supposed to produce was wrong.

## EVIDENCE
    kubectl logs -n databases deploy/minio-operator --tail=4
      W0823 21:43:10  watch of *v1.Service ended with: an error...
      W0823 21:43:10  watch of *v1.Pod ended with: an error...
      I0823 21:43:10  Stopping the minio controller
      E0824 00:39:10  Unhandled Error ... Failed to watch...
The controller stopped at 21:43 and the log is silent afterwards apart from one failed
watch retry. 21:43 is when the node it depends on wedged — the same window that left the
Flux controllers with a stale discovery cache.

RBAC was NOT the cause, despite the watch error: verified
    kubectl auth can-i watch pods --as=system:serviceaccount:databases:minio-operator -> yes
The permissions are fine now; the watches simply never came back.

## FIX
    kubectl rollout restart deploy/minio-operator -n databases
Applied 2026-08-24. The live StatefulSet went 512Mi -> 3328Mi within ~2 minutes, which is
eda0's minio sizing finally taking effect. It had been sitting in git and in the CR,
correct and inert, for hours.

## WHY THIS BELONGS IN wedge-buster
This is the same class as the alloy/mimir/spire-agent wedges already covered by the weekly
staggered rollout-restarts in infrastructure/base/kube-system/wedge-buster/: a controller
whose watches die, which keeps running, reports healthy, and silently stops doing its job.
Add minio-operator as a target.

The general lesson is worth recording separately: three times on 2026-08-23/24 the layer
REPORTING success was not the layer that was broken — Flux applying a revision that no
longer contained a change, a HelmRelease going Ready over values discarded by a duplicate
YAML key, and now an operator Running while not reconciling. When a control loop reports
success and the effect is absent, verify the OUTPUT object, not the controller's status.

title: tdarr-server unpinned from talos06 -- both stated reasons were false [DONE]
description:
DONE and verified. Commit d2ec6bfc.

applications/tdarr/base/server.yaml carried 'nodeSelector: kubernetes.io/hostname: talos06' under the comment '# Pin to talos06 for consistent PVC access', and a file header '# Tdarr Server - runs on talos06 (Intel Arc 140T)'. Both false:

  STORAGE -- all six volumes are NFS on 192.168.1.36. Verified every PV in the namespace:
    tdarr-config-pv / tdarr-logs-pv / tdarr-server-pv / tdarr-synology-movies / -tv / -666
    all 'type=NFS:192.168.1.36', none with nodeAffinity.
  GPU -- the live server container requested only cpu/memory and mounted no /dev/dri.
    Transcoding is the worker DaemonSet, which requests gpu.intel.com/i915: 1 and selects
    intel.feature.node.kubernetes.io/gpu-arc=true (matches talos02-gpu and talos06). Untouched.

Verification after removal: pod rescheduled to talos01 -- a node with no GPU and no tdarr storage --
and reached 2/2 Running, Deployment 1/1 Available. Both workers reconnected:
  'Tdarr_Node - Node connected & registered, count:2'

This is the same failure mode as the sonarr pin: a comment asserting a storage reason that the
storage classes contradict.

title: clickstack mongodb + hyperdx clickhouse exclude ALL control-plane nodes; only talos00 is tainted
description:
infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/clickstack/mongodb.yaml:107 and clickstack/clickhouse.yaml:76 both set requiredDuringScheduling nodeAffinity 'node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane DoesNotExist'. The documented reason is real and good: a local-path PV bound to talos00 while talos00 was schedulable, then the control-plane taint was restored and the pod could never be rescheduled -- permanently Pending after the 2026-08-20 reboot.

But the fix is wider than the bug. THREE nodes carry node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: talos00, talos01, talos03. Only talos00 is tainted:

  talos00  TAINTS: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane=:NoSchedule
  talos01  TAINTS: (none)
  talos03  TAINTS: (none)

So the affinity costs 3 of 5 nodes to protect against 1. It is a significant contributor to talos02-gpu carrying 148 running pods vs 25/55/42/59 on the others.

PROPOSAL (needs approval): narrow both to 'kubernetes.io/hostname NotIn [talos00]', which is exactly what infrastructure/base/monitoring/kernel-panic-capture/deployment.yaml already does for the same reason. Same protection, 4 nodes instead of 2. Caveat: it would need revisiting if talos01/talos03 ever get tainted -- worth a comment saying so.

title: Enable kubelet imageMaximumGCAge so container images prune by age, not only at 85% full
description:
Filed 2026-08-24. Root-cause fix behind TALOS-cd73.

## PROBLEM
Talos ships kubelet with age-based image GC disabled:
  imageGCHighThresholdPercent: 85
  imageGCLowThresholdPercent:  80
  imageMinimumGCAge: 2m0s
  imageMaximumGCAge: 0s        <- disabled
(verified: kubectl get --raw /api/v1/nodes/talos06/proxy/configz | jq .kubeletconfig)

That makes image GC purely a disk-pressure reflex. Images accumulate without bound until
a node crosses 85%, and then kubelet dumps down to 80% in one uncontrolled sweep. On
talos06 this let 306 unreferenced images (261.6 GB) sit untouched since April, and the
node coasted to 82.1% — permanently one bad pull away from a GC storm, and 10 percentage
points from the evictionHard nodefs.available=10% line.

The two media nodes are worst because they are the ones with the most churn, but every
node in the cluster has been growing ~2 GB/day since 2026-08-09 with nothing pruning.

## FIX
Add to the kubelet stanza in configs/nodes/worker-base.yaml and
configs/nodes/controlplane.yaml (and the per-node overrides that redefine kubelet:
talos06/worker-talos06.yaml, talos02/worker-talos02-gpu.yaml, talos01, talos03):

  kubelet:
    extraConfig:
      imageMaximumGCAge: 336h   # 14d — anything unreferenced for 2 weeks goes

Then 'talosctl apply-config' per node. NOTE: kubelet config changes do NOT require a
reboot — Talos restarts the kubelet service in place. Verify after with:
  kubectl get --raw /api/v1/nodes/<node>/proxy/configz | jq .kubeletconfig.imageMaximumGCAge

Consider also lowering imageGCHighThresholdPercent to ~75 on the two 1 TB media nodes so
GC has room to act before eviction pressure.

## CAVEAT
imageMaximumGCAge counts from last-use, and images pinned by a running container are
never collected, so this is safe for live workloads. It WILL evict images for
workloads that are scaled to zero but expected to come back — they re-pull on scale-up.

Blocks/relates: TALOS-cd73

title: Route Taskfile through talhelper and delete the old config paths
description:
Leaving both the old and new paths alive is how the repo ends up with two sources of truth again. Remove the old one.

Delete / rewrite:
- scripts/bootstrap-talos-patches.sh — DELETE. Patches are in the generated config now; a script that applies them post-hoc is precisely the failure mode being removed.
- talos:gen-config — rewrite to pull talsecret from 1Password, run talhelper genconfig, shred the plaintext.
- talos:apply-config — point at talos/clusterconfig/<node>.yaml, add a --dry-run variant.
- talos:patches / talos:patches-check — DELETE (obsolete with the script).

REMOVE THE RAW UPGRADE PATH. This matters more than it looks: `talosctl upgrade` defaults --image to ghcr.io/siderolabs/installer:<CLIENT version>. The local client is v1.13.3, the cluster runs v1.13.9 — so a hand-typed upgrade today would BOTH downgrade Talos by six patch releases AND strip every extension. Replace with a task wrapping `talhelper gencommand upgrade`, which emits the correct per-node factory --image derived from that node's schematic (verified in talhelper pkg/generate/command.go).

Also update: docs/05-runbooks/cluster-bootstrap.md, promote-workers-to-controlplane.md, kubernetes-upgrade.md, CLAUDE.md, QUICKSTART.md, and scripts/provision.sh (it still references configs/controlplane.yaml).

Add talos/clusterconfig/ and talos/talsecret.yaml to .gitignore; talhelper writes its own .gitignore but do not rely on it.
acceptance_criteria:
- bootstrap-talos-patches.sh and the patches tasks deleted
- gen-config/apply-config/upgrade route through talhelper
- No raw `talosctl upgrade` remains in the Taskfile
- Runbooks and provision.sh updated
- Generated output and talsecret gitignored
notes:
## PARTIAL 2026-08-24 — Taskfile routed through talhelper, stale paths defused

DONE:
  - task talos:verify and task talos:verify-dry-run added and working, both routed through
    talhelper genconfig against configs/talconfig.yaml
  - the strangler-fig swap completed: talos/ -> configs/, old tree archived to
    .scratch/__configs/ (NOT deleted — it holds untracked CA private keys)
  - four Taskfile vars that pointed at the now-gone configs/nodes/ repointed at the archive
    with an explicit 'this is an archive, not the source of truth' warning, plus the
    replacement commands documented in place

DELIBERATELY NOT DELETED: those vars are kept so any task still using them fails on a
clearly-marked archived path rather than silently succeeding against a stale config. Reading a
months-old hand-maintained file and believing it current is a worse failure than a missing one.

REMAINING:
  - scripts/provision.sh still references configs/controlplane.yaml. It builds a cluster from
    scratch, which is a genuinely different workflow under talhelper (talhelper gencommand
    apply-config) and needs its own rethink rather than a path substitution.
  - scripts/test-suspect-etcd-snapshot.sh has a documentation-only reference; harmless.
  - The older gen-config / apply-config tasks in Taskfile.talos.yaml still assume the
    hand-maintained flow and should be ported or removed.
close_reason:
DONE. Taskfile and scripts now route through talhelper; the dead configs/nodes paths are unreachable by construction rather than by comment.

PORTED (behaviour changed, not just paths):
  - scripts/provision.sh -> a read-only PLANNER. Preflights, refuses if any node in talconfig
    already answers the Talos API, runs talhelper genconfig, prints the ordered rebuild
    sequence from talhelper gencommand. Verified: ZERO mutating commands outside heredocs.
    The cluster CAN still be rebuilt — run task talos:provision, then run what it prints.
    What was traded is UNATTENDED execution, deliberately: the old script provisioned ONE node
    of five, and its step 8.5 removed the control-plane taint, which is now actively WRONG —
    talos00 carries a deliberate hard NoSchedule taint via machine.nodeTaints.
  - task talos:gen-config -> talhelper genconfig. The old talosctl gen config minted a secrets
    bundle unrelated to talsecret.yaml AND wrote talosconfig into the directory holding the
    live admin credential. Today it only errors; ON A FRESH CLONE that file is gitignored, so
    nothing would refuse and it would quietly write a talosconfig for a nonexistent cluster.
  - task talos:apply-config -> requires NODE=<hostname>, regenerates first, asks talhelper
  - scripts/upgrade-talos.py -> records upgrades in talconfig.yaml, not the deleted configs/nodes
  - scripts/bootstrap-talos-patches.sh -> REFUSES TO RUN. Kept as a file so task talos:patches
    explains rather than erroring 'no such file'. It was ALREADY DEAD: an entry packed three
    filenames into one string while the loop read it as a single path, so it hit 'missing patch
    file' and exit 1 before contacting any node, in --check too. Its memory-reserve and
    image-GC patches were never being applied.
    Coverage verified against the GENERATED per-node configs (what a rebuilt node actually
    receives), not against talconfig: all 5 nodes have 3/3 bind mounts, all 4 reserve/GC
    settings, and correct maxPods (200, except talos03 deliberately 60). No gap, no duplicates.

REMOVED: the four archive vars (CONTROLPLANE_CONFIG, WORKER_CONFIG, WORKER_TALOS01_CONFIG,
WORKER_TALOS02_CONFIG) — gen-config/apply-config were the only consumers and both now read
generated files. A comment records that they existed and why they went.
⚠️ DO NOT REINSTATE provision.sh's taint removal. It fights declared config.

DOCS: 9 rewritten, 15 bannered (procedures whose reasoning is still valuable), including all 11
docs/05-runbooks/talos-*-patch.yaml which now name their live configs/patches/ counterpart.
README.md rewritten separately — one line was ACTIVELY FALSE ('the machine configs actually in
use live in configs/nodes/'), which would have sent a reader to edit an archived file.

⚠️ RECOVERY DOC WAS BROKEN: docs/05-runbooks/cluster-bootstrap.md, described in its own index as
'the authoritative recovery path', still told you to run the retired script AND had a wrong
Step 1. Fixed. Separately talsecret-1password-backup.md was broken THREE ways on the one file
the cluster is unrecoverable without — wrong directory, wrong cert count (said 5, is 4), and a
'just regenerate' step sourcing an archived file. Replaced with a TESTED lossless extraction.

VERIFIED: task --list exits 0; all 31 talos: tasks --dry resolve; talos 31 / dev 25 / k8s 18 /
infra 12 / security 10 / certs 9. All 30 shell scripts parse, both python scripts compile.
task talos:verify reports 0 differences across all five nodes.

title: Guardrails: LimitRange defaultRequest, request-vs-usage alerts, extend Goldilocks, PriorityClasses
description:
Point fixes decay. 65 containers reached production with no memory request at all and
228 with no limit because nothing in the admission path required either. This ticket
adds the backstops so the epic does not have to be repeated in six months.

## 1. LimitRange with defaultRequest ONLY (not default limit)

    apiVersion: v1
    kind: LimitRange
    metadata:
      name: default-requests
    spec:
      limits:
        - type: Container
          defaultRequest:
            memory: 64Mi
            cpu: 10m

    defaultRequest applies a request to any container that declares none. It does NOT
    set a limit, so it cannot break the burstable workloads this epic deliberately
    leaves unlimited (tdarr, kometa, posterizarr, minio, mimir-compactor,
    mimir-store-gateway, plex, immich-ml, stash-ai, frigate).

    DO NOT add a `default:` (limit) stanza. That is the one change that would convert
    a legitimate transcode spike into a cluster-wide OOMKill policy.

    Roll out per namespace, application namespaces first. Note it only affects pods
    created AFTER it lands, and it does not apply to the control-plane static pods
    (kubelet creates those directly, bypassing API admission).

## 2. Alert on request-vs-usage drift

    Add to the baseline alert rules
    (infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/baseline-alerts):

    - alert: ContainerMemoryRequestUnderDeclared
      expr: |
        (
          max by (namespace, pod, container) (
            max_over_time(container_memory_working_set_bytes{container!=""}[24h])
          )
          /
          max by (namespace, pod, container) (
            kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="memory"} > 0
          )
        ) > 2
      for: 6h
      labels: {severity: warning}
      annotations:
        summary: "{{$labels.namespace}}/{{$labels.pod}}/{{$labels.container}} peaked at >2x its memory request"

    - alert: ContainerNoMemoryRequest
      expr: |
        count by (namespace, pod, container) (
          container_memory_working_set_bytes{container!=""}
        )
        unless
        count by (namespace, pod, container) (
          kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="memory"}
        )
      for: 1h
      labels: {severity: warning}

    - alert: NodeMemoryRequestsNearAllocatable
      expr: |
        sum by (node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="memory"})
        / on(node) kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="memory"} > 0.90
      for: 30m
      labels: {severity: critical}
      annotations:
        summary: "{{$labels.node}} has >90% of allocatable memory requested"

    The third one would have fired days before talos03 wedged: talos01 and talos03 have
    both been above 0.90 continuously.

## 3. Extend Goldilocks/VPA coverage

    vpa-recommender and Goldilocks are ALREADY DEPLOYED (kube-system/vpa-recommender,
    84 VPA objects) but only in 10 namespaces:

      monitoring 38, media 16, homepage 8, crossplane-demo 7, argocd 6,
      home-automation 3, scratch 3, traefik 1, honeypot 1, iocaine 1

    Missing entirely: kube-system, kyverno, flux-system, crossplane-system, kubevirt,
    cdi, authentik, crowdsec, boomtime, catalyst-llm, catalyst-data, forgejo,
    media-experimental, media-private, tdarr, minio, databases, backup, keda,
    external-secrets, cert-manager, vpn-gateway, downloads, openscad, gaming, pihole.

    Add the goldilocks.fairwinds.com/enabled=true label to those namespaces. This
    epic's analysis becomes self-maintaining -- next time it is `kubectl get vpa -A`,
    not a Mimir excavation.

    CAVEATS found while cross-checking (see the epic for the full comparison):
      - VPA has a hard floor around 125-250Mi. For anything genuinely smaller than
        that its recommendation is the floor, not evidence. Do not blindly apply it
        to exporters and sidecars -- it would ADD ~4 GiB of fictional requests across
        the ~25 small containers in this cluster.
      - VPA targets a percentile, not a peak, so it UNDER-recommends bursty workloads
        (it says 250M for mimir-compactor which peaks at 622M, and 125M for
        loki-chunks-cache/memcached which holds 8246M by design). Never apply VPA
        output to a BURST-NOLIM workload.
      - Where both methods have real data they agree closely: mimir-ingester 1.16x,
        argocd-application-controller 1.00x, tempo 1.00x, loki 0.98x.

## 4. PriorityClasses

    277 of 328 running pods have no priorityClassName. Under memory pressure the
    kubelet ranks eviction victims by QoS and by usage-over-request, with no way to
    express "evict the media app before the ingress controller".

    Define and apply, at minimum:
      platform-critical  (value 900000)  cilium, traefik, coredns, local-path,
                                         external-secrets-webhook, cloudnative-pg
      data-critical      (value 800000)  CNPG instances, minio, mimir-ingester
      observability      (value 100000)  the rest of monitoring
      default            (value 0)       everything else, globalDefault: true

    This is what converts "talos03 wedges" into "the least important pod on talos03
    is evicted", which is the outcome the node reservations in commit 4ec05ec1 were
    aiming at.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
DESIGN ONLY — nothing implemented. The headline finding changes this ticket's shape.

## THE GUARDRAIL ALREADY EXISTS AND IS POINTED AT THE WRONG HALF OF THE CLUSTER

VPA + Goldilocks are deployed and healthy, with 84 VerticalPodAutoscalers, and ALL 84 have live recommendations:
  kubectl get vpa -A -o json | jq '[.items[]|select(.status.recommendation!=null)]|length'  ->  84
  infra-control/goldilocks-controller 1/1, goldilocks-dashboard 1/1, kube-system/vpa-recommender 1/1

Coverage by namespace: monitoring 38, media 16, homepage 8, crossplane-demo 7, argocd 6, scratch 3, home-automation 3, traefik/iocaine/honeypot 1 each. Ten namespaces.

FIFTY-ONE namespaces have no VPA at all, and they include every platform namespace this epic is about: kube-system, flux-system, cert-manager, external-secrets, kyverno, databases, kubevirt, cdi, minio, backup, tdarr, downloads, local-path-storage, intel-device-plugins, registry, vpn-gateway, crossplane-system.

That is exactly where TALOS-gj3n's 87 groups and most of TALOS-ynzw's zero-request containers live. Where VPA WAS looking it was already right -- its target for argocd-application-controller is 1,836,551,791 bytes (1751Mi) against a 512Mi request, which independently corroborates TALOS-gj3n's 1536Mi proposal. Nobody was reading it.

So item 3 of this ticket ('extend Goldilocks') is not a nice-to-have addition, it is THE fix, and items 1/2 are the backstops. Recommend reordering.

Caveat when reading VPA output: targets of exactly 125Mi or 250Mi are the recommender's floor, not a real recommendation. Only byte-valued targets are measured. Several of the 250Mi entries (argocd-notifications-controller for one) are well above what I measured -- 122Mi peak over 24h.

## 1. LimitRange defaultRequest — endorsed, with one property that makes it better than proposed

Zero LimitRanges exist cluster-wide today (kubectl get limitrange -A -> 0).

The important property the ticket does not mention: LimitRanger is a BUILT-IN admission plugin running in-process in the apiserver, not a webhook. Verified on the live apiservers -- the flag is --enable-admission-plugins=NodeRestriction, which ADDS to the default-on set, and there is no --disable-admission-plugins, so LimitRanger is active.

That matters because Kyverno CANNOT mutate kube-system (it is in the resourceFilters exclusion list). A LimitRange can. So a LimitRange is the ONLY declarative way to reach the three cases I could not fix in manifests during TALOS-ynzw:
  intel-device-plugins/intel-gpu-plugin x3 -- the GpuDevicePlugin CRD has no resources field at all (kubectl explain confirms); the operator generates the DaemonSet
  minio/minio-pool-0/sidecar             -- injected by the MinIO operator
  kubernetes-dashboard x2                -- no manifest in this repo
Those 6 containers cannot be fixed any other way short of forking an operator.

Two corrections to the ticket's stanza:
  - The claim that it does not apply to control-plane static pods is CORRECT and worth keeping -- kubelet creates those directly and bypasses API admission entirely.
  - A container that sets a LIMIT but no request already gets request=limit from Kubernetes. defaultRequest only fires when NEITHER is set. So it cannot silently shrink anything that is already partly specified.

Agreed emphatically on NOT adding a 'default:' limit stanza. 177 of 368 running containers currently have no memory limit and a good number of those are deliberate -- tdarr worker and server, kometa, frigate, minio, mimir-compactor, mimir-store-gateway, posterizarr. A default limit would convert every one of those into an OOMKill policy.

## 2. Alerts — genuinely new, no overlap

Checked baseline-alerts/memory-pressure-alerts.yaml: it has CiliumAgentMemoryHigh/Critical/OOMKilled, NodeMemoryPressure, NodeMemoryHigh, NodeMemoryPSIHigh, Talos00MemoryProfile, Talos00CiliumAgentMemoryDanger, Talos00MemoryCgroupOOMKill. Every one is node-level or cilium-specific. There is NO per-container request-vs-usage rule anywhere. The three proposed rules are additive.

One change to ContainerMemoryRequestUnderDeclared: use a 7d window, not 24h. Measured proof from this session -- tdarr-node peaks at 1150Mi over 24h and 1259Mi over 7d. A 24h window sized that workload wrong and would have kept it under-declared. Episodic workloads (transcode, batch metadata, backup) need the longer window or the alert produces false confidence.

Add a fourth rule that would have caught the largest single problem in this epic directly:
  alert: NodeMemoryAvailableLow
  expr: min_over_time(node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes[7d]) < 2147483648
Measured now: talos03 got to 0.61 GiB free and talos01 to 1.20 GiB over the last 7 days, while talos02-gpu and talos06 never went below ~25 GiB. That one query identifies the wedge with no modelling in it at all.

## 3. PriorityClasses

Only four exist and two are built-in: system-node-critical, system-cluster-critical, kubevirt-cluster-critical (1000000000), pihole-critical (900000000). There is no tiering for anything else, so under memory pressure the kubelet's eviction order is decided entirely by usage-over-request -- which is exactly the number this epic just spent its time correcting. Worth doing, but AFTER the requests are honest; a priority scheme layered on fictional requests just encodes the fiction.

## SUGGESTED ORDER
  1. Extend VPA/Goldilocks to the 51 uncovered namespaces, platform first. Read what it already knows before writing any new policy.
  2. NodeMemoryAvailableLow + ContainerNoMemoryRequest alerts (cheap, immediate).
  3. LimitRange defaultRequest per namespace, application namespaces first, specifically to close the 6 operator-generated containers.
  4. ContainerMemoryRequestUnderDeclared at 7d, once the epic's own fixes have settled and it will not fire on everything.
  5. PriorityClasses last.

title: media/tdarr/GPU batch: burstable classification (no limits on transcode) + resize, net -11.6 GiB
description:
media / media-experimental / media-private / tdarr / downloads / openscad / gaming /
scratch / dungeon-library. 68 workload groups, NET -11.6 GiB (this batch gives memory
BACK). It also contains most of the workloads that must stay BURSTABLE.

## THE BURSTABLE RULE FOR THIS BATCH

Transcode, GPU, indexing and batch workloads idle low and spike hard. For these a
memory LIMIT is actively harmful: it converts a legitimate spike into an OOMKill in the
middle of a job, which loses the job's work and then retries it, producing a
worse-than-linear failure. Set an honest request (so the scheduler sees the steady
state) and NO limit.

    workload                  req now -> new   limit    measured p50/peak   ratio  why no limit
    tdarr/tdarr-worker  n=2     1024M -> 384M   NONE      323M / 826M       2.6x   transcode spike
    tdarr/tdarr-server          2048M -> 1024M  NONE      873M / 969M       1.1x   holds flow/queue state
    media/kometa                 512M -> 192M   NONE      105M / 105M       1.0x   library-scan batch;
                                                                                    peak is between runs
    media/posterizarr            512M -> 320M   NONE      250M / 253M       1.0x   asset-generation batch
    media/plex                   256M -> 512M   NONE      433M / 681M       1.6x   GPU transcode sessions
    media-private/immich-ml     1024M -> 320M   NONE      259M / 362M       1.4x   ML inference bursts
    media-private/stash-ai       2048M -> 128M  NONE       95M / 127M       1.3x   ML inference bursts
    scratch/frigate             2048M -> 512M   NONE      338M / 431M       1.3x   detection bursts

    kometa and posterizarr have peak == p50 over 14d, which means they were NOT
    observed mid-run in the window -- their true peak is above the measured number.
    That is exactly why they get no limit: the measurement cannot bound them and a
    guessed limit would be a guessed OOMKill. The requests above are set from
    observed steady state, deliberately not from peak.

## GPU PLACEMENT IS NOT A CONSTRAINT

    gpu.intel.com/i915 allocatable:  talos02-gpu 10,  talos06 10,  others 0
    (node label intel.feature.node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true is on talos01, talos02-gpu
     and talos06)

    Current GPU consumers: media/plex, media/jellyfin, media-private/stash,
    tdarr/tdarr-worker x2 -- all on talos02-gpu except one tdarr worker on talos06.

    talos02-gpu is at 90% of CPU requests. talos06 is at 32% CPU and 35% memory and
    has the same 10 i915 shares. Moving plex + jellyfin + stash to talos06 is
    unblocked by GPU and relieves talos02-gpu's CPU. See the evacuate/rebalance child.

## THE OVER-DECLARERS IN THIS BATCH

    namespace           workload/container            n  REQnow REQnew LIMnow LIMnew  p50   peak
    openscad            manyfold-perf-worker/worker   2   2048M   640M     0M  1024M  406M   413M
