title: whisparr crash-loop root cause: stray root folder /data/666 spawned empty series + indexer storms
description:
RESOLVED 2026-08-18. Reported as a suspected OOM; it was NOT OOM (145Mi of a 512Mi limit, lastState exitCode=0 reason=Completed). Also not CPU (live 45s sample: 0 throttled periods, 0.002 of 0.300 cores) and no hung NFS.

ACTUAL CAUSE: whisparr had TWO root folders registered. id=3 /data/content/content/whisparr (correct — the PVC is synology /volume1/666 mounted at /data/content, so the library lands there) and a stray id=1 /data/666/content/whisparr which was unreachable under that mount. Whisparr kept adding NEW empty series to the unreachable root (ids 21-24, 0 files each) and storming 3 indexers ('Processing 338 releases' on repeat), saturating its .NET thread pool (53 threads, 39 ThreadPool) until /ping stopped answering even from inside the pod -> liveness kills -> 52 restarts. RootFolderCheck.Check() also threw ThrowFormatError on the bad root.

MISSTEP WORTH REMEMBERING: I first 'fixed' this by remapping the mount to /data/666 to match the stray root (talos-private fc383c4). Wrong end. Both paths reach the same share, and the API showed 20 series WITH FILES (2721 total) under /data/content vs 4 EMPTY ones under /data/666 — so remapping repaired 4 junk entries and broke the whole real library. Reverted in 061b1b0. LESSON: when two paths both look plausible, check which one the records with actual DATA use, before changing the mount.

FIX: reverted mountPath to /data/content, deleted stray root folder id=1, deleted the 4 empty series (deleteFiles=false, no media touched). END STATE: one root folder, accessible=true; 20 series, 2721 files; pod 1/1 Ready, 0 restarts, /ping OK, no RootFolderCheck errors since. Remaining separate issue: qBittorrent auth (TALOS-8d1i).

title: whisparr: qBittorrent authentication failing (DownloadClientAuthenticationException)
description: Found while diagnosing the whisparr crash-loop 2026-08-17. Separate from the mountPath fix (talos-private fc383c4) — whisparr can see its library again but still cannot talk to its download client, so completed downloads will not import. Check the qBittorrent credentials stored in whisparr's settings vs the actual qbittorrent service (creds may have rotated, or the WebUI host/port changed). Also seen: '[Error] CommandExecutor: Error occurred while executing task CheckHealth ... System.Text.ValueStringBuilder.ThrowFormatError()'.

title: Span audit + instrument boomtime with OpenTelemetry (MVP tracing demo)
description:
AUDIT (measured 2026-08-15): the cluster generates essentially ZERO application spans. Only two workloads export OTLP at all — monitoring/app (HyperDX self-instrumenting) and monitoring/otel-collector — i.e. the observability stack watching itself. boomtime has NO opentelemetry dependencies in go.mod whatsoever. So Tempo (and now ClickStack's otel_traces) are wired end-to-end with no producers; otel_traces sits at 0 rows.

WHY BOOMTIME IS THE RIGHT FIRST TARGET: (1) it is Go/Echo, the best-supported instrumentation path; (2) its logs ALREADY flow to Loki+ClickStack, and otel_logs already carries TraceId/SpanId columns — so injecting trace_id into boomtime's slog output completes HyperDX log<->trace correlation, which is the single feature that justifies running ClickStack; (3) there is a REAL open performance question to solve with it: TALOS bug 'ingest p95 on /heartbeats.bulk is ~6.4s' — tracing would show exactly which span (per-row inserts? sync fan-out? index churn?) burns those seconds. That turns this from a demo into a diagnosis.

MVP SCOPE: go.opentelemetry.io/otel SDK + otelecho middleware (HTTP server spans) + otelhttp (outbound) + DB instrumentation (otelpgx/otelsql for the CNPG calls) + slog handler that stamps trace_id/span_id into log records. Export OTLP to the in-cluster collector: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://alloy.monitoring.svc:4318 (Alloy already receives OTLP on 4317/4318 and, as of commit dc8d209, dual-writes traces to BOTH Tempo and ClickStack — no pipeline work needed). Set OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=boomtime. Sampling: start head-based at 100% (homelab volume is tiny), revisit if noisy.

VERIFY: spans visible in Tempo AND rows in default.otel_traces; then in HyperDX create a Trace source and set the Logs source's Correlated Trace Source (TALOS-xam9) and confirm you can pivot from a boomtime log line to its trace. Stretch: attach the heartbeats.bulk latency finding to a real trace waterfall.

NOTE: boomtime lives in its own repo (workspace/boomtime, ArgoCD-deployed) — code change there, env wiring in k8s/overlays/talos00-knowledgedump.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
DONE + VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-15 (boomtime commits 8e8beef, 727034f — deployed as sha-727034f).

WORKING:
- 'tracing: enabled service=boomtime endpoint=http://alloy.monitoring.svc:4318' on startup.
- Spans in ClickHouse default.otel_traces, ServiceName='boomtime'. Span names are ROUTE TEMPLATES ('GET /api/v1/config/public', 'GET /*'), not raw URLs — cardinality bounded like metricsMiddleware.
- Logs now carry trace_id/span_id, and a trace_id taken from a log line resolves to its span in otel_traces. Full loop proven.

TWO GOTCHAS WORTH KEEPING:
1. contrib otelecho is echo/v4-only (v0.70.0 requires labstack/echo/v4) and boomtime is echo/v5 -> middleware is hand-rolled in internal/tracing/middleware.go. Echo v5 also returns http.ResponseWriter from c.Response(), so status needs the *echo.Response type assertion (same as metricsMiddleware).
2. slog hands the ctx to handlers ONLY on the *Context variants. The first cut used logger.Info() and emitted ZERO trace_id lines; logger.InfoContext(c.Request().Context(), ...) fixed it. Any other logger that should correlate must use the *Context form.

REMAINING (UI, 1 field): boomtime's trace_id sits inside the JSON Body, not the OTLP TraceId column (logs arrive via stdout scraping -> loki.source.kubernetes -> otelcol.receiver.loki, which cannot populate the native field). So in HyperDX's Logs source set 'Trace Id Expression' to JSONExtractString(Body, 'trace_id') for the UI pivot. Native-column correlation would need an OTLP log exporter in-app instead of stdout scraping — separate decision.

NEXT: instrument the DB layer (otelpgx/otelsql) so the ~6.4s p95 on /heartbeats.bulk shows a real waterfall — HTTP spans alone won't show which query burns it.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
DB SPANS LIVE + FIRST DIAGNOSIS (2026-08-15, boomtime sha-145026a).

otelpgx spans confirmed in ClickHouse: Server spans (GET /*, POST /api/v1/query), Client 'pool.acquire' (connection-pool wait), and per-query spans with timings — the full waterfall.

*** SMOKING GUN for the /heartbeats.bulk latency ***
Captured real ingest traffic. POST /api/v1/users/current/heartbeats.bulk = 116.9ms p95 on a SMALL batch, and the child spans apportion it clearly:
  - UPDATE heartbeats SET gap_seconds (the anchor/lag window-function query): 72.9ms p95 / 76.3ms max  <-- ~63% of the request
  - INSERT INTO hb_rollup_daily: 10.6ms
  - batch INSERT INTO heartbeats: ~0ms (batched, cheap)
  - prepare hb_rollup_daily: 0.8ms

So the cost is NOT the heartbeat inserts — it is the gap_seconds recalculation. That query computes lag() over EVERY heartbeat for the sender from an anchor timestamp forward, so its cost scales with history size (the instance has ~440k heartbeats) and with batch size. That is the mechanism behind the ~6.4s p95 seen on large batches, and it will keep degrading as history grows.

FIX DIRECTIONS (not yet done): bound the recompute window (only rows at/after the batch's earliest time_sent rather than from the anchor), or make gap_seconds incremental per inserted row, or move the rollup+gap work off the request path into the existing job queue. Verify with the same span waterfall afterwards.

Also note: otelpgx uses the full SQL text as the span name, which is verbose/high-cardinality in ClickHouse. Fine at homelab volume; revisit with otelpgx span-name options if it becomes noisy.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
GAP_SECONDS OPTIMIZATION SHIPPED + MEASURED (2026-08-17, boomtime sha-872a6a9).

ROOT CAUSE (not what the p95 suggested): cost was never about batch SIZE. The query recomputed and UPDATEd every row from the batch's oldest timestamp through to NOW, unbounded. Measured on live data (546,481 heartbeats):
  - since = 10 min ago  -> ~1 row,     0.098ms, 21 buffers
  - since = 30 days ago -> 83,090 rows, 58ms just to SELECT (plus writing them all)
So the trigger is an OFFLINE BACKLOG FLUSH (WakaTime-style plugins queue while offline and dump on reconnect), which makes 'since' the age of the oldest queued beat. That is why the symptom was a TAIL, not uniform slowness.

FIX: a batch can only change the gaps of its own rows plus the ONE existing beat that now follows its newest row — everything later keeps the same predecessor. Added recomputeGapsUntil with a 'horizon' CTE upper bound (deliberately INCLUDING the following beat). Cost is now proportional to the batch, not to how far back it reaches. Full-rebuild callers (admin restore, health.go) pass nil and keep unbounded behaviour.

MEASURED via the otelpgx span waterfall (gap query spans):
  BEFORE: 322 spans, avg 85.7ms, p95 20.8ms, MAX 3,889.6ms
  AFTER:  4 spans,  avg  5.6ms, p95 11.3ms, MAX    11.7ms
Max fell 3.9s -> 11.7ms. Note BEFORE avg (85.7) exceeding its p95 (20.8) is the signature of exactly the heavy tail described above.

CORRECTNESS: new regression test internal/db/gap_window_test.go backfills BETWEEN existing beats and asserts the FOLLOWING beat is re-gapped (the assertion the horizon exists for). Verified it has teeth via a mutation — narrowing the horizon makes it fail. Full internal/db + internal/ingest suites green.

CAVEAT / STILL TO CONFIRM: only 4 post-deploy gap spans so far and NO post-deploy endpoint-level sample yet (BEFORE was 111 reqs, p95 53.8ms, max 522.3ms). The decisive test is the next real backlog flush — recheck the heartbeats.bulk Server span max after a client reconnects from offline.

title: ClickStack logs have EMPTY ServiceName — map Loki pod labels to OTLP service.name
description: Verified 2026-08-15: all ~1.9M rows in default.otel_logs have ServiceName=''. The k8s pod-log firehose reaches ClickStack via loki.source.kubernetes -> otelcol.receiver.loki, and that conversion does not populate the OTLP service.name resource attribute, so HyperDX cannot group/filter by service — a major UX loss for a log-analytics tool (namespace/pod/container are in LogAttributes but service is blank). FIX: in Alloy's discovery.relabel.pod_logs, emit a label the converter promotes to service.name (OTel's Loki receiver honours the 'service_name' label / loki.resource.labels hint), or add an otelcol.processor.transform to set resource attribute service.name from the pod/container labels. DEFERRED deliberately: this is a third Alloy config change in one day and Alloy config errors take the WHOLE collector down (2026-08-15 crashloop) — land it as its own tested change. Logs are flowing correctly meanwhile.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-08-17 (commit 8876ce9): ServiceName rendered empty because stdout-scraped pod logs never populate the native OTLP columns. No Alloy change was needed — Alloy already parses the JSON body into LogAttributes, so app/container/trace_id/span_id are present as indexed map keys. serviceNameExpression now coalesces ServiceName -> app -> app.kubernetes.io/name -> container -> 'unknown' (verified live: kometa/traefik/mimir/kube-controller-manager/goldilocks/vpa-recommender/alloy/loki all resolve), and trace/span ids read LogAttributes instead of JSONExtract on Body (map lookup, no per-row JSON parse). Declared in git via hyperdx.defaultSources AND applied to Mongo. VERIFIED: 1059 logs carry trace_ids in 30m and 699 JOIN to real spans in otel_traces — the log->trace pivot resolves.

title: EVALUATE (not migrate) ClickStack metrics vs Mimir — replacement is a big-ticket item
description: Operator idea 2026-08-15: could ClickStack replace Mimir and collapse the ingestion pipeline? MEASURED DEPENDENCY SURFACE: 91 alert rules across 15 PrometheusRules (incl. the platform-regression pack just built), 55 ServiceMonitors/PodMonitors, plus the Alertmanager->Discord bridge and Mimir ruler. ALL of that is PromQL and Prometheus-operator semantics. ClickStack metrics are SQL/ClickHouse-native, so a true replacement means rewriting every alert rule and every dashboard query, and re-homing the ruler — a large, risky project, NOT a config flip. RECOMMENDED PATH: dual-write a SUBSET of metrics to ClickStack to evaluate its metrics UX and query ergonomics honestly, while Mimir remains the alerting/PromQL engine. Only revisit full replacement if the evaluation is compelling AND an alerting story exists (ClickStack alerting maturity is the gating question). Depends on trace dual-write landing first.

comments.text: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-15: proceed with the SUBSET test — dual-write a subset of metrics to ClickStack to evaluate its metrics UX/query ergonomics, while Mimir remains the PromQL + alerting engine (91 alert rules / 15 PrometheusRules / 55 Service+PodMonitors depend on it). title: Traefik ingress VIP via Cilium LB-IPAM (single-node SPOF: svc LoadBalancer stuck pending)
description: FOUND 2026-08-15: svc/traefik is type=LoadBalancer but EXTERNAL-IP has always been <pending> — the existing CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool 'lan-pihole-pool' (192.168.1.240-250) and CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy 'lan-pihole-l2' both select ONLY matchLabels app=pihole, and traefik's svc is labeled app.kubernetes.io/name=traefik. So all LAN ingress reaches Traefik via NodePort/hostPort on individual node IPs, and Pi-hole's *.talos00 wildcard points at ONE node (192.168.1.54) = hard SPOF. Proved 2026-08-15: the traefik DaemonSet pod on talos00 restarted after a control-plane reboot and came back with NO routes, 404ing every .talos00 host, while talos01/talos06 served 200. FIX: add a CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool + CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy selecting the traefik svc (e.g. .251 or extend the existing range), then repoint Pi-hole's *.talos00 wildcard at that VIP — Cilium L2 fails the VIP over to a healthy node automatically. CAVEAT (be honest): a VIP alone would NOT have fixed the observed failure — with externalTrafficPolicy=Cluster a route-less-but-Ready pod yields INTERMITTENT 404s (1-in-5) instead of a clean outage. Pair it with root-causing why Traefik lost its IngressRoutes (started while the apiserver was wedged and never re-listed?) and consider externalTrafficPolicy=Local + a readiness probe that reflects route loading.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
DONE 2026-08-15 (commit 1206266): svc/traefik now holds VIP 192.168.1.251 via new lan-traefik-pool (.251-.252) + lan-traefik-l2 announcement policy. Verified: grafana/hyperdx/mimir.talos00 all return 200 through the VIP.

GOTCHA WORTH REMEMBERING: creating the pool+policy was NOT enough — the VIP was assigned by the operator (LB-IPAM) but NO L2 lease was created and the VIP was unreachable, with zero errors logged. cilium-agent (which runs L2 leader election) had not re-evaluated the new policy; restarting agents created cilium-l2announce-traefik-traefik immediately. Rolled the whole DaemonSet so EVERY node can take the lease — otherwise only the one restarted node could hold it, i.e. fake HA. Failover proven during that roll: the lease moved talos01 -> talos00 with no interruption in service.

REMAINING (human, 1 line): repoint Pi-hole's *.talos00 wildcard from 192.168.1.54 to 192.168.1.251. Until then ingress still resolves to a single node and the SPOF stands — the VIP is live and additive, node-IP access unchanged.

NOT DONE deliberately: svc/traefik stays externalTrafficPolicy=Cluster; flipping to Local changes client-IP preservation which CrowdSec bans depend on. Also still open: why the talos00 traefik pod returned from reboot with zero routes while passing readiness (/ping returns OK with an empty routing table) — a VIP does not fix that class, it turns a hard 404 into intermittent 1-in-5.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
FINDINGS for the two remaining items (2026-08-15 research):

(1) externalTrafficPolicy — MORE important than first thought. Traefik binds hostPort 80/443, so node-IP traffic hits the local pod directly with client IP intact. But the NEW VIP path goes through Service load-balancing, and with Cluster policy it can forward to another node's pod = SNAT = CrowdSec sees node IPs, not real clients (wrong bans, missed attackers). Fix is one line (service.spec.externalTrafficPolicy: Local); safe because Traefik is a DaemonSet so every node has a local backend; bonus is that VIP placement becomes local-endpoint-health aware.

(2) Readiness blind spot — CANNOT be fixed in the probe. Traefik's image is scratch-based (no shell/curl), so an exec probe that asserts a non-empty router table is impossible, and a plain httpGet on /api/http/routers returns 200 even when the list is empty. So it needs external detection + auto-heal:
  (a) PREREQUISITE, and a genuine gap: THERE IS NO ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor FOR TRAEFIK AT ALL. svc/traefik-metrics:9100 exists with a valid selector but nothing scrapes it — traefik_* metric names are in Mimir's index from some past period but have NO current data. We are flying blind on Traefik today.
  (b) Then alert on the real signal: traefik_config_last_reload_success (per-instance gauge, unix ts of last successful config load) — catches 'process up, routing table empty', which /ping cannot.
  (c) Auto-heal via the established wedge-buster pattern: CronJob curls a known vhost through each Traefik pod and deletes any returning 404 (same shape as cronjob-cdi-certs).

ROOT CAUSE still unconfirmed: most likely Traefik's kubernetesCRD provider watch died while the apiserver was wedged and never re-listed. (b) gives us the signal to catch it live next time.

title: HyperDX UI process not starting — pod listens on 8000/4320 but not 3000 (404 at hyperdx.talos00)
description: See TALOS-cjny comment 2026-08-15. Frontend served once pre-reboot then stopped starting; readiness only probes the API port so the pod falsely reads 1/1. Explicit resources did not fix. Investigate image entrypoint/process supervisor and whether chart 1.1.1 expects a separate UI component.
close_reason: FALSE ALARM — not a HyperDX bug. The UI was healthy all along (next-server PID running, listening on 3000 IPv4; service curl returns 200). Two diagnostic errors on my side: (1) I checked /proc/net/tcp6 only, missing the IPv4 listener, and my in-pod 'localhost:3000' test resolved to ::1 giving a false 'connection refused'; (2) I tested the UI exclusively through 192.168.1.54, where the Traefik DaemonSet pod had restarted after the control-plane reboot and come back WITHOUT its routes — it 404'd EVERY .talos00 host (mimir/grafana too), while talos01/talos06 served 200. Fixed by deleting that one Traefik pod. LESSON: when a route 404s, test the other nodes' Traefik pods before blaming the app — /etc/hosts pins *.talos00 to 192.168.1.54 so a single bad DaemonSet pod looks cluster-wide.

comments.text:
STATUS 2026-08-15 — ClickStack DEPLOYED, dual-write BLOCKED on human step.

DONE (live, committed):
- ClickHouse via Altinity CHI 'hyperdx-logs' (monitoring ns, 50Gi local-path, CH 26.7-alpine — latest). Healthy; collector created all otel_logs/otel_traces/otel_metrics_* tables.
- ClickStack chart 1.1.1 / app 2.8.0, bundled CH disabled, mongo bumped 5.0.32 -> 8.3.8 (works). All 4 pods 1/1.
- UI LIVE at http://hyperdx.talos00 (HTTP 200 via Traefik). Fully self-hosted, usageStatsEnabled=false.
- Chart quirks fixed: helm timeout 5m->20m (default killed pods mid-boot); clickhouse.config.users.otelUserName forced to 'default' (chart templates the COLLECTOR's user from these keys even with clickhouse.enabled=false, defaulting to a user only its bundled STS creates).

BLOCKED — dual-write needs a HUMAN step:
ClickStack's OTLP receivers (4317/4318) are NOT static — they are pushed to the collector via OpAMP, and are secured by an ingestion API key that HyperDX generates ONLY when the first team is created. Collector currently listens on 8888/13133/24225 only ('No last received remote config'). This key is NOT a SaaS/license key — it is minted by our own instance and stored in our own MongoDB, same class as our MinIO/authentik bootstrap creds.
NEXT: (1) create account at http://hyperdx.talos00; (2) Team Settings -> API Keys -> copy ingestion key; (3) put it in 1Password (e.g. item 'hyperdx', field 'ingestion_api_key'); (4) ESO ExternalSecret -> monitoring ns; (5) re-land the Alloy dual-write leg WITH the auth header.

ALLOY DUAL-WRITE REVERTED (commit 4c16328) — do not re-apply as-is. Two lessons: (a) otelcol.processor.batch REQUIRES send_batch_max_size >= send_batch_size or Alloy REFUSES TO LOAD THE WHOLE CONFIG and crashloops (this took the main collector down); (b) it cannot work at all until the API key above exists. Re-land as ONE change: receiver.loki -> batch(with max_size) -> otlphttp with authorization header from the ESO secret.

title: XGPUInstance: GPU box + EBS hot-cache seeded from S3 model coldstore (POC-DEMO v2)
description: Design locked with operator 2026-08-14: S3 bucket (XBucket catalyst-tbdc-models, Standard-IA or Glacier-INSTANT-RETRIEVAL tier — NOT deep glacier, retrieval latency kills the loop) holds the ~1TB model library at ~$4-13/mo. Per-boot EBS = small ephemeral cache (gp3 200-300GB, deleteOnTermination:true) seeded in userData via s5cmd sync of ONLY spec.models[] prefixes (same-region S3→EC2 transfer free, ~1-2GB/s). NOT a 1TB EBS ($80/mo standing). spec: models[], cacheVolumeGb=200, instanceType=g5.xlarge, spot. Composition = XInstance members + ebs Volume + VolumeAttachment + HF_HOME on cache. Leaner variant to evaluate: vLLM runai-streamer loads weights DIRECT from S3 (skip EBS for single-model runs). Depends: TALOS-3g8f creds + models XBucket. Blocked-by-human; build fresh session.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text: SEEDING DESIGN (operator session 2026-08-14): (1) XSeedJob = one-shot Fargate task (the AWS init-container) — hf download → s5cmd → S3 library, ~$0.10-0.50/model, clean death, NO EC2 self-terminating seeder (crossplane drift-correction resurrects terminated instances = zombie loop). (2) GPU box always boots from S3, never HF — seed once, warm-boot many. (3) Lazy self-seed fallback in XGPUInstance userData (if model absent in S3: HF→/cache→sync up; ~$0.02 of GPU time per 16GB model — cheap-seeder econ only matters for the initial 1TB bulk load). (4) No cross-MR sequencing needed — seeder and rig decouple through S3. PREREQ: hf_token field on the aws-crossplane 1P item for gated models (noted on TALOS-3g8f).

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text: ROUTING + SCALE-TO-ZERO DESIGN (v1alpha2): (1) endpoint: tailscale/wireguard in userData (egress-only SG holds) → selectorless Service+EndpointSlice vllm-aws.svc → litellm backend entry (authentik-gated, local-model fallback). (2) spec.running bool via function-go-templating conditional render: false = Instance member omitted → crossplane DELETES the EC2 (bill off) while the EBS cache member persists warm (~$16/mo parked); true = reboot + remount, serving ~2min. KEDA canNOT stop EC2 and self-shutdown = drift-correction zombie — instead a KEDA-inspired idle-watcher CronJob queries Mimir for litellm aws-model request rate, idle>30m → kubectl patch running:false. Wake: manual flag or demand-watcher; litellm falls back local while down. Needs: function-go-templating package (add to aws-providers).

Self-destruct MUST live at the GIT layer: AMI self-termination = crossplane resurrects (zombie 1), in-cluster XR delete = flux reapplies (zombie 2), live running:false patch = flux reverts (zombie 3). v2 baked-in TTL = reaper CronJob that COMMITS the file-comment via scoped deploy key past ttlHours annotation. comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
IAM PROVISIONING REQUIREMENTS (operator checklist):

1) IAM user (programmatic access key only, no console) — e.g. `crossplane-talos-homelab`.

2) Attach this policy (scoped to the cluster naming convention catalyst-tbdc-*; the upjet provider OBSERVES every bucket sub-resource — acl/cors/website/logging/object-lock/replication — so s3:* on the managed ARNs beats enumerating ~30 actions):

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    { "Sid": "ManagedBuckets",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": "s3:*",
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::catalyst-tbdc-*", "arn:aws:s3:::catalyst-tbdc-*/*"] },
    { "Sid": "Discovery",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:ListAllMyBuckets", "s3:GetBucketLocation"],
      "Resource": "*" },
    { "Sid": "UsageMetricsForYACE",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["cloudwatch:GetMetricData", "cloudwatch:ListMetrics", "tag:GetResources"],
      "Resource": "*" }
  ]
}

3) 1Password item `aws-crossplane`, fields `access_key_id` + `secret_access_key` (exact names — the ExternalSecret templates them into AWS credentials-file format).

4) Nothing else: ESO syncs within 1h (or `kubectl annotate externalsecret aws-credentials -n crossplane-system force-sync=$(date +%s)`), ProviderConfig goes live, XBucket catalyst-tbdc-offsite-backups reconciles. The ExternalSecretNotReady alert stops firing = done signal.

NOTES: bucket-name convention catalyst-tbdc-* is load-bearing in the policy — new XBuckets must follow it (or widen the policy). Object-level perms are included because Velero BSL (TALOS-v6q2) + CNPG barman (TALOS-lajq) will initially reuse this key; per-bucket scoped IAM users are the v1alpha2 refinement (TALOS-l8ot). CloudWatch statement pre-provisions TALOS-gcf0 (YACE) so the key never needs a second touch.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
FARGATE ADDENDUM — widen the IAM policy with these statements (XFargateApp chain):
{ "Sid": "Fargate", "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["ecs:*", "logs:*", "ec2:*SecurityGroup*", "ec2:Describe*", "ec2:CreateTags", "ec2:DeleteTags"],
  "Resource": "*" },
{ "Sid": "ExecRoles", "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["iam:CreateRole","iam:DeleteRole","iam:GetRole","iam:TagRole","iam:ListRolePolicies","iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies","iam:AttachRolePolicy","iam:DetachRolePolicy","iam:PassRole"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:iam::*:role/*-exec" }
CONSOLE WALK for infrastructure/base/aws/apps/hello-whoami.yaml (idiot-proof): AWS console → VPC → Your VPCs → copy the DEFAULT VPC id → replace vpc-REPLACE-ME. Then VPC → Subnets → filter by that VPC → copy any TWO subnet ids → replace both subnet-REPLACE-ME lines. Commit. Result: traefik/whoami on a public Fargate IP (~$9/mo; delete the file to deprovision). NOTE: composition is schema-unvalidated until creds land (same as XBucket was) — verification ticketed.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-20 — the policy recorded on this bead is S3-ONLY, so satisfying it as written still cannot provision a GPU box. Re-scoped for the ephemeral-GPU epic (TALOS-tzr5 / TALOS-t3ic).

The IAM user needs, IN ADDITION to the existing S3 + CloudWatch-read grants:
  * ec2:* scoped to the target region — RunInstances/TerminateInstances/DescribeInstances,
    CreateVolume/DeleteVolume/AttachVolume/DetachVolume/DescribeVolumes,
    CreateSecurityGroup/AuthorizeSecurityGroupEgress/DescribeSecurityGroups,
    CreateTags, DescribeImages, and ssm:GetParameter for the DLAMI alias lookup
    (the AMI is resolved via resolve:ssm:/aws/service/deeplearning/...).
  * iam:CreateRole / DeleteRole / AttachRolePolicy / CreateInstanceProfile /
    AddRoleToInstanceProfile / PassRole — required by EPIC B's instance profile, without
    which the box's 's5cmd sync s3://' has no credentials and seeding fails on a running
    instance.
  * Spot: RequestSpotInstances / DescribeSpotInstanceRequests (the composition hardcodes
    instanceMarketOptions marketType: spot).

ORDERING WARNING: do NOT re-add the ec2/iam Crossplane providers before TALOS-t88y
(crossplane-core memory) is done. The 2026-08-15 incident that removed those providers was
CRD-load driven — ec2 alone registers ~250 CRDs and OOMKilled crossplane-core while
saturating the apiserver. Creds alone are safe; creds + providers on an under-resourced
crossplane is what wedged the cluster.

Cheapest first validation once creds land: XBucket models-library to READY=True (S3 only,
pennies) BEFORE attempting any EC2.

   immediately before configuring the forward.

title: dbgate: event-driven CNPG auto-connect via Kyverno mutate + Flux spec.ignore
description:
Replace the manual per-cluster dbgate env with a Kyverno mutateExisting policy so EVERY CNPG cluster appears in dbgate with zero changes. Chosen over a reconcile CronJob (Option A).

DESIGN:
- Flux Kustomization for dbgate: add spec.ignore for path /spec/template/spec/containers/0/env (target Deployment/dbgate) so Flux won't revert Kyverno's injected env. REQUIRES Flux 2.9 (blocked on the Flux upgrade ticket).
- dbgate deployment: keep only base env (WEB_ROOT, LOGINS); remove the static CONNECTION_* block (currently ships static crowdsec/forgejo/boomtime/homeassistant). Do NOT declare CONNECTIONS in git (Kyverno owns it — avoids the shared-key SSA fight).
- Kyverno ClusterPolicy (mutateExisting), trigger = mirrored <cluster>-app secret in databases ns (CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE), target = Deployment/dbgate:
  * patchStrategicMerge the env (merge-keyed by name → idempotent): ENGINE_/SERVER_/PORT_/USER_(secretKeyRef)/PASSWORD_(secretKeyRef)/DATABASE_/LABEL_ per cluster. No credential decoding (secretKeyRef).
  * recompute CONNECTIONS via apiCall context listing all -app secrets, set the full CSV (idempotent replace; handles add + makes deleted clusters inert).
- ACCEPTED TRADEOFFS: delete leaves inert leftover *_<id> env keys (harmless; recomputed CONNECTIONS excludes them). 
- homeassistant edge case: user-provided secret (only username/password, no cnpg.io/cluster label) — already annotated directly for reflector; handle its DATABASE default in the policy or keep a static entry.
- Verify ALL CNPGs visible in dbgate, then update docs/patterns/cross-namespace-secret-reflection.md with the FINAL event-driven implementation (user asked). 
- NOTE: a CronJob prototype was built + then reverted (superseded by this).

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
Implemented + verified (commit f5b44fc, pushed to origin/main).

CHANGES:
- infrastructure/base/kyverno-policies/dbgate-cnpg-connections.yaml — new mutateExisting ClusterPolicy. Trigger = source <cluster>-app secret (label cnpg.io/cluster), target = Deployment/dbgate container 0. patchStrategicMerge injects ENGINE_/SERVER_/PORT_/USER_/PASSWORD_/DATABASE_/LABEL_<id> (env merge-keyed by name → idempotent); secretKeyRefs point at the reflector MIRROR of the same name in databases. id=cluster with '-'→'_', cluster=name minus '-app', SERVER FQDN uses source ns. CONNECTIONS csv recomputed cluster-wide via apiCall (/api/v1/secrets?labelSelector=cnpg.io%2Fcluster) + nested regex_replace_all. mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate:true. + 2 aggregated ClusterRoles (background: deployments write & secrets read; reports: secrets read).
- clusters/catalyst-cluster/databases.yaml — spec.ignore on /spec/template/spec/containers/0/env (Flux 2.9.4 confirmed).
- infrastructure/base/databases/dbgate/deployment.yaml — dropped static CONNECTIONS + all per-cluster env; base env only (WEB_ROOT, LOGINS). CONNECTIONS not in git (Kyverno owns it).
- applications/home-automation/base/homeassistant/postgres.yaml — added cnpg.io/cluster label + dbname key so the user-provided secret flows through both policies uniformly (removed the static special-case).
- docs/patterns/cross-namespace-secret-reflection.md — rewrote consume section for the event-driven design (trigger-source/secretKeyRef-mirror rationale, CONNECTIONS recompute, Flux 2.9 spec.ignore, SSA no-shared-key reasoning, delete-drift note).

VERIFIED:
- ClusterPolicy Ready (Succeeded), mutate rulecount 1.
- dbgate env post-mutation contains ALL 5 CNPG clusters: crowdsec_postgres, forgejo_postgres, boomtime_postgres, plausible_db (crossplane-demo ns), homeassistant_postgres. CONNECTIONS csv complete.
- dbgate pod 1/1, 0 restarts → every injected secretKeyRef resolves.
- All 5 <cluster>-rw services exist matching the injected SERVER FQDNs.
- Forced 'flux reconcile kustomization databases' → injected env SURVIVES (spec.ignore works, no revert).
- Both aggregated ClusterRoles present + Flux-adopted.

ACCEPTED TRADEOFF (as-designed): the pre-migration static short-id env keys (*_crowdsec/_forgejo/_boomtime/_homeassistant) remain on the live Deployment because spec.ignore makes Flux leave the whole env path untouched (it never pruned them). They are INERT — not listed in CONNECTIONS so dbgate ignores them; they reference valid mirrored secrets so the pod stays healthy. A one-time 'kubectl patch' to strip them was blocked by the harness classifier (non-GitOps manual mutation); left as-is per the ticket's documented 'inert leftover keys' tradeoff. They self-clear if the Deployment is ever recreated from git.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text: RESOLVED via single-writer (not Kyverno mutate). The Kyverno mutateExisting-into-the-dbgate-Deployment design FAILED in practice: N per-secret triggers concurrently patch one shared Deployment → optimistic-concurrency conflicts, Kyverno doesn't retry → random subset of connections landed (e.g. forgejo/crowdsec ENGINE missing → dbgate 'could not get driver'). Also didn't survive Deployment recreation, and its injected env (background-controller field manager) wasn't pruned by Flux when the policy was removed (stale container.env CONNECTIONS overrode envFrom). Replaced with infrastructure/base/databases/dbgate-connection-sync: a single-writer CronJob (15m catch-up) + a dbgate initContainer ('a deploy = a run') sharing one script (ConfigMap) that rebuilds the COMPLETE dbgate-cnpg-connections Secret; dbgate envFroms it. Removed the mutate policy + RBAC + Flux spec.ignore. VERIFIED: all 5 CNPG clusters (boomtime/plausible/crowdsec/forgejo/homeassistant) present, no errors, deployment template clean (base env only). Kept reflector + reflect-cnpg-app-secrets. See bd memory kyverno-mutate-shared-target-and-flux-leftovers.

title: Investigate keepalived/VRRP for Pi-hole VIP (preferred-primary + auto-failback)
description: Pi-hole HA is currently 5 active-active pods (one per node, config synced by nebula-sync) behind a Cilium LB-IPAM L2-announced VIP 192.168.1.240 (CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy lan-pihole-l2, ETP=Local). Cilium L2 announcement is lease-based leader election with NO node preference and NO failback — the VIP sticks to whichever node last won the lease (currently talos06), so it 'rotates' after node reboots rather than preferring pihole-0. Functionally harmless (all Pi-holes are equal + synced), but the user would like a preferred-primary (pin to pihole-0) with automatic failback when it recovers. Cilium L2 can't do this. INVESTIGATE what a keepalived/VRRP-based VIP would look like: VRRP priorities (pihole-0 highest) + preemption for auto-failback, how it coexists with/replaces the Cilium LB-IPAM VIP on Talos (host networking constraints, no keepalived on the host — would run as a DaemonSet/pod with NET_ADMIN + VRRP multicast on the LAN), interaction with ETP=Local + nebula-sync, and whether the added complexity is worth it vs the harmless rotation. title: Uptime/SLO: 8 in-cluster blackbox probes reporting DOWN (likely probe config)
description:
The new Uptime/SLO dashboard (uid uptime-slo) shows 8 probe targets DOWN: graylog, alertmanager, grafana-svc, prometheus-svc, opensearch, traefik, mimir (404). Likely blackbox-exporter PROBE CONFIG issue (wrong path/module/5s-timeout), not the services actually being down — e.g. mimir returns 404 on the probed path. Investigate the 6 blackbox ServiceMonitor targets + the blackbox modules; fix the probe paths/modules/timeouts so healthy services read UP. probe_success is the metric. Surfaced by Playwright visual audit 2026-08-08.

--- ROOT CAUSE (2026-08-08) ---
Confirmed via Mimir (probe_success/probe_http_status_code/probe_duration_seconds by instance) + manual curl repro. NOT a services-down issue — the probe TARGETS are stale from the pre-v2-otel/Mimir migration. Blackbox targets live in TWO places, both wrong:
(A) HelmRelease ServiceMonitor targets — infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/blackbox-exporter/helmrelease.yaml (job=prometheus-blackbox-exporter, full-URL instance labels).
(B) Alloy static blackbox_probes — infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/alloy/helmrelease.yaml (job=blackbox-probes, friendly instance labels).

Per-target failure (grounded):
1. grafana-svc (A) http://kube-prometheus-stack-grafana.monitoring.svc:80 → status 0, fast-fail. Service does not exist; grafana-operator serves it as grafana-service:3000 (the Alloy `grafana` probe uses that and is UP).
2. prometheus-svc (A) http://kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus.monitoring.svc:9090 → status 0. No Prometheus server exists in v2-otel; Mimir replaced it (already probed by Alloy mimir target).
3. alertmanager (A) http://kube-prometheus-stack-alertmanager.monitoring.svc:9093 → status 0. Service gone; Alertmanager is now mimir-alertmanager:8080 (curl / → 200).
4. traefik-dashboard (A) http://traefik.traefik.svc:9000/dashboard/ → status 0, duration EXACTLY 5.0s = module timeout. The `traefik` service does NOT expose 9000; dashboard/api/ping are on traefik-internal:9000 (curl traefik-internal:9000/ping → 200; traefik:9000 → hang/000).
5. graylog (A) http://graylog.observability.svc:9000 → status 0, fast. observability namespace is EMPTY — Graylog not deployed.
6. opensearch (A) http://opensearch-cluster-master.observability.svc:9200 → status 0, fast. No OpenSearch cluster deployed; only opensearch-operator is installed.
7. mimir (B) http://mimir-nginx.monitoring:80/ready → HTTP 404, fast. mimir-nginx gateway serves 200 on / but 404 on /ready (only individual components expose /ready). Verified curl / → 200, /ready → 404.
8. traefik (B) http://traefik.traefik:9000/dashboard/ → status 0, duration 5.0s = timeout. Same root cause as #4 (wrong service; should be traefik-internal:9000).

--- FIX (2026-08-08) — authored, NOT applied (main session deploys) ---
File A: infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/blackbox-exporter/helmrelease.yaml (serviceMonitor.targets):
  - grafana → http://grafana-service.monitoring.svc:3000/api/health (http_2xx)
  - alertmanager → http://mimir-alertmanager.monitoring.svc:8080/ (http_2xx)
  - traefik-dashboard → http://traefik-internal.traefik.svc:9000/ping (http_2xx)
  - prometheus → DISABLED (commented): no Prometheus server in v2-otel; Mimir already covered by Alloy mimir probe.
  - graylog → DISABLED (commented): not deployed (observability ns empty).
  - opensearch → DISABLED (commented): no cluster yet; when deployed it is HTTPS+auth, so use tcp_connect on :9200 (stub left commented).
File B: infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/alloy/helmrelease.yaml (discovery.relabel blackbox_probes):
  - mimir __param_target /ready → / (mimir-nginx gateway 200 on /).
  - traefik __param_target http://traefik.traefik:9000/dashboard/ → http://traefik-internal.traefik:9000/ping.

VERIFY (post-deploy, main): after Flux reconciles blackbox HelmRelease + Alloy config, query Mimir `probe_success` by instance — grafana/alertmanager/traefik(-dashboard)/mimir should read 1. graylog/opensearch/prometheus series drop out (targets removed) rather than staying DOWN. Dashboard uptime-slo is templated on label_values(probe_success,instance) so it auto-adjusts.
close_reason: DONE + verified (2026-08-08): blackbox probe targets were stale pre-Mimir-migration cruft (kube-prometheus-stack-* svcs + empty observability ns). Repointed grafana->grafana-service:3000/api/health, alertmanager->mimir-alertmanager:8080, traefik->traefik-internal:9000/ping, mimir /ready->/ (nginx 404s /ready); removed prometheus/graylog/opensearch (gone). Critic curl-verified all 200. Deployed + verified: probe_success==0 count now EMPTY (0 down, was 8).

title: LB-IPAM: 2 LoadBalancer Services unsatisfied (no external IP)
description:
cilium_operator_lbipam_services_unsatisfied_total = 2 — two type=LoadBalancer Services can't get an external IP despite the lan-pihole-pool having 10 IPs / 1 used (not exhausted). Likely a pool-selector/annotation mismatch or the services request a specific IP/class the pool doesn't serve. Identify the 2 Services (kubectl get svc -A -o wide | grep pending EXTERNAL-IP), root-cause why LB-IPAM won't satisfy them, fix (assign to a pool / fix selector/annotation). Surfaced by network-ops LB-IPAM overlay + Playwright audit 2026-08-08.

--- ROOT CAUSE + FIX (2026-08-08) ---
The 2 services: minio/minio (port 80) and minio/minio-console (port 9090), both type=LoadBalancer, EXTERNAL-IP <pending> 91d. Owned by MinIO Tenant `minio` (operator v6.0.4).

Root cause (grounded): each service's status condition cilium.io/IPAMRequestSatisfied = 'There are no enabled CiliumLoadBalancerIPPools that match this service'. The ONLY pool, lan-pihole-pool (infrastructure/base/cilium/lb-ipam.yaml), has serviceSelector matchLabels app=pihole and is INTENTIONALLY scoped to Pi-hole only (documented in-file). The minio services carry labels v1.min.io/tenant=minio and v1.min.io/console=minio-console, so they never match any pool → unsatisfied. Pool is NOT exhausted (10/11 free); it's a selector non-match. The LB type itself comes from the Tenant's exposeServices:{minio:true,console:true}, which makes the operator create both services as type=LoadBalancer.

Decision: these are leftovers that should NOT be LoadBalancer. MinIO is reached via Traefik IngressRoutes (s3.talos00 -> svc minio:80, minio.talos00 -> svc minio-console:9090) and internally by Mimir/Loki/Tempo over the ClusterIP — no external LB IP is wanted (the lb-ipam.yaml comment explicitly wants minio to stay cluster-internal).

Fix (authored, NOT applied): infrastructure/base/minio/tenant.yaml — set exposeServices.minio=false and exposeServices.console=false (was true/true) with an explanatory comment. The operator reconciles both services from LoadBalancer back to ClusterIP; they still exist for ingress + internal consumers, but no longer request an LB IP. Pool left as-is (its Pi-hole-only scoping is intentional).

Verify on main after Flux applies: kubectl get svc -n minio minio minio-console -o wide shows TYPE=ClusterIP (no <pending>); cilium_operator_lbipam_services_unsatisfied_total -> 0. Confirm IngressRoutes s3.talos00 / minio.talos00 still resolve and Mimir/Loki/Tempo still reach minio.minio.svc.
close_reason: DONE + verified (2026-08-08): minio + minio-console were type=LoadBalancer (Tenant exposeServices) but no CiliumLBIPPool matched (lan-pihole-pool is app:pihole-scoped) -> 2 unsatisfied 91d. Flipped exposeServices false -> operator demoted both to ClusterIP in-place (S3 consumers use headless minio-hl, IngressRoutes use DNS name -> no disruption, critic-confirmed). Verified: both svc now ClusterIP, cilium_operator_lbipam_services_unsatisfied_total=0.

title: Storage: nfs_backend exporter emits -2GiB / 100% sentinel for NAS
description:
central-cluster-storage Summary row NAS tiles read NAS Free/size/used = -2 GiB and NAS %used = 100% — the nfs_backend exporter is emitting a negative sentinel. Pre-existing (outside the new kubelet_volume_stats NFS rows). Investigate the nfs_backend exporter (what scrapes the NAS df, why negative — likely df parse overflow/sentinel or the NAS reporting oddly) + the panel query; fix the exporter or guard the panel. Surfaced by Playwright visual audit 2026-08-08.

--- ROOT CAUSE (2026-08-08) ---
NOT a scrape-error sentinel. nfs_backend_scrape_success=1; df of the probe mount succeeds. The -2 GiB is a 32-bit signed integer overflow in the exporter, not a deliberate sentinel.

Exporter: infrastructure/base/monitoring/nfs-storage-exporter/probe.sh (Deployment `nfs-storage-exporter` in ns monitoring, image alpine:3.20 → busybox awk). It runs `df -Pk /nas` on an NFS probe PVC and awk-formats size/used/avail byte gauges.

The bug: awk printed the byte gauges with `printf "...%d\n"`. busybox awk converts %d through a 32-bit C int, so any value > 2 GiB saturates to INT32_MIN = -2147483648 = exactly -2 GiB. The NAS is ~71 TiB (df 1024-blocks = 74,951,876,992), so size/used/avail ALL overflowed to -2147483648. Confirmed live in-pod AND in Mimir: nfs_backend_size_bytes = nfs_backend_used_bytes = nfs_backend_avail_bytes = -2147483648. Dashboard %used = 100*max(used)/max(size) = 100*(-2^31)/(-2^31) = 100%. That reproduces every symptom.
Reproduced in the pod's own busybox awk: `printf "%d", 74951876992*1024` -> -2147483648; `printf "%.0f"` -> 76750722039808 (correct).

--- FIX (2026-08-08) ---
Root-caused in OUR exporter (not third-party) so fixed at source; dashboard untouched. Changed the three byte-gauge printfs in probe.sh from `%d` to `%.0f` (formats the double as a full-precision integer with no 32-bit cast; exact well past petabytes) + added a comment explaining the busybox-awk %d trap.
File edited: infrastructure/base/monitoring/nfs-storage-exporter/probe.sh (only the size/used/avail printf lines + comment).

Verify on main: apply the ConfigMap change + restart the deployment (`kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deploy/nfs-storage-exporter`), then re-query Mimir — nfs_backend_size_bytes ~= 76,750,722,039,808 (69.8 TiB), used ~48.5 TB, avail ~28.3 TB, %used ~63% (matches df's 63% capacity), all positive. Verified the fixed awk block against live df in-pod pre-rollout: size 76750722039808 / used 48468318879744 / avail 28282403160064 / pct 63.15. NOT committed/applied.
close_reason: DONE + verified (2026-08-08): busybox awk printf %d cast NAS byte gauges (~71TiB) through int32 -> saturated to INT32_MIN (-2GiB), rendering 100% used. Fixed %d->%.0f in nfs-storage-exporter/probe.sh. Deployed + verified: nfs_backend_size_bytes=76.75TB (69.8TiB), matches df 63%.

title: Upgrade Cilium 1.16.6 -> 1.18.x (EOL + off k8s 1.34 support matrix)
description:
Cilium 1.16.6 is EOL and NOT in the Kubernetes v1.34 compatibility matrix (we're now on k8s 1.34.10). TALOS-firz research recommends 1.18.x for KPR/endpoint-restore fixes that also narrow the pod-startup apiserver-ClusterIP race. CRITICAL: explicitly AVOID Cilium 1.19.3/1.19.4 on Talos — confirmed regression where KPR kills Talos host networking during BPF/veth init on Talos 1.13.2 (cilium/cilium#46010); 1.18.9 confirmed working there. Deploy target: latest 1.18.x. Config: infrastructure/base/cilium/helmrelease.yaml (currently chart 1.16.6). Plan carefully — CNI upgrade on a live single-CP cluster; stage + verify agent health + no meltdown (watch CiliumIdentity count per TALOS-yyt). See TALOS-firz research section for full context.

====================================================================
UPGRADE DOSSIER (2026-08-08)  — operator-ready, grounded in OUR config
====================================================================

SAFE TARGET: Cilium v1.18.12 (latest 1.18.x patch; tag confirmed present on
quay.io/cilium/cilium). STEPWISE REQUIRED: 1.16.6 -> latest 1.16.x -> 1.17.x
-> 1.18.12. Cilium only tests/supports consecutive-minor upgrades; do NOT jump
1.16->1.18 directly. (https://docs.cilium.io/en/v1.18/operations/upgrade/)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 — OUR CILIUM INVENTORY (from values.yaml + live cilium-config)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Running: v1.16.6 (client+daemon), image 9e9f0989. 5 nodes, Talos v1.13.2,
k8s v1.34.10, kernel 6.18.29-talos. Live counts: 218 CiliumIdentities /
240 CiliumEndpoints (HEALTHY ratio post-TALOS-yyt fix; watch this number).

Enabled features / non-default values (file: infrastructure/base/cilium/):
- kubeProxyReplacement: true (boolean form; live kube-proxy-replacement=true)
- k8sServiceHost=localhost k8sServicePort=7445  (KubePrism — decouples agent
  bootstrap from eBPF datapath; load-bearing for meltdown avoidance)
- routingMode=tunnel, tunnel-protocol=vxlan (live). MTU=1250 (Nebula overlay)
- ipam=kubernetes
- bpf.masquerade=true (enable-bpf-masquerade=true), enable-ipv4-masquerade=true
  bpf.policyMapMax=65536, bpf.lbMapMax=65536 (raised from defaults)
- ipv4NativeRoutingCIDR=10.100.0.0/16 (Nebula native-route carveout)
- l2announcements.enabled=true (+ enable-l2-neigh-discovery=true live),
  k8sClientRateLimit qps10/burst20
- LB-IPAM: CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool 'lan-pihole-pool' (192.168.1.240-250) +
  CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy 'lan-pihole-l2' (ARP, no BGP)  [lb-ipam.yaml, v2alpha1]
- Hubble: relay+ui enabled, metrics (dns/drop/tcp/flow/port-dist/icmp/policy/httpV2)
  port 9965, eventBufferCapacity 16383 (live cm still shows 8191 — drift), openmetrics
- Dedicated Envoy: external-envoy-proxy=true LIVE — cilium-envoy DaemonSet
  already running 5/5. L7 proxy enabled (enable-l7-proxy=true).
- Cilium mutual auth / SPIRE: authentication.mutual.spire.enabled=true,
  mesh-auth-mutual-enabled=true, self-installed SPIRE in cilium-spire ns.
  SPIRE server runAsUser 0, 1Gi local-path PVC. spire-agent SA-token TTL
  patched 600->3600s via HR postRenderer (op:test guards volumes[3]).
- ClusterMesh: useAPIServer=true but apiserver SCALED TO 0 (no peer yet;
  TALOS-fed-enable). cluster id=1 name=talos-home.
- prometheus agent 9962 / operator 9963 (PodMonitor, no ServiceMonitor)
- dnsProxy.enableTransparentMode=false (Talos hostDNS)
- cgroup.autoMount=false hostRoot=/sys/fs/cgroup; Talos cap set; cgroupv2
- identity labels DENY filter (anti-bloat, TALOS-yyt): denies controller-uid,
  pod-template-hash, batch.kubernetes.io, job-name, dagster, helm.sh,
  velero pod-volume-backup/repo-name. identity-allocation-mode=crd.
- livenessProbe.failureThreshold=10 (5min), updateStrategy maxUnavailable=1
- egressGateway=false, wireguard/ipsec DISABLED, localRedirect=false,
  bpf-lb-sock=false, CiliumEndpointSlice not enabled, BGP not enabled.
- CRDs installed: LBIPPool/L2Announce/CIDRGroup/PodIPPool = v2alpha1;
  CNP/CCNP/endpoints/identities/nodes = v2. CiliumExternalWorkloads present.
- CNP/CCNP in use: honeypot (3), iocaine (3), grpc-example mTLS (2, uses
  authentication.mode=required -> exercises SPIRE mutual auth). No CIDRGroup
  CRs, no BGP CRs, no EgressGatewayPolicy CRs.
- Flux Kustomization clusters/catalyst-cluster/cilium.yaml: prune=FALSE (never
  auto-prune CNI). HR install/upgrade crds=CreateReplace, force=false.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 2 — UPGRADE PATH RESEARCH (per minor)  [sources inline]
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Official stance (both guides): only consecutive-minor upgrade/rollback tested;
set upgradeCompatibility=<current minor> on each helm upgrade; do NOT use
--reuse-values on a minor bump (drops new values / render errors); upgrade to
the latest patch of the current minor BEFORE crossing a minor boundary.
Source: https://docs.cilium.io/en/v1.17/operations/upgrade/ ,
        https://docs.cilium.io/en/v1.18/operations/upgrade/

1.16 -> 1.17  (intersecting OUR features):
- Consul removed; WireGuard userspace fallback removed; metallb-bgp flags
  removed; pod proxy-visibility annotations removed; pod-managed etcd removed;
  IPsec single-key removed. NONE apply to us (no consul/metallb/ipsec/visibility).
- Helm: tls.secretsBackend deprecated -> tls.readSecretsOnlyFromSecretsNamespace
  + tls.secretSync (we don't set secretsBackend — no action). Hubble direct
  cert/key values deprecated -> existingSecret (we use tls.auto — no action).
- Default: dnsProxy.endpointMaxIpPerHostname 50->1000 (we don't override; benign).
  Hubble cert validity 1095->365d (auto-rotated; benign).
- NEW default: --bpf-lb-proto-diff ON. Services created WITHOUT explicit proto
  must be deleted+recreated to benefit. Applies to our pihole LB + ClusterIPs.
  Low blast (functional either way) but note for smoke test.
- Deprecations flagged for 1.18 removal that WE touch: External Workloads
  feature (we have the CRD + clustermesh useAPIServer), enable-k8s-terminating-
  endpoint (live=true) becomes unconditional, enableRuntimeDeviceDetection
  (live enable-runtime-device-detection=true).
- CRD: no forced v2 migration at 1.17 for our in-use kinds.

1.17 -> 1.18  (intersecting OUR features):
- kernel >= 5.10 required — OK (6.18 talos).
- CRD v2alpha1->v2 migration: CiliumBGP* + CiliumCIDRGroup. We have NO BGP CRs
  and NO CIDRGroup CRs, so nothing to convert; CreateReplace installs new
  served versions. LBIPPool/L2Announce remain v2alpha1 in 1.18 — our lb-ipam.yaml
  stays valid.
- KPR: --enable-node-port/--enable-host-port/--enable-external-ips deprecated;
  those features now gate on kubeProxyReplacement=true. We already run KPR=true
  — no behavior change, but drop any standalone enable-* if present (we don't set).
- IDENTITY (TOP RISK): io.cilium.k8s.policy.serviceaccount is now included by
  default in identity-relevant labels. "Temporary identity count increases
  during upgrade may cause connection drops; exclude this label if needed."
  Directly reawakens the TALOS-yyt identity-churn/meltdown class.
- Helm renames/removes intersecting us: l2PodAnnouncements.interface ->
  interfacePattern (we don't set); ciliumEndpointSlice.sliceMode removed (n/a);
  hubble.relay.dialTimeout removed (n/a); hubble.export moved under
  hubble.export.static/dynamic (n/a). Default l2NeighDiscovery.enabled -> false
  and L2 neigh now uses base_reachable_time_ms sysctl instead of
  arping-refresh-period. WE USE L2 ANNOUNCEMENTS -> must confirm neigh discovery
  stays ON post-upgrade (l2announcements should auto-enable it; verify live
  enable-l2-neigh-discovery=true after).
- Removals: External Workloads feature removed — delete CRD
  ciliumexternalworkloads.cilium.io; NOTE our clustermesh.useAPIServer=true is
  ClusterMesh (still supported) not external-workloads, but the apiserver is
  scaled to 0 so this is low-risk. enable-k8s-terminating-endpoint flag removed
  (now unconditional). enableRuntimeDeviceDetection option removed (behavior
  kept). CONNTRACK_LOCAL removed.
- Agent flag renames (informational; chart-managed): kvstore-* ->
  identity-allocation-*; --datapath-mode=lb-only -> --bpf-lb-only;
  --enable-ipv4-egress-gateway -> --enable-egress-gateway.
- Metrics renames (fix our dashboards/alerts): bgp reconcile_error_count ->
  _errors_total; doublewrite_* renamed; node_connectivity_status /
  _latency_seconds REMOVED; cilium_agent_bootstrap_seconds histogram->gauge.
  Check infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/baseline-alerts/cilium-bpf-alerts.yaml.
- Envoy: we already run the dedicated cilium-envoy DaemonSet (external-envoy-
  proxy=true, 5/5) — NO embedded->dedicated migration surprise for us. L7 CNP
  (grpc mTLS) + any future Ingress/GatewayAPI keep working through it.
- Deprecated-for-1.19 we touch: clustermesh.apiserver.kvstoremesh.enabled
  (auto-enables later); policy-default-local-cluster semantics change in 1.19
  (ClusterMesh) — irrelevant while apiserver=0.

TALOS SUPPORT / VERSION SAFETY:
- 1.18.x supported on Talos 1.13.2 + k8s 1.34 (1.34 in 1.18 compat matrix;
  1.16 is NOT — the reason for this ticket).
- cilium/cilium#46010 CONFIRMED + now CLOSED: KPR kills Talos host networking
  during veth/BPF init, affects ">=1.19.3 and <1.20"; 1.18.9 confirmed WORKING
  on the SAME Talos 1.13.2 / kernel 6.18.29 / KPR=true profile as ours. Fix
  landed for 1.19.5 (PR #45572). The ENTIRE 1.18.x line (incl. 1.18.12) is
  BELOW the affected range -> SAFE. Do NOT go to 1.19.x yet.
  Source: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/46010

--------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 3 — WHAT BREAKS FOR US (ranked; feature -> change -> blast -> mitigation)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
R1 (HIGH) IDENTITY CHURN via new default serviceaccount label (1.18).
  Change: io.cilium.k8s.policy.serviceaccount joins identity-relevant labels ->
  identity recompute for most endpoints during upgrade. Blast: transient
  connection drops + CiliumIdentity count spike = the exact TALOS-yyt meltdown
  class (LIST storms -> etcd/apiserver pressure -> agent restart loop).
  MITIGATION (VALUES EDIT BEFORE 1.18): append '!io.cilium.k8s.policy.serviceaccount'
  to the existing `labels:` deny filter in values.yaml to keep identity space
  stable (unless mTLS policies need SA identity — grpc mTLS uses SPIRE mutual
  auth, not SA-label identity, so denying is safe). Watch `kubectl get
  ciliumidentities | wc -l` throughout; abort if it climbs past ~a few hundred.

R2 (MED) L2 announcements neigh-discovery default flip (1.18: l2NeighDiscovery
  default->false; arping-refresh-period -> base_reachable_time_ms).
  Blast: pihole VIP (192.168.1.240) ARP stops -> LAN DNS outage if neigh
  discovery ends up off. MITIGATION: confirm live enable-l2-neigh-discovery=true
  after upgrade; if not, set l2NeighDiscovery.enabled=true explicitly. Smoke
  test: arping the pihole VIP from a LAN host post-upgrade.

R3 (MED) SPIRE / mutual-auth postRenderer fragility across chart bumps.
  Our HR patches spire-agent volumes[3] SA-token TTL with an op:test guard on
  the volume ordering. A 1.17/1.18 chart may reorder the SPIRE DaemonSet
  volumes -> op:test fails LOUD -> helm-controller aborts render (per
  helm-postrenderer memory). MITIGATION: before each minor, `helm template` the
  new chart and re-verify volumes[3] is still the spire-server audience token;
  adjust index if moved. Also re-confirm cilium-spire ns PSA labels patch still
  targets a rendered namespace.

R4 (MED) Prometheus metric renames/removals (1.18) break Cilium alerts/dashboards.
  node_connectivity_status/_latency REMOVED; bootstrap_seconds histogram->gauge;
  bgp + doublewrite renamed. MITIGATION: update
  infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/baseline-alerts/cilium-bpf-alerts.yaml
  and any Grafana panels; non-blocking for datapath.

R5 (LOW) bpf-lb-proto-diff default-on (1.17): existing Services without explicit
  protocol don't get proto differentiation until recreated. Blast: cosmetic /
  none for our pihole LB + ClusterIPs. MITIGATION: optional delete+recreate;
  smoke-test service reachability.

R6 (LOW) External Workloads CRD removal (1.18) + kvstoremesh/terminating-endpoint
  flag churn. We use ClusterMesh apiserver (scaled 0), not external workloads.
  MITIGATION: after 1.18, `kubectl delete crd ciliumexternalworkloads.cilium.io`
  if orphaned; no runtime impact.

Config edits REQUIRED BEFORE upgrading: R1 (labels deny serviceaccount) is the
only pre-flight VALUES edit. R2/R3 are verify-and-maybe-edit gates per step.
Nothing forces mass pod restart EXCEPT identity recompute (R1) — the churn lever
to watch.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 4 — SAFE ROLLOUT PLAN
--------------------------------------------------------------------
PRE-FLIGHT (once):
- Snapshot: `kubectl get ciliumidentities | wc -l` (~218) + endpoints (~240);
  cilium status; `cilium-dbg identity list` baseline.
- Run cilium preflight DaemonSet (image pre-pull + CNP validator) per upgrade guide.
- Confirm KubePrism healthy on all nodes (127.0.0.1:7445 LISTEN, KubePrismStatus).
- Confirm Flux Kustomization prune=false (it is) so a bad render can't delete CNI.
- Ensure scripts/cleanup-cilium-identities.sh is ready as a safety valve.
- Stage R1 values edit (deny serviceaccount label) in a branch, NOT applied yet.

STEPWISE (one minor at a time; each = helm/Flux chart bump + upgradeCompatibility):
1. 1.16.6 -> latest 1.16.x patch. Verify agents green, identity count flat.
2. -> latest 1.17.x (v1.17.18). Set upgradeCompatibility=1.16. Verify.
   Watch bpf-lb-proto-diff; smoke-test pihole LB + a ClusterIP.
3. Land R1 values edit (deny serviceaccount) + re-verify SPIRE volumes[3] index.
   -> 1.18.12. Set upgradeCompatibility=1.17. Verify enable-l2-neigh-discovery
   stays true; arping pihole VIP; check identity count did NOT spike.
   Update Cilium metrics in baseline-alerts. Delete stale ExternalWorkloads CRD.
Because it's Flux-managed: bump chart version in helmrelease.yaml + set
upgradeCompatibility in values per step; DO NOT set --reuse-values (Flux uses
valuesFrom, fine). maxUnavailable=1 already limits agent-rotation blast.

POST-UPGRADE VERIFY (each step):
- All cilium + cilium-envoy + operator pods Ready; no restart storm.
- `cilium status --brief`; connectivity: pod->pod, pod->svc(ClusterIP),
  LAN->pihole VIP (ARP), DNS resolution through Talos hostDNS.
- CiliumIdentity count within ~2x baseline (abort/rollback if climbing).
- Hubble relay/ui up, flows visible; grpc mTLS (SPIRE mutual auth) still passing.
- SPIRE agent no CrashLoop (token TTL patch intact).

ROLLBACK:
- Cilium supports rollback only one minor at a time; keep upgradeCompatibility.
- Flux prune=false means reverting helmrelease.yaml chart version + re-reconcile
  restores prior minor without resource deletion. Rollback the SAME step you
  just took; never skip a minor on the way down either.
- If identity storm starts: run cleanup-cilium-identities.sh + revert R1 posture.

STOP LINE: Do NOT advance to 1.19.x until #46010 fix (1.19.5+) is validated on a
throwaway Talos node — 1.19.3/1.19.4 brick host networking on our exact profile.

title: Cilium pod-startup apiserver-ClusterIP EPERM race (KSM canary)
description:
At pod startup, pods connecting to apiserver ClusterIP 10.96.0.1:443 before Cilium programs their endpoint get EPERM 'operation not permitted' (datapath drop). KSM surfaced this (1198 restarts) because it has no client-creation retry; loosened its probes as mitigation (commit 54cc474). Deeper fix: investigate Cilium endpoint-programming latency / kube-proxy-replacement service-backend readiness on workers (esp talos06), consider adding monitoring/KSM to the wedge-buster backstop (infrastructure/base/kube-system/wedge-buster/). Affects any pod that talks to the apiserver early in startup.

=====================================================================
RESEARCH (2026-08-08)
=====================================================================
Deployed: Cilium **1.16.6** (infrastructure/base/cilium/helmrelease.yaml pins chart 1.16.6), kubeProxyReplacement=true, socket-LB default-on, bpf.masquerade=true, k8sServiceHost=localhost:7445 (KubePrism). Talos 1.13.x / K8s v1.34.

ROOT MECHANISM (confirmed upstream, not a guess):
- The EPERM comes from Cilium's **socket-LB cgroup connect4 hook REJECTING the connect() syscall when the service->backend lookup finds no backend** for the ClusterIP at that instant. It is NOT a policy drop at the veth. Upstream considered this errno a bug and changed it EPERM -> EHOSTUNREACH in PR cilium/cilium#45185, shipped v1.19.4 / v1.20.0-pre.2 — precisely because apps treat EPERM as fatal (as KSM does). https://github.com/cilium/cilium/releases/tag/v1.19.4
- Windows where the LB-map entry for 10.96.0.1 is empty: sock-LB cgroup program re-attach + service resync during cilium-agent restart (matches "worsens during agent restarts"); single control-plane = exactly 1 backend, so any apiserver endpoint flap empties the service.
- Secondary contributor: new endpoints carry **reserved:init identity** until identity/labels resolve; if any policy selects the namespace, traffic is dropped until first regeneration completes. https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/security/policy/lifecycle/ — identity/CEP churn (our TALOS-yyt bloat history) stretches this window. Related upstream: empty-policy-map-after-regeneration-retry race https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/38998 ; agent<->apiserver restart cascade https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/34653

RANKED REMEDIATIONS (impact x safety, single-CP Talos+KPR homelab):
1. **[LOW RISK — do first] Workload-side wait/retry for early-API pods** (KSM + anything hitting apiserver at t=0):
   - initContainer gate: `until wget -q --spider --no-check-certificate https://10.96.0.1:443/healthz; do sleep 1; done` (EPERM fails instantly, so the loop is cheap) — converts crashloop into a clean wait.
   - startupProbe with generous failureThreshold (partially done for KSM in 54cc474).
   - Add monitoring/KSM to wedge-buster backstop (original ticket idea) as belt-and-braces.
   - KSM upstream has a history of hard-fail-no-retry on client creation: https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/issues/542 , https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/issues/683
2. **[MEDIUM RISK — needed anyway] Upgrade Cilium 1.16.6 -> latest 1.18.x patch.** 1.16 is EOL and NOT in the K8s v1.34 compatibility matrix (1.34 pairs with 1.18.x+): https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/network/kubernetes/compatibility/ . 1.17/1.18 carry KPR + endpoint-restore + service-sync fixes that narrow the race. **AVOID 1.19.3/1.19.4 on Talos for now**: confirmed regression — KPR kills Talos host networking during endpoint/veth/BPF init on Talos 1.13.2 (1.18.9 confirmed working there): https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/46010 . Note the errno fix (#45185, EPERM->EHOSTUNREACH) only lands in 1.19.4+, so on 1.18.x apps still see EPERM — item 1 stays necessary regardless.
3. **[LOW-MED RISK toggle] Enable CiliumEndpointSlice** (`ciliumEndpointSlice.enabled: true`) to cut CEP/identity apiserver churn that lengthens endpoint programming during agent restarts — directly relevant given the identity-bloat history. Roll during a quiet window (operator + agents restart).
4. **[KEEP AS-IS] `k8sServiceHost: localhost` / `k8sServicePort: 7445` (KubePrism)** is already the correct Talos pattern and breaks the cilium#41108 agent-bootstrap chicken-and-egg — but it protects the AGENT only, not workload pods (pods still resolve KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST to the ClusterIP through sock-LB). Talos guidance: https://docs.siderolabs.com/kubernetes-guides/cni/deploying-cilium
5. **[LOW RISK, conditional] Allow the `init` entity in any CiliumNetworkPolicy-covered namespaces** so pre-identity endpoints aren't policy-dropped during the reserved:init window: https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/security/policy/lifecycle/
6. **[INVESTIGATED — NO-OPs for this bug, don't spend time]:** `cni.exclusive` (only controls wiping other CNI confs; CNI ADD already blocks sandbox creation until endpoint create — the residual window is identity + LB-map programming, which happens after ADD returns); `endpoint-gc-interval` (CEP garbage collection, not programming latency); `bpf.hostLegacyRouting` / `enableEndpointRoutes` (routing-path choice, unrelated to sock-LB reject); `socketLB.hostNamespaceOnly` (would swap fast EPERM for per-packet drops/timeouts — strictly worse); `enable-k8s-terminating-endpoint` (default true since 1.11, already active).
7. **[OBSERVABILITY] Alert on the signal, not the symptom:** Hubble drop metrics are already enabled — add PromQL alerts on `cilium_drop_count_total` (reason=Service/no-backend class) and on KSM container restart rate, so the next widening of this window pages before a 1198-restart pileup.

title: Provision NVMe-backed block storage for stateful workloads (Longhorn?)
description: Final resting place for CNPG/DB volumes: SSD/NVMe-backed BLOCK storage (evaluate Longhorn vs alternatives). Replaces the interim fatboy-nfs-appdata for databases. Goal: low-latency, node-independent, replicated block storage so CNPG clusters get fast local-like performance without node-affinity lock-in. Interim state (now): CNPG moved local-path -> fatboy-nfs-appdata + instances:3. This issue tracks the proper block-storage layer.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
PREREQ if Longhorn is chosen (from TALOS-v3wy investigation, 2026-08-24):

Longhorn on Talos requires TWO system extensions on EVERY node:
  siderolabs/iscsi-tools        (iscsid/iscsiadm for volume attach)
  siderolabs/util-linux-tools   (fstrim, for volume trimming)

Current fleet state: iscsi-tools is on talos01 and talos03 ONLY; util-linux-tools is on
no node at all. So choosing Longhorn means a schematic change on all five nodes, which
is 'talosctl upgrade' + REBOOT each — not a config apply. Budget five rolling reboots
(control plane last) as part of this work, and add both extensions in ONE pass so no
node reboots twice.

Also note: on Talos v1.13.x the Longhorn data dir uses UserVolumeConfig rather than the
older kubelet extraMounts /var/lib/longhorn bind mount — the pre-1.10 docs pattern does
not apply to this cluster.

The existing kubelet extraMounts for /etc/iscsi and /var/lib/iscsi are already present
on all five nodes (configs/patches/all-kubelet-baseline.yaml), so that part is done.

title: Migrate all non-CNPG Postgres to CloudNativePG
description:
Consolidate every in-cluster Postgres onto CloudNativePG (CNPG), the repo standard (forgejo/plausible/boomtime/scratch already CNPG; crowdsec migrated 2026-08-08 under TALOS-pbn).

Goal: no raw postgres Deployments/StatefulSets, no embedded chart subcharts, no in-pod sidecar DBs. Each app gets a CNPG Cluster + repointed connection string; data dumped/restored where it matters.

Source repos live in the workspace (/Users/panda/catalyst-devspace/workspace/): catalyst-data, catalyst-llm, dungeon-library are live-only / ArgoCD-from-elsewhere (NOT in talos-homelab).

Recurring risks:
- pgvector / pgvecto.rs: CNPG operand image must ship the matching extension (immich is version-locked to pgvecto.rs/VectorChord and validates at boot -> hardest).
- 3 source manifests (catalyst-data, catalyst-llm, dungeon-library) live outside talos-homelab.

Suggested order (easy->hard): HA, dagster, dungeon, zipline -> authentik, linkwarden, knowledge, stash-ai -> litellm(9G), immich.

Separately flagged: cloudnative-pg operator pod at ~1268 restarts — investigate (not part of this epic's DB migrations).

title: CrowdSec custom Cowrie parser -> ssh-bf scenario (honeypot auto-ban when public)
description: UNBLOCKED: crowdsecurity/cowrie-logs parser EXISTS in the hub (per security-agent handoff) — earlier assumption of 'no collection' was wrong. TO IMPLEMENT: add crowdsecurity/cowrie-logs to agent.env.COLLECTIONS in crowdsec/helmrelease.yaml (acquisition already wired: namespace honeypot, podName cowrie-*, program cowrie); pair with an ssh-bf-style scenario for bans. Deferred: internal honeypot IPs are RFC1918-whitelisted so no auto-ban fires until the honeypot is publicly exposed. Verify agent installs the parser (bad name fails agent startup).
notes:
## DESIGN 2026-08-24 (user): DELAYED bounce — harvest ~5 min of attacker data, THEN ban

User's words: 'enable the bouncer ... with some sort of latent delay we can bounce them after 5
minutes on the honeypot ideally so we can get some data from these hackers'.

Bumped P4->P2. This is active once the honeypot goes public (TALOS-ezcu).

## ⚠️ THE ARCHITECTURAL FACT THAT MAKES THIS CLEANER THAN IT SOUNDS

The ONLY bouncer that exists is the Traefik plugin (verified: cscli bouncers list shows 5
traefik@... bouncers, type Crowdsec-Bouncer-Traefik-Plugin, nothing else). The Traefik bouncer
blocks HTTP ONLY.

Cowrie is SSH/telnet on hostPort 2222/2223 — it is NOT behind Traefik. So a CrowdSec ban
decision triggered by Cowrie activity does NOT and CANNOT kick the attacker off the honeypot SSH
session. There is no SSH-layer remediation.

THIS IS A FEATURE, NOT A BUG, FOR THIS GOAL. It means:
  - the honeypot NEVER cuts the attacker's SSH session — they can flail in the fake shell as
    long as they like, maximum intel capture
  - the ban decision protects EVERYTHING ELSE — every real Traefik-fronted app is now closed to
    that IP, and the signal is shared to CrowdSec CAPI / community CTI
The honeypot becomes a tripwire that feeds the fleet-wide blocklist, while remaining open itself.

## THE '5-MINUTE DELAY' — two mechanisms, pick one

Approach A (RECOMMENDED — no new component): tune the scenario's leaky bucket so the ban
decision fires only after ~5 min of sustained engagement rather than on first connection. A
CrowdSec scenario is a leaky bucket (capacity + leakspeed); size it so a real attacker session
overflows it around the 5-min mark. Cowrie acquisition is ALREADY wired (helmrelease.yaml:31 —
program: cowrie, parsing cowrie.json from the logship sidecar). What is missing is the
custom parser + scenario, which is the original scope of THIS ticket. No crowdsecurity/cowrie
hub item exists, so the parser is hand-written against cowrie.json events
(cowrie.session.connect / .login.success / .command.input).

  Bucket data collected first, then ban -> the delay is inherent, and the ban duration is
  configurable (e.g. 4h-24h). This gives 'data then bounce-from-real-apps' with zero new moving
  parts.

Approach B (only if the user wants the SSH SESSION itself killed at 5 min): needs an SSH/network
-layer remediation — cs-firewall-bouncer on the node, or a Cilium-based bouncer that drops the
banned IP at L3/L4. Bigger lift on Talos (no easy host firewall access; would likely be a
CiliumNetworkPolicy or a bouncer that writes CiliumCIDRGroups). Do NOT build this unless the
user confirms they want the honeypot session terminated, because it REDUCES intel capture — the
whole point was to keep them engaged.

RECOMMENDATION: Approach A. Keep the honeypot session open indefinitely (max data), let the ban
protect the real estate. Revisit B only if a specific attacker overstaying becomes a problem.

## SEQUENCING

  1. TALOS-ezcu — honeypot goes public (real attacker traffic to tune buckets against)
  2. THIS (0ru) — custom cowrie parser + scenario, bucket tuned to ~5 min, ban -> traefik bouncer
  3. TALOS-t1w — separate: flip AppSec default_remediation allow->ban after observation

⚠️ Internal IPs are currently whitelisted in the bouncer (from TALOS-e9h) — keep that, or a
CrowdSec decision could lock the operator out of real apps. Verify the honeypot's own LAN
probes / pod-CIDR do not trip the scenario and self-ban.

Do NOT implement blind before the honeypot is public — the bucket tuning needs real traffic to
calibrate the 5-min window against, and calibrating against zero traffic is guesswork.

title: CrowdSec network-layer bouncer via Cilium (L3/L4 enforcement) — idea
description: IDEA/future. Today the crowdsec-bouncer-traefik-plugin only blocks HTTP (L7). A network-layer bouncer that pushes CrowdSec decisions into Cilium would drop banned IPs at L3/L4 for ALL protocols (SSH, honeypot, non-HTTP), strictly stronger than the L7 bouncer. Options: cs-cilium/firewall-style bouncer that watches the LAPI decisions stream and programs CiliumNetworkPolicy/CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy (or hostFirewall) to drop the IPs; or a cs-firewall-bouncer on the nodes. Not a data source (Cilium is L3/L4, CrowdSec is L7 logs) — this is an ENFORCEMENT enhancement. Pairs with TALOS-pbn. Evaluate maturity of any existing cilium<->crowdsec integration first.

title: Pi-hole DNS split: ~20% of queries served by ft6np (talos03), not just the mainline (talos06)
description:
The new 'DNS Served per Instance' panel revealed that TWO Pi-hole instances serve DNS concurrently, not single-active: fqzgm@talos06 ~1 q/s (mean 0.99) AND ft6np@talos03 ~0.2 q/s (mean 0.205, ~17-20% of traffic) all day. Others negligible.

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis): the shared VIP 192.168.1.240 (LB-IPAM sharing-key 'pihole') has its two Cilium L2 announcement leases on DIFFERENT nodes — cilium-l2announce-pihole-pihole-dns=talos06, cilium-l2announce-pihole-pihole-web=talos03. So .240 is ARP-announced by both nodes; LAN clients resolve .240 to whichever node's MAC they cached, splitting DNS between talos06 (fqzgm) and talos03 (ft6np).

IMPACT: functionally OK (both instances have identical config/blocklists), but it's not the intended single-active + clean failover; per-client stats are split across two FTL DBs, and it complicates the 'active instance' mental model.

FIX DIRECTIONS: get both pihole-dns + pihole-web L2 announcements onto the SAME node (investigate Cilium L2 behavior with shared IPs across 2 services / sharing-key), or announce the shared VIP from a single L2 lease. Verify with the new dashboard panel (want ONE green line, others flat).
notes:
Fix A applied 2026-08-06 (commit 478a22c): pihole-web -> ClusterIP. Verified: .240 now has a SINGLE l2announce lease (pihole-dns@talos06); web lease gone; DNS resolves via .240; web UI still served via Traefik. DNS split root cause removed. Watch the 'DNS Served per Instance' panel — ft6np should decay to ~0 as client ARP caches expire (few min). Close once the graph shows single-active.

title: vpn-rotator CronJob wedge: apk add hang, no activeDeadlineSeconds
description: Job vpn-rotator-29665655 has been running 54 days at 0/1 with pod pid1 stuck on 'apk add python3' (Alpine repo unreachable during that specific run). concurrencyPolicy: Forbid blocks every subsequent /35min schedule fire; kube-controller-manager fires TooManyMissedTimes warning each schedule window. Add activeDeadlineSeconds so future wedges self-heal; kill the current stuck job to unblock.
close_reason: Root cause: dtzar/helm-kubectl:latest ships without python and the CronJob installed it via 'apk add python3' at every run. A single failed apk fetch on 2026-05-28 wedged the job forever (pid1 sh sleeping on apk, concurrencyPolicy: Forbid blocked all subsequent /35min windows for 54d). Fix: (1) swap image to alpine/k8s:1.34.9 which pre-bakes python3 + kubectl + helm (matches cluster k8s minor); rotate.py only uses stdlib so no pip needed. (2) activeDeadlineSeconds: 1500 on the job spec as belt-and-braces so any future hang self-heals in 25min. Verified end-to-end via 'kubectl create job --from=cronjob/vpn-rotator …' — new job pulled the image, python3 launched immediately, rotate.py entered its normal jitter phase and started emitting JSON logs.
