title: Cowrie: readOnlyRootFilesystem=true + bound the emptyDirs (deferred from pre-exposure hardening)
description:
Two hardening items deliberately NOT done in the pre-exposure pass (e9fa912c),
because destabilising a working honeypot on the day of exposure is a bad trade.
Neither blocks going public.

## 1. readOnlyRootFilesystem: true on the cowrie container

Currently false — the weakest remaining control on the pod. The logship sidecar
already has it true. Cowrie writes SSH host keys and a PID file into its working
tree, so this needs additional emptyDir mounts for var/run and etc/ssh before it
will start. Verify by rollout, not by dry-run: the failure is at runtime.

Value is post-RCE only (everything else — non-root, all caps dropped, seccomp
RuntimeDefault, no SA token, default-deny egress — is already in place), which
is why it was safe to defer.

## 2. emptyDir sizeLimit on cowrie-var-lib / cowrie-var-log

Both are unbounded. Cowrie writes one ttylog per session plus its json/text logs.
MEASURED and this is NOT urgent: talos06 has ~836 GiB allocatable ephemeral
storage and events run ~360 bytes, so even a heavy public honeypot would take
years to fill it. Loki (30d retention, 1 stream, 10 MB/s ingestion cap versus
~18 MB/DAY at 50k events/day) has enormous headroom and is the durable record.

Worth adding anyway as cheap insurance: a sizeLimit converts a hypothetical
node-wide eviction cascade on talos06 into "the honeypot pod alone is evicted",
which is the correct blast radius. Left as an operator decision because it
introduces a new eviction behaviour that was not asked for.

Note the in-pod logs are lost on every reschedule regardless — that is by design;
do not add a PVC, it would pin the pod to a node and fight the hostPort placement.

Context: docs/05-runbooks/cowrie-public-exposure.md

title: Per-pod power attribution (Kepler) + true wall-power via smart plugs
description:
Follow-up to enabling node-exporter RAPL (node_rapl_* now flowing; panels on catalyst-k8s-dashboard 'Nodes' row).

Two gaps the RAPL work deliberately did NOT cover:

1. PER-POD ATTRIBUTION. RAPL is per-node only. Kepler (eBPF) attributes power to pods/containers, but it is a new privileged DaemonSet + scrape target + model server, so it was rejected for the node-power ask. Revisit only if per-workload power/cost becomes a real question.

2. TRUE WALL POWER. RAPL package covers CPU package only -- it excludes discrete GPUs, disks, RAM, fans and PSU losses, so the ~51W cluster figure understates the real draw. kasa-exporter already exposes 'current_consumption' (real watts) but for ONE device ('Reality Forge', KP125M). Putting each node on a metered smart plug would give ground-truth wall power per node and let us calibrate the RAPL number.

Also noted: the 'psys' RAPL zone is NOT trustworthy fleet-wide (reads ~21W on talos02-gpu but ~0.15W on talos01/talos06), which is why 'package' is used. talos03 is AMD and exposes only package/core. talos00 is a VM with an empty /sys/class/powercap and emits no node_rapl_* series at all.

title: bt-radar: expose Bluetooth radios as catalyst.io/bluetooth via KubeVirt USB device plugin
description:
Once Bluetooth works at the kernel level, expose the radios as an assignable Kubernetes
resource so the scheduler stops double-booking them and can reach the 5th and 6th.

## WHAT THIS BUYS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT

BUYS: the scheduler will not place two BLE consumers on the same radio, and it can place a
second consumer on the second radio of talos03/talos06 (2 radios each). Capacity is computed
automatically from USB enumeration.

DOES NOT BUY: deprivileging. That was the original hope and it is unreachable. Verified
against kernel source:
    af_bluetooth.c bt_sock_create()  if (net != &init_net) return -EAFNOSUPPORT
        -> a pod outside the host netns cannot create ANY Bluetooth socket. hostNetwork is
           a hard kernel requirement.
    hci_sock.c hci_sock_bind() HCI_CHANNEL_USER  requires CAP_NET_ADMIN
        -> HCI User Channel is what go-ble uses.
    hci_sock.c hci_sock_sendmsg()  commands above HCI_SFLT_MAX_OGF (5) bypass the security
        filter and need CAP_NET_RAW -> LE Set Scan Parameters / LE Set Scan Enable are
        OGF 0x08, i.e. exactly what this application issues.
There is also no device node to hand over: hciN exists only as a socket endpoint plus a sysfs
directory. Allocate() returns device nodes, mounts and env vars — it cannot return a network
namespace or a capability.

CONSEQUENCE: the allocation is ADVISORY, not enforced. For gpu.intel.com/i915 the device
cgroup physically gates /dev/dri. Here there is no device node, so the cgroup gates nothing —
any pod with hostNetwork+NET_ADMIN can still grab a radio without asking. Real mutual
exclusion comes from the kernel: hci_dev_test_and_set_flag(HCI_USER_CHANNEL) -> -EUSERS for
the second binder.

## ADOPT KUBEVIRT — no new components

KubeVirt is already running here and already advertises devices.kubevirt.io/*. Its USB device
plugin serves ORDINARY PODS, not only VMs — verified in
pkg/virt-handler/device-manager/usb_device.go: Allocate() returns a DeviceSpec with no VMI
check anywhere. It does not detach btusb (the USBDEVFS_DISCONNECT that real VM passthrough
needs happens in virt-launcher/qemu), so hciN survives allocation. virt-handler runs on all
five nodes.

Rejected: a bespoke Go plugin (unjustifiable), generic-device-plugin (a whole DaemonSet to
save a 2-line edit), and Akri (alive and well at v0.13.8, runs broker-less, and is the only
option that can match on USB CLASS rather than vendor:product — but a CNCF-sandbox controller
plus admission webhook is not worth it for five essentially static radios, in a cluster
already carrying Flux, ArgoCD, Crossplane, KubeVirt, Kyverno and ESO through an upgrade
campaign). Revisit Akri if dongle models start changing often.

## THE TRAP — one entry per chipset, never one entry with five selectors

discoverAllowedUSBDevices() calls localDevices.fetch(selectors) requiring ALL selectors
present SIMULTANEOUSLY. Multiple selectors in one entry describes a COMPOSITE device. Put all
five pairs in one entry and every node reports capacity 0. KubeVirt's own docs show the
composite form (keyboard+mouse+smartcard) and it is the wrong pattern here.

  infrastructure/base/kubevirt/cr.yaml
    developerConfiguration:
      featureGates: [HostDevices]
    permittedHostDevices:
      usb:
      - {resourceName: catalyst.io/bluetooth, selectors: [{vendor: '8087', product: '0032'}]}  # talos01
      - {resourceName: catalyst.io/bluetooth, selectors: [{vendor: '8087', product: '0037'}]}  # talos02-gpu
      - {resourceName: catalyst.io/bluetooth, selectors: [{vendor: '8087', product: '0026'}]}  # talos03 + talos06
      - {resourceName: catalyst.io/bluetooth, selectors: [{vendor: '0bda', product: 'b85b'}]}  # talos03
      - {resourceName: catalyst.io/bluetooth, selectors: [{vendor: '0bda', product: 'a728'}]}  # talos06

The outer loop appends into the same plugins[resourceName] slice, so repeated resourceName is
correct and is what aggregates capacity.

Verify the webhook accepts a non-kubevirt.io/ prefix; fall back to kubevirt.io/bluetooth.

TESTABLE BEFORE ANY KERNEL WORK — this is pure USB enumeration and does not care that
CONFIG_BT is unset:
    kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[]|{n:.metadata.name, bt:.status.allocatable["catalyst.io/bluetooth"]}'
    expect talos01=1, talos02-gpu=1, talos03=2, talos06=2, talos00 absent

## DO NOT apply a sharedDevNum multiplier

We correctly set sharedDevNum: 10 for the Intel GPU (intel-gpu-plugin-cr.yaml:48 — one
physical Arc advertised as ten allocatable units). Bluetooth is the opposite: HCI User Channel
is genuinely exclusive, so capacity = radio count, full stop.

## CONSUMER CHANGE

Minimal: keep the DaemonSet and the NFD nodeSelector, add
    limits: { catalyst.io/bluetooth: 1 }
hostNetwork and NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW stay — they are kernel requirements, not policy.

To actually reach all six radios: a Deployment with replicas 6 and NO nodeSelector, letting
the scheduler place purely by free capacity. Then two things become mandatory:
  - strategy: {type: Recreate}. Default maxSurge 25% creates a surge pod that can never
    schedule against a fully-allocated exclusive resource, and the rollout wedges.
  - -status-listen= (empty). bt-agent binds :8478 by default and under hostNetwork the second
    pod on talos03 collides on the port.
Cost: replicas becomes a hand-maintained number tracking physical hardware.

## WHY THE 5TH AND 6TH RADIOS ARE WORTH IT FOR THIS USE CASE

Not for trilateration — two radios on one node are the same vantage point. For DETECTION
PROBABILITY: BLE advertising uses three primary channels (37/38/39) and one controller dwells
on one at a time, so a single scanner misses infrequent advertisements, which is exactly the
covert-tracker case. And bt-agent's -advertise flag means one radio must interleave
advertising with scanning, cutting scan duty cycle. With two radios you dedicate one to
scanning at ~100% duty and one to advertising. Worth measuring rather than assuming, but the
direction is not in doubt.

## GATING CHECK — PASSED

/dev/bus/usb is populated with real device nodes on talos03 and talos06, verified read-only
2026-08-24. All adopt options were viable.

BLOCKED ON: bt-extension delivering working radios. There is no consumer until hciN exists.
notes:
## CORRECTION 2026-08-24 — THE SELECTOR LIST ABOVE IS WRONG. Use this one.

Verified directly from /sys/kernel/debug/usb/devices on every node (Cls=e0(wlcon) is the
Bluetooth device class):

    talos00       none              VM. Keep module signature enforcement ON.
    talos01       8087:0026         Intel      <- NOT 8087:0032 as originally recorded
    talos02-gpu   8087:0037         Intel
    talos03       0bda:b85b         Realtek    <- ONE radio, not two
    talos06       0bda:a728         Realtek
                + 8087:0026         Intel      <- the ONLY capacity-2 node

TWO ERRORS IN THE ORIGINAL, both of which would have produced a wrong capacity map:

 1. talos01's product ID was 0032; it is 0026. A selector for 0032 matches nothing, so
    talos01 would have advertised capacity 0 and never been schedulable.
 2. talos03 was recorded as having two radios. It has one. Its second USB device is
    0d8c:0014, a C-Media AUDIO adapter (Cls=01(audio), with HID) — which is also why NFD
    labels that node usb-03.present and no other node does. Counting it as a radio would have
    advertised capacity 2 on a node with one, and the second pod would have failed at
    HCI_USER_CHANNEL bind with -EUSERS rather than failing to schedule, which is a much more
    confusing symptom.

Total is still 5 radios, so the headline count was right. The distribution was not.

CORRECTED KubeVirt config. Note 8087:0026 appears on BOTH talos01 and talos06, so four
selector entries cover five radios:

    permittedHostDevices:
      usb:
      - {resourceName: catalyst.io/bluetooth, selectors: [{vendor: '8087', product: '0026'}]}  # talos01 + talos06
      - {resourceName: catalyst.io/bluetooth, selectors: [{vendor: '8087', product: '0037'}]}  # talos02-gpu
      - {resourceName: catalyst.io/bluetooth, selectors: [{vendor: '0bda', product: 'b85b'}]}  # talos03
      - {resourceName: catalyst.io/bluetooth, selectors: [{vendor: '0bda', product: 'a728'}]}  # talos06

EXPECTED after applying:
    talos01=1  talos02-gpu=1  talos03=1  talos06=2  talos00 absent

## FURTHER KERNEL FINDINGS THAT REFINE THE DESIGN

From the bt-extension agent, read from source:

 - hostNetwork is MANDATORY and unavoidable: net/bluetooth/af_bluetooth.c:121 bt_sock_create()
   returns -EAFNOSUPPORT when net != &init_net. Bluetooth is not netns-aware at all, and
   bt_sock_family_ops.create is the single entry point for ALL of PF_BLUETOOTH, so this gates
   HCI, L2CAP, RFCOMM and SCO alike. The plugin cannot deliver 'no hostNetwork'. What it CAN
   deliver is arbitration plus dropping full privileged:true to two capabilities.
 - Allocate() cannot use the Devices field. bt_class is a bare sysfs class with no devnode —
   /sys/class/bluetooth/hciN exists, /dev/hciN does not. The adapter INDEX must be conveyed by
   env var instead.
 - Capacity is 1 per radio, kernel-enforced: hci_sock.c User Channel bind does
   hci_dev_test_and_set_flag(hdev, HCI_USER_CHANNEL) and the second opener gets -EUSERS. Bind
   also fails -EBUSY if the adapter is already UP, and calls mgmt_index_removed(), so a User
   Channel holder and bluetoothd are mutually exclusive by construction.
 - ⚠️ hci INDEX IS NOT STABLE ACROSS REBOOTS — it is enumeration order. The plugin must key its
   device IDs on something stable (the USB path via /sys/class/bluetooth/hciN/device) and
   resolve to an index at Allocate time. go-ble binds by index:
       unix.SockaddrHCI{Dev: uint16(id), Channel: unix.HCI_CHANNEL_USER}
   so the index is what has to be passed, but it must not be what is remembered.
TRIAGE 2026-08-24 (read-only): no work possible yet — bt-agent cannot enumerate a radio at all (4/4 pods CrashLoopBackOff on the no-Bluetooth-subsystem preflight), so there is nothing for a device plugin to allocate. Strictly downstream of TALOS-1mog. Separately: the bt-agent DaemonSet is currently generating a continuous Kyverno pod-security-baseline PolicyViolation (hostNetwork + NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW forbidden under the baseline profile) on every pod and daemonset reconcile. That will need an exemption regardless of how the radios get exposed.

title: bt-radar: trilaterate real positions from multiple node radios instead of faking bearing
description:
The bt-radar POC plots bearing as a stable hash of the MAC, because a single BLE radio
CANNOT measure direction — it only reports RSSI. Real direction finding needs Bluetooth 5.1
AoA/AoD with a multi-antenna array, which none of our dongles have.

But we do not need an antenna array. WE ALREADY HAVE AN ARRAY: four physically separate
machines, each with its own Bluetooth radio.

## THE IDEA

Run the scanner as a DaemonSet on every node with a radio. Each node reports (mac, rssi, ts)
for what it can hear. When three or more nodes hear the same device inside a short time
window, trilaterate a real 2D position from the per-node distance estimates.

This is exactly how ESPresense and similar presence systems work, and it turns the radar from
an illustrative display into a measured one. It also upgrades the app's story from 'device
tracker' to 'indoor positioning', which is a far better demo.

Radios available (from docs/07-reference/node-inventory.md):
    talos01       Intel 8087:0032
    talos02-gpu   Intel 8087:0037
    talos03       two radios, incl. a Realtek
    talos06       Intel 8087:0026 + Realtek 0bda:a728 (Bluetooth 5.4)
    talos00       VM, no radio
Four usable listening positions, which is one more than the three needed for 2D trilateration.

## WHAT IT NEEDS

 1. Scanner becomes a DaemonSet rather than a single pinned Deployment, with the node name
    attached to every sighting. The schema already has a sightings table; it needs a node
    column and an index on (mac, ts).
 2. A NODE POSITION SURVEY. Trilateration needs the physical x,y of each machine in a common
    frame — measured with a tape, not guessed. This is the part that actually gates the
    feature, and it is manual. Store it as a ConfigMap so it can be corrected without a rebuild.
 3. A solver. Least-squares multilateration over 3+ (position, distance) pairs; scipy-style
    but in Go, or just Gauss-Newton by hand — it is a small problem.
 4. Time alignment. Sightings must be bucketed (~2-5s) so you are solving against one moment,
    not smearing a moving device across a minute.

## THE HONEST CAVEATS, which belong in the UI the same way the current ones do

 - RSSI-derived distance is noisy: 2-3x error through walls, and it changes with device
   ORIENTATION because bodies and hands attenuate. Expect metres of error, not centimetres.
 - IF THE NODES ARE PHYSICALLY CLOSE TOGETHER, THIS DEGENERATES. Trilateration needs
   geometric spread; four machines in one rack give nearly identical distances and the solve
   becomes ill-conditioned. Measure the actual separation BEFORE building the solver — if they
   are all in one cupboard, the answer is that this feature is not possible here, and finding
   that out early is cheap.
 - Report a confidence radius, not a point. A solve from three noisy distances has real
   uncertainty and the UI should show it.

## ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED: a real AoA array

Bluetooth 5.1 direction-finding hardware (e.g. a Nordic nRF52 AoA locator array) would give
true bearing from one point. Rejected as the primary path for now: it is new hardware, it needs
its own firmware, and it solves a narrower problem than multilateration does. Worth revisiting
only if the node-array approach fails the geometry test above.

## DEPENDS ON

Bluetooth working at all, which today it does not — no bluetooth modules exist in the Talos
kernel. Blocked behind the system-extension work.
notes:
## GEOMETRY: the existing nodes CANNOT provide it — distributed Pis will

Confirmed with the user 2026-08-24: the four radio-bearing nodes are CO-LOCATED. That
settles the degeneracy question this ticket raised — trilateration from them alone would be
ill-conditioned, because four machines in one rack produce near-identical distances to any
target.

They are NOT wasted. They remain valid anchors and add redundancy to a solve. They simply
cannot supply the geometric spread on their own.

The plan is to add DISTRIBUTED nodes: Raspberry Pis running Talos, placed for coverage. That
is what makes the array real, and it means the auto-calibration work described above becomes
MORE valuable, not less — hand-surveying the position of Pis scattered around a house is
exactly the chore MDS self-calibration removes.

## CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BLUETOOTH ENABLEMENT WORK

Pi Bluetooth is not the same problem as x86 Bluetooth, and assuming it is would waste the
amd64 effort:

    x86 (Intel/Realtek)   USB      btusb + btintel/btrtl   fw: intel/ibt-*.sfi+.ddc, rtl_bt/*
    Raspberry Pi (Broadcom) UART   hci_uart + btbcm        fw: brcm/BCM*.hcd

Two architectures, two driver families, two firmware sets. Both still gated on CONFIG_BT,
which is unset in the Talos kernel on (expected) both arches.

## AND IT STRENGTHENS THE bt-agent / bt-collector SPLIT

The architecture already assumed the agent is dumb and replaceable — 'an ESP32 running the
same POST contract would work'. A Pi running the same contract is exactly that case. The
collector, database and radar UI are unaffected by where the radios live.

## AUTO-CALIBRATION OF THE ARRAY GEOMETRY (restored — an earlier --notes overwrote this)

A tape-measure node survey is probably NOT needed. The array can largely calibrate itself.

### HOW: let the nodes hear each other

Each bt-agent both SCANS and ADVERTISES. Every node then measures RSSI to every other node,
giving pairwise inter-node distances. Feed that distance matrix to classical multidimensional
scaling (MDS) and it recovers the relative geometry of the array directly. No measuring, no
hand-entered coordinates.

### WHAT IT RECOVERS, AND WHAT IT CANNOT

RECOVERS: the SHAPE of the array and its SCALE. RSSI distances are metric, so unlike a
bearing-only method the solution is not scale-free.

CANNOT RECOVER, and no cleverness changes this:
  - ABSOLUTE ROTATION. A distance matrix is invariant under rotation, so 'which way is north'
    is unknowable from RSSI alone.
  - REFLECTION. A mirrored layout yields an identical distance matrix.
Both are fixed by ONE piece of human input, e.g. 'node A is north of node B'. The honest claim
is 'auto-calibrating up to rotation and reflection, with one hint to pin the frame' — never
'it knows which way is north'. Say so in the UI.

### WHY IT SHOULD BEAT ORDINARY RSSI RANGING

The anchors are STATIONARY and MAINS-POWERED. Unlike a phone in a pocket, inter-node RSSI can
be averaged over hours or days, which kills variance. Multipath BIAS remains — that does not
average out. Run calibration continuously, keep a long-window median per ordered pair, and
re-solve periodically. It also SELF-HEALS when a node is physically moved, which a
hand-entered ConfigMap never does. With Pis scattered around a house this is the difference
between a chore and a non-issue.

### IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH

 1. Agents advertise a known service UUID so they identify each other unambiguously rather
    than guessing from MAC.
 2. Collector keeps a rolling median RSSI per ORDERED node pair, then symmetrises — A->B and
    B->A differ with antenna orientation and TX power.
 3. Classical MDS: double-centre the squared-distance matrix, eigendecompose, take the top two
    eigenvectors. Small problem, no library needed.
 4. Optionally refine with a few Gauss-Newton steps against raw distances.
 5. Apply the human hint to fix rotation/reflection, then FREEZE the frame so the radar does
    not spin between refreshes.
 6. Report per-node residuals. Large residuals mean degenerate geometry — which makes the
    viability test MEASURABLE instead of a judgement call.

### THE GEOMETRY TEST COMES FREE

Build calibration FIRST. Its residuals and the spread of the recovered layout tell you
directly whether positioning is viable, with nothing measured by hand.

### 3D

Ignore it. Recovering z from RSSI across floors is far harder and residuals will be dominated
by floor attenuation. 2D per floor is the realistic target.
TRIAGE 2026-08-24 (read-only): bt-radar is DEPLOYED but has NEVER RECORDED A SINGLE OBSERVATION. Verified in-cluster: namespace bt-radar, bt-collector 1/1 Running, bt-radar-postgres 2/2 Running on local-path, IngressRoute present. Database 'btradar': devices=0, sightings=0. bt-agent DaemonSet is 4 desired / 0 ready, all four pods in CrashLoopBackOff with 35-41 restarts, exiting on the preflight 'The kernel has no Bluetooth subsystem' message — the intended, honest failure. wifi-agent Deployment is replicas:0 by deliberate choice (see the comment block in applications/bt-radar/base/30-wifi-agent.yaml). So the solver this ticket describes has no input data from EITHER source; it is blocked behind TALOS-1mog, not merely sequenced after it.

title: talos01 advertises intel.feature.node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true but has no GPU driver
description:
talos01 carries the label intel.feature.node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true while being incapable of
GPU work. Anything that selects on that label alone will schedule there and fail.

## EVIDENCE
    node         PCI device                                    i915 allocatable
    talos02-gpu  0x8086:0x7d51 Arrow Lake-P [Arc Pro 130T/140T]  10
    talos06      0x8086:0x7d51 Arrow Lake-P [Arc Pro 130T/140T]  10
    talos01      0x8086:0x46b3 Alder Lake-UP3 GT1 [UHD Graphics] (none)

talos01 has an Intel iGPU, so the label is not strictly false — but it has NO i915 Talos
extension, therefore no /dev/dri, therefore zero allocatable gpu.intel.com/i915. Its
intel-gpu-plugin pod says so directly:
    failed to read by-path dir: /dev/dri/by-path: no such file or directory

Compare the label sets. The real GPU nodes carry three more labels talos01 does not:
    extensions.talos.dev/i915 = 20260810-v1.13.9
    intel.feature.node.kubernetes.io/gpu-arc = true
    node.kubernetes.io/gpu-model = intel-arc-140t

## NOT CURRENTLY BITING, AND WHY
plex and jellyfin both select on this label AND request gpu.intel.com/i915: 1. The resource
request is the real gate — talos01 advertises zero, so the scheduler cannot place them
there regardless of the label. Verified both running on talos02-gpu with /dev/dri/card0 and
renderD128 present in-container.

So this is a latent trap, not an active outage: the first workload that selects on the label
WITHOUT also requesting the resource lands on a node with no /dev/dri.

## THE LABEL RE-APPLIES — a manual fix does not work
    kubectl label node talos01 intel.feature.node.kubernetes.io/gpu-
    -> 'node/talos01 unlabeled', then the label is BACK within ~20 seconds, confirmed over
       three polls.
It is not in talos01's machine.nodeLabels and there is no node-feature-discovery Deployment
I could find, so something else re-asserts it — most likely an NFD sidecar shipped with the
intel-gpu-plugin DaemonSet. FIND THAT SOURCE FIRST; removing the label by hand is wasted
effort.

## FIX, in order of preference
 1. Stop consuming the label as a GPU-capability signal. The accurate selectors already
    exist and are already used correctly by tdarr-worker:
        resources.limits['gpu.intel.com/i915']   <- the real gate, scheduler-enforced
        intel.feature.node.kubernetes.io/gpu-arc <- only on nodes with the driver
    Consumers to migrate: applications/arr-stack/overlays/gpu/plex-gpu-patch.yaml,
    jellyfin-gpu-patch.yaml, and scripts/gpu-vs-cpu-test.sh (which counts GPU nodes by this
    label and will report 3 where there are 2).
 2. Configure whatever emits the label so it requires the driver, not just the PCI device.

Found while auditing node affinities (TALOS-3hl8). Non-critical, no workload currently
mis-scheduled.

title: scrypted pinned to talos02-gpu to co-locate with frigate; expressed as a hostname instead of podAffinity
description:
applications/scratch/scrypted/deployment.yaml:26-28: '# Run on same node as Frigate for low latency' + nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname: talos02-gpu.

The REASON is real (scrypted rebroadcasts Arlo cameras as RTSP for frigate to consume, so same-node keeps that traffic off the wire). The EXPRESSION is wrong: it hard-codes a hostname to express 'wherever frigate is'. If frigate ever moves, this silently stops co-locating and nobody finds out.

Scrypted needs no GPU: no gpu.intel.com/i915 request, no /dev/dri mount (verified on the live pod).

BLOCKED ON STORAGE: scrypted-config is a 1Ti local-path PVC bound to rec-scratch-scrypted-config with PV nodeAffinity to talos02-gpu. So this cannot be unpinned by editing the Deployment.

PROPOSAL: when TALOS-3hl8.1 settles frigate's placement, replace this nodeSelector with a required podAffinity on app=frigate, topologyKey kubernetes.io/hostname. Then the stated intent and the mechanism are the same thing and it follows frigate automatically. Do it together with the frigate change, not before.

title: cowrie honeypot pinned to talos03 for hostPort; node choice is arbitrary and the docs point at the wrong IP
description:
infrastructure/base/honeypot/deployment.yaml:30 sets nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname: talos03.

The MECHANISM is justified: the pod is reached via hostPort 2222/2223, so its address is a node IP and moving it changes that address. The manifest even goes out of its way to keep the pod otherwise movable -- cowrie-var-lib is an emptyDir with a comment saying it is ephemeral specifically to avoid 'the local-path PVC getting pinned to a node that doesn't match the hostPort nodeSelector'. Volumes are a ConfigMap + two emptyDirs, so there is NO storage pin. This is genuinely pure metadata.

But the NODE is arbitrary, self-admittedly: clusters/catalyst-cluster/honeypot.yaml:6 says '(soft nodeSelector: talos03 -- the node is NOT tainted; dedicating a box is a later phase)'. It is also INTERNAL-ONLY -- same file: 'Deliberately NOT internet-exposed: no external-dns, no IngressRoute, no Cloudflare', LAN only. So there is no router DNAT to break.

Two things to fix:
  1. talos03 is the least-RAM node and it wedged today. A honeypot -- a workload whose entire job is to attract hostile traffic -- is the worst tenant for the weakest node. Recommend moving it.
  2. THE DOCS ARE ALREADY WRONG ABOUT WHERE IT IS. infrastructure/base/honeypot/dashboard.sh:194 and :206 tell the operator 'ssh -p 2222 root@192.168.1.54' -- that is talos00. The pod is on talos03 = 192.168.1.30 (which tests/pentest-job.yaml:97 correctly uses). Whatever node is chosen, dashboard.sh needs to match it.

One-word change in the manifest plus the dashboard.sh fix. Needs a decision on target node only.

title: two backup-schedule collisions — 02:00 and 04:00 each fire two CNPG backups at once
description:
The fleet is deliberately staggered across 02:00-04:15 so fifteen CNPG backups do not all
hit MinIO in the same minute. Two slots have two clusters each:

    02:00  catalyst-data/dagster-postgres   +  forgejo/forgejo-postgres
    04:00  boomtime/books-postgres          +  openscad/manyfold-postgres

Full current layout, 15 schedules across 13 distinct times:
    02:00 dagster, forgejo      02:10 postgres-knowledge   02:15 authentik
    02:30 crowdsec              02:45 linkwarden           03:00 homeassistant
    03:05 arr-postgres          03:10 bookorbit            03:15 plausible-db
    03:30 zipline               03:45 boomtime             04:00 books, manyfold
    04:15 guacamole

BOTH COLLISIONS PREDATE the CatalystCNPGAppDB conversions — the conversions preserved every
existing schedule verbatim, which was the correct behaviour. This is a pre-existing gap
that only became visible once all fifteen were listed together.

## OWNERSHIP MAKES THIS AWKWARD, WHICH IS THE REAL POINT
    dagster-postgres    ArgoCD, sister repo (catalyst-data)
    books-postgres      ArgoCD, sister repo (boomtime)
    manyfold-postgres   ArgoCD, sister repo (openscad)
    forgejo-postgres    Flux, this repo

So the 04:00 collision is between TWO sister-repo clusters and cannot be fixed from
talos-homelab at all. For 02:00 the only side we control is forgejo.

Free slots: 02:05, 02:20, 02:35, 02:50, 03:20, 03:35, 03:50, 04:05, 04:30.

## SUGGESTED
 - Move forgejo-postgres 02:00 -> 02:05 in this repo. Clears the 02:00 collision outright.
 - The 04:00 pair needs a change in one of the sister repos. Mind the branch trap recorded
   on 2026-08-21: run 'git branch --show-current' first and verify the push against the
   branch actually pushed to, not reflexively origin/main.

## WORTH CONSIDERING INSTEAD
CatalystCNPGAppDB requires backupSchedule with no default precisely so nobody silently
collapses the stagger. But requiring a value does not stop two authors picking the same
minute. A validating policy asserting schedule uniqueness across ScheduledBackups would
catch this at admission rather than by someone eyeballing a sorted list — that would be a
better fix than moving two times and hoping.

Low priority: MinIO handled two concurrent backups without complaint. This is about not
letting the stagger quietly erode.

title: CNPG barman-cloud sidecars: 35 containers injected with resources:{} — set via ObjectStore.instanceSidecarConfiguration
description:
Every CNPG instance pod carries a `plugin-barman-cloud` sidecar injected with literally
`resources: {}`. 35 such containers across 12 namespaces, all invisible to the
scheduler.

    kubectl get pods -n media -l cnpg.io/cluster=arr-postgres -o json | ...
      postgres              {'requests': {'cpu': '100m', 'memory': '512Mi'}}
      bootstrap-controller  {'requests': {'cpu': '100m', 'memory': '512Mi'}}
      plugin-barman-cloud   {}                                      <-- restartPolicy: Always

It is a native sidecar (restartPolicy: Always init container), so on k8s 1.29+ its
request DOES count toward pod scheduling -- and it is contributing zero.

## DISTRIBUTION

    talos06 10, talos02-gpu 9, talos01 9, talos03 7   = 35 containers

## MEASURED (14d, per container)

    namespace/cluster                    n    p50    peak
    boomtime/boomtime-postgres           3    26M    139M
    media/arr-postgres                   3    33M    136M
    catalyst-data/dagster-postgres       1    20M    171M
    authentik/authentik-postgres         3    84M     85M
    home-automation/linkwarden-postgres  3    83M     83M
    crowdsec/crowdsec-postgres           3    22M     82M
    home-automation/homeassistant-pg     3    21M     75M
    forgejo/forgejo-postgres             3    32M     75M
    crossplane-demo/plausible-db         3    30M     72M
    media-private/zipline-postgres       3    43M     67M
    media-experimental/bookorbit-pg      3    20M     65M
    openscad/manyfold-postgres           1    57M    102M
    boomtime/books-postgres              1    23M     62M
    catalyst-data/postgres-knowledge     1    32M     62M
    gaming/guacamole-postgres            1    19M     38M
    databases/plugin-barman-cloud        1    36M     45M   (the plugin deployment itself)

    total peak across all 35 sidecars: ~2.8 GiB currently unaccounted

Peak is driven by backup upload; p50 is idle. The 171M outlier (dagster) is a real
backup run.

## FIX -- declarative, at the ObjectStore CR (15 CRs cover all 35 sidecars)

The CRD supports it directly, no patching or Kyverno needed:

    kubectl explain objectstores.spec.instanceSidecarConfiguration.resources
      -> "Resources define cpu/memory requests and limits for the sidecar that runs
          in the instance pods."

Add to each of the 15 ObjectStore CRs:

    spec:
      instanceSidecarConfiguration:
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 25m
            memory: 64Mi
          limits:
            memory: 256Mi

    class: BURSTABLE. 64Mi covers idle p50 across every cluster; 256Mi gives 1.5x
    headroom over the worst observed backup peak (171M) without risking an OOMKill
    mid-upload.

    scheduler accounting delta: 35 x 64Mi = +2.19 GiB honest

## LIST THE 15 OBJECTSTORES

    kubectl get objectstore -A

## RELATED
Backup demarcation is unchanged -- CNPG still owns postgres backups, Velero still
excludes them. This ticket only gives the sidecar a request.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
CORRECTION — the premise of this ticket does not hold. Verified against the live cluster.

CLAIMED: 35 CNPG barman-cloud sidecar containers injected with resources:{}.

ACTUAL, from kubectl:
  kubectl get pods -A -l cnpg.io/podRole=instance -o json
  -> CNPG instance pods contain exactly ONE container each:
       postgres   35 pods   without requests: 0
     Every one of the 35 postgres containers HAS a memory request. There are no barman
     sidecars injected into instance pods at all.

  Searching every pod in the cluster for a container named *barman* returns ONE result:
       databases/plugin-barman-cloud-556c88b76d-ttqlw   container=barman-cloud   requests=None

So the real finding is a SINGLE unrequested container — the barman-cloud plugin Deployment
in the databases namespace — not 35. That is still worth fixing, but it is roughly 1/35th
of the impact this ticket claims and it does NOT need ObjectStore.instanceSidecarConfiguration
to fix; it is an ordinary Deployment and takes ordinary resource requests.

For the record ObjectStore.spec.instanceSidecarConfiguration DOES exist and does expose
resources, so the mechanism described here is real — it is simply not in play, because
these clusters are not running injected sidecars.

RESCOPED: set requests/limits on the plugin-barman-cloud Deployment in the databases
namespace. Measure it first — it is a long-lived controller, so its steady state is
meaningful, unlike a short-lived job.

Flagging the process point rather than the arithmetic: this number came from an automated
analysis and was taken at face value into a P1 ticket. The other children of TALOS-ri7d
should be spot-checked against live state before anyone executes them — particularly any
that quote a container count or a total-GiB reclaim, since those are the easiest figures to
get wrong and the most persuasive when wrong.

title: hot-ones image v3 missing from the local Nexus registry
description:
media-private/hot-ones is ImagePullBackOff and has been for at least an hour (0 restarts,
so it has never started this incarnation).

    image: registry.talos00/talos00-registry/hot-ones:v3
    error: ErrImagePull ... NotFound

The tag is absent from the local Nexus registry. This is a first-party image built from a
sister repo, so nothing upstream can restore it — it has to be rebuilt and pushed, or the
Deployment repointed at a tag that actually exists.

NOT caused by today's Talos upgrade: it predates the drains and shows 0 restarts, meaning
this pod never ran. Filed at P3 because nothing depends on it.

Check first whether v3 was ever pushed, or whether the manifest was bumped to v3 ahead of a
build that never happened — 'kubectl get deploy hot-ones -n media-private -o yaml' plus the
Nexus tag list will settle it in a minute.

Found during EPIC 2 post-upgrade verification.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
SOURCE LOCATED: hot-ones is NOT in talos-homelab. It is deployed by the ArgoCD app
arr-stack-private from the private sister repo git@github.com:TheBranchDriftCatalyst/talos-private.git
(path '.'), tracking-id arr-stack-private:apps/Deployment:media-private/hot-ones.

So the fix belongs in that repo, not here — either rebuild and push registry.talos00/talos00-registry/hot-ones:v3,
or repoint the Deployment at a tag that exists.

SIDE EFFECT WORTH KNOWING: this single pod is why the ArgoCD application arr-stack-private
reports health=Progressing. The app is Synced and every other resource is Healthy; ArgoCD
just cannot mark the app Healthy while one Deployment has no available replicas. So
'arr-stack-private degraded' in any status report traces to this ticket and nothing else.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-23 — this is registry-migration fallout, not a missing build.

hot-ones is deployed with:
    image: registry.talos00/talos00-registry/hot-ones:v3
That is a NEXUS path. Nexus is GONE. The registry namespace now runs zot:
    kubectl get pods -n registry  ->  zot-75f76dd56c-7k4jc  Running  7h33m
    kubectl get svc  -n registry  ->  zot  ClusterIP  5000/TCP
There is no nexus Deployment, Service or pod. The /talos00-registry/ path prefix was a
Nexus repository name and has no equivalent in zot, which serves repositories at the root.

So the pull was never going to succeed regardless of whether the image was built — the
address itself no longer resolves to anything. That also explains the 0 restarts: the pod
has never started in this incarnation, it has only ever failed to pull.

## WHERE THE MANIFESTS LIVE — three places, easy to conflate
 1. workspace/hot-ones/deploy/k8s/base/deployment.yaml declares
       catalyst-dev-registry:5005/hot-ones:dev
    That is the LOCAL DEV manifest, driven by Tilt with live_update and Vite HMR per the
    Taskfile. It is NOT what runs in the cluster and is not the thing to change.
 2. The live Deployment is owned by ArgoCD, tracking-id
       arr-stack-private:apps/Deployment:media-private/hot-ones
    from the private sister repo git@github.com:TheBranchDriftCatalyst/talos-private.git
 3. The application source is workspace/hot-ones (branch main, clean, remote hot-ones.git).

## WHAT ACTUALLY HAS TO HAPPEN
 a. Build the image from workspace/hot-ones (it has a Dockerfile and a Taskfile build task:
    frontend yarn build, then CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o bin/hot-ones ./cmd/server).
 b. Push it to zot. zot requires auth — anonymous /v2/_catalog returns 0 repositories and
    /v2/hot-ones/tags/list returns UNAUTHORIZED — so credentials are needed first.
 c. Update the image reference in talos-private, dropping the /talos00-registry/ prefix.
    MIND THE SISTER-REPO BRANCH TRAP: run 'git branch --show-current' before committing and
    verify the push against the branch actually pushed to, not reflexively origin/main.

## WORTH CHECKING SEPARATELY
If hot-ones pointed at a dead Nexus path, other workloads may too. Grep the cluster for
registry.talos00 image references and see whether anything else is only working because its
image happens to still be cached on the node it runs on — that is a latent outage that
surfaces on the next reschedule, exactly like the forgejo 16.0.2 manifest issue earlier
today.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
SECOND INSTANCE of the same dead-registry problem, found by grepping every pod:

    registry.talos00/talos00-registry/plausible-stats-exporter:latest   (1 pod)
    registry.talos00/talos00-registry/hot-ones:v3                       (1 pod)

plausible-stats-exporter is currently RUNNING — but only because its image is already
cached on the node it happens to occupy. Its address is just as dead as hot-ones'. The
moment that pod is rescheduled, drained or its node rebuilt, it fails to pull exactly the
same way. That is a latent outage sitting in the cluster right now with no symptom.

Same class as the forgejo 16.0.2 case earlier today: a workload that looks healthy purely
because of a node-local cache, one reschedule away from being unrunnable. Worth fixing both
together while the registry migration is fresh, rather than discovering the second one
during an unrelated drain.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
*** CORRECTION — TWO OF MY EARLIER CLAIMS ON THIS TICKET ARE WRONG. ***
Independently re-verified against zot with real credentials before writing this.

WRONG CLAIM 1: 'Nexus is gone, so the registry.talos00/talos00-registry/ path no longer
resolves.' The hostname and the talos00-registry/ prefix were DELIBERATELY PRESERVED across
the Nexus->Zot cutover, per TALOS-6vf's close reason: 'Preserve registry.talos00 hostname +
user panda token for transparent pull hotswap.' The authenticated catalog proves it:
    {"repositories":["talos00-registry/crossplane-demo-flex",
                     "talos00-registry/hot-ones",
                     "talos00-registry/plausible-stats-exporter","testrepo"]}
The path is fine. Nothing needs repointing.

WRONG CLAIM 2: 'plausible-stats-exporter is Running only because its image is cached on its
node, and is one reschedule from being unrunnable.' It is not. Its running digest matches
what zot serves right now
(sha256:c321be3cc83bc3922fb9e535bc7b6cad46a5fc6d8fde46546ba25367fc1b6540, HTTP 200) and it
carries imagePullPolicy: Always, so it re-resolves on every start. It reschedules fine and
is NOT a latent outage.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG: I queried zot anonymously. Its config sets defaultPolicy: ["read"] but
no anonymousPolicy, so every unauthenticated request 401s — including /v2/_catalog, which
then reads as an empty registry. I saw '0 repositories' and concluded the content was gone,
when in fact I simply had no credentials. Anonymous pulls are impossible against this
registry; any new namespace pulling from zot needs the nexus-pull-dockercfg secret.

## THE ACTUAL SCOPE — one broken workload, not two
    media-private/hot-ones                    hot-ones:v3   NOT in zot (repo exists,
                                                            tags: [])  <- THE ONLY BREAKAGE
    crossplane-demo/plausible-stats-exporter  in zot, healthy, pulls fine
    crossplane-demo/demo-flex                 in zot, replicas: 0 (paused, TALOS-4gg) —
                                              a third reference I had missed entirely
    applications/poisonarr/base/deployment.yaml:21 -> registry.talos00:5000/poisonarr:latest
                                              dormant: no namespace, not in flux-system,
                                              and :5000 is the wrong port for the Traefik
                                              route. Broken but never applies.

## WHY hot-ones FAILS, precisely
The pull error is NotFound — not Unauthorized, not x509. That proves containerd
authenticated and completed TLS, then got a clean 404. The image was built and never pushed.
It exists only in one laptop's Docker cache:
    registry.talos00/talos00-registry/hot-ones:v3  d8e1b8b505d6  178MB  linux/amd64  2026-06-15
All five nodes are amd64, so the arch matches.

## RECOMMENDATION — push the existing local v3
Repointing is not available: hot-ones is first-party, has no ghcr or upstream image, and the
repo has NO .github/workflows, so every build is manual from a laptop. That missing CI is the
real fragility here and deserves its own ticket.

Pushing the local v3 is one command, needs no manifest edit and no private-repo commit.
Tradeoff stated honestly: it pins production to a 2026-06-15 artifact whose only copy is one
laptop's Docker cache — but pushing is precisely what fixes that, moving it into durable
storage. Rebuilding from HEAD (2026-07-22) as v4 would need a talos-private commit plus an
unverified yarn+Go build, turning a one-command fix into a build-test-deploy cycle on a
service that is already down. v4 should be separate tracked work.

AWAITING APPROVAL for the push. Credentials work and nothing has been pushed.

Note: an empty repo directory talos00-registry/hot-ones now exists in zot ({"tags":[]}),
created by a write test against a non-existent path. No blobs, nothing pullable. zot runs
gc: true with gcDelay: 2h so it self-reclaims, and a real push fills it.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
RESOLVED 2026-08-24. hot-ones is Running.

    docker push registry.talos00/talos00-registry/hot-ones:v3
    -> v3: digest sha256:94b57e3763ceb61f65b753bd558a7159143e6362286bb23ddea461da10108dd1
    zot now: {"name":"talos00-registry/hot-ones","tags":["v3"]}
    pod: hot-ones-56844d75fd-f4h6w Running

The image had existed only in one laptop's Docker cache since 2026-06-15 (d8e1b8b505d6,

than Unauthorized: containerd authenticated fine and got a clean 404 for a tag that was

## STILL OPEN, and it is the real problem
hot-ones has NO CI. workspace/hot-ones has a Dockerfile and a Taskfile build task but an

or, as here, not pushed at all. Production now runs a 2026-06-15 artifact while the repo

Worth its own ticket: add a build-and-push workflow so an image reaching the cluster is a

## ALSO SETTLED HERE
The other two registry.talos00 references are fine and need no action:
  crossplane-demo/plausible-stats-exporter  in zot, healthy, imagePullPolicy Always
  crossplane-demo/demo-flex                 in zot, replicas: 0 (paused, TALOS-4gg)
And applications/poisonarr/base/deployment.yaml:21 points at registry.talos00:5000 (wrong

My earlier claims on this ticket that the registry path was dead and that
plausible-stats-exporter was one reschedule from failing were both WRONG and are corrected

title: gaming Kustomization health-checks a VM that is deliberately Halted — never passes
description:
The gaming Flux Kustomization lists VirtualMachine/gaming/windows-gameserver in its
healthChecks. That VM has runStrategy: Halted and has been Stopped for 105 days — it is
OFF ON PURPOSE. Its Ready condition is permanently False with reason VMINotExists (VMI does
not exist), so the health check can never pass.

Effect: gaming reports Ready=False with 'health check failed after 15m0s: timeout waiting
for: [VirtualMachine/gaming/windows-gameserver status: InProgress]', retries forever, and
lastAppliedRevision falls permanently behind git. All FIVE actual workloads in the namespace
(guacamole, guacamole-postgres, guacd, opensim, windows-novnc) are healthy the entire time.

Found 2026-08-23 while gating Flux stability before the control-plane promotion (EPIC 1).
It surfaced only because the virt-api expired-cert issue (TALOS-172v) put gaming in the
spotlight — otherwise a permanently-not-Ready Kustomization was just background noise.

## FIX — pick one
 (a) Remove the VirtualMachine from spec.healthChecks. A VM whose desired state is Halted has
     no meaningful readiness, so health-checking it is a category error.
 (b) If the VM is meant to be startable on demand, health-check something that reflects the
     Kustomization's real success — the Deployments — and leave the VM out.
 (c) If the VM is genuinely dead weight after 105 days stopped, delete it. Note it holds
     windows-gameserver-disk (1Ti local-path claim on talos06) plus virtio-drivers and
     windows-iso — real space, and PVCs that pin a node. That is EPIC 3 (TALOS-3hl8) scope.

## WHY IT MATTERS
A Kustomization stuck not-Ready is indistinguishable at a glance from one that is genuinely
broken. It cost real time during a pre-flight check, and it means any future 'is Flux green'
gate has a permanent false positive in it. It also means gaming has not actually applied a
git revision since b8797fea while HEAD has moved many commits.

Related: TALOS-172v (virt-api cert), TALOS-3hl8 (node affinities).
close_reason: Fixed in 99fd273a. Real cause was spec.wait: true (which makes kustomize-controller ignore spec.healthChecks and wait on every applied object), not a VM listed in healthChecks — see correction comment. gaming now Ready=True at main@sha1:2021370c, reconciles in 4.4s. CatalystCNPGAppDB/guacamole-postgres created, SYNCED=True READY=True. Live Cluster untouched: 23 tables, 0 restarts, prune=disabled intact.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
CORRECTION — the diagnosis in the description was right about the VM but wrong about
the mechanism, and that matters for the fix.

The VirtualMachine was NOT listed in spec.healthChecks. The only entry there was
Deployment/opensim, and opensim has been 1/1 Available the whole time:

  $ kubectl get deploy opensim -n gaming
  NAME      READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
  opensim   1/1     1            1           105d

The real mechanism is spec.wait: true. When wait is enabled, kustomize-controller
IGNORES spec.healthChecks and instead waits for every applied object to reach kstatus
Current. So the declared health check was never evaluated at all, and the Halted VM got
health-checked implicitly, as one of the 32 objects in the apply set:

  error: "health check failed after 15m0.048638429s: timeout waiting for:
  [VirtualMachine/gaming/windows-gameserver status: 'InProgress']"

Fix applied = option (b), but implemented as wait: false rather than by editing the
healthChecks list — removing the VM from healthChecks would have changed nothing, since
that list was inert. wait: false is what re-enables it. healthChecks extended to all four
Deployments (opensim, guacamole, guacd, windows-novnc); timeout 15m -> 5m now that it no
longer has to cover VM boot. Rationale is written into the file so it does not get
reverted.

Second contributor worth recording: Job/guacamole-dbinit sets ttlSecondsAfterFinished:
600, so it self-deletes and Flux recreates it every reconcile — under wait: true a
freshly-created (InProgress) Job was routinely in the wait set too.

Impact was worse than "background noise": the 15m stall per attempt meant the
CatalystCNPGAppDB/guacamole-postgres committed in d161ad72 had not been created. It now
exists (SYNCED=True READY=True).

Commit: 99fd273a

title: CNPG operand images inconsistent across fleet — one on Debian 11, one on deprecated system variant
description:
Surfaced while resolving TALOS-hx77.11. Five distinct operand images across 15
CNPG clusters, and two of them are on tags nobody chose deliberately.

  16.4                    plausible-db, books-postgres, boomtime-postgres
  17.0                    authentik, forgejo, crowdsec, guacamole, zipline,
                          linkwarden, homeassistant
  18.4        (plain)     manyfold-postgres
  18.4-system-trixie      arr-postgres
  18.4-standard-trixie    postgres-knowledge, dagster-postgres, bookorbit-postgres

TWO THAT ARE ACTUALLY WRONG, not just old:

 1. manyfold-postgres is on plain 18.4, which is NOT a modern flavour tag. Probed
    directly: it is Debian GNU/Linux 11 (bullseye) with barman-cloud binaries
    bundled — a legacy system-flavour image. Running a current PG major on a
    near-EOL base OS is the opposite of what the tag suggests.

 2. arr-postgres is on 18.4-system-trixie. The system flavour is DEPRECATED
    upstream — it is standard plus bundled barman-cloud binaries, and the project
    says to migrate to minimal or standard with the separate barman-cloud plugin,
    which this cluster already runs (plugin-barman-cloud v0.14.0). The bundled
    binaries are dead weight.

THE SWAP IS CHEAP AND PROVEN. bookorbit-postgres moved system-trixie ->
standard-trixie in place: same PG major, same PVC, so a rolling restart rather than
a re-initdb, and ContinuousArchiving stayed true throughout on an image with NO
bundled barman binaries — direct confirmation the CNPG-I plugin owns archiving and
the system flavour buys nothing here.

SUGGESTED TARGET: ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:18.4-standard-trixie
everywhere, pinned explicitly on every Cluster. Standard is the variant that
carries pgvector, so standardising on it also means no future pgvector migration
has to think about the image at all. Beware -minimal-, which does NOT carry vector.

CAVEATS: the 16.x and 17.x clusters are a MAJOR VERSION UPGRADE, not an image swap
— that is dump/restore or pg_upgrade, and each needs its own decision. Only
manyfold (18.4 -> 18.4-standard-trixie) and arr-postgres (18.4-system-trixie ->
18.4-standard-trixie) are same-major in-place swaps.

SEPARATELY, and worth more than the image spread: arr-postgres is C collation on
all seven of its databases and already holds migrated data, so correcting it is a
dump/restore rather than a recreate. Needs a deliberate call on whether Servarr
text ordering justifies the cost. Not folded into this ticket because it is a data
operation, not an image bump.

title: Clean up 14 Released PVs (~83Gi) left by the CNPG migrations
description:
Filed 2026-08-22. NOT YET SAFE TO DO — these are deliberate rollback points. Read the gate below before touching any of them.

## WHAT THEY ARE
14 PVs in Released state, all storageClass fatboy-nfs-appdata, all reclaimPolicy Retain,
~83Gi total on the Synology (192.168.1.36:/volume1/appdata). Every one is a byproduct of
the 2026-08-22 CNPG work:

  FROM THE NFS -> LOCAL NVMe MIGRATION (TALOS-bna2) — these are the rollback copies:
    authentik/authentik-postgres-1,2,3         8Gi each = 24Gi
    boomtime/boomtime-postgres-1,2,3          10Gi each = 30Gi

  FROM THE instances 3 -> 1 SCALE-DOWNS:
    crossplane-demo/plausible-db-3,4           2Gi each
    home-automation/homeassistant-postgres-1,3 2Gi each
    openscad/manyfold-postgres-2,3            10Gi each = 20Gi

  UNRELATED / OLDER:
    media-private/zipline-postgres             1Gi
    scratch/cdi-smoke-test                    ~284MB

## *** GATE — DO NOT DELETE YET ***
The authentik and boomtime volumes are the ONLY pre-migration copies of those databases
outside barman. They are the rollback if the NVMe move turns out to have a problem that
only surfaces under load or after a restart. Keep them until:
  - authentik SSO and boomtime have run a sensible period on NVMe without incident, AND
  - a CNPG backup taken AFTER the migration has been verified RESTORABLE (not merely
    reported complete).
Only then are these redundant. The scale-down leftovers (plausible, homeassistant,
manyfold) are lower stakes — those clusters still hold their data on the surviving
instance — but there is no urgency to reclaim 2-10Gi either.

## TWO LAYERS TO CLEAN, NOT ONE
1. The PV objects: kubectl delete pv NAME
2. *** THE DATA ON THE NAS. *** The fatboy-nfs-appdata StorageClass sets
   archiveOnDelete: true, so nfs-subdir-external-provisioner ARCHIVES the directory
   instead of removing it. Deleting the PV therefore reclaims NOTHING on the Synology —
   it renames the directory with an archived- prefix. Reclaiming the ~83Gi needs a
   second, manual step on the NAS. Verify the archive path and prefix before assuming
   any space came back. The SC pathPattern is namespace/pvc-name.

## WHY THEY EXIST (and why NOT to keep doing this for CNPG)
Retain was correct for these: at the time they were single-copy database volumes. It is
NOT the right default going forward. CNPG deletes PVCs as part of NORMAL operation —
rolling storage migration, scale-down, failover recovery, instance replacement — so
Retain would strand an orphaned PV on every rebuild and slowly fill the node. The new
CNPG volumes on local-path correctly use the StorageClass default of Delete; their
durability comes from 3 replicas plus barman to object storage, not from a reclaim
policy.

Principle worth keeping: Retain protects data that has no replication and no backup. It
is the wrong tool for data that has both.

## ALSO CHECK WHILE IN HERE
media-private/zipline-postgres is Released, but zipline was never migrated to NVMe — it
was already instances:1 on NFS. Work out WHY that PV was released rather than just
cleaning it up; it may point at unrelated PVC churn worth understanding.

Related: TALOS-bna2 (the migration that created most of these).
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-24 (read-only verification): the count in the title has grown. There are now 38 PVs in Released state cluster-wide, not 14. The additional ones came from the 2026-08-23/24 CNPG migrations (forgejo, crowdsec, and the five single-instance scale-ups). Re-inventory before acting; the rollback-point gate in the description still applies to the original 14.

title: gaming Kustomization never converges: health check on deliberately-Halted VM windows-gameserver
description:
Found while verifying TALOS-a38d.5 (unrelated to it -- gaming contains no HelmRelease).

flux-system/gaming reconciles for 15m then fails:
  health check failed after 15m0s: timeout waiting for:
  [VirtualMachine/gaming/windows-gameserver status: 'InProgress']

The VM is intentionally stopped -- spec.runStrategy: Halted, printableStatus
Stopped, Ready=False reason=VMINotExists since 2026-08-08. Flux's health check
treats a Halted VM as InProgress forever, so the Kustomization can never go
Ready. lastAppliedRevision has been stuck at b8797fea for two weeks while the
Kustomization retries every 10m and burns a 15m health-check timeout each cycle.

Everything else in gaming is healthy (guacamole, guacd, opensim, windows-novnc
all Running; opensim 1/1 and it IS in spec.healthChecks and passes).

Fix options: drop the VM from spec.healthChecks, or gate it on runStrategy, or
start the VM if it is meant to be running. Side effect worth noting: whoami and
anything else downstream of a gaming dependency inherits the not-ready state.

title: Create an Argo CD Application for the boomtime-dev preview overlay
description:
Follow-up to TALOS-hvcf (closed).

The boomtime-dev environment (dev.boomtime.knowledgedump.space) is now captured in
git at boomtime:k8s/overlays/talos00-dev/ — deployment (replicas:0), service, and
both IngressRoutes. Live matches git exactly; kubectl apply -k reproduces it.

WHAT IS STILL MISSING: continuous reconciliation. It needs its OWN Argo CD
Application, because it CANNOT be folded into the existing boomtime Application.

WHY NOT: the talos00-knowledgedump overlay carries a kustomize images:
transformer for ghcr.io/thebranchdriftcatalyst/boomtime, and the Application
layers a kustomize.images override that image-updater rewrites on every prod
publish. Kustomize matches images by NAME, so any boomtime container built under
that kustomization gets its tag rewritten. VERIFIED empirically: a deployment
pinned to :gaka-domain-framework builds out as :latest. Folding dev in would make
the preview env silently run prod's image — destroying its entire purpose.

THE FIX: add an Application in this repo at
infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/ pointed at repo boomtime, path
k8s/overlays/talos00-dev, targetRevision main, with NO kustomize.images override
and NOT registered with the boomtime ImageUpdater CRD.

Note the existing boomtime Application already ignoreDifferences on
apps/Deployment /spec/replicas — carry that over, it is what lets a manual
scale-to-1 survive selfHeal, which is exactly the revive workflow this env needs.

title: Strip the 11 hand-written velero.io/exclude-from-backup labels now that cnpg-velero-exclude is live
description:
FOLLOW-UP to TALOS-a38d item 4. The ClusterPolicy cnpg-velero-exclude landed 2026-08-21 (commit 7dd63f0b) as a deliberate ZERO-DIFF change: it is live and Ready, but every manifest still carries the literal label, so nothing has actually moved yet. This issue is the second half — removing the literals.

PRECONDITION (satisfied): policy must be live BEFORE any manifest loses its label, because the label is only re-added when the object is next admitted. It is live now.

SCOPE — 9 of the 11 clusters, NOT 11:
  Flux, in this repo (7): infrastructure/base/authentik/postgres.yaml,
    infrastructure/base/crowdsec/postgres.yaml, infrastructure/base/forgejo/postgres.yaml,
    applications/home-automation/base/homeassistant/postgres.yaml,
    applications/home-automation/base/linkwarden/postgres.yaml,
    applications/crossplane-demo/plausible/postgres.yaml,
    applications/zipline/postgres.yaml
  ArgoCD, SISTER repos (2): boomtime/boomtime-postgres, openscad/manyfold-postgres

  EXCLUDED — gaming/guacamole-postgres and boomtime/books-postgres. Both have NO barman
  plugin, so the policy will NOT re-add the label and stripping it would change real
  behaviour (Velero would start covering them). Resolve TALOS-rs99 and TALOS-1psu first;
  those decide whether each cluster wants CNPG backups or Velero coverage.

METHOD — one cluster at a time, verify in between:
  1. Remove the 3 inheritedMetadata lines from ONE manifest.
  2. flux reconcile kustomization <ks> --with-source (fetch source first, or you verify
     stale state).
  3. Confirm the live object STILL has the label:
     kubectl get cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io -n <ns> <name> -o jsonpath='{.spec.inheritedMetadata}'
     If the label is gone, STOP and revert — Velero will begin snapshotting a live Postgres
     data directory.
  4. Only then move to the next.

GOTCHA — the 2 ArgoCD ones are the risky half. Stripping the label from a sister repo makes
the LIVE object (mutated by admission) differ from git, so ArgoCD will report OutOfSync and,
if the Application has selfHeal, will fight the webhook. Either add an ignoreDifferences
entry for /spec/inheritedMetadata/labels on those Applications, or just leave those two
literals in place — the policy is a safety net for them either way and the 2 duplicated
blocks are cheap. Both boomtime and openscad are Synced/Healthy today; check them after.

Verification that the policy does the work is already recorded on TALOS-a38d.4 / commit
7dd63f0b: live admission tests showed the label added on a cluster with no inheritedMetadata,
added alongside an unrelated label and annotations without clobbering, and NOT added to a
cluster with no barman plugin.

title: DRY-up audit: consolidate ~160 duplicated config blocks into Kyverno policies
description:
Full audit 2026-08-21 of duplicated config across talos-homelab, ranked by (copies eliminated x blast-radius safety). Nothing implemented yet — this is the backlog.

## TIER 3 — dead config, delete today, NO policy needed
9. TWO SUPERSEDED NETPOLS ARE LIVE TWICE RIGHT NOW (verified in-cluster):
     argocd/allow-monitoring-to-argocd-dragonfly  (generated, 10d)
     argocd/allow-monitoring-to-dragonfly         (hand, 11d)  <- same podSelector app=argocd-dragonfly
     authentik/allow-monitoring-to-authentik-cache (generated, 10d)
     authentik/allow-monitoring-to-dragonfly       (hand, 11d)  <- same podSelector app=authentik-cache
   dragonfly-allow-monitoring.yaml claims to replace both, but the files are still referenced
   (argocd/kustomization.yaml:19, authentik/kustomization.yaml:12).
   CAUTION: KEEP allow-monitoring-to-repo-server (:8081) in the argocd file — the generate policy does NOT cover it. The authentik file can be deleted outright.
10. crowdsec/postgres.yaml:27-32 hand-writes the 4 reflector annotations that reflect-cnpg-app-secrets already stamps (verified live). Only 1 of 11 CNPG clusters still does this; forgejo/postgres.yaml:16 documents the correct 'no per-cluster inheritedMetadata needed'.

## TIER 1 — high value, low risk
1. gethomepage.dev/href scheme — 50 copies/50 files. The EXISTING homepage-annotation-derivation.yaml already derives href but hard-codes http://; that is the only reason ~45 hand-written overrides exist. Verified: no IngressRoute lists both entrypoints (79 websecure-only, 111 web-only), so contains(spec.entryPoints,'websecure') is a clean discriminator. One-line change, no new RBAC, add-if-absent preserves real overrides (pihole /admin, iocaine).
2. gethomepage.dev/widget.url — 17 copies, byte-identical to siteMonitor in 17 of 17. Third rule on the same policy.
3. tls: {} on websecure IngressRoutes — 65 copies/58 files. Only 2 use non-empty tls (vpn-gateway secure-chrome/secure-webtop, both passthrough:true). New mutate on traefik.io/v1alpha1/IngressRoute.
4. CNPG velero.io/exclude-from-backup — 11 copies (8 in-repo, 3 in SISTER repos). A ClusterPolicy is the only way this repo can enforce the invariant on boomtime/books/manyfold postgres. RISK: mutates an ArgoCD-TRACKED top-level resource (unlike oidc-hostalias which mutates Pods) — can show OutOfSync. Sequence: land policy while manifests still carry the label (zero diff), THEN strip manifests one at a time.
5. HelmRelease remediation retries:3 — 77 blocks/44 files. GOTCHA: parent keys must be plain, not +() — use spec.install.+(remediation).+(retries):3, since a +() anchor on an existing install: will not recurse. Dry-run with kyverno apply over all 44 first.

## TIER 2 — real but more design
6. Per-site analytics middleware pair (4 objects). sites-middlewares.yaml literally documents a copy-paste protocol. Kyverno generate off catalyst.io/analytics=true.
7. Anti-control-plane nodeAffinity — 2 copies (clickstack mongodb.yaml:107, clickhouse.yaml:76). Borderline by the 2-copy rule, but the BUG CLASS is generic (local-path WaitForFirstConsumer pins the PV; restoring the control-plane taint stranded both). An opt-in catalyst.io/no-control-plane mutate names the pattern.
8. default-deny + allow-dns CiliumNetworkPolicy — 2 copies (honeypot, iocaine). HIGHEST blast radius on the list: a default-deny generated into a wrong namespace black-holes it. Only worth it if more tarpit namespaces are expected.

## REJECTED, with reasons (do not re-litigate)
- cluster-wide securityContext mutate: 141 occurrences but runAsUser takes 8 distinct image-specific values. Namespace PSS labels are the right tool.
- authentik forward-auth middleware injection: 49 routes, 19 use the /api-exclusion two-route pattern; a mutate.foreach bug either strips auth from a UI route or breaks nzb360/LunaSea/RSS.
- Flux prune:true default (58 copies): add-if-absent on a DESTRUCTIVE default means a forgotten field silently enables pruning.
- cross-namespace secrets: already solved (ghcr-secret is a ClusterExternalSecret across 57 ns; the 3x discord-webhook / 3x cloudflare-dns ExternalSecrets target DIFFERENT keys and reflector copies bytes without renaming — crowdsec/externalsecret.yaml:74-78 documents this).
- ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor consolidation: already done (cnpg-clusters, mongodb-clusters, rabbitmq-clusters, redis-exporter are fleet-wide).

## WRONG MECHANISM — flagged, NOT Kyverno
- authentik/externalsecret.yaml (449 lines): 12 near-identical authentik-<app>-oidc ExternalSecrets + 4 byte-identical Password generators. Densest duplication in the repo. Native fix is ESO ClusterGenerator + a kustomize component. *** DANGER: changing sourceRef.generatorRef changes the ES spec, which REGENERATES the secret — rotating live OIDC client secrets and breaking the Authentik handshake for immich/audiobookshelf/komga/kavita. See the ESO generator-rotation gotcha. ***
- applications/media-experimental/base/*/patch-ingressroute.yaml: 8 files ~90% identical -> kustomize component, not Kyverno.
- infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/*.yaml: 8 Applications -> ApplicationSet with a list generator. A Kyverno default on syncPolicy.automated would silently enable auto-prune+selfHeal on future manual-sync Applications.

## SUGGESTED ORDER
9+10 first (pure deletion, minutes). Then 1+2 (one file, no new RBAC, ~67 lines). Then 3. Then 4 with the land-then-strip sequencing. 5 last with a dry-run.

## UNVERIFIED
- Whether Kyverno can inject a CRD-REQUIRED field (the flux sourceRef block, 78 copies/64 Kustomizations). Mutating webhooks run before schema validation so it should work — untested, and surprising enough not to recommend regardless.
- ArgoCD diff behaviour for #4 on the 3 sister-repo Clusters depends on per-Application server-side diff, not checked.

title: CrowdSec: onboard UniFi + Synology DSM (syslog acquisition, not pod logs)
description:
Wave 1+2 covered every app running IN the cluster (16 acquisition sources, 25 collections). The remaining blind spots are the two appliances OUTSIDE it, both of which have hub support:

  crowdsecurity/unifi          UniFi controller — login brute-force, admin access
  crowdsecurity/synology-dsm   Synology DSM at 192.168.1.36 — the NAS backing every media/appdata PV

WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE OF WORK: all current acquisition reads
/var/log/containers/*.log via the agent DaemonSet. Neither appliance runs in
k8s, so there are no pod logs to tail. They must SHIP logs to CrowdSec instead:
 1. enable remote syslog on the UniFi controller and on DSM (Control Panel ->
    Log Center -> forward), pointed at a syslog listener
 2. stand up that listener — either a syslog acquisition on the agents
    (source: syslog, listen_addr/port) or a small syslog-ng/rsyslog shim that
    writes to a file the agents already tail
 3. add the collections and label the source so the parsers match (verify each
    parser's  filter first — the *arr parsers needed CAPITALISED values
    and Forgejo needed 'gitea', both of which would have silently parsed nothing)
 4. ship the scenarios in SIMULATION first, per the wave-1/2 convention

VALUE: the Synology is the storage substrate for essentially all media and
appdata PVs — a compromise there is worse than most in-cluster app compromises.
UniFi is the network control plane.

PREREQ CHECK: confirm a UniFi controller actually exists on this network and
where it runs. It is NOT in the cluster (verified 2026-08-21). If there is no
controller, only the Synology half applies.

CAUTION: opening a syslog listener on the agents adds an inbound network surface
to every node. Prefer binding it to the LAN interface only.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
DONE 2026-08-22 via TALOS-zjh0, migrated alongside postgres-knowledge.

Correction to the likely assumption behind this ticket: dagster-postgres was NOT
pgvector. It ran postgres:16-alpine and pg_extension contained plpgsql only, so it
is a stock CNPG cluster with no extension question at all.

Measured 493 MB datadir / 437 MB database, 22 tables, 443075 rows dominated by
event_logs (323779). New PVC sized 10Gi against a 1Ti inherited claim. All 22 tables
verified identical by count and content checksum.

One nuance recorded for the future: the alpine source ran musl, whose en_US.utf8
collates like C. The CNPG cluster uses real glibc en_US.utf8, so text ORDER BY in
dagster genuinely differs from the source. Chosen deliberately — it matches the
locale the database always claimed and matches the rest of the fleet — and indexes
were rebuilt on restore so there is no collation-mismatch corruption risk.

Old Deployment and PVC left at 0 replicas as the rollback; deletion is user-gated in
TALOS-qrna.

notes: DECISION (2026-08-07): go with PLAUSIBLE Community Edition (not PostHog). Rationale: it's the actual GA replacement (privacy-first, cookieless); deps are ClickHouse+Postgres ONLY → map 1:1 to the Altinity + CloudNativePG operators from TALOS-ja5; ~2-4Gi footprint (fits one node) vs PostHog ~32Gi + Kafka (Strimzi/Redpanda not installed) + officially-unsupported-on-K8s since 2023. title: NFD master/worker high restart churn
description: node-feature-discovery-master ~772 restarts and each node-feature-discovery-worker ~1300 restarts over ~63d (~12-20/day). Labels are stable despite the churn (discovery still works), but the crash cadence suggests OOM or liveness-probe flapping. Investigate resources/probes in infrastructure/base/intel-gpu/nfd-helmrelease.yaml. Discovered during TALOS-ea6.
notes: ROOT CAUSE: NFD v0.17.4 treats transient kube-API VIP (10.96.0.1:443) loss as FATAL. NOT OOM (limits 4Gi master/512Mi worker; Last State=Error not OOMKilled), NOT probe-flapping (no probe-fail events). Worker exits 1 on 'no route to host' getting own pod for ownerReference. Master exits 2 via SIGSEGV nil-deref in leader-election shutdown path (NamespaceLister.stop) — and runs -enable-leader-election despite replicaCount=1 (pure downside). CHURN ALREADY STOPPED: all restart counts froze 2026-07-06 ~16:33 (one cluster-wide API/Cilium blip), clean 26d since; benign (labels persist). Fragility remains for next blip. FIX OPTIONS: A) bump chart 0.17.*->0.18.* (addresses both, confidence med on worker path); B) Flux postRenderer stripping -enable-leader-election from single-replica master (deterministic master fix, worker still restarts benignly on 0.17.x). Do NOT raise mem/loosen probes.
close_reason: Fixed via chart bump 0.17.x->0.18.3. Root cause: NFD v0.17.4 fatal-on-transient-API-loss (worker exit1; master SIGSEGV in leader-election shutdown). Churn was already dormant (froze 26d ago after one Jul-6 blip). Verified: all 6 NFD pods rolled to v0.18.3, 0 restarts, HelmRelease Ready, NodeFeatureRule + gpu/gpu-arc labels survived, tdarr workers healthy.

title: Talos nodeLabels not reconciling on worker nodes
description: machine.nodeLabels in Talos worker configs (node.kubernetes.io/workload-type, topology.kubernetes.io/zone, node-role.kubernetes.io/worker) never appear on the K8s Node objects. Verified on talos06 + talos02-gpu: labels present in live machineconfig (talosctl get mc) but absent from 'kubectl get node'. node-role.kubernetes.io/* is expected (reserved prefix Talos drops), but the non-reserved ones should apply and don't. A custom homelab.dj/gpu-worker test label patched live also never appeared. Root-cause: Talos version (1.13.2) behavior, kubelet NodeRestriction, or a feature gate. Not urgent — no workload currently depends on Talos-set nodeLabels (tdarr migrated to NFD gpu-arc label in TALOS-ea6). Discovered during TALOS-ea6.
notes: ROOT CAUSE: Talos k8s.NodeApplyController submits ALL machine.nodeLabels as ONE atomic Node update using the node's kubelet identity (system:node:<name>). kube-apiserver NodeRestriction (confirmed enabled) rejects the WHOLE update because it contains node-role.kubernetes.io/* labels (worker, gpu-worker) which a node may never self-assign. Atomic = the permitted labels (node.kubernetes.io/workload-type, topology.kubernetes.io/zone, *-model) are collateral damage and never persist either. Proof: machined logs show 'NodeApplyController failed: nodes talosNN is forbidden: is not allowed to modify labels: node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu-worker, node-role.kubernetes.io/worker' retrying ~60s. gpu-model on talos06 is an orphan manual kubectl label, not proof Talos works (siblings absent). FIX: remove node-role.kubernetes.io/{worker,gpu-worker} from machine.nodeLabels on ALL workers (talosctl patch mc, NO reboot); permitted labels land next reconcile. Do NOT re-add role labels to config (use kubectl one-shot or Talos CCM if ROLES column wanted). Reboot does NOT help. Adjacent: taint regression siderolabs/talos#13443 on v1.13.3.
close_reason: Fixed. Root cause: atomic NodeApply rejected wholesale by NodeRestriction because machine.nodeLabels contained node-role.kubernetes.io/{worker,gpu-worker}, poisoning all permitted labels. Stripped node-role labels from live machineconfigs on talos01/02-gpu/03/06 via talosctl patch mc (no reboot). Verified: NodeApplyController errors stopped, and workload-type/zone/*-model labels now land on all 4 workers for the first time. Synced gitignored local config files. Role labels intentionally NOT re-added (would re-poison); use kubectl/Talos CCM out-of-band if ROLES column wanted.

title: etcd-backup CronJob: prune command broken (awk missing in minio/mc image, 312 snapshots accumulated)
description:
## Why

Discovered during the 2026-05-29 manual snapshot trigger test. The `upload` container of `etcd-backup` runs `mc` (minio/mc image) for S3 upload + retention pruning, but the prune step uses `awk` which isn't in the minio/mc image:

```
[*] Pruning to last 168...
/bin/sh: line 18: awk: command not found
[*] Done. Total snapshots: 312
```

Retention is `RETENTION_COUNT: "168"` (1 week at hourly) but we have **312 snapshots** in S3. This isn't causing cluster impact (S3 is fine), but it IS quietly violating the retention policy.

## Fix options

1. Replace awk with mc's own listing/sort + jq/grep tail:
   ```sh
   mc ls --json "${S3_DIR}" | jq -r '.key' | sort | head -n "${to_delete}"
   ```
   (jq is also not in minio/mc... so really only `sort | head` portable tools)

2. Add a tiny image with both tools (busybox-multi-arch + mc)

3. Use `mc ilm` (information lifecycle management) on the bucket to auto-prune by age — proper S3-native retention. Much cleaner.

**Recommended: option 3** (mc ilm).

## File

`infrastructure/base/backup/etcd-backup.yaml` lines ~119-130

## Acceptance

- Prune works (either via fixed script or mc ilm)
- Backup count stays at or below RETENTION_COUNT
- Verify by checking S3 backup count over 7 days
acceptance_criteria:
- Snapshot count stays ≤ RETENTION_COUNT after fix
- No prune errors in next 7 runs of the CronJob

title: Re-enable Cilium ClusterMesh when federation peer cluster goes live
description:
## Why

- It was running 3 containers (etcd + apiserver + kvstoremesh) pinned to the control-plane via `requiredDuringScheduling` nodeAffinity
- `enable-external-workloads=false` — no peer cluster registered yet
- Its embedded etcd was contributing to control-plane load and likely a meltdown trigger
- The whole 4-day-meltdown cycle was partly attributable to this overload

## What to do when bringing federation live

1. Confirm the AWS lighthouse peer cluster is actually ready (certs valid, NodePort 32379 reachable from peer side via Nebula IP `10.100.2.1`)
2. **Before scaling back to 1**: re-evaluate the nodeAffinity pin to control-plane.
   - Original justification: NodePort 32379 needs to be at Nebula IP `10.100.0.1` (only on talos00)
   - After **TALOS-ha-cp** lands and all 3 CPs have Nebula, this pin can be removed (clustermesh-apiserver can run on any CP, NodePort still routes correctly)
   - Until then, keep the pin but acknowledge the load it adds
3. Scale to 1: `clustermesh.apiserver.replicas: 1`
4. Render manifests, helm apply (Cilium is not in GitOps — see TALOS-cilium-gitops)
5. Verify cross-cluster pod-to-pod connectivity works
6. Update ADR / docs

## Acceptance

- Federation peer cluster verified ready
- clustermesh-apiserver scaled back to 1 in `configs/cilium-values.yaml`
- Cross-cluster connectivity verified
- Monitoring includes ClusterMesh API health alert
acceptance_criteria:
