- clustermesh-apiserver: replicas=1 + cross-cluster pod ping works
- Decision made on nodeAffinity (keep / remove based on HA state)

title: Auto-heal stuck Cilium agents — START IN DRY-RUN (Discord notify only, no delete)
description:
## Why

Today's recovery was 80% "delete the cilium pod and let it restart" — once the control plane was healthy, the fresh cilium pods came up clean on the first try. This pattern is mechanical enough to automate.

## ⚠️ DEPLOYMENT STRATEGY: Dry-run first

**Phase 1 (initial deployment):** DRY-RUN MODE — observe-only.
- CronJob runs every 5 min
- Evaluates would-heal candidates (same logic as Phase 2)
- Posts to Discord: "🔍 [DRY-RUN] would have deleted pod `cilium-XXX` on `talos02-gpu` (CrashLoopBackOff 23m, restarts 47). All safety gates passed."
- Does NOT actually call `kubectl delete`
- Toggle via `DRY_RUN=true` env var on the CronJob (default: true)

**Phase 2 (after we trust the logic):** ACTIVE MODE — flip `DRY_RUN=false` after observing dry-run notifications for at least a week and confirming:
- No false positives (didn't propose deletes during a real meltdown)
- Detection threshold is right (not too eager, not too slow)
- Discord notifications are readable and actionable

## What it should do

A CronJob (every 5 min) that:
1. Checks all cilium-agent pods
2. If any pod has been in CrashLoopBackOff > 15 minutes AND its restart count is climbing AND **the control plane is reachable** (don't make a partition worse), it would `kubectl delete pod` (but in dry-run, just logs/notifies)
3. Always logs to Discord via the existing notification system:
   - Dry-run: "🔍 [DRY-RUN] Would heal `cilium-XXX` on `nodeY` (CrashLoopBackOff Zm, NN restarts). Safety gates: ✓ CP reachable, ✓ Only 1 pod unhealthy, ✓ Not recently healed."
   - Active mode (later): "🔧 Auto-healed `cilium-XXX` on `nodeY` (was in CrashLoopBackOff for Zm)"
   - Always: "🚫 Skipped heal of `cilium-XXX` because <safety gate that failed>"

## Safety gates (CRITICAL — these MUST work correctly in dry-run before activating)

- Skip if `kubectl get --raw /readyz` doesn't return 200
- Skip if any apiserver static pod has a recent (<5m) restart
- Skip if MORE than 1 cilium pod is unhealthy (smells like network meltdown — needs human)
- Max 1 deletion per cron run
- Rate-limit: don't delete the same pod twice within 30 min (in dry-run: don't re-notify about the same pod within 30 min)

## Files

`infrastructure/base/monitoring/cilium-self-heal/cronjob.yaml` (new dir)
- ConfigMap with the shell script (or small Go binary baked into image)
- ServiceAccount + RBAC: get/list pods in kube-system, delete pods in kube-system, get /readyz
- CronJob with env vars: `DRY_RUN=true`, `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_SECRET=discord-webhook`, thresholds

## Acceptance

- Phase 1: CronJob deployed in dry-run, posts to Discord on its first eligible evaluation
- Safety gates verified by simulating apiserver unreachable → CronJob skips and notifies "🚫 Skipped — CP unreachable"
- Dry-run notifications run for ≥1 week with no false positives before flipping DRY_RUN to false
- Phase 2 toggle is a 1-line env var change (no logic change)
- Documentation explains how to toggle and how to permanently disable
acceptance_criteria:
- Phase 1: CronJob deployed in DRY-RUN mode, posts to Discord on first eligible evaluation
- Phase 1: Safety gate test passes (simulate apiserver unreachable → CronJob skips & notifies)
- Phase 1: ≥1 week observation with no false positives before considering Phase 2
- Phase 2: 1-line env var toggle to activate, no code/logic change
- Documentation includes both toggle and permanent-disable instructions

title: Rename talos02-gpu -> talos02 — NOT SAFE as a simple rename; needs storage evacuation first
description:
Requested for naming consistency. Investigated 2026-08-24: a straight rename would strand 15
volumes and destroy data on 10 of them. Recording the analysis so the cost is known.

## WHY IT IS NOT A SIMPLE RENAME

    15 local-path PVs pin to 'talos02-gpu' by nodeAffinity
    22 manifest files in git reference the name
    15 running pods select on it via nodeSelector/affinity

PersistentVolume.spec.nodeAffinity IS IMMUTABLE — verified with a server-side dry-run patch,
which the API server rejects outright. So those 15 cannot be re-pointed; they would have to be
deleted and recreated.

RECLAIM POLICY ON THE 15:
    Delete: 10      <- deleting the PV DELETES THE UNDERLYING DATA
    Retain:  5

The ten Delete-policy volumes include boomtime-postgres-1, authentik-postgres-1,
bt-radar-postgres-2 and mimir-store-gateway. Renaming the node without evacuating first
destroys those.

## THE CONSISTENCY ARGUMENT IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS

 - talos06 ALSO has an Intel Arc GPU and carries no -gpu suffix, so the suffix is already not
   a reliable signal for 'this is the GPU node'.
 - There is no talos04 or talos05; the sequence is already non-contiguous.
 - The suffix currently does useful work — it is how you tell at a glance which box has
   transcode hardware.

A cheaper way to get consistency: give talos06 a -gpu suffix instead, or drop the idea that
hostnames encode hardware and rely on the NFD labels, which already answer this correctly
(feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-0300_8086_7d51.present on both GPU nodes).

## ONE GENUINE ARGUMENT FOR DOING IT

talos02-gpu's META partition already contains 'hostname: talos02' — its pre-rename name. That
is a latent hazard recorded in the talhelper cutover runbook: if config ever fails to load at
boot, the node comes up as talos02, registers as a NEW Node object, and all 15 pinned PVs
become unschedulable. Renaming the node to talos02 would RESOLVE that mismatch rather than
documenting around it.

But  resolves it too, at a fraction of the cost.

## IF IT IS DONE ANYWAY, THE ORDER IS

 1. Evacuate stateful workloads off talos02-gpu — CNPG replica migration one at a time, the
    documented pattern; let local-path PVs be recreated elsewhere.
 2. Confirm zero PVs remain pinned to the name.
 3. Rename in talconfig + machine config.
 4. Update the 22 manifest references.
 5. Delete the stale META key so the fallback identity matches.

That is a multi-session piece of work and it COLLIDES with the talhelper cutover, which is at
parity and twice-audited. Doing it underneath that migration means re-running both audits
against a moving target.

RECOMMENDATION: not now. After the cutover lands and settles, if still wanted.

DEFERRED 2026-08-24. Recorded so a future attempt does not restart from nothing.

WHY DEFERRED: the user could not locate their Alfa USB adapter, and the project's purpose
shifted to counter-surveillance — detecting devices NOT associated with our network. BLE
answers that directly (advertisements are broadcast by everything nearby, no association
needed), so Bluetooth became the MVP and WiFi dropped behind it. See TALOS-1mog.

## VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE CLUSTER

Hardware is present and idle — every node is wired, so the radios are unused:
    talos01      Intel Alder Lake-P PCH CNVi WiFi   PCI 0280, 8086:51f0
    talos02-gpu  Intel Arrow Lake CNVi WiFi         PCI 0280, 8086:7740
    talos06      Intel Arrow Lake CNVi WiFi         PCI 0280, 8086:7740
    talos03      Realtek RTL8852BE 802.11ax         PCI 0280, 10ec:b852
    talos00      none (VM)

Idle is not usable. From /proc/config.gz on a live node:
    CONFIG_WIRELESS=y
    # CONFIG_CFG80211 is not set        <- no wifi stack at all
    # CFG80211 needs to be enabled for MAC80211
No wlan* interface exists on any node; nothing is bound to that hardware.

## WHY THIS IS HARDER THAN BLUETOOTH, NOT EASIER

 1. MUCH LARGER CONFIG DELTA. Bluetooth needed two lines (CONFIG_BT=m, CONFIG_BT_HCIBTUSB=m)
    and everything else came from Kconfig select. WiFi needs CFG80211 and MAC80211 both, plus
    iwlwifi/iwlmvm for the three Intel parts and rtw89 for the Realtek, each with firmware.
 2. ⚠️ THE n→m DISCIPLINE MAY NOT HOLD. The Bluetooth work was safe because EVERY config delta
    was n→m, so nothing built-in changed and the CRC equivalence gate passed — 313 symbols,
    zero mismatches. CFG80211 selects RFKILL, currently n, and there may be others that land
    as =y. If any symbol outside the target namespace flips to =y, that equivalence no longer
    holds and the approach collapses into a real kernel fork. THIS IS THE FIRST THING TO
    CHECK and it is cheap: generate the config, diff it, look for n→y.
 3. INTEL CNVi SHARES ONE RADIO BETWEEN WIFI AND BLUETOOTH. That is why those same machines
    enumerate Intel 8087:* Bluetooth radios over USB. Bluetooth is now real on those nodes, so
    whether iwlwifi contends with btusb for the shared module is an open and now-load-bearing
    question. NOT INVESTIGATED.
 4. INTEL MONITOR MODE IS UNRELIABLE. iwlwifi's support is partial and generation-dependent.
    Even with the stack built, usable probe-request capture is not guaranteed — and monitor
    mode is the ENTIRE point for counter-surveillance. Verify capability before building
    anything; a clean module build that cannot capture a frame is worthless here.

## THE EASY PATH IF IT RESUMES: a USB adapter, not the built-in cards

An Alfa AWUS036-series adapter (the user owns one, currently misplaced) sidesteps most of this:
    AWUS036NHA    AR9271     ath9k_htc   IN-TREE, best-in-class monitor mode
    AWUS036ACM    MT7612U    mt76x2u     in-tree, good
    AWUS036AXML   MT7921AU   mt7921u     in-tree, good
    AWUS036ACH    RTL8812AU  88XXau      ⚠️ OUT-OF-TREE, materially harder
USB means its own radio and antenna — no CNVi contention with Bluetooth — and it is portable
between nodes. NFD already labels USB devices by class, so a node with it plugged in is
selectable automatically.

## WHY UNIFI CANNOT SUBSTITUTE — verified

    GET /proxy/network/api/s/{site}/stat/sta      returns only ASSOCIATED clients, i.e.
                                                 precisely the devices that are NOT of interest
    GET /proxy/network/api/s/{site}/stat/rogueap  returns neighbouring ACCESS POINTS, not
                                                 unassociated client devices
Probe requests are not exposed through the API at all. So there is no API shortcut to
unassociated-device detection; monitor mode is genuinely required.

## REUSE THIS, DO NOT REBUILD IT

bt-extension's approach and gate scripts solve the shared problem: rebuild the OFFICIAL kernel
from pinned inputs with a minimal delta, discard the kernel, ship only the .ko files. Nodes
keep Sidero's vmlinuz. crcgate.py and rungate.py implement the reboot-free CRC/vermagic
equivalence proof and are reusable as-is. See docs/05-runbooks/bluetooth-enablement.md.

ONE KERNEL BUILD SHOULD EMIT BOTH. If WiFi resumes while Bluetooth is still being iterated,
combine the config deltas rather than running two builds — the build is the expensive artefact
(~45 min emulated) and two builds produce two Module.symvers that each need re-gating.

⚠️ module.sig_enforce=0 SILENTLY FAILS — Talos appends extras after defaults and the kernel
refuses the downgrade with -EROFS. The correct form is the negation, -module.sig_enforce,
proven by control experiment. Verify by ABSENCE of the token in /proc/cmdline.

title: topology.kubernetes.io/zone is set on only 2 of 5 nodes; RabbitMQ spreads on it
description:
Only talos02-gpu and talos06 carry topology.kubernetes.io/zone=homelab. talos00, talos01 and talos03 have no zone label at all.

boomtime/boomtime-rabbit-server and crossplane-demo/demo-rabbit-server both set a topologySpreadConstraint on topology.kubernetes.io/zone. With three of five nodes unlabelled and the other two sharing a single zone value, that constraint can never spread anything. whenUnsatisfiable is ScheduleAnyway so it is soft and nothing is broken today -- it is simply dead config that reads as if it provides HA.

Either label all five nodes with a zone that means something, or drop the constraint. Currently it is neither.

No action taken. Filed so the talos00 assumption gets re-verified before clustermesh is turned on.

title: Add non-root USER to tools/carrierarr/Dockerfile
description:
carrierarr's Dockerfile runs as root in the final image — no `USER` instruction in the runtime stage. Add a non-root user (uid 10001, no shell) and chown the /app directory accordingly.

Snippet to add before ENTRYPOINT:
```
RUN addgroup -g 10001 -S carrierarr && \
    adduser -u 10001 -S -G carrierarr carrierarr && \
    chown -R carrierarr:carrierarr /app
USER carrierarr
```

Verify the runtime deps (aws-cli, openssh-client) work as non-root — they should, but test before shipping. Drop CAP_NET_BIND if container is using port < 1024 (it's not — 8090 — so no concern).

Also consider for the same Dockerfile:
- Add BuildKit cache mount for `go mod download` (10x faster repeated builds)
- Audit .dockerignore in repo root

Discovered during TALOS-r5w (multi-stage-dockerfile skill smoke-test).
acceptance_criteria: Image rebuilds, container starts non-root (verify with `docker run --rm carrierarr id`), health check passes, no permission errors in logs.

title: Remove vestigial 'Copy this file to talos-homelab' comment in catalyst-llm ArgoCD Application

# ArgoCD Application manifest for catalyst-llm

description:
